title: muon_ns_xtx CUDA kernel produces incorrect results on RTX 5070 (sm_120)
description: test_muon_ns_xtx_cuda (kernels/teeny-kernels/tests/test_optim_muon.rs) fails with a numerical mismatch on RTX 5070 (sm_120): got=0.19849598 expected=0.13091198 at index 1 of the T = X @ X.T output. Test currently marked #[ignore] to unblock CI/local test runs. Likely related to the recent GPU execution fixes for RTX 5070 (commit 376554b9d) that did not fully resolve this kernel's correctness.
acceptance_criteria: test_muon_ns_xtx_cuda passes on RTX 5070 without the #[ignore] attribute; #[ignore] removed from kernels/teeny-kernels/tests/test_optim_muon.rs:204
notes:
Retested 2026-09-29 and still reproduces, bit-identically: got=0.19849598 expected=0.13091198 at index 1, exactly the values in the original 2026-07-24 report.

Environment has moved on since then, so this rules several things out:
- CUDA toolkit upgraded to 13.4 (V13.4.92), driver 610.43.02, same RTX 5070 sm_120.
- teenygrad-dd1 is fixed, so ptxas no longer rejects the module over the unresolved
  $L__info_string0 label; the kernel now loads and runs cleanly.
- teenyc rebuilt (rustc 1.99.0, 2026-09-26) including the teenygrad-5sk tensordesc fix.

The result being bit-for-bit the same wrong value across a toolkit major version, a
driver change and a compiler rebuild says this is deterministic and not a JIT, ptxas
or driver artifact -- it is a genuine error in the kernel or in our codegen for it.
Worth noting the matmul it is compared against (cpu_matmul in the test) is a hand
written Rust reference, so the possibility that the reference is wrong rather than
the kernel has not been excluded; a PyTorch fixture would settle that. See the
computed-verification audit: test_optim_muon is one of the files still asserting
against values computed in the test rather than a fixture.

Still #[ignore]d in kernels/teeny-kernels/tests/test_optim_muon.rs:290.

title: feat: an input axis whose tile is a fixed fraction of the output's (upsample)
description:
## Goal

Let an input axis declare that its tile is a fixed fraction of the output's,
which is what nearest-neighbour upsampling needs and what `divide_by` looks
like it should already do.

## The gap

`upsample_nearest2d_forward` maps an output index to an input index by integer
division:

    let ih = oh / SCALE_H;
    let iw_range = ow_range / SCALE_W;

So an output tile of `block` reads `ceil(block / SCALE)` input elements. That is
a different arithmetic from `TileWindow`'s receptive field, which only ever
grows a region.

`TileAxisBinding::divide_by` appears to cover it, but does not.
`resolve_inputs` applies it in exactly one place -- the branch where the caller
supplies a full extent:

    let block = match resolved.iter().find(|(name, _)| *name == axis.extent_param) {
        Some((_, block)) => Some(*block),                                    // propagated: as-is
        None => consts.get(axis.extent_param)
            .map(|extent| extent / axis.divide_by.unwrap_or(1).max(1)),      // full extent: divided
    };

A *propagated* block is used unchanged. That matches `divide_by`'s documented
contract, which is about an axis's usable full extent (GroupNorm's
`channels_per_group = C / G`) rather than about a per-tile ratio between an
input and an output. The two are genuinely different things and conflating them
would break the GroupNorm case.

## What is needed

Either a new binding field for a per-tile ratio between an output axis and the
input axis resolved from it, or an explicit statement that this family is
route 3 and will not carry a spec. Deciding which is the work here.

Note the ratio is not always exact: `ceil(block / scale)` is only `block /
scale` when the block divides evenly, and the resolution path has no `ceil`
today.

## Discovered by

`teenygrad-1tl.5`, auditing the statically-indexed shape changers. Upsample is
the only member of that rung needing this; the pads need a naming convention
(`teenygrad-1tl.7`) and transpose needs two blocked axes
(`teenygrad-1nr.18.5`).
notes:
Confirmed from teenygrad-1tl.5 (PR #67) that a TileWindow provably cannot
stand in for this, so the choice this issue poses is real and not avoidable by
reusing the window path:

(block - 1) * stride + kernel is minimised at stride = 1, kernel = 1, where it
equals block. So a receptive field is NEVER smaller than the output tile.
Upsample needs ceil(block / SCALE), which is smaller. The pad family, declared
in PR #66, sits exactly on that floor (stride 1, kernel 1 => block), so the two
families bracket the window arithmetic from opposite sides and upsample falls
outside it.

So the options stand as written: a new per-tile ratio field, or route 3 for
this family. The reason is recorded on upsample_nearest2d_forward itself.

Note 1tl.5 did NOT wait on this -- its own "Done when" accepts a written-up
gap, and this issue is that write-up.
close_reason:
DECISION: route 3 for this family -- no ratio field, no spec. This issue's
stated work was "deciding which", and the deciding evidence is that the family
has exactly one member.

A tree-wide search for a shrinking index map (integer division applied to a
tile range) finds upsample_nearest2d_forward and nothing else: no
upsample_nearest1d/3d, no bilinear/interp/resize, no pixel_shuffle. Widening
TileAxisBinding -- a type every spec in the repo carries, and which validate,
resolve_inputs, untiled_dims and mem_footprint all read -- to serve one kernel
is not proportionate.

Also established in PR #67: a TileWindow provably cannot stand in.
(block - 1) * stride + kernel is minimised at stride = 1, kernel = 1 where it
equals block, so a receptive field is never SMALLER than the output tile.
Upsample needs ceil(block / SCALE). The pad family sits exactly on that floor,
so pads and upsample bracket the window arithmetic from opposite sides.

The reason is recorded on upsample_nearest2d_forward itself, including the note
that divide_by is not the field for it (resolve_inputs applies divide_by only
where the caller supplies a full extent, never to a propagated block, matching
its GroupNorm contract).

REOPEN THIS when a second member appears -- an upsample_nearest1d/3d, a
bilinear or bicubic interpolation, a resize, or a pixel_shuffle. At two kernels
the per-tile ratio field earns its place, and the analysis above is the design.

title: acos/asin/atan compile to CUDA libdevice extern calls on every target; RISC-V fails LLVM IR translation
description:
Found 2026-09-11 running the RISC-V suite one test binary at a time against teenyc from teeny feat/triton-riscv-rvv @ 9f48d7207fa: TEENYC_PATH=<teeny>/build/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/stage1/bin/teenyc INSTA_FORCE_PASS=1 cargo test -p teeny-kernels --no-default-features --features riscv,training --test <name> -- --test-threads=1. Overall: 69 binaries, 63 passed; 245 tests passed, 15 failed.

Failing tests (3): test_elemwise_unary::test_acos_source, test_asin_source, test_atan_source. acosh/asinh/atanh pass.

Error:
  error: cannot be converted to LLVM IR: missing `LLVMTranslationDialectInterface` registration for dialect for op: triton_cpu.extern_elementwise
  CpuBackend: failed to translate MLIR module to LLVM IR
  thread 'rustc' panicked at compiler/rustc_codegen_llvm/src/mlir/backend.rs:145:38: Triton passes failed: CodegenFailed { err: "Triton compilation failed" }

Cause: the teeny frontend (compiler/rustc_codegen_llvm/src/mlir/codegen/triton/ops/triton/tensor.rs, codegen_atan_call at ~3519 and the acos/asin equivalents) always emits tt.extern_elementwise with libname "libdevice" and symbol __nv_atanf/__nv_acosf/__nv_asinf, because math.atan has no lowering in Triton's TritonGPUToLLVM pipeline. On RISC-V that symbol does not exist, and the TritonCPU pipeline can only lower triton_cpu.extern_elementwise inside MathToVecLib, which (as upstream triton-cpu) only runs when a vector math library is usable: libsleef needs neon/sse/avx, libmvec needs avx512f. RISC-V has neither, so the op reaches LLVM IR translation unlowered.

Fix (in teeny): for non-CUDA targets emit math.acos/math.asin/math.atan instead; CpuBackend's makeLLIR runs math_to_libm, which lowers them to libm calls. Keep the libdevice extern for CUDA. Rerun test_elemwise_unary for riscv and cuda.

title: feat: convert the 26 single-read kernels to In<Tile<..>> (12 pads, 10 reduce_*, 2 global pools, 2 scans)
notes:
## CORRECTION: not 26 convertible today -- ZERO are, measured 2026-10-02

This rung was filed saying "26 convertible today, no blocker: a single read at
program_id offsets, which is exactly what the auto-prelude emits". Attempting it
on one kernel from each of the three sub-groups shows otherwise. The three
sub-groups are uniform in their READ and not in what the prelude accepts.

  2 scans (cum_sum, cum_prod)
      Compile. Then teenyc ICEs:
        'tt.call' op '.._Triton15expand_dims_i32' does not reference a valid
        function
      Filed as teenyc-u9z. Two blocked axes put them on the N-blocked-axis
      prelude path, which uses `expand_dims_i32` -- a trait method added by
      teenygrad-1nr.18.5 that teenyc has no lowering for. That prelude path has
      never been compiled by teenyc: .18.5's probe asserted tile_spec() and
      never called compile_kernel, and every two-blocked-axis kernel in the tree
      is route 2 with a hand-written body.

 12 reduce_* and global pools
      Rejected by the prelude's own validation: "`x` declares an axis the output
      does not ... must either match an output axis by name, or be left off
      entirely (which broadcasts it)". A reduced axis has no output counterpart
      by construction and must be read IN FULL, not broadcast.
      -> teenygrad-29qp

 12 pads
      Same validation, different reason: the input axis is `L` against the
      output's `OL`, related by a window. The error names it:
      "An axis related to an output axis by a stride/padding window is
      teenygrad-1nr.18.2, not this prelude".
      -> teenygrad-jpdb

## So this rung is blocked on three issues, not zero

teenyc-u9z (the ICE), teenygrad-29qp (reduced axis), teenygrad-jpdb (windowed
axis without a loop). The first is a one-line compiler fix with an identical
handler already present for `expand_dims`; the other two are prelude features
that unlock 12 kernels each.

Worth noting what this says about the earlier estimate: "a single read at
program_id offsets" was the right observation about the kernels and the wrong
conclusion about the work, because it described what the kernel does rather than
what the prelude will generate for it. The measurement took three attempted
conversions and found three different blockers.

## SECOND CORRECTION: 15 of 26 land; the 2 scans are not a compiler problem -- 2026-10-05

Closed since the correction above: teenygrad-29qp (10 reduce_* + 2 global pools,
PR #82) and teenygrad-jpdb (the constant pads, PR #83). teenyc-u9z is fixed
(teeny PR #9) and teenygrad PR #84 carries the matching prelude fix.

Standing at 15 of 26:

  12 reduce_* + global pools   DONE, PR #82
   3 constant pads             DONE, PR #83
   9 other pads                NOT a prelude feature (see jpdb)
   2 scans                     NOT blocked on u9z -- see below

### The scans need a new prelude concept, not the compiler fix

u9z was the recorded blocker and it is fixed. With it the scans compile and
their numerics pass. The conversion was still reverted.

Declaring `block = BLOCK_INNER` on the inner axis makes the spec claim that axis
is TILEABLE. It is not: a scan's prefix dependency means a second block along it
would scan only its own slice and lose the carry. Two things hide this, which is
why it survived a passing test run:

  - the test's `launch_config_with_grid(n_outer, ..)` is hand-written and
    launches one block along the inner axis, ignoring the spec's grid;
  - every reduction fixture has INNER_R == BLOCK_INNER, so there is never a
    second block.

So the tests pass while the spec lies, and anduin reads the spec -- which is the
whole reason this epic prefers tiles to pointers. The axis stays in
`untiled_dims`, as the comment on
test_rank_changing_reductions_resolve_without_a_new_spec_field already said it
must.

What they need: an axis loaded whole and masked, but NEITHER gridded NOR
reduced. `reduce` supplies the load and the no-grid but also marks
`reduction_axis` and the rank change, which a scan must not have. That is a
prelude feature, filed separately.

### Why u9z was recorded as the blocker

The ICE was real and is fixed, but it was the first failure, not the only one.
Behind it sat a second bug in the same never-compiled path (ranges expanded but
not broadcast, so 'arith.andi' rejected the operand types) and then this design
constraint. Reading one error and filing it as THE blocker is what put "2 scans"
in this rung's title.

The pattern now holds for all three sub-groups in this rung: the count described
what the kernel does, not what the prelude can generate for it.
close_reason: Anduin fusion work discontinued; closed with the Anduin-related issues

title: feat: the prelude reads an axis whole without gridding or reducing it (the scans)
description:
The 2 scans (cum_sum, cum_prod) cannot convert to In<Tile<..>> with today's attribute vocabulary, and teenyc-u9z was not what stood in the way. Measured 2026-10-05 in teenygrad PR #84.

## The problem

A scan reads its inner axis IN FULL and keeps it in the output. Declaring `block = BLOCK_INNER` gets the read, but it also puts the axis in the grid, and the spec then claims the axis is tileable. It is not: the prefix dependency means a second block along that axis would scan only its own slice and lose the carry.

anduin reads the spec, so a spec that lies is worse than the raw pointer the kernel uses today. The axis must stay in untiled_dims.

## Why the tests do not catch it

Both hide the failure:

  - launch_config_with_grid(n_outer, ..) in test_reduction.rs is hand-written and launches ONE block along the inner axis regardless of the spec's grid;
  - every reduction fixture has INNER_R == BLOCK_INNER (64), so a second block never exists.

Numerics passed with the broken declaration. Worth fixing the fixture side too: a scan case with n_inner > BLOCK_INNER would make this visible, and should land with the feature.

## What is needed

An axis loaded whole and masked, but NEITHER gridded NOR reduced.

`reduce` already supplies two thirds of that -- it loads the whole axis, masks the tail, and keeps the axis out of the grid -- but it also sets reduction_axis in the spec and routes through the rank-reducing path. A scan is rank-PRESERVING, so neither is correct.

Likely shape: a separate marker (`whole`, say) reusing reduce's load and grid treatment while leaving reduction_axis as None and the axis present in the output. Check against what resolve_inputs expects for an untiled dim, and against the comment on test_rank_changing_reductions_resolve_without_a_new_spec_field, which already states the invariant.

## Scope

2 kernels (cum_sum_forward, cum_prod_forward). The last 2 of teenygrad-1a1j's 26.
close_reason: Anduin fusion work discontinued; closed with the Anduin-related issues

title: feat: the 9 reflection/replication/circular pads read a computed index
description:
The other 9 of teenygrad-1a1j's 12 pads. The 3 constant pads landed in PR #83; these did not, and the reason is structural rather than a missing prelude key.

## Measured, not assumed (2026-10-05)

constant_pad{1,2,3}d load their operand ONCE, at a shifted coordinate. That is what teenygrad-jpdb's generated windowed read emits, so they converted and their bodies are now a single store.

reflection_pad, replication_pad and circular_pad (3 ranks each) load their operand THREE times -- centre, left and right candidates -- and select among them. The auto-prelude generates ONE load per parameter, so no combination of today's attributes expresses them.

## Two ways forward

1. A declaration for a computed index: reflected, clamped or wrapped. This keeps the kernels' current structure and extends the attribute vocabulary with an index TRANSFORM rather than the affine `stride/pad/kernel` window jpdb added.

2. Restructure each body to a single load at a computed index, then convert with what exists. This is a behaviour change to nine kernels and wants its numerics re-verified individually.

(2) is probably right -- three loads where one would do is the kind of thing the Tile ABI should remove, not preserve -- but it is nine separate numerical verifications, so it should not ride along with a prelude feature.

## Note on the estimate

jpdb was filed as "12 pads" and delivered 3. The count came from the kernels all being pads, not from how each one reads. Same error as teenygrad-1a1j's original "26 convertible today". Counts in teenygrad-3rk6 are upper bounds until a conversion is attempted.
close_reason: Anduin fusion work discontinued; closed with the Anduin-related issues

title: spec: TritonFusionBackend — graph-level operator-fusion trait + lowering to fused Triton kernels
description:
## Goal

A detailed design spec (no implementation in this issue) for a `TritonFusionBackend`:
a trait + eventual implementation that (a) identifies fusable regions of a `Graph`
and (b) lowers each fused region to a single generated Triton kernel, replacing
today's per-op-only Triton lowering for those regions. This issue's deliverable is
the spec itself — an enumeration of every fusion case the design must account for,
a sketch of the trait boundary, and the concrete points in the existing
graph/lowering/compiler pipeline it has to plug into. Implementation is tracked
separately once the spec is agreed.

## Why now / prior art

This generalizes work already scoped narrowly elsewhere:

- **spinorml-1fj** (vision-rs beads project) — investigation showing TensorRT's
  Myelin JIT fuses ~26% of YOLO26n's GPU kernel time via arbitrary op-chain fusion,
  not just fixed conv+BN+activation patterns. Empirical nsys findings from that
  issue are load-bearing for this spec (cited throughout below).
- **spinorml-1fj.1** — narrow "happy path": fuse elementwise/reindex chains that
  all share one physical CTA/thread mapping, via source concatenation + MLIR
  inline/DCE. Phase 1 (graph-side `Op::Fused { members }`, `is_fusable_elementwise`,
  `Graph::fuse_elementwise_chains()`) shipped in teenygrad (commit efc1a4e5d). Phase
  2 — the actual Triton lowering — is explicitly unimplemented: see
  `kernels/teeny-kernels/src/graph/mod.rs:2949-2961`, which returns
  `Err("Op::Fused lowering is not implemented yet ... see spinorml-1fj.1")` for
  *any* `Op::Fused` node reaching the Triton backend today.
- **spinorml-1fj.2** — investigates the harder case 1fj.1 explicitly excluded:
  chains containing a reduction (or any op with a different natural CTA/thread
  shape), which need real index/retiling, not just concatenation.
- **arXiv:2602.19762** ("Hexagon-MLIR: An AI Compilation Stack For Qualcomm's
  NPUs") — a `linalg.generic`-based fusion formalization, cited below for
  vocabulary and for edge cases it independently ran into (softmax needing two
  passes, non-affine/data-dependent ops being unfusable, tiling-for-memory-
  hierarchy interacting with fusion). Useful as an existence proof that the case
  taxonomy below (elementwise / broadcast / reduction / multi-reduction / hard
  barriers) is the right cut, not teenygrad-specific.

This issue's job is to stop treating "elementwise-only" (1fj.1) and "has a
reduction" (1fj.2) as separately-scoped efforts and instead spec one backend
abstraction that both are instances of, plus the cases neither covers yet
(GEMM/conv epilogues, multi-input/fan-out regions, custom ops, training-mode
backward).

## Existing building blocks this must integrate with

- `core/teeny-core/src/graph/mod.rs`
  - `Op::Fused { members: Vec<Op> }` (~L408) — a linear chain of single-input/
    single-output ops. **Too narrow for most cases below** — see "Representation"
    open question.
  - `is_fusable_elementwise(op)` (~L1992) — hand-maintained allowlist (Relu,
    Sigmoid, Silu, Tanh), chosen because all four dispatch through teeny-kernels'
    identical fixed `BLOCK_SIZE=1024` elementwise kernel shape.
  - `Graph::fuse_elementwise_chains()` (~L1856) — opt-in graph rewrite pass, single-
    consumer linear-chain merge to a fixed point. Not called by `optimise()`.
  - `Op::Conv2dBnSilu` (~L374) — a *hand-written*, single hard-coded fusion pattern
    (Conv2d→BatchNorm2d→SiLU), produced directly by `Graph::optimise()`. Precedent
    for GEMM/conv-epilogue-style fusion, structurally distinct from elementwise-
    chain fusion.
- `core/teeny-core/src/model/mod.rs`
  - `Lowering<'a>` trait (~L368): `lower(graph, mode) -> Dag<Box<dyn ExecutableOp>>`,
    plus `lower_with_mapping` (graph-node-idx → dag-node-idx) and
    `extra_dag_names` (for the *split* case: one graph node → many DAG nodes, e.g.
    Conv2d-with-bias). Fusion is the mirror case — many graph nodes → one DAG node
    — and needs the same care to keep `graph_to_dag` and named-parameter loading
    correct.
  - `RuntimeOp` trait (~L69): `block()`, `grid(output_shape)`, `n_activation_inputs()`,
    `param_shapes()`, `param_names()`, `pack_args()`, `n_launches()`. This is the
    *only* place CTA/thread-shape is authoritatively known today. Notably it's built
    during `teeny-kernels`' lowering, not at `Graph::optimise()` time — see the
    "when does fusion get decided" open question below.
  - `LoweringMode::{Inference, Training}` — training additionally wires up backward
    kernels per `ExecutableOp::backward_kernel_source()`.
- `core/teeny-core/src/graph/compiler.rs` — `GraphCompiler::compile<L: Lowering, T:
  Target>(graph, lowering, target, mode, force)`.
- `compiler/teeny-compiler/src/compiler/mod.rs` — `Target` trait; backend `Module`/
  `Compiler` enums (LLVM/MLIR backend, `ndarray` backend) in
  `compiler/teeny-compiler/src/compiler/backend/mod.rs`.
- `kernels/teeny-kernels/src/graph/mod.rs` — `TritonLowering` (struct ~L526, `impl
  Lowering<'a>` ~L2976). `KernelInstance::source` (`core/teeny-core/src/model/mod.rs`
  ~L38-47) is literal generated Rust source text: a generic `#[kernel]` fn body plus
  a synthesized `#[no_mangle] extern "C"` entry point that monomorphizes and calls
  it — confirmed via `kernels/teeny-kernels/tests/snapshots/test_linear__linear_source.snap`.
  Each kernel's generic fn is pointer-in/pointer-out, not value-in/value-out.
- `kernels/teeny-triton/src/triton/mod.rs` — the Triton-in-Rust kernel-authoring
  DSL (this project's `tl`-equivalent). The actual lowering *target* language for
  fused regions; not itself a fusion mechanism today.
- Recent related fix: commit `43f0c0f9d` ("serialize concurrent compiles of the
  same kernel hash") — fused kernels will mint new source per graph shape, so
  kernel-hash stability/collision behavior for synthesized fused sources is a
  real testing concern, not hypothetical.

## Cases the spec must enumerate and resolve a fusion strategy for

Each case below needs: (a) how to *detect* it's fusable, (b) what CTA/thread
structure the fused kernel ends up needing, (c) what — if anything — blocks it.
Grounded against spinorml-1fj's empirical Myelin nsys findings (TensorRT's own
JIT fusion compiler, profiled on the same YOLO26n model) wherever they apply,
since that's real evidence about which of these cases matter in practice and
what structural choices a correct fusion makes.

1. **Pure elementwise chains, single input/output.** Already modeled (narrowly)
   by `Op::Fused`. Generalize `is_fusable_elementwise` from a fixed allowlist to
   a real predicate: "shares an identical `block()`/`grid()` shape with its
   neighbours." Matches Myelin's `__myl_Silu`, `__myl_SiluAdd`-style kernels:
   uniform `block=(256,1,1)`, zero shared memory.

2. **Multi-input elementwise / fan-in (broadcast, residual-add).** E.g. `x +
   f(x)`, bias-add, two-branch elementwise merge. `Graph::fuse_elementwise_chains`
   today assumes a linear chain with exactly one consumer per interior node —
   this case needs a DAG *region* (multiple producers feeding one elementwise op),
   not a chain. Must also handle broadcast shape mismatches between operands
   (different rank/strides feeding the same fused iteration domain).

3. **Fan-out: a value consumed by multiple downstream ops.** Can't simply inline-
   and-discard; must choose materialize-once (write to memory, multiple readers)
   vs. recompute-per-consumer (duplicate the producing op's work inside each
   fused branch). The Hexagon-MLIR paper explicitly flags "re-computations" as a
   fusion-correctness/cost concern for exactly this reason — this must be a
   deliberate cost-model decision in the spec, not silently defaulted either way.

4. **Reduction-terminated regions** (elementwise producer(s) → a single
   `Op::ReduceSum`/`ReduceMax`/`ReduceMean`/`ReduceProd`/`ReduceL1`/`ReduceL2`/
   `ReduceLogSum`/`ReduceLogSumExp`/`ReduceSumSquare`/etc. — all already itemized
   in `Op`). Per spinorml-1fj's Myelin nsys data, a reduction forces ONE CTA/
   thread structure for the *entire* fused region, not just the reduction op
   itself (`__myl_MulMaxrSubExpSum`: `block=(32,4,1)`, warp-per-row, all
   surrounding elementwise ops run under that shape, not their own natural
   256-wide one). This is exactly spinorml-1fj.2's "retiling" problem — this spec
   must specify how the fused kernel's launch config is chosen (driven by the
   most demanding member) and how non-reduction members' index arithmetic gets
   re-derived under it, not just flag that retiling is needed.

5. **Reduction with an elementwise epilogue** (RMSNorm-shaped: reduce sum-of-
   squares → rsqrt → elementwise divide+scale). Reduction is not the last op in
   the region; downstream elementwise ops consume the *reduced scalar/vector*
   alongside the original tensor. Distinct from case 4 in data flow shape (one
   input feeds both the reduction and, later, the epilogue directly).

6. **Multi-reduction / softmax-shaped regions.** `Mul→Max→Sub→Exp→Sum` (or
   `LogSoftmax`, `SoftmaxCrossEntropyLoss`) has two *sequential*, dependent
   reduction passes over the same axis (max, then sum), each needing the
   completed result of the previous pass before starting. Cannot collapse into
   one single-pass generic region. Hexagon-MLIR hits the identical wall:
   "softmax, prefix-sum, TopK etc need other control-flow ops along with
   linalg.generic to make them representable" — i.e. genuinely needs a staged
   two-phase kernel body (compute+store row max, barrier/re-read, compute
   exp-sum, barrier, compute output), not a trick that avoids the second pass.
   Spec must say whether v1 handles this at all or defers it (existing
   `SoftmaxForward`/`LogSoftmaxForward` kernels are presumably already internally
   fused by hand — confirm and treat as the reference implementation for what a
   generated version must match).

7. **"Free" reindex ops folded via address arithmetic** (reshape/slice/concat/
   transpose expressed as index math, not a structural change to block/grid
   shape). Per spinorml-1fj's nsys data this is legitimately free for
   reshape/slice/concat (`__myl_MoveResh`, `__myl_Conc`, `__myl_SlicTran` all keep
   `block=(256,1,1)`, zero shared memory) but **transpose is only free when it
   doesn't touch the coalescing-sensitive dimension** — transposes that do
   (`__myl_DivMulTran`, `__myl_ReshTranSlic`) show non-zero static/dynamic shared
   memory (a shared-memory staging tile), even though the surrounding ops are
   otherwise plain elementwise. The spec must distinguish "transpose as pure
   index relabeling" from "transpose needing a staging tile" and route the
   latter through case 4's retiling treatment, not case 1/7's free-fusion path.

8. **GEMM/conv epilogue fusion** (existing `Conv2dBnSilu`, `Conv2dBnSiluGemm`,
   `Conv2dBnSiluTiled`; `Linear` + bias + activation is the same shape). Different
   tiling paradigm entirely — tensor-core `T::dot()`-based tile shapes (see
   `teenygrad-3i0`, `teenygrad-ejt`), output-tile-per-CTA with a K-dim reduction
   loop, nothing like the flat elementwise grid. Per spinorml-1fj's finding, even
   TensorRT's Myelin never fuses *through* a conv/GEMM — only elementwise/BN-style
   epilogues get absorbed into its write-back. Spec must state this backend
   **does not** attempt to merge GEMM/conv main loops with the generic
   elementwise-fusion machinery in cases 1-7; epilogue absorption into an
   existing GEMM/conv kernel's own write-back is a separate, narrower mechanism
   (already partially precedented by the hand-written `Conv2dBnSilu*` family).

9. **Hard fusion barriers: grid-wide-coordination ops.** Top-k, sort/argsort,
   NMS-prep, nonzero, and anything needing the *entire* grid's output (not one
   CTA's slice) before proceeding. Per spinorml-1fj's finding, a kernel-launch
   boundary is a grid-wide sync/visibility barrier that `__syncthreads()` cannot
   substitute for; providing that inside a single generated kernel needs
   cooperative-groups grid-sync, itself capped by SM-residency (`__myl_Topk` uses
   `grid=(1,1,1)` specifically to sidestep this). The spec must define these as an
   explicit non-fusable-boundary op-list (mirroring `is_fusable_elementwise` but
   as a stop-list), not something the analysis discovers by absence of a rule.

10. **Custom ops (`Op::Custom`/`CustomOp` trait).** Opaque by construction — no
    generic body to inline, only a `name()`/`lower()` contract. Must be a hard
    fusion boundary unconditionally; the analysis pass cannot special-case
    around this.

11. **dtype-promotion boundaries.** Some kernels internally upcast (e.g. an f16 op
    accumulating in f32 — flagged by `spinorml-4gx`/`teenygrad-3i0`'s precision
    notes for tensor-core paths). Fusing two ops whose individual
    "public" dtype is the same but whose *internal* precision handling differs
    must not silently change numerics. Spec needs a rule: either every member's
    precision contract is preserved unchanged post-fusion, or a fusion is
    rejected across a promotion boundary it can't prove preserves numerics.

12. **Training-mode / backward.** `LoweringMode::Training` wires up
    `ExecutableOp::backward_kernel_source()`/`backward_kernel_entry_point()` per
    node. A fused-forward region either needs a coherent fused (or
    per-member-composed) backward, or the analysis must refuse to fuse under
    `LoweringMode::Training` for regions it can't derive one for. Decide which,
    and whether it can differ per-case (e.g. case 1 might be backward-safe,
    case 6 almost certainly isn't for a first pass).

## Trait sketch (illustrative — not a final API; this issue is not the
implementation)

```rust
/// Identifies fusable regions of a `Graph` and lowers each to one Triton kernel.
/// Implementations own both halves so the fusion *decision* and the fusion
/// *lowering* can share the same notion of "these ops fit in one kernel" —
/// see "when does fusion get decided" below for why that coupling is likely
/// required rather than incidental.
pub trait TritonFusionBackend {
    /// Analysis: rewrite `graph`, replacing fusable regions with a fused
    /// representation (see "Representation" open question — likely richer
    /// than today's linear-chain-only `Op::Fused`).
    fn plan_fusions(&self, graph: &Graph) -> Graph;

    /// Lowering: given one already-isolated fused region, emit ONE Triton
    /// kernel (source + entry point + a `RuntimeOp` synthesized for the whole
    /// region, not delegated from a single member) implementing it. Called
    /// from `TritonLowering::lower_with_mapping`'s fused-region arm — the
    /// current stub is `kernels/teeny-kernels/src/graph/mod.rs:2949-2961`.
    fn lower_fused_region(
        &self,
        region: &FusedRegion,
        mode: LoweringMode,
    ) -> Result<KernelInstance>;
}
```

## Open questions the spec must close out

- **Representation.** Is `Op::Fused { members: Vec<Op> }` (linear chain) extended
  to a real subgraph/region type (needed for cases 2, 3, 5, 6), or do those cases
  get their own `Op` variants the way `Conv2dBnSilu` is its own variant rather
  than an `Op::Fused` instance? Precedent in this codebase favors the latter for
  structurally-distinct patterns.
- **When is fusion decided?** `Graph::optimise()` runs before any `RuntimeOp`
  exists (per spinorml-1fj.1's own comment: "RuntimeOp... doesn't exist yet at
  the point optimise() runs — it's built later, during teeny-kernels' lowering").
  Today's `is_fusable_elementwise` sidesteps this with a hand-verified allowlist.
  A general backend needs real `block()`/`grid()` comparison, which only exists
  post-RuntimeOp-construction. Spec must pick one: (a) keep the allowlist model
  and extend it case-by-case with manually-verified equivalence classes, or (b)
  move the fusability *decision* into `TritonLowering` itself (post-RuntimeOp,
  pre-kernel-source-generation), with `Graph::optimise()` only doing the
  backend-agnostic region-*identification* (candidate grouping), not the
  final fuse/don't-fuse call.
- **Kernel body composition.** Do fused kernels keep spinorml-1fj.1's
  scratch-buffer-threading approach (pointer-in/pointer-out members chained
  via small ping-pong buffers — real launch-count win, no register residency),
  or does this spec commit to the harder refactor (splitting each kernel's
  pointer I/O from its pure compute step so fused members compose at the
  value level, register-resident)? 1fj.1 treats the former as an acceptable
  first pass; this spec should state whether it's also this backend's v1 or
  whether v1 targets the harder version directly.
- **Retiling mechanism (case 4/6).** Concretely: given N member ops with
  differing "natural" `block()`/`grid()`, how is the winning shape chosen (most
  demanding member — reduction/GEMM > elementwise, per empirical Myelin
  evidence) and how do the losing members' per-thread index arithmetic get
  re-derived under it? This is spinorml-1fj.2's open problem; this spec should
  either absorb a concrete answer or explicitly scope multi-shape retiling out
  of v1 and restrict `plan_fusions` to same-shape regions only (case 1, 2, 7)
  plus the single-reduction-drives-everything case (case 4) if tractable.
- **Where the stop-list (case 9/10) lives.** Shared with, or independent of,
  `is_fusable_elementwise`'s allowlist? Getting this wrong either blocks a
  legitimately fusable op or — worse — silently attempts to fuse across a
  grid-wide-barrier op and produces a wrong kernel.

## Non-goals for this spec

- No implementation, no new kernel source, no benchmark numbers.
- Does not re-litigate spinorml-1fj.2's retiling *algorithm* — it should either
  cite a concrete resolution to that issue or explicitly punt case 4/6 out of
  v1 scope, but designing the retiling algorithm itself can stay in
  spinorml-1fj.2 if that's still open when this is written.
- Does not cover CUDA/Vulkan driver-level changes; this is graph/lowering-level
  only (`teeny-core`, `teeny-compiler`, `teeny-kernels`).

## Deliverable / acceptance criteria

A written spec (design doc, PR description, or issue comment — format TBD by
whoever picks this up) that: enumerates all 12 cases above with a concrete
fuse/don't-fuse/defer decision for each; answers all five open questions;
sketches the final trait shape (superseding the illustrative one above) and
exactly where it's constructed/invoked in `TritonLowering::lower_with_mapping`;
and identifies which cases are in v1 implementation scope vs. explicitly
deferred. No code changes required to close this issue.

## References

- spinorml-1fj / spinorml-1fj.1 / spinorml-1fj.2 (vision-rs beads project —
  different `.beads` DB, prefix `spinorml`; not directly linkable as a `br dep`
  from this project's DB, referenced here by ID).
- arXiv:2602.19762, "Hexagon-MLIR: An AI Compilation Stack For Qualcomm's Neural
  Processing Units (NPUs)" — §4.2 (`linalg.generic`/indexing-map fusion
  formalization), §4.3 (producer/consumer fusion composition), §4.4 (tiling for
  memory hierarchy interacting with fusion boundaries).
- `teenygrad-3i0`, `teenygrad-ejt` — tensor-core GEMM/epilogue work relevant to
  case 8 and case 11.

comments.text:
Case 1 decision landed (teenygrad-1bf.1): see `.ai/specs/fusion/case-1-elementwise-chains.md`.

Summary for parent open questions, scoped to case 1:
1. **When is fusion decided?** Keep/extend `is_fusable_elementwise` allowlist at graph time (RuntimeOp does not exist yet). Lowering asserts block/grid equality as a safety net, not as the primary decision.
2. **Kernel body composition?** v1 = scratch-buffer / ping-pong pointer threading (spinorml-1fj.1). Register-resident composition deferred.
3. **FusedRuntimeOp:** may delegate block/grid to any member **only** under the allowlist's CTA-identical-by-construction precondition (document explicitly). Relu's hardcoded `block()=[128,1,1]` currently breaks that precondition and must be fixed before Phase-2 lowering.

comments.author: Arshad Mahmood
comments.text:
**Prior art: torch/_inductor's Triton fusion — cross-cutting notes**

Posted detailed comments on each case sub-issue (teenygrad-1bf.1 through .14) comparing against how `torch/_inductor` implements Triton kernel fusion, with file:line pointers into this checkout's `torch/_inductor/`. Summarizing the cross-cutting takeaways here since several bear directly on this issue's open questions rather than any single case.

**"When is fusion decided?"** Inductor's answer is a clean version of option (b): it cleanly separates two decisions this spec currently risks conflating.
1. *Iteration-domain legality* — decided during a single scheduler fusion pass (`Scheduler.fuse_nodes_once`, `scheduler.py:6484`) run to a fixed point immediately after the whole graph is lowered to IR (`GraphLowering._update_scheduler`, `graph.py:2992`). This uses only symbolic `numel`/`rnumel`/tiling signatures (`SchedulerNode._compute_attrs`, `scheduler.py:2280-2294`) that exist for free right after lowering — no concrete GPU launch parameters (block/grid) are needed to answer "can these fuse," because PyTorch shapes are known from trace time. There's no analogue to teenygrad's "RuntimeOp doesn't exist yet" gap.
2. *Concrete launch config* (block size, persistent-vs-looped reduction, `ReductionHint`) — decided per already-fused kernel, later, during Triton codegen/autotuning (`TritonKernel.should_use_persistent_reduction`, `codegen/triton.py:3759`).

Every case comment (especially teenygrad-1bf.1 and .4) traces through why this split works: fusability only ever needs a symbolic shape/tiling *comparison*, never a concrete `block()`/`grid()` *value*. This suggests this design's open question should resolve toward: `Graph::optimise()`-time (or a pass immediately after) does region identification using whatever symbolic shape info is already available pre-`RuntimeOp`, and `TritonLowering` materializes `block()`/`grid()` once per already-decided fused region — not the other way around, and not requiring the allowlist-and-manually-verify-equivalence-classes model to scale past case 1.

**"Representation" — is `Op::Fused{members}` (linear chain) enough?** No — and inductor is a clean existence proof of why not, and what the alternative costs. Inductor never had a chain-shaped fusion primitive to begin with: a `SchedulerNode`/`FusedSchedulerNode` models one output buffer with an arbitrary-arity read-dependency set derived from the IR node's `inner_fn` (`dependencies.py`), so fan-in (case 2), fan-out (case 3), and reduction-with-epilogue's two-role input (case 5) all fall out of the *same* generic dependency-matching code as the single-input case (case 1) — see the teenygrad-1bf.2 and .5 comments for the concrete mechanism. None of these needed a special-cased detector once the representation stopped assuming linearity. This is fairly strong evidence for this spec's stated preference ("Precedent in this codebase favors the latter for structurally-distinct patterns") in the *other* direction than expected: rather than giving every structurally-distinct case its own `Op` variant the way `Conv2dBnSilu` is, a single DAG-region representation (replacing `Op::Fused`'s `Vec<Op>`) plausibly *reduces* the number of cases needing bespoke logic, since inductor's fusability check doesn't care about region topology at all — only about per-buffer read/write dependencies and shape/tiling compatibility. Cases 1/2/3/5 in particular look like they'd collapse into one mechanism under that representation, the way they did in inductor.

**Retiling (case 4/6) — the concrete mechanism, not just "reduction wins":** inductor never literally re-derives a losing member's index arithmetic under a winning shape. Instead `SIMDScheduling.can_fuse`'s reduction-fusion path (`simd.py:2201-2231`) requires `numel1 == numel2 * rnumel2` (producer's total footprint equals the reduction's input footprint) and then checks every member's ranges are compatible with the reduction's `(numel2, rnumel2)` domain via `SIMDKernel.is_compatible` — i.e. fusion is *gated* on shape-compatibility rather than *achieved* via index-rewriting. If a producer's natural shape doesn't already tile into the reduction's domain, it simply doesn't fuse. This is a materially smaller mechanism than "retiling," and might be a better v1 target than designing a general index re-derivation algorithm from scratch (see teenygrad-1bf.4's comment).

**Case 6 (softmax) is solved further than the taxonomy assumes.** Inductor never emits two kernel launches for a softmax-shaped region, in either its online-softmax fast path (`OnlineSoftmaxReduction`, `ir.py:2576-2610`, flash-attention-style running max/sum rescale, single pass) or its non-online fallback (`SIMDKernel.prepare_softmax_twopass_fallback`, `simd.py:1478-1483`, two dependent reduction passes inside one persistent-reduction kernel body, no grid-wide barrier needed since a persistent reduction already holds the whole axis in one CTA). Worth revisiting whether case 6 needs to stay in the "probably deferred" bucket, or whether the non-online two-pass-in-one-persistent-kernel form is tractable for a first pass — it's a meaningfully smaller lift than full online-softmax rescaling. See teenygrad-1bf.6's comment.

**Training/backward (cases 12/13) — the sharpest structural difference found.** Inductor itself has zero special machinery for fused-region backward, because AOTAutograd's decomposition + min-cut-partitioner (`torch/_functorch/partitioners.py`) already turns every backward into ordinary forward-lowerable ops *before* Inductor's fusion pass ever runs — e.g. `silu_backward` is a four-op decomposition (`torch/_decomp/decompositions.py:302-307`), not a monolithic kernel with a fixed calling convention. This means Inductor never needed to solve teenygrad-1bf.13's y-style/x-style backward-ABI problem at all. This is a bigger architectural swing than this spec's current scope (composing hand-written per-op backward kernels), but worth an explicit go/no-go decision rather than defaulting into the narrower "add a second ABI class" fix, given that a third/fourth ABI class is predictable for the next op that doesn't fit either shape (see teenygrad-1bf.13's comment for the concrete argument).

**Dtype promotion (case 11) — also a different shape of answer than either option this spec poses.** Inductor makes precision promotion a property of the *generated instruction stream* (`DtypePropagationOpsHandler`, applied uniformly post-fusion), not a property of the *op/member* that has to be checked for cross-member compatibility before fusion is allowed — sidestepping the "prove numerics preserved" problem entirely rather than solving it. See teenygrad-1bf.11's comment.

No changes recommended to this issue's non-goals or deliverable — this is meant as reference material for whoever resolves the open questions and per-case decisions, not a proposal to re-scope the spec itself.

comments.author: Arshad Mahmood
comments.text:
**Consolidated: the TensorRT Myelin analysis this spec is built on**

This spec's case taxonomy repeatedly cites `spinorml-1fj` (vision-rs's beads project) for empirical grounding, but that evidence is currently only quoted piecemeal inside individual case descriptions. Since `spinorml-1fj` lives in a different `.beads` DB (vision-rs, not teenygrad) and isn't `br`-linkable across projects, consolidating the full analysis here as a standing reference, plus flagging the parts that *aren't* yet reflected anywhere in this spec.

**Source:** `spinorml-1fj` (+ children `spinorml-1fj.1`, `spinorml-1fj.2`), vision-rs beads project. Methodology: `nsys` wrapping `trtexec` against a pre-built `yolo26n.engine` (TensorRT 10.16.1.11), RTX 5070, 100 timed iterations, `cuda_gpu_kern_sum`; a follow-up pass pulled exact grid/block launch configs per kernel from the nsys trace's sqlite export (`CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_KERNEL` table).

**Headline breakdown of TensorRT's GPU kernel time on YOLO26n:**
```
Tensor-core implicit-GEMM conv (TF32)        45.6%
Myelin JIT-fused kernels                     25.7%
Tensor-core GEMM (non-conv)                  14.6%
Non-tensor-core conv (small/odd shapes)       9.8%
Depthwise conv / pooling (dedicated kernels)  2.9%
Other                                         0.8%
```
Myelin's op-fusion (25.7%) is TensorRT's graph compiler JIT-generating bespoke fused kernels for arbitrary op-chains found in the traced graph — kernel names are literally generated from the fused op sequence (`__myl_SiluSpli_*`, `__myl_MulMaxrSubExpSum_*`, an 11-op `__myl_ConcSigmAddSubConcMulConcTranSlicMaxrReshSlic_*` covering the whole detection-head decode/NMS-prep step, even `__myl_Topk_*`).

**Finding 1 — structure is shared until a reduction enters the chain (relevant to cases 1, 4, 6, 7, 9 — teenygrad-1bf.1/.4/.6/.7/.9):**
The large majority of `__myl_*` kernels share one uniform structure: `block=(256,1,1)`, grid sized to element count. This includes chains with Reshape/Slice/Concat/Transpose folded in as pure address arithmetic — no CTA/thread mismatch, because every op in these chains is still a per-element map. The moment a real reduction enters the chain, the structure changes for the **whole fused kernel**, not just that op:
- `__myl_MulMaxrSubExpSum` (softmax-shaped): `block=(32,4,1)` — one warp x 4 independent rows, 64B dynamic shared mem, classic warp-shuffle row-reduction.
- `__myl_ConcSigmAddSubConcMulConcTranSlicMaxrReshSlic` (the 11-op mega-fusion): **same** `block=(32,4,1)`, same 64B shared mem — all 10 surrounding elementwise/reindex ops run under the reduction's warp-oriented mapping, not their own natural 256-wide one.
- `__myl_Topk`: `grid=(1,1,1)` — a single CTA, 16.5KB static shared memory, 125 registers/thread. Whole-tensor coordination needs one block's shared memory and barriers, not a grid-stride pattern at all.

Myelin doesn't stitch per-op phases together with internal barriers — it picks one CTA/thread scheme up front, driven by the single most constraining op in the chain, and reformulates everything else around it.

**Finding 2 — transpose isn't always free (case 7 — teenygrad-1bf.7):** even within the simple 256-thread bucket, `__myl_DivMulTran` (4224B), `__myl_ReshTranSlic` (3208B), and `__myl_Move` (3852B) — all involving a transpose that permutes the coalescing-sensitive dimension — show non-zero static/dynamic shared memory, a genuine shared-memory staging tile. Reshape/slice/concat are free; a real transpose costs a shared-memory tile even when folded into an otherwise-simple elementwise-shaped kernel.

**Finding 3 — conv/GEMM never appears inside a `__myl_*` fusion (case 8 — teenygrad-1bf.8):** every conv is its own separate `xmma_fprop_implicit_gemm` kernel across the whole trace; only BN/activation-style epilogues get folded in. Myelin fuses AROUND conv, not THROUGH it — confirmed empirically, not inferred from Myelin being a black box.

**Finding 4 — pooling gets a third bucket, separate from both conv and Myelin fusion (case 14 — teenygrad-1bf.14):** "Depthwise conv / pooling (dedicated kernels)" is its own 2.9% category in the headline breakdown, distinct from the 25.7% Myelin bucket. TensorRT doesn't route pooling through its general op-fusion mechanism at all — it uses separate hand-optimized dedicated kernels. This wasn't previously called out anywhere in this spec's case-14 discussion; see the additional-info comment added there.

**Finding 5 — why naive kernel-source-concatenation isn't sufficient in general (NOT currently reflected anywhere in this spec — most load-bearing for the "kernel body composition" open question):** `spinorml-1fj`'s second follow-up comment reasons through this concretely, grounded in the launch-config data above, not just intuition:
1. A kernel launch has one fixed grid/block shape for its entire body. Concatenating two kernels' source doesn't reconcile their differing natural thread mappings — the fused kernel runs under one config, and the other kernel's indexing math (written assuming its own original config) is now wrong under it. This retiling — pick one structure driven by the most demanding op, reformulate everything else around it — is exactly what Myelin's fusion does; it's a bespoke transformation per fusion, not something generic MLIR inlining/DCE provides.
2. Store->load forwarding across a kernel seam only works cleanly when the intermediate is thread-local or block-shared-sized and alias-free (i.e., only in the same-structure case). For an intermediate larger than what one thread/block naturally holds, it has to round-trip through shared or global memory regardless of source-level concatenation.
3. A kernel-launch boundary is a **grid-wide** sync/visibility barrier, not just a per-block one. If a downstream op needs all of a previous op's output across the entire grid, inlined source running inside one kernel can't provide that without cooperative-groups grid-sync (capped by SM residency) — likely why `__myl_Topk` uses `grid=(1,1,1)`: sidestepping the need for grid-wide sync entirely by using one block. This is a hardware execution-model limit, not a compiler gap.
4. Register/shared-memory pressure is roughly the union of every phase's needs, not the max (unless liveness genuinely doesn't overlap and the register allocator reclaims dead ranges between phases). The real Myelin kernels show wide variance (16-125 registers/thread, 0-16.5KB shared memory) — suggestive of real per-fusion resource tuning, not something that falls out of blind concatenation.
5. CTA/thread-shape metadata alone is necessary but not sufficient: knowing "this op wants `block=(32,4,1)`" is a useful signal, but nothing consumes it to actually rewrite a *different* member's indexing to be correct under that shape. The metadata surfaces that a conflict exists; it doesn't resolve it.

**Where naive concatenation *is* legitimate, not a hack:** chains that are entirely elementwise/reindex — same 1:1 per-element mapping throughout, register-resident, no cross-thread/cross-block dependency. Per Finding 1, this is also the *majority* of what Myelin itself fuses. This is `spinorml-1fj.1`'s scope (source concatenation + MLIR inline/DCE), already shipped as teenygrad's Phase 1 (`Op::Fused`, `is_fusable_elementwise`, `Graph::fuse_elementwise_chains()`, commit `efc1a4e5d`) — i.e. this design's case 1 (teenygrad-1bf.1) is directly targeting the subset vision-rs's own analysis says the technique is actually sufficient for, not just a simplification for tractability.

**Practical scoping conclusion `spinorml-1fj` landed on**, directly mirroring this spec's own case boundaries: (1) free-form elementwise/reindex fusion, arbitrary chain length, address-arithmetic only, no reduction — case 1/2/3/7; (2) let a chain carry at most one reduction and pick its CTA shape from that — case 4/5/6; (3) never fuse conv/GEMM beyond the epilogue pattern already used — case 8. This spec's 12-case taxonomy is a formalization/generalization of exactly this empirically-derived boundary, not a superset invented independently of it — worth stating explicitly since it's good evidence the taxonomy's case boundaries are drawn in the right places rather than arbitrarily.

Cross-referenced additional-info comments added to teenygrad-1bf.1, .4, .6, .7, .8, .9, and .14 with the specific numbers/reasoning most relevant to each.

comments.text:
teenygrad-3w0 specs a tile-based DSL over teeny-triton + a Welder-style
(OSDI'23 Shi et al.) tile-graph scheduler, one layer below this issue's
TritonFusionBackend trait. It includes a case-by-case mapping of how that
scheduler would affect this issue's 12 fusion cases (resolves 1/2/4/5/7
directly, partially covers 6, revises case 8's "never fuses through GEMM/conv"
premise against Welder's own Table 4, loosens case 10 into an opt-in rather
than hard boundary, no change to 9/11/12) and a concrete answer to this
issue's "when is fusion decided" open question: KernelTileSpec is generated
by the #[kernel] macro at compile time, independent of RuntimeOp construction,
so Graph::optimise() could query real tile-shape data before any RuntimeOp is
built. See teenygrad-3w0 for the full writeup.

title: fusion case 1: pure elementwise chains (single input/output)
description:
## Scope

Case 1 of teenygrad-1bf's fusion-case taxonomy: pure elementwise chains,
single input/single output per member.

Already partially modeled by `Op::Fused { members: Vec<Op> }`
(`core/teeny-core/src/graph/mod.rs` ~L408) and `is_fusable_elementwise()`
(~L1992, currently a fixed allowlist: Relu, Sigmoid, Silu, Tanh) plus
`Graph::fuse_elementwise_chains()` (~L1856). The Triton-lowering half is an
explicit unimplemented stub at `kernels/teeny-kernels/src/graph/mod.rs:2949-2961`.

## Acceptance Criteria

A written decision (fold into teeny-1bf's spec) covering:

- Whether `is_fusable_elementwise`'s hand-verified allowlist model is kept and
  extended op-by-op, or replaced with a real `block()`/`grid()` equality check
  against neighbouring `RuntimeOp`s (this is the parent issue's "when is fusion
  decided" open question, scoped down to just this simplest case first).
- The kernel-body composition strategy for this case specifically: does v1 keep
  spinorml-1fj.1's scratch-buffer-threading approach (pointer-in/pointer-out
  members chained via ping-pong buffers), or go straight to value-level/
  register-resident composition? This is the cheapest case to answer that
  question for, since there's no reduction/retiling complexity in the way.
- Confirms `RuntimeOp` synthesis for the fused node: `block()`/`grid()` can
  legitimately delegate to any one member's only because this case is
  CTA/thread-shape-identical by construction (per spinorml-1fj.1's Phase-1
  comment) — state this explicitly as a documented precondition, not an
  accident.

## References

Parent: teenygrad-1bf. Prior art: spinorml-1fj.1 (vision-rs beads project,
Phase 1 shipped commit efc1a4e5d, Phase 2/lowering still open — this subtask
is that Phase 2, formally specified).

No code changes required.

comments.author: Arshad Mahmood
comments.text:
# Fusion case 1: pure elementwise chains (single input/output)

Status: **decided** (teenygrad-1bf.1)  
Parent: teenygrad-1bf (`TritonFusionBackend` spec)  
Prior art: spinorml-1fj.1 Phase 1 (graph `Op::Fused` + allowlist; commit `efc1a4e5d`)

This note answers the three acceptance questions for case 1 only. Broader
cases (fan-in, reduction, epilogue, …) stay on their own child issues.

## Scope reminder

Case 1 is a **linear chain** of single-input / single-output elementwise ops,
each shape-preserving, each with exactly one consumer on interior nodes.
Already modeled by:

- `Op::Fused { members: Vec<Op> }`
- `is_fusable_elementwise()` + `Graph::fuse_elementwise_chains()`
- Triton lowering stub that still errors on `Op::Fused`

---

## Decision 1 — fusability gate: keep the allowlist (with a hard contract)

**v1 keeps and extends `is_fusable_elementwise`'s hand-verified allowlist.**
It does **not** replace graph-time fusion with a live `RuntimeOp::block()` /
`grid()` equality check.

### Why

`Graph::fuse_elementwise_chains()` runs on the `teeny-core::Op` graph, before
any `RuntimeOp` exists. A real `block()`/`grid()` comparison is only available
inside `TritonLowering`, after per-op runtime ops are constructed. Moving the
*decision* entirely into lowering would either:

- duplicate the chain-finding rewrite after RuntimeOps exist, or
- leave `Op::Fused` production in the graph layer with no authoritative gate

For case 1, the allowlist **is** the equality check, compiled offline: every
listed op is an equivalence class of kernels that share one CTA / thread /
`BLOCK_SIZE` mapping when lowered the normal way.

### Contract the allowlist must satisfy

An op may be added to `is_fusable_elementwise` only when, under
`TritonLowering`'s standard construction for that op, all of the following
match every other allowlisted member:

1. `RuntimeOp::block()`
2. `RuntimeOp::grid(output_shape)` for any shape (same formula)
3. Kernel `BLOCK_SIZE` const used in the `pid * BLOCK_SIZE + arange` mapping
4. Pointer-in / pointer-out forward signature shape (so members chain)

Structural graph rules stay as today: shape-preserving, one input, single
consumer on interior nodes. Ops that fail any of (1)–(4) stay off the list
even if they are "elementwise" in the math sense (e.g. Softmax — different
block formula; norms — not this shape class).

### Safety net at lower time (not a second decision)

When Phase-2 lowering synthesizes a fused kernel, it **must assert** that
every member's constructed `RuntimeOp` agrees on `block()` / `grid(shape)`
before emitting. That catches allowlist drift; it does not replace the
graph-time allowlist for case 1.

### Parent open question (when is fusion decided?)

For case 1 specifically: **(a) keep the allowlist**, extended op-by-op under
the contract above. Hybrid later is fine for other cases: graph identifies
candidate regions; lowering may refuse or re-shape. Case 1 does not need to
move the decision into `TritonLowering` to ship.

### Prerequisite defect (blocks "delegate to any member")

Today's allowlist claims uniform `BLOCK_SIZE = 1024` CTA structure, but
`ReluForward` / `ReluBackward` hardcode:

```rust
fn block(&self) -> [u32; 3] { [128, 1, 1] }
```

while construction uses `ReluForward(1024)`, `grid()` uses `self.block_size`,
and Sigmoid / Silu / Tanh use `[self.block_size as u32, 1, 1]`.

So the Phase-1 "identical CTA" claim is **already false for Relu**. Fix Relu
(and `backward_block`) to use `self.block_size` before Phase-2 trusts
member-delegating `FusedRuntimeOp`. Prefer a small regression test that
allowlisted RuntimeOps agree on `block`/`grid` for a sample shape.

---

## Decision 2 — kernel-body composition: scratch-buffer threading for v1

**v1 keeps spinorml-1fj.1's scratch-buffer / ping-pong approach**, not
value-level register-resident composition.

### Mechanics

1. Concatenate each member's generic `#[kernel]` fn body into one compilation
   unit (dedupe shared imports).
2. Synthesize one entry point that calls members in order.
3. Thread intermediates via a small ping-pong pair of buffers:
   member *N*'s output pointer = member *N+1*'s input pointer.
4. External input feeds member 0; final member writes the fused node's output.

### Why not register-resident yet

Existing activation kernels are pointer-in / pointer-out. True register
fusion needs each body split into "load / pure compute / store" so fused
members compose on values. That is a real refactor across every allowlisted
op (and every future add). Scratch-buffer fusion already collapses **N
launches → 1**, which is the bulk of the measured glue-launch win from
spinorml-1fj, without that refactor. MLIR inline + DCE may still erase some
store/load pairs when aliasing is provable; treat that as opportunistic, not
required for correctness of v1.

**Follow-up (out of case-1 AC):** value-level composition as an explicit
later upgrade once case-1 lowering works end-to-end.

---

## Decision 3 — `FusedRuntimeOp` may delegate to any member, under precondition

For case 1 only, a synthesized `FusedRuntimeOp` may implement `block()`,
`grid()`, `pack_args()` (adjusted for the fused entry's buffer wiring), etc.
by **delegating to any one member's** `RuntimeOp`.

This is legitimate **only because case 1 is CTA/thread-shape-identical by
construction** via Decision 1's allowlist contract — not because fused
regions in general may pick an arbitrary member.

Document that precondition at:

- `Op::Fused` / `is_fusable_elementwise` docs (graph side)
- the `Op::Fused` lowering arm / `FusedRuntimeOp` (kernels side)

If the equality assert at lower time fails, refuse to lower (hard error), do
not silently pick a member.

Cases with mismatched natural shapes (reduction-terminated, multi-reduction,
GEMM epilogues, …) must **not** use this delegation rule; they synthesize a
region-level launch config by their own case rules.

---

## Case-1 v1 implementation checklist (not part of this decision issue)

Tracked for the implementation follow-up after teenygrad-1bf agrees:

1. Fix Relu `block()` / `backward_block()` to `self.block_size`; add allowlist
   RuntimeOp agreement test.
2. Implement `Op::Fused` lowering: source concat + ping-pong entry +
   `FusedRuntimeOp` with equality assert.
3. Keep `fuse_elementwise_chains()` opt-in until (2) lands; then consider
   wiring into the fusion backend's `plan_fusions`, still not blindly into
   `Graph::optimise()` for every backend.
4. Extend allowlist op-by-op only under Decision 1's contract (Gelu, etc.
   are candidates once verified).

## Non-goals for case 1

- Fan-in / broadcast / residual-add (case 2)
- Fan-out materialize-vs-recompute (case 3)
- Any reduction or retiling (cases 4–6)
- Training fused backward policy (case 12) — inference-first for v1 lowering
  is acceptable; training may refuse `Op::Fused` until specified

comments.text:
Update to Decision 1/3 after removing RuntimeOp::block()/backward_block():

- CUDA thread counts were never driven by RuntimeOp (executor uses PTX metadata).
- Allowlist contract is now: matching BLOCK_SIZE + grid() formula + pointer I/O shape.
- FusedRuntimeOp may delegate grid() (not block()) to any member under that precondition.

comments.author: Arshad Mahmood
comments.text:
**Prior art: how torch/_inductor handles this case**

Inductor's fusion model is structurally different in a way that's directly relevant to this issue's acceptance criteria, so noting it here as a reference point.

Inductor has **no `is_fusable_elementwise`-style allowlist of op names at all**. Fusability is a purely structural check on the iteration-domain signature, not a per-op-identity check:

- Every op is lowered to IR first (`ir.Pointwise`/`ir.Reduction` inside a `ComputedBuffer`); a `Scheduler` is only constructed *after* the whole FX graph is lowered (`torch/_inductor/graph.py:2992`, `GraphLowering._update_scheduler`). By that point every buffer's shape is already fully known/symbolic from trace time — there's no teenygrad-style "RuntimeOp doesn't exist yet" gap to worry about.
- Each buffer becomes a `SchedulerNode` whose `.group = (device, group_fn(sizes))` is computed in `SchedulerNode._compute_attrs` (`torch/_inductor/scheduler.py:2280-2294`), where `sizes = (pointwise_dims, reduction_dims)` derived straight from the buffer's index formula.
- `Scheduler.can_fuse` (`scheduler.py:8066`) -> `_can_fuse` (`scheduler.py:8112`) does legality checks (device match, ordering, aliasing) then defers to the backend: `SIMDScheduling.can_fuse` (`torch/_inductor/codegen/simd.py:2060`). For pure pointwise-pointwise fusion this just requires `numel1 == numel2 and rnumel1 == rnumel2` (`simd.py:2143`) plus a tiling-compatibility check via `node.get_tiling()` (`simd.py:2174-2199`).
- Actual merging into a `FusedSchedulerNode` happens in `Scheduler.fuse_nodes_once` (`scheduler.py:6484`), run to a fixed point.

So: **any** two pointwise ops with matching shape/tiling fuse, regardless of which specific op they are (Relu vs. some future op nobody's added to an allowlist yet). This is the strongest version of this issue's "real `block()`/`grid()` equality check" option, and it's decided at a point (post-lowering, pre-codegen) where shapes are always already known — which also bears on the parent spec's "when is fusion decided" open question: inductor cleanly separates *iteration-domain legality* (decided during the scheduler fusion pass, cheap symbolic shape/tiling comparison) from *concrete launch config* (block size, persistent-vs-looped; decided later, per already-fused kernel, during codegen/autotuning — see the case-4 comment on teenygrad-1bf.4 for specifics). That maps to this design's option (b): move the fusability decision into the lowering/scheduling stage rather than requiring `RuntimeOp::block()/grid()` to already exist.

Kernel-body composition note: inductor never threads scratch buffers between fused members either — since there's no separate "kernel per op" step to begin with, a fused pointwise chain's `inner_fn`s are composed at the index-formula level (value-resident), not via ping-pong pointer buffers. Relevant if this issue ends up recommending v1 go straight to register-resident composition rather than spinorml-1fj.1's scratch-buffer approach — inductor is an existence proof that skipping the scratch-buffer stage is viable, though it required never having per-op kernels in the first place rather than retrofitting it.

comments.author: Arshad Mahmood
comments.text:
**Additional info: why scratch-buffer concatenation is legitimate for this case specifically (not just a simplification), per vision-rs's TensorRT analysis**

Full writeup posted as a comment on the parent (teenygrad-1bf); summarizing what's directly relevant to this issue's "kernel body composition" acceptance-criteria question.

`spinorml-1fj` (vision-rs) reasoned through *why* naive source-concatenation + inline/DCE (the approach this issue is deciding between vs. register-resident composition) is actually sufficient — not just adequate — specifically for same-CTA-shape chains like this case's scope:
- A kernel launch has one fixed grid/block shape for its whole body; concatenation only produces correct indexing when every member already shares that shape (true here, since `is_fusable_elementwise`'s allowlist is chosen precisely because all four ops dispatch through the same fixed `BLOCK_SIZE=1024` kernel shape).
- Store->load forwarding across the seam between two concatenated kernels only works cleanly when the intermediate is thread-local/block-shared-sized and alias-free — again, exactly the same-structure case this issue covers.
- Per `spinorml-1fj`'s nsys data, this is also the *majority* of what TensorRT's own Myelin JIT fuses in practice (`__myl_Silu`, `__myl_SiluAdd`, `__myl_Conc`, `__myl_MoveResh`, etc. are all plain `block=(256,1,1)`, zero shared memory) — i.e. getting this case right captures a large share of the real-world win without needing retiling solved first.

This directly supports keeping v1 at spinorml-1fj.1's scratch-buffer/ping-pong approach (already shipped in teenygrad Phase 1) rather than jumping to register-resident composition: the vision-rs analysis's own conclusion is that concatenation is the *legitimate* technique here, not a stopgap being tolerated until something better arrives. Register-resident composition would still be a real further win (avoiding the round-trip through scratch buffers entirely — `spinorml-1fj.1`'s comment notes each member's generic fn is pointer-in/pointer-out today, so true register residency needs refactoring each kernel to split pointer I/O from pure compute, explicitly deferred there too), but it's an optimization on top of a correct v1, not a correctness requirement for this case.

title: fix ReluForward/Backward RuntimeOp::block() to use block_size (allowlist CTA mismatch)
description:
## Problem

`is_fusable_elementwise` and spinorml-1fj.1 Phase 1 claim Relu/Sigmoid/Silu/Tanh share a uniform fixed-block elementwise CTA shape (`BLOCK_SIZE=1024`). That is false for Relu today:

- Lowering constructs `ReluForward(1024)` / `ReluBackward(1024)` (`kernels/teeny-kernels/src/graph/mod.rs`).
- `grid()` uses `self.block_size`.
- `block()` / `backward_block()` hardcode `[128, 1, 1]` in `kernels/teeny-kernels/src/nn/activation/relu.rs`.
- Sigmoid/Silu (and other float unary activations) use `[self.block_size as u32, 1, 1]`.

This breaks teenygrad-1bf.1's Decision 3 precondition: a case-1 `FusedRuntimeOp` may only delegate `block()`/`grid()` to any member when the allowlist equivalence class is actually identical.

## Fix

- Change Relu forward/backward `block()` / `backward_block()` to `[self.block_size as u32, 1, 1]`.
- Add a regression test that allowlisted ops' RuntimeOps agree on `block`/`grid` for a sample shape under the same construction path TritonLowering uses.

## Refs

Decision: `.ai/specs/fusion/case-1-elementwise-chains.md` (teenygrad-1bf.1).
close_reason: Obsolete: RuntimeOp::block()/backward_block() removed; CUDA threads come from PTX metadata. Case-1 fusability compares BLOCK_SIZE + grid(), not block().

title: fusion case 1: dtype-consistency guard + bool-terminal-only rule for pointwise chains
description:
fuse_pointwise_chain_pass() (kernels/teeny-kernels/src/graph/optimizer/anduin.rs:63-131) reads parent_dtype and child_dtype independently but never compares them before fusing; PointwiseFuse::dtype keeps only the childs dtype for the whole chain, and lower_pointwise_fuse() calls a single member_kernel(m, dtype) per member using that one dtype.

PointwiseFuse::lower() -> dtype_name() only accepts F32/F64 and panics on anything else (pointwise_fuse.rs:105-110, "PointwiseFuse::lower failed: {e}"). Ops resolved via make_num_kernel! (Abs, Neg, Sign, ...) support integer dtypes, and probe_pointwise_op() only checks block_size/grid compatibility, not dtype. So a graph like Abs(i32) -> Neg(i32) can pass the graph-time fusibility check and then PANIC at lowering time instead of failing gracefully or simply not fusing.

Separately, IsNaN/IsInf change output dtype to Bool mid-chain; nothing currently stops them from being fused as a non-terminal member, which would silently break the single-dtype-chain assumption every other part of this code relies on.

Acceptance criteria:
- fuse_pointwise_chain_pass() (or pointwise_parts()) rejects fusing when parent_dtype != child_dtype, before constructing a PointwiseFuse.
- Non-float dtypes (or any dtype dtype_name() would reject) are excluded from fusion at graph-optimization time, not left to panic in lower().
- Bool-producing ops (IsNaN, IsInf) are only eligible as the terminal member of a chain, never interior.
- Regression tests: mixed-dtype chain does not fuse; int-dtype chain does not fuse (and does not panic); IsNaN/IsInf mid-chain does not fuse.

Found during an investigation into case-1 (teenygrad-1bf.1) pointwise op coverage; see that issues comments for the fuller op inventory this spawned.

title: fusion case 1: fuse zero-param float activations (Selu, Gelu, Mish, Hardsigmoid, Hardswish, Softsign, Silu, Logsigmoid, Tanhshrink)
description:
Batch 1 of case-1 op coverage. These 9 ops already have forward kernels wired through TritonLowerings normal op table with the same BLOCK_SIZE-const + n_elements:i32 ABI that probe_pointwise_op()/member_kernel() require, so they are likely fusable via the existing generic PointwiseFuse mechanism already -- they are just untested and not confirmed.

Scope: forward-only fusion (no backward -- none of these have any backward kernel today, fused or unfused). Verify each op individually chains with itself and with the already-shipped Relu/Sigmoid/Tanh (e.g. Relu -> Gelu -> Silu), add fixtures/snapshot tests mirroring test_anduin_pointwise.rs, and confirm numerically against PyTorch per existing fixture conventions.

Depends on the dtype/bool-terminal guard landing first so these tests exercise the hardened fusibility check, not the current gap.

title: fusion case 1: fuse parameterized float activations (Elu, Celu, Hardtanh, Hardshrink, LeakyRelu, Threshold, Softshrink, Softplus)
description:
Batch 2 of case-1 op coverage. These 8 ops carry extra scalar consts (alpha, lambd, min/max, threshold/value, beta) alongside BLOCK_SIZE, unlike batch teenygrad-1bf.1.3s zero-param set. They already route through the same lower_unary_op() path, so the scalar consts should thread through member_kernel() correctly, but this is exactly the kind of thing more likely to break when concatenating kernel bodies (const name collisions between two members that each declare e.g. ALPHA) or when packing args for the fused entry point.

Scope: forward-only fusion. Verify each op individually and in mixed chains with a scalar-param op adjacent to a zero-param op (e.g. Relu -> LeakyRelu{alpha=0.1} -> Sigmoid), add fixtures/snapshot tests, confirm numerically against PyTorch.

Depends on the dtype/bool-terminal guard (teenygrad-1bf.1.2) landing first.

title: fusion case 1: fuse transcendental math ops (Exp, Log, Sqrt, Erf, Reciprocal)
description:
Batch 3 of case-1 op coverage. Zero-param float unary ops, forward-only (no backward exists for any of these today). Same generic-probe fusibility as the activation batches, just a different kernel family. Add fixtures/snapshot tests (e.g. Exp -> Reciprocal, Log -> Sqrt), confirm numerically against PyTorch.

title: fusion case 1: fuse trig/hyperbolic math ops (Sin, Cos, Tan, Asin, Acos, Atan, Sinh, Cosh, Asinh, Acosh, Atanh)
description:
Batch 4 of case-1 op coverage. 11 zero-param float unary ops, forward-only. Largest single batch by op count but lowest priority -- these rarely chain with each other in real models (more likely to appear standalone or adjacent to activations already covered by other batches), so treat as a mechanical sweep: fixtures/snapshot tests per op plus one or two mixed chains (e.g. Sin -> Tanh), confirm numerically against PyTorch.

title: fusion case 1: fuse rounding/sign math ops (Abs, Neg, Sign, Ceil, Floor, Round)
description:
Batch 5 of case-1 op coverage. Abs and Neg already have real (non-y-style) backward kernels wired at the op level today -- forward-fusion for this batch is in scope, but do NOT fold their backward into is_y_style_pointwise_bwd; that needs the x-style backward ABI work tracked separately. Sign/Ceil/Floor/Round have no backward at all.

Abs/Neg/Sign are resolved via make_num_kernel! and support integer dtypes at the op level, but PointwiseFuse::dtype_name() only accepts F32/F64 -- confirm this batchs tests stay float-only until/unless int support is explicitly scoped, and that the guard from teenygrad-1bf.1.2 is what stops int chains from reaching these kernels, not an accident of test coverage.

Depends on teenygrad-1bf.1.2 (dtype/bool-terminal guard).

title: fusion case 1: investigate eliminating scratch-buffer store/load round-trips in PointwiseFuse lowering
description:
Op::Fused / `PointwiseFuse` chains lower via scratch-buffer ping-pong
(`kernels/teeny-kernels/src/graph/optimizer/ops/pointwise_fuse.rs:56-64`
doc comment, `n_scratch` wiring ~L170-215, entry synthesis ~L459-539),
shipped in commit 618007e6d (#25) "lower Op::Fused elementwise chains with
scratch ping-pong". Each interior member writes its output to a scratch
pointer in global memory and the next member reloads it, rather than
composing values in registers.

teenygrad-1bf.1's Decision 2 (comment, 2026-08-10) explicitly deferred
this: "MLIR inline + DCE may still erase some store/load pairs when
aliasing is provable; treat that as opportunistic, not required for
correctness of v1" and flagged "value-level composition as an explicit
later upgrade once case-1 lowering works end-to-end."

Now that case-1 lowering has actually landed (618007e6d), investigate
whether those scratch store/load round-trips are being optimized out in
practice:

- Check whether MLIR inline + DCE (or any pass already in the pipeline)
  eliminates the store-then-immediate-load pairs for scratch0..scratchN in
  generated/lowered fused kernels -- inspect the MLIR snapshots for fused
  chains (e.g. the Anduin Conv2d->BN->SiLU integration test added in
  618007e6d) to see whether scratch stores/loads survive to the final IR.
- If they survive, determine whether a targeted store-forwarding / dead
  store elimination pass, or restructuring `PointwiseFuse::lower` to emit
  register-resident (load/compute/store split, composed on values instead
  of pointers) composition, is worth doing -- and at what chain length it
  starts to matter.
- Backward reuses forward scratch buffers to walk the chain in-place on
  `dx` (doc comment L63-64) -- confirm any fix here doesn't break that
  reverse-mode reuse.
- Quantify against the N-launches->1 win already captured by scratch
  fusion: is the remaining store/load traffic actually measurable for the
  chain lengths seen today (2-4 members, per the static `n_scratch` tables
  at ~L194-198)?

Acceptance: a written decision (mirrors teenygrad-1bf.1's Decision-2
format) on whether to (a) rely on existing MLIR DCE as sufficient, (b) add
a dedicated store/load elimination pass, or (c) move to value-level /
register-resident composition -- plus, if (b) or (c), a follow-up issue
scoping the implementation.
