title: RISC-V row-wise reductions and softmax return NaN under QEMU
description:
Found 2026-09-11 running teeny-kernels with --features riscv,training,hardware,qemu (the new QEMU launch in teeny-riscv) against teenyc from teeny feat/triton-riscv-rvv @ 9f48d7207fa.

Failing tests (8), each returning NaN at element 0 where the fixture is finite:
- test_reduction: test_reduce_max (expected 1.9389584), test_reduce_min (0.50756866), test_reduce_log_sum_exp (5.556284), test_global_max_pool (1.9389584)
- test_softmax: test_softmax_forward (0.00013586755)
- test_extra_activations: test_log_softmax_forward (-4.7296047)
- test_loss_nll: test_cross_entropy_loss_forward (2.5555873), test_cross_entropy_loss_backward (0.0028614243)

Common shape: one program id per row (let row = program_id(X); if row >= n_outer { return; }), a masked load over BLOCK_INNER columns with a padding value (reduce_max pads with f32::MIN, not -inf), then a reduction over the row. Elementwise, pooling, BCE, lppool and flash_attn2 kernels match their fixtures through the same launch path, so buffer marshalling and program-id passing are unlikely causes.

Not yet known whether CUDA hardware gives the same result (the NVIDIA kernel module isn't loaded on this machine).

Next steps: dump reduce_max_forward's LLVM IR and assembly for riscv64-generic (RUSTC_LOG=rustc_codegen_llvm::mlir=debug) and check how the early return and the row reduction are lowered; rerun on CUDA once the driver works.

title: spec: tile-spec resolution testable without anduin, plus the data-dependent fallback
description:
## Goal

Make the tile-spec layer **testable without anduin**, and settle the one
kernel family that has no kernels to declare axes on.

## Scope change, 2026-09-23

This epic originally also owned per-family `KernelTileSpec` coverage, assuming
hand-authored `const`s at `TritonLowering` call sites. That work moved to
`teenygrad-1tl`, which produces the same specs by declaration on the kernel
signature instead — closer to the kernel, and enforceable by a test that a
converted kernel really declares its axes.

Closed into that ladder: `.3` (flat elementwise) into `1tl.2`/`.3`/`.4`, `.4`
(windowed) into `1tl.7`, `.5` (matmul) into `1tl.10`, plus `teenygrad-1nr.14`
and `.15` into `1tl.8`, `.16` into `1tl.9`, and `.12` into `1tl.11`. Each close
carries the reasoning forward; see those issues' close reasons.

What remains here is the isolation mechanism itself, which is shipped, and
`.6`, which does not fit the ladder — see below.

## The isolation mechanism (delivered)

`propagate` is two things welded together: a graph walk, and a per-node
resolution of one `KernelTileSpec` against one output tile. **The second half
is a pure function and does not need a graph, a scheduler or hardware.**

```rust
// teeny-core — a self-check on the data's own invariants
impl KernelTileSpec { pub fn validate(&self) -> Result<()>; }

// teeny-kernels — given this kernel's output tile, the input tile each
// operand must supply
pub fn resolve_inputs(spec: &KernelTileSpec, output_tile: &TileShape,
                      consts: &impl ConstLookup) -> Result<Vec<TileShape>>;
```

The split is **vocabulary vs. logic**. The spec types have to be in
`teeny-core` — `ExecutableOp::tile_spec()` is a trait method there and
`teeny-core` holds `Dag<Box<dyn ExecutableOp>>`, so the return type must be
nameable in that crate. Tile-resolution arithmetic does not: it is scheduler
semantics and belongs where `propagate` will live.

**Constraint on `teenygrad-1nr.25`:** the re-landed `propagate` must *call*
`resolve_inputs`, not reimplement it. Otherwise the tested path and the
scheduled path drift, which is the drift this epic exists to prevent.

## Why `.6` stays here

`Gather`/`Scatter` and friends have `Op` variants in `teeny-core` but **no
Triton kernels** — `TritonLowering`'s arms for them are `todo!()`. There is no
signature to declare axes on, so the question is not a conversion and does not
belong on the `1tl` ladder. It is a design decision about what a spec says when
the input region depends on runtime values, and it can be settled before the
kernels exist.

## Done when

- `validate()` passes for every registered spec, enforced by a test. **Done**
  (`teenygrad-1iy.1`).
- `resolve_inputs` exists as a standalone, tested function. **Done**
  (`teenygrad-1iy.2`).
- The data-dependent fallback is explicit and tested (`teenygrad-1iy.6`).
close_reason: Anduin fusion work discontinued; closed with the Anduin-related issues

title: feat: KernelTileSpec::validate() + a test that runs it over every registered spec
description:
## Goal

`KernelTileSpec::validate()` in `core/teeny-core/src/model/tile_spec.rs`, plus
a test that runs it over every spec the lowering registers.

## Why first

Nothing checks a spec today. The invariants are stated in prose on the types
and enforced nowhere:

- `TileAxisBinding.dims` — *"every index must be `< rank`, and no index may
  repeat across one"* binding.
- `TensorTileSpec.axes` may cover fewer dims than `rank`; the remainder is
  `untiled_dims`, which must not overlap the tiled ones.
- `reduction_axis` must be in range.
- `loop_spec` naming consts that exist.

A malformed spec currently fails at the point a consumer indexes it — which,
with no consumer in the tree, means it does not fail at all.

## Scope

- `validate(&self) -> Result<()>` with a typed error naming the spec, the
  tensor param and the offending index.
- A `const`-compatible path if cheap, so a bad spec is a compile error rather
  than a test failure — `KernelTileSpec` is already `Copy`/`const`-built.
  Do not contort the API for this; a test is acceptable.
- One test enumerating every registered spec and asserting `validate()`.

## Done when

Every spec in `kernels/teeny-kernels/src/graph/mod.rs` validates, and a
deliberately malformed spec fails with a message naming the axis.
close_reason: Delivered by PR #45 (squash 0ec5d2aae on feature/anduin-v2). KernelTileSpec::validate plus TensorTileSpec/TileAxisBinding::validate, with 14 unit tests in teeny-core. The companion test enumerating every registered spec was removed later in the same PR, when the hand-authored specs it enumerated were deleted -- validate() now guards the macro-derived specs instead, which is what teenygrad-1tl produces.

title: feat: resolve_inputs in teeny-kernels — per-node tile resolution as a pure function
description:
## Goal

`resolve_inputs(spec: &KernelTileSpec, output_tile: &TileShape) -> Result<Vec<TileShape>>`
in **`teeny-kernels`**: the per-node half of `propagate`, as a pure function
with no graph, scheduler or hardware dependency.

This is the mechanism that makes the rest of this epic testable. Every
coverage subtask asserts its specs through this function.

## Where it lives, and why not `teeny-core`

The spec *types* stay in `teeny-core` — `ExecutableOp::tile_spec()` is a
trait method there, and `teeny-core` holds `Dag<Box<dyn ExecutableOp>>` in
`Lowering`/`Model` (`model/mod.rs:402,426`), so the return type has to be
nameable in that crate. An associated type does not escape this: it would
force `dyn ExecutableOp<TileSpec = ..>` across `teeny-cuda`, `teeny-test`
and five files in `teeny-kernels`, and `teeny-core` still could not name a
concrete one.

The distinction being held is **vocabulary vs. logic**. Types in
`teeny-core` so the trait can speak about them is fine. Tile-resolution
arithmetic there is not: it is scheduler semantics in the published `no_std`
foundation crate, which no other `teeny-core` consumer needs.

`teeny-kernels` is the home, for three concrete reasons:

- `propagate`'s graph walk will live there (`teenygrad-1nr.25`), so the two
  halves stay in one crate and one review.
- The registered specs live there — `MATMUL`/`BATCHNORM2D`/`CONV1D`/
  `CONV3D_TILE_SPEC` in `graph/mod.rs` — so the tests sit beside the data
  they check, next to `teenygrad-1iy.1`'s validation test.
- A tile *shape* is a kernels-level concept, not a foundation one (see
  below).

`teenygrad-1iy.1`'s `validate()` stays in `teeny-core`: it is a self-check
on the data's own declared invariants, with no tile shapes and no
scheduling semantics involved.

`teeny-triton` is the fallback if a second kernel crate ever needs this;
`teeny-kernels` already depends on it, and it is where these types lived
before `84ca6eedf`.

## Tile representation: deliberately minimal

`resolve_inputs` takes and returns a plain per-axis extent list —
`Option<usize>` per axis, reusing `teeny_core::graph::Shape`'s established
idiom where `None` means unknown/unresolved.

It must **not** take `TileDim`. `TileDim`/`TileEdgeShape` lived in the
deleted `tile_graph/types.rs` and come back with `teenygrad-1nr.25`;
depending on them would block this issue on the very work the epic exists to
run ahead of. Reconciling the two representations is a design point for
`.25`/`teenygrad-1nr.26` — most likely a conversion at the graph boundary,
since `TileDim::Sym`'s name and max extent matter to the search but not to
this arithmetic.

## Semantics

Per input tensor, per axis:

- tiled axis, no window — the output tile's block for that bound axis
- tiled axis with a `TileWindow` — the receptive field,
  `(block - 1) * stride + kernel_size`, which is `TileWindow`'s own
  documented contract. Padding shifts the origin, not the extent.
- axis in `untiled_dims`, or a `reduction_axis` with no output counterpart —
  full extent, the existing fallback
- flattened multi-dim binding (`TileAxisBinding.dims` with >1 entry) — the
  block spans the flattened run; innermost dim carries it, outer dims
  collapse to 1, matching the convention `teenygrad-1nr.8`/`.9` established

Forward region arithmetic throughout. It is not an inverse of
`infer_output_shape` — see `teenygrad-1nr.30` for why that distinction is
load-bearing, and `teenygrad-3fy` for the approach that was rejected.

## Boundary with teenygrad-1nr.25

`.25` re-lands `propagate`'s **graph walk**. It must call `resolve_inputs`
for the per-node step rather than reimplement it, so the path tests exercise
and the path the scheduler runs are the same code.

## Done when

- `resolve_inputs` handles the four axis cases above.
- Tests cover a flat elementwise spec, `MATMUL_TILE_SPEC`, `CONV1D_TILE_SPEC`
  (windowed) and `BATCHNORM2D_TILE_SPEC` (flattened), against hand-computed
  input tiles for real shapes.
- A windowed axis with `stride > 1` and non-zero padding resolves to the
  receptive field, independent of the padding value.
- Nothing in `teeny-core` changed to make it work.
close_reason: Delivered by PR #45 (squash 0ec5d2aae). resolve_inputs in kernels/teeny-kernels/src/graph/tile_resolve.rs -- the per-node half of Welder's Propagate as a pure function, with ConstLookup/NoConsts and TileShape. Tests use local fixtures rather than production specs, since the hand-authored ones were deleted in the same PR. Constraint carried to teenygrad-1nr.25: the re-landed propagate must CALL this, not reimplement it.

title: feat: KernelTileSpecs for the flat elementwise family (activations, unary/binary math)
description:
## Goal

`KernelTileSpec`s for the flat, single-axis elementwise kernels — the
activations (`nn/activation/*`), unary math and binary elementwise ops
(`nn/tensor/elemwise_unary.rs`, `elemwise_binary.rs`).

## Why this is the cheap one

These are the shape-preserving case: one tiled axis, output tile equals input
tile, no window, no reduction, no flattening. `#[tiled_kernel]`'s
`In<Tile<T, D>>` prelude already generates for exactly this shape
(`c69c08b63`), so most of these kernels are already in the right form — the
specs are declarations, not design.

Do this group first to shake out `validate()`/`resolve_inputs` on the case
where the right answer is obvious, before the families where it is not.

## Scope

- Audit which elementwise kernels have a derived `tile_spec()` already and
  which need one.
- Multi-input elementwise (`Add`, `Mul`, ...) needs `inputs` with one
  `TensorTileSpec` per operand — check `resolve_inputs` returns the right
  arity, since this is the first family with more than one input.
- Broadcasting: an operand broadcast along an axis does **not** get the
  output's block on that axis. Establish what the spec says here, or record
  that broadcast operands fall back to full extent.

## Done when

Every elementwise kernel reachable from `TritonLowering` has a spec or a
recorded reason, all validate, and `resolve_inputs` round-trips them to the
identity tile.
notes:
ANSWERED by teenygrad-1tl.4 (PR #57), 2026-09-29.

The broadcast question this issue raises -- what the spec says about an operand broadcast along an axis, which therefore does not get the output's block -- is settled: an operand declares exactly the axes it has. One that shares no blocked axis carries no TileAxisBinding on any axis and resolves to its own full extent.

That required a macro fix, not just a convention. #[tiled_kernel] had been giving every tensor the FIRST tile parameter's axis list, so channel_bias_add_forward's (C,) bias reported rank 2 with N blocked -- an axis it does not have. Each parameter now reports its own declared axes; bias is rank 1, axes empty, untiled ["C"]. Asserted in graph/tile_resolve.rs::test_a_broadcast_operand_resolves_to_its_own_full_extent.
close_reason: Superseded by the teenygrad-1tl ladder, which produces the same specs by declaration on the kernel signature rather than hand-authored consts. Scope split three ways: 1tl.2 (unary flat elementwise, ~53 kernels), 1tl.3 (multi-input, incl. this issue's resolve_inputs arity question), 1tl.4 (the broadcast/mixed-extent convention this issue asked to establish). Correction carried over: this issue said 'most of these kernels are already in the right form' -- measured, 2 of ~53 generate a tile_spec today.

title: feat: KernelTileSpecs for the windowed family (conv 1/2/3d + the nine pools)
description:
## Goal

`KernelTileSpec`s for the windowed family: `Conv1d`/`2d`/`3d` and all nine
pooling variants (`AvgPool`/`MaxPool`/`LpPool` x 1d/2d/3d).

## Current state

`CONV1D_TILE_SPEC` and `CONV3D_TILE_SPEC` are hand-authored
(`kernels/teeny-kernels/src/graph/mod.rs:378,427`); `Conv2dForward::tile_spec()`
is macro-derived. **No pooling kernel has a spec at all** — nine kernels,
one mechanism.

## Why conv and pool are one group

Both are `(block - 1) * stride + kernel_size` along each spatial axis — the
receptive field `TileWindow` already documents. Pooling differs only in
having no weight operand and no channel change. Splitting them by `nn`
module would duplicate the interesting part.

## Scope

- `TileWindow` on each spatial axis of the input tensor, naming the real
  stride/pad/kernel consts on each kernel.
- Pools: channel axis is untiled or passthrough, no weight operand.
- Assert through `resolve_inputs` (`teenygrad-1iy.2`) that a `BLOCK`-sized
  output tile resolves the input axis to the receptive field, **clamped to
  the real extent at the boundary but never to the padding value** — the
  resolved extent must not depend on the padding const. That single assertion
  catches the most likely error in this family.

## Relationship to teenygrad-1nr.29

`.29` teaches `#[tile(..)]` to *express* a strided/padded window so these
specs can be derived from the kernel signature instead of hand-authored.
This issue can proceed with hand-authored consts and be migrated, or wait
for `.29` — decide when starting. The tests written here stay valid either
way, which is the point of testing through `resolve_inputs`.

## Done when

All twelve kernels have a spec, all validate, and each resolves a known
output tile to a hand-computed input region.
close_reason: Superseded by teenygrad-1tl.7, which covers the same 13 kernels (conv 1/2/3d + nine pools) and additionally declares the real TileWindow consts rather than leaving x_ptr with no bindings. Receptive-field derivation stays in teenygrad-1nr.30.

title: feat: KernelTileSpecs for the matmul family (Gemm transpose-aware, QLinearMatMul, Linear)
description:
## Goal

`KernelTileSpec`s for the matmul family beyond the one that exists:
`Gemm` (transpose-aware), `QLinearMatMul`, `Linear`, and batched matmul.

## Current state

`MATMUL_TILE_SPEC` (`graph/mod.rs:207`) is the only one, and it is the
reference for the two-tiled-axes-plus-reduction shape.

## What is interesting here

- **The reduction axis.** `K` is reduced away: it has no output counterpart,
  so it takes the full-extent fallback. Assert that through
  `resolve_inputs` rather than assuming it.
- **Transpose.** `Gemm{trans_a, trans_b}` changes which tensor axis the
  `M`/`N` blocks bind to. A spec is static, so either it is authored per
  transpose combination, or `TileAxisBinding.dim` is resolved at
  construction time from the op's flags — the same answer
  `TileAxisBinding::divide_by` took. Settle this here.
- **Linear** is matmul with a bias operand; check the bias tensor's spec
  does not claim a block on an axis it does not have.

## Done when

Each kernel has a spec, all validate, and `resolve_inputs` gives the
hand-computed `[M_block, K_full]` / `[K_full, N_block]` operand tiles —
including for both transpose settings of `Gemm`.
close_reason: Superseded by teenygrad-1tl.10. Carried over: the K-block sizing problem (both GEMM input tiles resolve at full K, so a 1024-cubed f32 GEMM at a 64x32 tile needs 384KiB and looks unfusable) is recorded there as needing a seed channel into resolve_inputs that ConstLookup is the wrong vehicle for.

title: feat: settle tile specs for data-dependent kernels (Gather/Scatter) — conservative fallback
description:
## Goal

Settle what happens for kernels whose input positions are **data-dependent**:
`Gather`, `Scatter`, `GatherElements`, `ScatterND`, `OneHot`, `NonZero`,
`Compress` and friends.

## Expect the answer to be "no spec"

The input region a `Gather` output tile reads is a function of the index
tensor's *runtime values*, not of any static shape. No amount of
`TileAxisBinding` expresses that.

Welder does not solve it either — §3.1 (Shi et al., OSDI '23, p. 704) says
its expression analysis *"provides a conservative upper bound as the input
tile shape"* for exactly this class: *"irregular patterns such as sparse or
noncontinuous access (e.g., `Gather` or Convolution with strides)"*.

## Scope

This issue is about making the fallback **explicit and tested**, not about
inventing a spec.

- Decide the representation: no `tile_spec` at all (the current implicit
  fallback), or a spec that marks the data-dependent axis so a consumer can
  tell "not tiled" from "not described". The second is more honest and costs
  one variant.
- Whichever is chosen, `resolve_inputs` must return the **full extent** for
  that axis — an upper bound. Never a block. Under-reporting here under-sizes
  a real buffer, and footprint is checked against a hard capacity
  (`teenygrad-1nr.27`).
- A test per op asserting the conservative answer.

## Done when

Every data-dependent kernel either has a spec whose data-dependent axes
resolve to full extent, or a recorded reason it has none — and a test proves
the fallback is the conservative direction.
close_reason: Anduin fusion work discontinued; closed with the Anduin-related issues

title: Dedup CUDA module loads across DAG nodes referencing the same compiled kernel
description:
## Problem

teeny-cuda's model-loading loop (drivers/teeny-cuda/src/model/mod.rs, ~line 285)
reads cn.ptx_path and calls CudaProgram::try_from_ptx() (-> cuModuleLoadDataEx)
once per DAG node, with no cache/dedup keyed by kernel identity. If multiple DAG
nodes reference the same compiled kernel (same ptx_path / identical PTX content),
the CUDA driver redundantly JIT-compiles and loads it multiple times as separate
CUmodule handles.

## Evidence (vision-rs YOLO26n bench, RTX 5070, nsys trace of the full process)

- cuModuleLoadDataEx: 295 calls, 38.7ms total (131us avg/call), during model setup.
- Only 38 unique compiled kernel files exist in the teenyc cache dir for this model
  (192 DAG nodes / 224 kernel launches at runtime) — i.e. ~7-8x more module-load
  calls than unique kernels, meaning most calls are redundant re-JITs of PTX
  already loaded earlier in the same process.
- Confirmed separately that the teenyc-compiled ".o" cache files are literally PTX
  assembly text (`file` reports "assembler source, ASCII text"; `cuobjdump` refuses
  them as "does not contain device code") — so even with a fully warm teenyc
  cache, the CUDA driver's own PTX->cubin JIT always runs at process start; the
  teenyc cache only saves the Rust/MLIR->PTX compile step, not this step.
- For context: cuCtxCreate/cuCtxDestroy (~257ms combined) dominate one-time setup
  cost and are not addressable, but cuModuleLoadDataEx (38.7ms) is the second-
  largest chunk and is within our control.

## Suggested fix

Cache loaded CUmodule/CudaProgram handles keyed by ptx_path (or a content hash of
the PTX) at the point model/mod.rs loads programs for each DAG node, and reuse
the existing handle instead of calling try_from_ptx again for an already-seen
kernel. Expect roughly proportional reduction in cuModuleLoadDataEx time (295
calls -> ~38 calls, plausibly ~39ms -> ~5ms), improving cold-start / time-to-
first-inference. Does not affect steady-state per-image latency (module loading
happens once at model load, not in the per-inference timed loop).

## Scope note

This doesn't affect vision-rs's benchmark throughput numbers (load time is
outside the timed loop) but matters for cold-start scenarios (e.g. a
server that loads a fresh model per request rather than staying resident).

title: feat(anduin): conv2d -> batchnorm2d -> silu schedules as one tiled kernel anchored at conv2d
description:
## Goal
`input -> conv2d -> batchnorm2d -> silu`, lowered through the real `TritonLowering` and scheduled with the production `TeenygradCaps`, becomes ONE `Tiled` kernel {conv2d, batchnorm2d, silu} anchored at conv2d, with a tiling equivalent to the hand-fused `Conv2dBnSiluForward`: conv2d's grid, per-(b, c_out) units and a halo'd input read.

## Acceptance test
`test_conv2d_batchnorm_silu_schedules_as_one_tiled_kernel` in kernels/teeny-kernels/src/graph/optimizer/anduin/schedule/mod.rs. It was added on 2026-10-23 on branch feature/anduin-tile-group and is not yet committed. It currently fails with:
`["Opaque(conv2d_forward)", "Tiled([batch_norm_2d_nchw_forward_inference, silu_forward], anchor batch_norm_2d_nchw_forward_inference)"]`.
Commit it `#[ignore]`d with a reason naming this issue, and remove the ignore when this closes. Extend it once the blockers land to check the tiling too:
- the grid is conv2d's (units = B·C_out·OH·cdiv(OW, BLOCK_OW));
- conv2d's input region is Tiled with a halo on H and W;
- no region is Full on B or C;
- footprint within the shared-memory budget.

## Blockers (in order)
1. teenygrad-2pvx: conv2d lowering attaches its grid spec (it is otherwise opaque).
2. teenygrad-8x1t: conv -> bn fusion under TeenygradCaps, with conv as anchor (BN inference as a rider).
3. teenygrad-yf8f: BatchNorm2d binds B and C (P4).
4. teenygrad-a19a: production ConstLookup (P3), so conv's windowed axes are not Full.
5. teenygrad-3f4z: model reduction loops (P6 rsteps, conv2d's `tile_loop`), bind conv2d's own B/C_OUT/OH (P4), and add its weight (P5), so the footprint is not over-estimated.

## Experiment record
With blocker 1 patched in and `TritonCaps` (fuse anything), all three ops fuse, but:
- anchor = bn;
- BLOCK_HW = 512 and only 2 units, each covering every (b, c) and half the rows;
- footprint 90112 B, traffic[0] = 114688 B;
- conv2d's input region is [Full, Full, Full, Full].
So the fusion is "feasible" only because the specs are under-described.
notes: 2026-10-23: 2pvx, yf8f, 8x1t done (1064a280a, 883f7785b, 0a6c7b5b3). Acceptance test un-ignored and passing for nodes/anchor/knob BLOCK_OW. Remaining for tiling quality: a19a (P3), 3f4z (P6 + conv2d's own P4/P5); then extend the test with grid/halo/footprint checks.
close_reason: Acceptance test extended and passing in 3f18d5207

title: spec: Welder-style TileGraph scheduler (memory-hierarchy search, not case-based fusion)
description:
## Goal

Supersedes `teenygrad-1bf` (deleted 2026-08-18 — its case taxonomy and prior-art
comments were written before Anduin existed and are no longer an accurate
starting point). This issue specs the real Welder algorithm (OSDI'23, Shi et
al.) as the fusion/scheduling mechanism, replacing both `teenygrad-1bf`'s
case-taxonomy approach and Anduin's current hand-coded pattern detectors —
neither of those is what Welder actually does.

## Current state (what's real today, and what it is *not*)

- **Anduin exists and works**, but it is a set of hand-coded pattern
  detectors, not Welder. `kernels/teeny-kernels/src/graph/optimizer/` has 4
  strategies, each built by hand for one shape: `PointwiseFuse` (linear unary
  chains, `is_pointwise_fuse_dtype`), `TileFuse` (fan-in binary tail),
  `ReduceFuse` (chain → reduction, `is_reduce_fuse_member`),
  `SharedTransposeFuse` (chain → transpose). Each is a special-cased matcher
  over `Op` shapes — there is no general graph-to-tile-schedule algorithm
  here, and no memory-hierarchy search. Do not describe this as "how Welder
  works" — it isn't; it's the ad-hoc precursor this issue replaces.
- **The synthesis mechanism these 4 strategies use is also broken.**
  `ReduceFuse`/`PointwiseFuse` build the fused kernel by concatenating each
  chain member's `FusionCore::body_source` (`kernels/teeny-triton/src/fusion_core.rs`)
  — literal Rust source text, spliced into a hand-built wrapper string, with
  no variable-renaming step.
  - **Reproduced, concrete bug** (diagnostic test added this session):
    `kernels/teeny-kernels/tests/test_anduin_reduce_fuse.rs::test_anduin_reduce_fuse_relu_sigmoid_sum_matches_pytorch`
    builds `Relu → Sigmoid → ReduceSum`; fails at `teenyc` compile time
    because `sigmoid_forward`'s core references its own `BLOCK_SIZE`, which
    `ReduceFuse`'s synthesized wrapper never declares (it only has
    `BLOCK_INNER`). Left failing (not `#[ignore]`d) on purpose as a live
    regression test.
- **The hand-fused `conv2d_bn_silu` kernels are not the direction.** Removed
  from test coverage this session (kernel sources/bench left in place,
  untested, in `kernels/teeny-kernels/src/nn/fused/`). The target scenario is
  composing the *individual* existing kernels via the mechanism below, not a
  hand-written monolithic kernel.

## The real Welder algorithm (what this issue actually specs)

Welder does not pattern-match op shapes. It works purely at the level of
memory availability and bandwidth, via a general search:

1. **Graph → TileGraph.** Every op becomes a TileGraph node: an
   input/output tile shape plus a candidate memory location (which
   hierarchy level the tile lives at). This is the `TileGraph` data
   structure discussed earlier this session — not yet built.
2. **Backward shape propagation.** Starting from the graph's final output,
   propagate its tile shape backward through the TileGraph via each op's
   shape-transfer function. Because a single shared choice (e.g. a block
   size) determines shapes at every node it touches, tile shapes throughout
   the graph end up expressed as expressions in shared free variables, not
   fixed numbers — the search is over these variables, not over hand-picked
   cases.
3. **Per-node memory-hierarchy placement.** For each node, decide where its
   output tile should live based on real memory availability at each
   hierarchy level: try the smallest/closest level first (registers); if the
   tile doesn't fit, fall through to the next level (shared memory, L2,
   global memory). Each (tile-shape, memory-level) choice for a node is a
   candidate, added to a config.
4. **Cost-model-pruned top-k.** A cheap analytic cost model (the
   `mem_traffic`/`CostModel::penalized_traffic*` machinery already in
   `kernels/teeny-triton/src/tile.rs` is the right building block here)
   scores candidate configs and keeps only the top-k — pruning a
   combinatorially large space rather than exhaustively evaluating it.
5. **Real-hardware validation.** The analytic cost model is only accurate
   enough for pruning. Final selection among the top-k compiles and runs
   each candidate on real hardware and picks the winner by measured
   performance, not the analytic estimate.

The algorithm's real details are more involved than this summary, but the
key property is: it never special-cases "elementwise chain" vs "reduction"
vs "transpose" vs "conv epilogue" — those are all just TileGraph nodes with
different shape-transfer functions, competing in the same memory-availability
search. Anduin's 4 strategies are what you get *without* this — a reasonable
stopgap, not the target architecture.

## Composition mechanism: Tile-value functions, not text splicing

Regardless of which strategies survive vs. get subsumed by the general
search, the *lowering* mechanism for a chosen fusion needs to change from
`FusionCore` source-splicing to real function composition:

`#[tiled_kernel]`-annotated functions stop being pointer-in/pointer-out,
independently-launchable kernels. They become composable, device-only helper
functions: `Tile<D> → Tile<D>` (or multiple `Tile<D>` params in, tuple out —
needed for conv2d's `x`/`w`, batchnorm's `scale`/`shift`, etc.). `#[kernel]`
keeps today's pointer-based, host-launchable contract — it becomes the
*wrapper* the TileGraph schedule's chosen memory-level assignments compile
down to: `pid` decode, shared-memory allocation, calls to the composed
`#[tiled_kernel]` functions, boundary load/store to global memory.

**KernelTileSpec moves to the wrapper** — `#[tiled_kernel]` functions no
longer take pointers/extents, so block/extent declarations for the cost
model describe the wrapper's `load_tile`/`store_tile` calls.

**Composing kernel-functions requires passing `Tile` *values* through shared
memory, not "tile pointers."** Resolved by reading `../teeny`'s actual
implementation (`teenyc`, this project's compiler fork — not upstream
Triton, not Gluon):

- `T::shared_alloc`/`shared_store_index`/`shared_barrier`/`shared_trans`/
  `shared_load_index` (`kernels/teeny-triton/src/triton/mod.rs`) are **real,
  working, non-stub** primitives. They emit real `tt.shared_*` marker ops
  (`../teeny/compiler/rustc_codegen_llvm/src/mlir/codegen/triton/ops/triton/tensor.rs`),
  lowered by a real MLIR pass
  (`../teeny/src/triton/lib/Dialect/TritonGPU/Transforms/LowerIndexedSharedMemory.cpp`),
  proven end-to-end to real PTX
  (`../teeny/compiler/rustc_codegen_llvm/tests/test_indexed_shared_memory_kernel.rs`).
- Deliberately **not** hand-built low-level ops and **not** Gluon — they go
  through the same `convert-triton-to-tritongpu` layout-inference pipeline
  as `tt.load`/`tt.store`, so a `Tensor<D>` read back via `shared_load_index`
  gets a real `#ttg.blocked` encoding and interoperates with ordinary tensor
  arithmetic with no special handling.
- **The real constraint:** these only support rank-2 buffers sliced by
  integer row index — no general pointer arithmetic into shared memory, and
  no conversion from `SharedMem<D>` to `Pointer<D>`. So `Tile<D>` composition
  moves whole `Tensor<D>` values through a store/barrier/load round-trip,
  not an addressable pointer passed as an `InPtr<T::Pointer<D>>` argument.

**Which memory level a tile lives at is tagged with
`teeny_core::device::hardware::MemoryLevelKind`** (`Register`/`SharedMemory`/
`L1Cache`/.../`DeviceMemory`) — the same enum `HardwareProfile` uses, so the
TileGraph's placement search and the cost model's hardware vocabulary are one
enum. `#[non_exhaustive]`, purely descriptive today.

## Open problems

1. **`TileGraph` doesn't exist yet.** Needs: a node type carrying tile
   shape (as an expression over shared free variables, not fixed numbers)
   and candidate memory location; backward shape propagation from a graph's
   output; and a way to enumerate/rank (shape, memory-level) candidates per
   node. This is the actual deliverable of Welder's algorithm above — not a
   5th hand-coded Anduin strategy.
2. **`program_id` doesn't compose.** Every existing kernel body does its own
   `T::program_id`-based pid decode internally. If a wrapper calls multiple
   `#[tiled_kernel]` functions inside one physical launch, they all see the
   *same* `pid` — the outer launch's. A composed tile-op must not re-derive
   its own tile position from `pid`; that has to happen exactly once, in the
   wrapper. Real surgery on `#[tiled_kernel]`'s codegen (or a new mode of
   it).
3. **Real-hardware validation loop.** Step 5 of the algorithm (compile + run
   top-k candidates, pick by measured performance) needs a real
   compile/launch/time harness wired into the search — not just the
   analytic cost model teeny-triton already has.

## Diagnostic test already in place

`kernels/teeny-kernels/tests/test_anduin_reduce_fuse.rs` — `Relu → Sigmoid →
ReduceSum` via `ReduceFuse`, PyTorch-fixture-validated
(`kernels/teeny-kernels/tests/fixtures/anduin_reduce_fuse_relu_sigmoid_sum/`).
Deliberately small (not the full conv2d+BN+SiLU case) but exercises both
same-shape chaining and a shape-changing reduction — chosen to surface
splicing bugs cheaply. Currently red on purpose; this is the correctness
oracle the eventual fix (whether that's the Tile-composition rework alone,
or the full TileGraph search) should turn green.

## Related

- `teenygrad-3w0` (closed) — the tile-shape DSL / Welder cost-model design
  this builds on. Not stale, still the right prior art for `KernelTileSpec`/
  `CostModel`/`MemoryLevelKind`.
- `core/teeny-core/src/device/hardware.rs` — `HardwareProfile`/`MemoryLevelKind`
  (added this session, on `feature/3w0-tile-dsl-welder-scheduler`).
close_reason: Closed together with the teenygrad-1nr epic (Welder-style TileGraph scheduler)

title: Rework tiled_kernel API to compose Tile<D> functions (not pointer-in/pointer-out kernels)
description:
## Boundary with teenygrad-1nr.18 (settled 2026-09-22)

This issue predates the `In<Tile<T, D>>`/`Out<Tile<T, D>>` ABI, which has
since shipped (`c69c08b63`) and is live in real kernels — see
`kernels/teeny-kernels/src/nn/activation/tanh.rs:31` and
`nn/tensor/elemwise_unary.rs:815`. The "kernels take `InPtr`/`OutPtr`
pointers" premise below is therefore **already false for flat, single-axis
elementwise kernels**. Read the scope as what remains.

`teenygrad-1nr.18` generalises that ABI to N-D/looped kernels and derives
`tile_spec()` from the signature. It names this issue's "`program_id`
doesn't compose" problem as the same problem, and settles the design point
this issue left open: the per-axis block/extent attribute drives **only**
the wrapper's generated prelude and `tile_spec()` generation, and must not
re-splice index arithmetic into the kernel author's body — that coupling is
why `84ca6eedf` removed the original `#[tile(..)]`.

Split of ownership:

| concern | owner |
|---|---|
| per-param/per-axis block+extent association on `Tile` params | `.18` |
| wrapper-generated load / index / loop / store prelude, N-D | `.18` |
| deriving `KernelTileSpec` from the kernel signature | `.18` |
| loop-carried state for windowed/looped wrappers | `.12` |
| **composing several tile functions inside one launch** | **this issue** |
| **`Tile<D>` hand-off via shared-memory store/barrier/load round-trip** | **this issue** |
| **tagging a round-trip with `MemoryLevelKind`** | **this issue** |
| **the `#[kernel]` wrapper contract that owns the single pid decode** | **this issue** |

So `.18` builds the wrapper prelude machinery; this issue composes multiple
tile functions inside one wrapper on top of it. Hence the `blocks` edge.
`teenygrad-1nr.19`–`.24` depend on this issue for the shared-memory hand-off
specifically, which `.18` does not cover.

## Goal

Rework `#[tiled_kernel]` from today's independently-launchable,
pointer-in/pointer-out kernel contract into the composable, device-only
`Tile<D> -> Tile<D>` helper-function contract described in the parent issue's
"Composition mechanism" section. This is the concrete API/codegen work that
the eventual TileGraph search (open problem 1 on the parent) will target when
choosing which memory level a tile lives at and which functions to compose --
it can and should proceed independently of the search itself.

## Scope

- `#[tiled_kernel]`-annotated functions take `Tile<D>` (or multiple `Tile<D>`
  params, tuple return for multi-output ops like conv2d's `x`/`w` or
  batchnorm's `scale`/`shift`) instead of `InPtr`/`OutPtr`/`InOutPtr`
  pointers -- no pointer arithmetic, no extents, inside these functions.
- `#[kernel]` becomes the wrapper contract these compose into: owns `pid`
  decode, shared-memory allocation, boundary `load`/`store` to global memory,
  and calls into the composed `#[tiled_kernel]` functions.
- `KernelTileSpec`/block/extent declarations move from the individual
  `#[tiled_kernel]` functions to the wrapper (they describe the wrapper's
  load/store calls now, not the composed functions' signatures).
- Moving `Tile<D>` values between composed functions goes through
  `T::shared_alloc`/`shared_store_index`/`shared_barrier`/`shared_trans`/
  `shared_load_index` (`kernels/teeny-triton/src/triton/mod.rs`) -- real,
  working primitives, proven end-to-end in `teenyc`
  (`../teeny/compiler/rustc_codegen_llvm/tests/test_indexed_shared_memory_kernel.rs`).
  These are rank-2, integer-row-indexed only, and there is no
  `SharedMem<D>` -> `Pointer<D>` conversion -- composition is a full
  store/barrier/load round-trip of `Tensor<D>` values, not passing an
  addressable tile pointer.
- Which memory level a given `Tile<D>` round-trip uses is tagged with
  `teeny_core::device::hardware::MemoryLevelKind`
  (`core/teeny-core/src/device/hardware.rs`), matching `HardwareProfile`'s
  vocabulary.

## The blocking problem to solve here

**`program_id` doesn't compose today.** Every existing kernel body does its
own `T::program_id`-based pid decode internally. If a wrapper calls multiple
composed `#[tiled_kernel]` functions inside one physical launch, they must
not each re-derive their own tile position from `pid` -- that has to happen
exactly once, in the wrapper, and the composed functions must receive their
tile position (or nothing positional at all -- just `Tile<D>` values) instead
of calling `T::program_id` themselves. This requires real surgery on
`#[tiled_kernel]`'s codegen (`macros/teeny-macros/src/macros/tiled_kernel.rs`),
not just a type-signature change.

## Out of scope (belongs to the parent issue / other subtasks)

- The `TileGraph` data structure, backward shape propagation, and
  memory-hierarchy placement search (parent issue, open problem 1).
- The cost-model-pruned top-k and real-hardware validation loop (parent
  issue, open problem 3).
- Anduin's actual scheduling logic (`Anduin::optimize` stays a `todo!()`
  until the TileGraph search exists) -- this subtask only needs to make the
  composed-function *lowering* mechanism real so that search has something
  to target.

## Correctness oracle

`kernels/teeny-kernels/tests/test_anduin_reduce_fuse.rs` -- currently red on
purpose (`ReduceFuse`'s `FusionCore` text-splicing leaves `BLOCK_SIZE`
unbound). This is the test the reworked composition mechanism should
eventually turn green, once something drives the new `#[tiled_kernel]`
contract end-to-end (may need a hand-written composition first, ahead of the
TileGraph search choosing it automatically).
close_reason: Closed together with the teenygrad-1nr epic (Welder-style TileGraph scheduler)

title: feat: TensorTileSpec can't express an axis subdivided by a grid constant (GroupNorm's C/G)
description:
## Goal

`group_norm_forward`'s real kernel (`kernels/teeny-kernels/src/nn/norm/groupnorm.rs`)
is grid `[N*G]` (one CTA per (sample, group)), iterating `BLOCK_NL`-wide
tiles over `channels_per_group * L` where `channels_per_group = C / G` --
i.e. its real per-CTA tile spans only a *fraction* (`1/G`) of the channel
axis, flattened with the spatial axis `L`, not the whole channel axis the
way BatchNorm2d's `H*W` flattening (teenygrad-1nr.8) covered a *whole*
pair of axes.

`TensorTileSpec`/`TileAxisBinding` has no primitive for "this axis's real
per-tile extent is divided by a compile-time constant not otherwise named
anywhere." The only two ways an axis's tile can resolve today are:
name-matched propagation from an output axis sharing the same
`extent_param`, or falling back to that axis's own full, untiled extent.
Neither can express `C/G` -- `G` isn't a graph-level shape dimension or an
`extent_param` anything else names, it's an internal kernel constant.

Whatever spec is authored for GroupNorm, the channel axis's resolved tile
can only ever come out as the *full* channel count `C` (via the untiled
fallback), never the correct `channels_per_group` -- silently
over-estimating footprint/traffic for this op by a factor of `G`, not a
crash.

(Also noteworthy, found reading the same kernel: `group_norm_forward` has
*three* real `Out` params -- `y_ptr`, `mean_ptr`, `rstd_ptr` -- extra
concrete evidence for the separate multi-output issue.)

## Reproduction

`kernels/teeny-kernels/src/graph/optimizer/anduin/tile_graph/mod.rs::tests::propagate_cannot_express_a_dim_subdivided_by_a_grid_constant`
(added, currently failing). Builds a 3-D `[N, C, L]` node with a
`groupnorm_shaped_spec` (only `L` bound via `TileAxisBinding`, channel
axis deliberately left untiled -- the best available authoring choice
today), `N=2, C=8, L=16, G=2` (so `channels_per_group=4`), and asserts the
resolved channel-axis tile is `4`. Fails: resolves to `8` (the full
channel count) every time.

## Fix plan (sketch)

Not fully designed here -- options worth weighing when this is picked up:

1. A new field on `TileAxisBinding` (or a new binding kind) naming a
   divisor: e.g. `divide_by: Option<&'static str>` (a `{NAME}: i32`
   kernel param, like `G`), so the untiled/full-extent fallback becomes
   "full extent divided by this param" instead of always the raw full
   extent. Minimal, but only covers exact, evenly-dividing subdivision
   (true for GroupNorm's `C % G == 0` case; may not generalize).
2. Something more general: let an axis's extent be an arbitrary named
   expression over other `{NAME}: i32` params, not just identity /
   divide-by-constant -- bigger scope, closer to Welder's own symbolic
   tensor-expression IR (which this codebase's `propagate` deliberately
   doesn't have -- see `TileGraph::propagate`'s own doc comment).

Either way, needs its own regression coverage once implemented, and
should be checked against `mem_footprint_with_config`/
`mem_traffic_with_config`'s existing "optimistic-not-pessimistic" numbers
for other ops to make sure a fix doesn't change already-correct behavior
elsewhere.

## Non-goals

- Writing the real `GROUPNORM_TILE_SPEC` / wiring it into `Op::GroupNorm`
  -- blocked on the fix above; a spec today can only be wrong.
- The multi-output gap (`y_ptr`/`mean_ptr`/`rstd_ptr`) -- tracked
  separately.

title: feat: TileGraph::propagate ignores every KernelTileSpec output but outputs[0]
description:
## Goal

`KernelTileSpec.outputs` can already declare more than one real output
tensor's `TensorTileSpec` -- the type supports it -- but
`TileGraph::propagate` only ever reads `spec.outputs.first()`
(`teeny_core::model::tile_spec.rs`'s own doc comment says so plainly:
"`TileGraph::propagate` uses `outputs[0]` -- every `TileOp` is
single-output today"). Any `extent_param` named only on a second (or
later) output is never seeded into `propagate`'s `resolved` map, so an
input axis bound to that name always falls back to its full, untiled
extent, regardless of what that second output's own tile might be.

This is a real, motivated gap, not hypothetical -- found surveying
kernels for tile-spec fit (this session):

- `flash_attn2` forward (`nn/attention/flash_attn2.rs`) produces both
  `o_ptr` (the attention output) and `l_ptr` (logsumexp, needed for
  backward) from one kernel launch.
- `group_norm_forward` (`nn/norm/groupnorm.rs`, teenygrad-1nr.10) has
  *three* real `Out` params: `y_ptr`, `mean_ptr`, `rstd_ptr`.

Deeper structural note: `TileGraph`/`TileEdge` itself only ever
synthesizes *one* output edge per node (`TileGraph::from_dag`) -- so even
once `propagate` is taught to read every declared output, there's
currently nowhere on the graph to seed a second output's own requested
tile shape from. Fixing `propagate`'s read side alone isn't sufficient;
this needs a graph-model change too.

## Reproduction

`kernels/teeny-kernels/src/graph/optimizer/anduin/tile_graph/mod.rs::tests::propagate_ignores_every_output_but_the_first`
(added, currently failing as expected -- see below). Builds a node with a
`two_output_spec` (`outputs: &[Y1, Y2]`, `Y1`'s axis named `"M"`, `Y2`'s
axis named `"aux"`; the one real input axis is bound to `"aux"`, matching
only `Y2`). Seeds the node's one real (`TileGraph`-level) output edge as
if it were `Y1`'s tile. Asserts the input's resolved tile is *not* simply
its full, untiled extent -- i.e. that `Y2`'s declared axis had *some*
influence. It always is exactly the full extent: `propagate` never reads
`outputs[1]` at all, so `"aux"` never enters `resolved`, regardless of
what's seeded.

Note the test can't seed a "correct" value for what `Y2`'s tile *should*
be -- there's no second output edge on `TileGraph` to seed it onto, per
the structural note above -- so it asserts the weaker, still-meaningful
"not always the full-extent fallback" rather than a specific expected
number.

## Fix plan (sketch)

1. `TileGraph`/`TileEdge`: give a node more than one real output edge
   (or otherwise represent "this node's second/third output value"), not
   just the single boundary/child edge every node gets today.
2. `TileGraph::propagate`: loop `spec.outputs` (not just `.first()`),
   seeding `resolved` from whichever of a node's *several* output edges
   corresponds to each declared `TensorTileSpec`, matched by `param` name
   or declaration order.
3. `SubGraphTilingResult`/`Trace::trace_graph`/`codegen`: audit whether
   any of those already assume one output per node structurally (likely,
   given they're all built on the same `TileGraph`/`SubGraphTilingResult`
   shape) -- probably needs its own follow-up once scoped.

This is a bigger structural change than teenygrad-1nr.7/.8/.10 (which
were all fixable inside `propagate` alone) -- expect it to touch
`TileGraph`'s core edge model, not just `propagate`.

## Non-goals

- Actually modeling `flash_attn2`'s loop-carried accumulator state --
  tracked separately (`TileLoopSpec`/`TileCarryBinding` revival).
- Writing real `KernelTileSpec`s for `flash_attn2`/`GroupNorm` -- blocked
  on this and (for GroupNorm) teenygrad-1nr.10.
notes: Superseded by the v2 TileGraph rewrite (9b9f58b28), which deleted this implementation along with builder.rs, memory.rs, propagate.rs, search.rs and sub_graph_tiling.rs. The algorithm is being re-landed against v2 by teenygrad-1nr.25 - do not assume this code exists in the tree. Left closed because the design decisions recorded here still hold; only the code was removed.
close_reason: Implemented: TileGraph::from_dag synthesizes an unlinked secondary output edge per additional declared KernelTileSpec output; propagate now resolves every output whose edge is seeded, not just outputs[0]. Both regression tests pass.

comments.author: Arshad Mahmood
comments.text:
Reproduction test added: kernels/teeny-kernels/src/graph/optimizer/anduin/tile_graph/mod.rs::tests::propagate_ignores_every_output_but_the_first

Uses two_output_spec (Y1 names "M", Y2 names "aux"; the one input axis is
bound to "aux", matching only Y2). Confirmed failing: the input's resolved
tile is always exactly the full untiled extent (Fixed(1000)) regardless of
what's seeded, since propagate never reads outputs[1] -- asserts left != right
where both sides are Fixed(1000).

As noted in the issue, this asserts the weaker "not always the fallback"
rather than a specific correct value, since there's no second output edge on
TileGraph to seed Y2's own tile onto -- that's part of the gap itself.

comments.author: Arshad Mahmood
comments.text:
Implemented and verified.

TileGraph (tile_graph/mod.rs):
1. New field secondary_outputs: Vec<Vec<EdgeId>>, populated by from_dag.
   For a node whose tile_spec declares outputs.len() > 1, one extra
   boundary edge is synthesized per additional output (index i -> spec.
   outputs[i+1]'s edge). Every axis is an unresolved TileDim::Sym
   placeholder (no ExecutableOp::output_shape equivalent exists for a
   non-primary output). Pushed via secondary_outputs.push(...) in
   node-index order rather than indexed writes, to keep clippy's
   needless_range_loop happy on the existing multi-purpose `for index in
   0..n` loop.
2. Deliberately NOT linked into outgoing/incoming at all. Confirmed by
   inspection that children/parent_edges/input_edge_id/output_edge_id/
   extract_subgraph/boundary_edges/topological_sort are all built
   entirely on outgoing[node]/incoming[node] (never scan self.edges
   directly except topological_sort, which only counts edges with BOTH
   producer and consumer set -- secondary edges have consumer: None, so
   they're excluded there too). So these new edges are completely
   invisible to fusion/scheduling/footprint/traffic -- exactly the
   minimal, scoped blast radius the issue called for.
3. New accessor: TileGraph::secondary_output_edges(node) -> &[EdgeId].

TileGraph::propagate: after resolving the primary output (outputs[0],
unchanged -- still a hard boundary on rank mismatch, exactly as before),
now additionally loops spec.outputs[1..], and for each one whose
secondary_output_edges(node) entry has been seeded in the caller's
output_tiles map (via `tiles`), adds its axis contributions into the same
`resolved` map used for input resolution. An unseeded or rank-mismatched
secondary output simply contributes nothing -- it does NOT hard-boundary
the whole node, unlike a bad primary output. (Had to collect these into
owned Vec<Option<TileEdgeShape>> storage up front, mirroring how
`output_tile` is already owned -- a first attempt read straight from
`tiles` inline and hit a real borrow-checker conflict against `tiles.
insert(...)` later in the same node's processing.)

Tests: the original teenygrad-1nr.11 red test
(propagate_ignores_every_output_but_the_first) is replaced by two real
ones:
- propagate_resolves_a_second_declared_output_when_its_edge_is_seeded:
  seeds both Y1's primary edge and Y2's secondary edge on the same
  two_output_spec used before; asserts the input axis bound only to Y2's
  "aux" name now resolves to Y2's actual seeded value (20), not Y1's (50)
  or the full-extent fallback (1000). Passes.
- propagate_leaves_an_unseeded_second_output_without_a_full_shape_fallback:
  companion test confirming an unseeded secondary output still correctly
  falls back to full extent (1000), and doesn't hard-boundary the node.
  Passes.

Verification: cargo check --workspace (clean), ./scripts/test.sh -p
teeny-core -p teeny-kernels --lib (74 passed, 3 known pre-existing/
tracked failures -- DagCodegen todo!() stub, teenygrad-1nr.9, teenygrad-
1nr.10 -- all unrelated), cargo clippy --no-deps (0 new warnings after
restructuring the from_dag loop to avoid a needless_range_loop lint on
the new code), cargo fmt --check (clean). Also re-ran the existing
conv2d/batchnorm/silu and reduction fusion tests plus the full
Anduin::optimize test -- all unaffected, confirming this is fully
additive for every existing (single-output) tile_spec.

Not done (explicitly out of scope, matching the issue's own non-goals):
writing real KernelTileSpecs for flash_attn2/GroupNorm -- flash_attn2
still needs teenygrad-1nr.12's loop-carry support too, and GroupNorm
still needs teenygrad-1nr.10's grid-constant-subdivision support.

title: feat: revive TileLoopSpec/TileCarryBinding for loop-carried kernels (flash attention)
description:
## Correction, 2026-09-22: the types already exist

This issue's premise is stale. `TileLoopSpec` and `TileCarryBinding` are in
`core/teeny-core/src/model/tile_spec.rs` (lines 206-228), and
`KernelTileSpec::loop_spec: Option<TileLoopSpec>` is declared. They were
revived after this was filed.

What is missing is a *user*: every hand-authored spec in
`kernels/teeny-kernels/src/graph/mod.rs` carries `loop_spec: None`, and
`TileCarryBinding`'s own doc says declaring `loop_spec` *"does not by itself
fix"* propagate/mem_traffic/mem_footprint treating a loop-carried kernel's
inputs as fully materialized - *"it only makes the loop's existence and
carried shape queryable."*

So the work is: write the first real `loop_spec: Some(..)` for
`flash_attn2`, and make a consumer honour it. Validate through
`KernelTileSpec::resolve_inputs` (`teenygrad-1iy.2`) rather than waiting for
the scheduler - that is what this epic's isolation harness is for.

## Goal

`flash_attn2` forward (`kernels/teeny-kernels/src/nn/attention/flash_attn2.rs`)
runs a real online-softmax loop over K/V blocks (`for k_row in
0..n_ctx_k`), carrying `m_i`/`l_i`/an accumulator across iterations. No
`KernelTileSpec` can describe this today, at all -- not an authoring
difficulty like teenygrad-1nr.8/.10, a genuinely absent capability.
`teeny_core::model::tile_spec`'s own module doc comment says so
explicitly: `TileLoopSpec`/`TileCarryBinding` (flash-attention-style
loop-carried accumulator state, present in the original pre-revival
design) were "deliberately not revived here -- no consumer needs them
yet." This issue is that follow-up, now that a consumer (this survey)
has identified the need concretely.

Also relevant, tracked separately (teenygrad-1nr.11): `flash_attn2`
additionally has two real outputs (`o_ptr` + `l_ptr`, logsumexp) --
`propagate` couldn't consume a loop-aware spec's second output correctly
even once loop-carry itself is modeled, without that fix too. The two
gaps are independent; flash attention just happens to hit both at once.

## Why this is harder than teenygrad-1nr.7/.8/.10

Those three were all "the type can describe it, `propagate` just needs
teaching" (or, for .10, "the type needs one more field"). This one is
different in kind: `propagate`'s entire model is a single-pass,
non-iterative name-resolution walk (Fig. 6-style) over a *static* set of
axis bindings -- there's no notion of "state carried across N loop
iterations, each touching a different K/V block, whose final resolved
tile depends on how many iterations ran." Modeling it faithfully needs:

1. A way to declare a loop dimension (e.g. the K/V sequence length,
   iterated in `BLOCK_KV`-sized chunks) separately from the axes that are
   resolved once per kernel launch.
2. A way to declare which values are carried/accumulated across that
   loop (the original design's `TileCarryBinding`) versus freshly loaded
   per iteration.
3. `mem_footprint`/`mem_traffic` need to understand that a loop-carried
   accumulator's footprint is *not* the full K/V sequence length's worth
   of memory -- it's one iteration's block, resident the whole loop,
   which is the entire memory-saving point of flash attention in the
   first place. Getting this wrong (treating flash attention's inputs as
   fully materialized, like every other op today implicitly does when
   `tile_spec` is absent) would silently produce wildly pessimistic
   footprint estimates for exactly the kernel this whole scheduler is
   often most relevant for.

## No code-level regression test added

Unlike teenygrad-1nr.7/.8/.10 (fixed a real bug or extended a real,
already-present type -- reproducible by constructing an instance and
showing `propagate` misbehaves), this is a *missing type*:
`TileLoopSpec`/`TileCarryBinding` don't exist in the codebase to
construct an instance of, so there's no "red test against reality" to
write yet. The meaningful regression test is a downstream artifact of
designing and landing this feature, not something separable from it.

## Fix plan (sketch -- design, not implementation)

1. Revive `TileLoopSpec`/`TileCarryBinding` from the pre-revival design
   this whole `tile_spec.rs` module is already a revival of (see
   `kernels/teeny-triton/src/tile.rs`'s deleted history at `84ca6eedf^`,
   per this module's own doc comment) as a starting point -- check what
   shape they had there before reusing/adapting.
2. Extend `KernelTileSpec` with an optional loop description; extend
   `TileGraph::propagate` (or add a parallel loop-aware resolution path)
   to compute a loop-carried tensor's *steady-state per-iteration*
   footprint rather than a single static tile.
3. Write `FLASH_ATTN2_TILE_SPEC` (or equivalent) as the first real
   consumer/proof this works, alongside teenygrad-1nr.11's multi-output
   fix (both needed for a complete, correct flash-attention spec).

## Non-goals

- The multi-output gap itself -- teenygrad-1nr.11.
- `TileWindow`-aware propagation -- separate, already-flagged follow-up.
- Any other loop-carried kernel beyond flash attention as the motivating
  case (there may be others; not surveyed here).
close_reason: Superseded by teenygrad-1tl.11 for the declaration work. This issue's three-way split is preserved: item 1 (revive TileLoopSpec/TileCarryBinding) landed with teenygrad-1nr.18; item 2 (node-level working-set term so loop_spec reaches the cost model) is now teenygrad-1nr.31; item 3 (graph-level attention Op + lowering arm, without which any flash-attn spec is unreachable from Anduin) is now teenygrad-1nr.32.

comments.author: Arshad Mahmood
comments.text: No code-level regression test added -- explained in the issue body: TileLoopSpec/TileCarryBinding don't exist yet, so there's no type to construct an instance of and demonstrate propagate misbehaving against. The meaningful test is a downstream artifact of implementing this feature, not separable from it.

comments.author: Arshad Mahmood
comments.text:
Investigation (not implemented -- recording findings, per request).

## The original design existed and is fully recoverable

Found the exact prior implementation: commit fc5a4fb0c "feat: teenygrad-3w0.7
-- flash-attn loop-carried accumulator primitive" (10 days before the
84ca6eedf^ deletion this module's doc comment references). Full diff:

  pub struct TileCarryBinding {
      pub name: &'static str,              // e.g. "acc"
      pub shape_consts: &'static [&'static str], // e.g. ["HEAD_DIM"]
  }
  pub struct TileLoopSpec {
      pub carries: &'static [TileCarryBinding],
      pub trip_count_param: &'static str,  // e.g. "n_ctx_k"
  }
  // + KernelTileSpec gains: pub loop_spec: Option<TileLoopSpec>

Porting these two structs + the KernelTileSpec field back is genuinely
small and mechanical -- maybe 20-30 lines, plus adding `loop_spec: None`
to every existing KernelTileSpec literal (same mechanical churn as
divide_by in teenygrad-1nr.10, ~10-15 call sites). This part is low-risk
and matches the issue's own "revive from the pre-revival design" framing
exactly.

## But loop_spec was NEVER consumed, even in the original design

Checked every commit touching kernels/teeny-triton/src/tile.rs across the
whole history (git log -p, grepped for loop_spec/TileLoopSpec/TileCarryBinding
in every diff): it's constructed, and asserted on in one test
(flash_attention2_forward_tile_spec_declares_loop_carry_only), and that's
it. propagate_within_kernel (teenygrad-3w0.8, the original Propagate) sets
`loop_spec: None` in every one of its own constructed specs and never reads
the field. CostModel's shared-memory capacity term (teenygrad-3w0.4) doesn't
reference it either. So "reviving" the type is not "restoring behavior that
used to work" -- the original codebase itself never got past declaring the
metadata. Every consumer still needs to be designed from scratch; there's no
prior art to port for that part.

## The original design left q_ptr/k_ptr/v_ptr/o_ptr/l_ptr *completely
untagged* -- no TensorTileSpec at all

From the same commit's own doc comment: "HEAD_DIM-wide loads are
compile-time-fixed, not a grid-varying tile, so #[tile(...)] doesn't apply
to them either." Confirmed by the test: `spec.inputs.len() == 0`,
`spec.outputs.len() == 0`. All the interesting metadata lived in loop_spec
alone.

This changes teenygrad-1nr.11's relevance: I'd assumed a real flash_attn2
spec would need o_ptr+l_ptr as two real TensorTileSpec outputs (motivating
teenygrad-1nr.11's fix). The original design's own precedent says
otherwise -- it deliberately left every pointer untagged and relied
entirely on loop_spec. teenygrad-1nr.11 is still real (GroupNorm's three
real Out params are a genuine, unrelated case for it), but may not
actually be a hard prerequisite for *this* issue the way I'd previously
implied.

## The *current* flash_attention2_forward kernel has no block-tiled K/V
loop at all -- nothing for a scheduler to search over

Re-read the current (not deleted) kernel
(kernels/teeny-kernels/src/nn/attention/flash_attn2.rs:57-137). Grid is
`(N_CTX_Q, BH, 1)` -- one CTA per (batch_head, single q row), no BLOCK_M
tiling of Q either. The k_row loop is `for k_row in 0..n_ctx_k` -- one row
at a time, no BLOCK_KV/BLOCK_N const generic anywhere in the signature.
This is not the block-tiled K/V-loop flash-attention algorithm a
`TileLoopSpec`-driven `enumerate_subtiles` search would have anything to
vary for; the loop's trip count is just the full n_ctx_k, hardcoded. So
even a fully-wired TileLoopSpec wouldn't feed a *search* here (there's no
block-size choice to make) -- its only possible value is *cost-model
accuracy*: telling mem_footprint/mem_traffic the real per-CTA working set
is O(HEAD_DIM) (acc/m_i/l_i), not O(N_CTX x HEAD_DIM) (what an untagged
node's full-shape fallback would otherwise imply if q/k/v ever *did* get
TensorTileSpecs).

## Loop carries aren't edges -- they don't fit TileGraph's edge-keyed cost
model at all

acc/m_i/l_i are kernel-body-local variables, never materialized as a
TileEdge (they never cross a pointer parameter). mem_footprint_with_config/
mem_traffic_with_config are both entirely EdgeId-keyed (TileConfig ==
HashMap<EdgeId, TileEdgeShape>). There is currently no notion of "extra
per-CTA working-set bytes not tied to any edge" anywhere in the cost
model. Consuming loop_spec for anything beyond documentation needs a
genuinely new cost-model term/API (e.g. a node-level "resident working
set" contribution added into sub_graph_tiling's capacity check
alongside the edge-based footprint) -- not just a hook into existing
mem_footprint/mem_traffic, which have nowhere to put this today.

## Flash attention isn't reachable from the graph/Anduin pipeline at all
today

grepped teeny_core::graph::Op and TritonLowering's match arms: there is no
Op variant for flash/scaled-dot-product attention, and no lowering case
for it. TileGraph::from_dag only ever sees Dag<Box<dyn ExecutableOp>> nodes
TritonLowering produced from a graph-level Op. So even a complete, fully-
wired FLASH_ATTN2_TILE_SPEC has nowhere to attach today -- there's no
Op::-level node for Anduin/TileGraph to ever see in the first place. Adding
one (a new Op variant + TritonLowering match arm) is a separate, unrelated
addition to the graph/lowering layer, not a tile-spec/scheduling change,
and not something this issue's own scope (or teenygrad-1nr's) currently
covers.

## Revised understanding: this is really three separable pieces, not one

1. Revive TileCarryBinding/TileLoopSpec + KernelTileSpec.loop_spec --
   small, safe, mechanical, zero behavior change (matches the original's
   own scope, which never went further than this). Doable in isolation.
2. Design + implement a real cost-model consumer for loop_spec (the
   "resident working set, not edge-keyed" extension) -- genuinely new,
   no prior art, needs its own design pass and probably its own issue.
3. Add an Op variant + TritonLowering lowering case for
   flash/scaled-dot-product attention so it's reachable from
   Anduin/TileGraph at all -- unrelated to tile-spec modeling, blocks any
   real spec regardless of (1)/(2), arguably its own issue entirely
   outside teenygrad-1nr's scope (graph/lowering, not scheduling).

Recommend splitting into these before picking any of it up for real --
(1) is a reasonable follow-up on its own merits (metadata parity with the
pre-revival design, unblocks nothing by itself but costs little), (2) and
(3) are each substantial enough to want their own tracked scope and
probably their own reproduction/test strategy once picked up. Leaving
teenygrad-1nr.12 open; not implementing any of this now per the request
that started this investigation.

comments.author: Arshad Mahmood
comments.text:
Item 1 from this issue's own "revised understanding" (revive TileCarryBinding/TileLoopSpec + KernelTileSpec.loop_spec, mechanical/safe) is done, as part of teenygrad-1nr.18 -- see that issue's progress comment for the diff. One deliberate deviation from the sketch here: `trip_count_param: &'static str` became `trip_count_factors: &'static [&'static str]`, since the first real consumer (conv2d's `(C_IN/G)*KH*KW`) isn't a single named param the way flash-attn's `n_ctx_k` would be -- it mixes a runtime param with consts. `CONV2D_TILE_SPEC` now carries a real `loop_spec` (`acc: [BLOCK_OW]`, `trip_count_factors: ["C_IN","G","KH","KW"]`) as the first real usage.

Items 2 (cost-model consumer) and 3 (flash-attn Op variant + lowering) are still untouched, per this issue's own recommendation to split them out -- still open.

title: feat: KernelTileSpecs for the padding family (Constant/Reflection/Replication/Circular × 1d/2d/3d)
description:
## Goal

All 12 padding kernels (`ConstantPad`/`ReflectionPad`/`ReplicationPad`/
`CircularPad` × `1d`/`2d`/`3d`, `kernels/teeny-kernels/src/nn/pad/*.rs`)
have no `KernelTileSpec` yet. Confirmed by reading every one of their real
signatures: they are structurally identical to the pooling family
(`windowed_last_axis_tile_spec`, just landed) -- `input_ptr`/`output_ptr`,
grid decodes to `(b, c[, d[, h]], ow-tile)`, only the innermost spatial
axis is genuinely block-tiled (`BLOCK_OL` for 1d, `BLOCK_OW` for 2d/3d),
everything else (batch, channels, outer spatial axes) is grid-driven.
E.g. `constant_pad2d_forward<T, D, const PT, PB, PL, PR, BLOCK_OW>(input_ptr,
output_ptr, _B, C, H, W, OH, OW)`.

This is not a new design question -- it's the exact same shape already
solved for `Conv1d`/`2d`/`3d` and `AvgPool`/`MaxPool`/`LpPool`
`1d`/`2d`/`3d` (teenygrad-1nr's broad annotation sweep). Filed as its own
issue rather than folded into that sweep only because it wasn't reached
in the same pass, not because it's harder.

## Fix plan

Reuse the existing `windowed_last_axis_tile_spec(rank, block_const,
extent_param, input_param, output_param)` helper
(`kernels/teeny-kernels/src/graph/mod.rs`) exactly as already done for
the pooling family -- one call per op, wired into each `Op::*Pad*`
match arm the same way (`let mut exec = make_num_kernel!(...); exec.tile_spec
= Some(windowed_last_axis_tile_spec(rank, "BLOCK_O{L,W}", "O{L,W}",
"input_ptr", "output_ptr")); exec`):

- `ConstantPad1d`/`ReflectionPad1d`/`ReplicationPad1d`/`CircularPad1d`:
  rank 3, `BLOCK_OL`/`"OL"`.
- `ConstantPad2d`/`ReflectionPad2d`/`ReplicationPad2d`/`CircularPad2d`:
  rank 4, `BLOCK_OW`/`"OW"`.
- `ConstantPad3d`/`ReflectionPad3d`/`ReplicationPad3d`/`CircularPad3d`:
  rank 5, `BLOCK_OW`/`"OW"`.

No new type/mechanism needed. Verify each real kernel signature isn't
just structurally similar but *actually* input_ptr/output_ptr/rank/axis
as expected before wiring (spot-checked `constant_pad2d_forward`/
`reflection_pad2d_forward`/`replication_pad2d_forward`/
`circular_pad2d_forward`/`constant_pad1d_forward`/`constant_pad3d_forward`
already -- all confirmed identical shape; the remaining 6 weren't
individually re-read but follow the same file-naming/doc-comment
convention as every other kernel family checked this session).

## Non-goals

- Any other still-missing op family (normalization row-reduction ops,
  `Softmax`, `ReduceSum`-style reduction ops) -- tracked separately.
close_reason: Implemented: all 12 padding ops wired to windowed_last_axis_tile_spec, reusing the pooling family's helper unchanged. Verified via cargo check/test/clippy/fmt.
