title: feat: KernelTileSpecs for whole-row-reduction ops (LayerNorm/InstanceNorm/RmsNorm/Softmax)
description:
## Goal

`LayerNorm`, `InstanceNorm1d`/`2d`/`3d`, `RmsNorm`, and `Softmax` all have
no `KernelTileSpec`. Read each real kernel this session:

- `layer_norm_forward_inference<T, D, const BLOCK_N>(x_ptr, y_ptr,
  weight_ptr, bias_ptr, _M, N, eps)` -- grid `[M]`, one CTA per row,
  `BLOCK_N` covers the reduced axis `N`. Single output --
  `graph/mod.rs` dispatches `LayerNormForwardInferenceRuntimeOp`, the
  correct single-output inference variant (confirmed via `graph/mod.rs`
  line ~1528).
- `instance_norm_forward_inference<T, D, const BLOCK_L>(x_ptr, y_ptr,
  weight_ptr, bias_ptr, _N, C, L, eps)` -- same shape, `BLOCK_L` over `L`.
  Single output -- `graph/mod.rs` dispatches `InstanceNormForwardInference`
  (line ~1576), also correctly the single-output variant.
- `softmax_forward<T, D, const BLOCK_SIZE>(x_ptr, y_ptr, _n_rows, n_cols)`
  -- same shape, simplest of the four (no weight/bias at all).
- `rms_norm_forward<T, D, const BLOCK_N>(x_ptr, y_ptr, weight_ptr,
  rrms_ptr, _M, N, eps)` -- **different from the other three**:
  `graph/mod.rs` dispatches plain `RmsNormForward` (line ~1568), not an
  inference-only variant, so it has a real second output (`rrms_ptr`)
  unconditionally. Worth a separate look at whether an inference-only
  `RmsNorm` variant should exist (mirroring `LayerNorm`/`InstanceNorm`'s
  choice) before or alongside writing its tile spec -- flagged here, not
  resolved.

## The real open question (not just "which axis to tile")

All four reduce over the *entire* row/instance in one CTA -- there's no
grid-driven loop chunking `N`/`L`/`n_cols` the way pooling/conv chunk
their spatial axis across multiple CTAs. `BLOCK_N`/`BLOCK_L`/`BLOCK_SIZE`
has to be `>= N` (or a power of two covering it) for the reduction to be
correct in one pass -- unlike `BLOCK_OW` in the conv/pool family, where a
smaller candidate genuinely produces a smaller, still-valid output tile.

This matters for `TileGraph::enumerate_subtiles`'s power-of-two ladder:
declaring `N`'s axis as an ordinary `TileAxisBinding` would let the
search try candidates smaller than `N`, which may not correspond to
anything the real kernel can produce (the whole-row assumption baked
into the loop body) -- the same *kind* of "candidate doesn't correspond
to a real kernel configuration" gap teenygrad-1nr.9 fixed for flattened
axes, but here it isn't about flattening, it's about a hard minimum-size
floor on one axis. Needs deciding before writing a spec that could
otherwise mislead `enumerate_subtiles`/`sub_graph_tiling`'s search into
capacity-checking a tile the kernel can't actually materialize.

## Fix plan (sketch)

1. Confirm (read the kernel body, not just the signature) whether
   `BLOCK_N < N` is genuinely invalid for these kernels, or whether it's
   masked/handled some other way that makes a smaller candidate safe.
2. If a hard `>= N` floor is confirmed, either: (a) still declare the
   axis normally and accept the search may try invalid-but-harmless
   candidates (`propagate`/`mem_footprint` would just report a footprint
   for a config the real kernel would reject -- not silently wrong, just
   a wasted/misleading search entry), or (b) extend the tile-spec model
   with an explicit "minimum extent" concept the search must respect
   (a new, small addition, narrower than `divide_by`/`dims` but
   conceptually similar in spirit -- teenygrad-1nr.10's own precedent).
3. Write `LAYERNORM_TILE_SPEC`/`INSTANCENORM_TILE_SPEC`/`SOFTMAX_TILE_SPEC`
   (single input/output each, matching `RELU_TILE_SPEC`'s shape-preserving
   pattern but rank-2, `[M, N]`/`[N, C, L]`/`[n_rows, n_cols]`) once (1)/(2)
   are resolved. `RmsNorm` needs teenygrad-1nr.11's multi-output mechanism
   too (already implemented, just needs wiring) given its real `rrms_ptr`
   output, or a resolution to the inference-variant question above first.

## Non-goals

- Changing which kernel variant `graph/mod.rs` dispatches for `RmsNorm`
  -- flagged as worth a look, not decided or implemented here.
- `GroupNorm` -- tracked separately (teenygrad-1nr.10), different shape
  of problem (grid-subdivided axis, not whole-row).
- `ReduceSum`-style reduction ops -- tracked separately, a different
  (rank-changing input/output) problem.
close_reason: Superseded by teenygrad-1tl.8, which covers LayerNorm/InstanceNorm/RmsNorm/BatchNorm/softmax plus GroupNorm in one rung, since reduction_axis, divide_by and flattened dims all land together there.

title: feat: write the real GROUPNORM_TILE_SPEC (combines divide_by + flattened dims + multi-output)
description:
## Goal

`Op::GroupNorm` still has no `KernelTileSpec`. The two mechanisms it
needs are both implemented (teenygrad-1nr.10, teenygrad-1nr.11), but
never combined or tried together against the real `group_norm_forward`
kernel:

- `group_norm_forward`'s real per-CTA tile spans
  `channels_per_group * L` where `channels_per_group = C / G` --
  `L` and the channel subdivision are read *jointly* in one
  `BLOCK_NL`-wide flattened loop (`nn::norm::groupnorm.rs`), unlike
  teenygrad-1nr.10's own reproduction test, which deliberately modeled
  the channel axis and `L` as two *separate* `TileAxisBinding`s (matching
  the shape the fix's regression test needed, not the real kernel's true
  joint flattening). Combining `TileAxisBinding::dims` (multi-dim
  flattening, teenygrad-1nr.8/.9) with `divide_by` (teenygrad-1nr.10) on
  the *same* binding -- one axis whose `dims` spans channels *and* `L`,
  where the channels portion is additionally divided by `G` -- has never
  been implemented or tested. `apply_divide_by`
  (`tile_graph/mod.rs`) only ever divides the *whole* resolved/fallback
  value on the innermost dim; it has no notion of "divide by `G` before
  folding into a multi-dim product."
- `group_norm_forward` has three real outputs (`y_ptr`/`mean_ptr`/
  `rstd_ptr`) -- teenygrad-1nr.11's `secondary_output_edges` mechanism
  covers this structurally, but has never been exercised on a spec that
  *also* uses `divide_by`/multi-dim `dims` at the same time.

## Fix plan (sketch)

1. Design how `divide_by` and multi-dim `dims` compose on one binding:
   most likely, the combined ladder's extent should be computed as
   `(channels_extent / G) * L_extent` rather than the current
   `apply_divide_by`-after-the-fact approach, meaning
   `search_axes_for`/`propagate`'s combined-extent computation
   (`tile_graph/mod.rs`) needs to apply `divide_by` *per-dim*, before
   taking the product, not just to the final resolved/fallback value.
   Needs its own regression test proving `channels_per_group * L`
   resolves correctly as one joint quantity, not two independent ones.
2. Write `GROUPNORM_TILE_SPEC` using the result: `x_ptr`/`y_ptr` (shape-
   preserving, `..X` like `BATCHNORM2D_TILE_SPEC`) plus `mean_ptr`/
   `rstd_ptr` as the two secondary outputs (`KernelTileSpec.outputs`
   entries 1/2).
3. Wire into `Op::GroupNorm`'s match arm (`graph/mod.rs`), same pattern
   as `BATCHNORM2D_TILE_SPEC`.
4. Verify against a real `conv2d -> groupnorm -> silu`-style fusion test
   (mirroring `conv2d_batchnorm_silu_schedule_...`), confirming the
   schedule doesn't regress and the new spec's numbers are sane (no
   footprint larger than `C * L`, the pre-fix full-shape fallback).

## Non-goals

- Changing `apply_divide_by`'s existing single-dim behavior (BatchNorm2d/
  the standalone `groupnorm_shaped_spec` test fixture must keep passing
  unchanged).
- Any other still-missing op family -- tracked separately
  (teenygrad-1nr.13 padding, teenygrad-1nr.14 row-reduction norms,
  and the reduction-op issue for `ReduceSum`-style ops).
close_reason: Superseded by teenygrad-1tl.8. Carried over: this issue's own framing -- that .10 and .11's mechanisms were built but never combined against the real kernel -- is why divide_by, reduction_axis and flattened dims are deliberately on one rung. Also recorded there: divide_by is fixed at spec-construction time while GroupNorm's G is a runtime parameter, so its tile_spec() must be built per instance, and the generated-spec route may not express that at all.

title: feat: TensorTileSpec can't express rank-changing input/output (ReduceSum-style reductions)
description:
## Goal

`ReduceSum`/`ReduceMean`/`ReduceSumSquare`/etc. (`nn::tensor::reduction.rs`)
have no `KernelTileSpec`, and unlike every op tagged so far, no existing
spec shape actually fits them.

`reduce_sum_forward<T, D, const BLOCK_INNER>(x_ptr, y_ptr, n_inner,
n_outer)`: the real kernel reshapes its input to `[n_outer, n_inner]` and
reduces the inner axis away entirely -- `y_ptr`'s real rank is *one less*
than `x_ptr`'s (e.g. reducing over the last axis of a `[2048, 4096]`
tensor produces a `[2048]` output). Every `KernelTileSpec` written so far
(`RELU_TILE_SPEC`-style flat elementwise, `MATMUL_TILE_SPEC`,
`BATCHNORM2D_TILE_SPEC`, the conv/pool family) has input and output at
the *same* rank -- `TensorTileSpec::rank` is declared independently per
tensor, so nothing structurally prevents `inputs[0].rank != outputs[0].rank`,
but `TileGraph::propagate`'s axis-resolution logic has never been
exercised with that combination, and this codebase's graph-level `Shape`
model for the reduction *output* itself needs checking: does
`Op::ReduceSum`'s own declared output shape actually drop the reduced
axis, or keep it at extent 1 (`keepdims`-style)? `Op::ReduceSum` has a
`keepdims: bool` field -- the `false` case (used throughout this
session's own test graphs, e.g. `two_pointwise_then_reduction_..._preserves_chain`)
genuinely drops the axis (confirmed: that test's `reduced_shape` has one
fewer dim than `shape`).

## Why this needs more than "just write ReduceSum's TensorTileSpec"

1. **Which real axis does the reduced dim correspond to, on either side?**
   `x_ptr`'s `n_inner`/`n_outer` are the kernel's *own* flattened view --
   the doc comment (found via the earlier kernel survey, teenygrad-1nr.9's
   own predecessor investigation) says the caller reshapes input to
   `[n_outer, n_inner]` before the kernel sees it, which the module doc
   comment flagged as unclear for a *non-trailing*-axis reduction (may
   need a transpose upstream that isn't representable in `tile_spec` at
   all -- a graph-lowering question, not a tile-spec one).
2. **`TileAxisBinding::dims` indexes are per-tensor**, but nothing in
   `propagate` currently maps "input axis N was reduced away, so output
   axis N doesn't exist, output axis N+1 onward shift down by one" --
   every existing spec's axes on different tensors either share the same
   real dim count (BatchNorm2d) or have entirely disjoint dim spaces
   (GEMM's A/B/C, each their own rank-2). A reduction needs an explicit
   mapping between "this input dim" and "this (differently-indexed)
   output dim" that doesn't exist as a concept anywhere in `TensorTileSpec`
   today.
3. **`reduction_axis: Option<usize>`** already exists on `TensorTileSpec`
   (used by `MATMUL_TILE_SPEC`'s `K`) but is documentation-only -- not
   read by `propagate` (confirmed via the same grep sweep that found
   `untiled_dims`/`window` inert before their respective fixes). Whether
   reviving it is *part* of the fix here, or a separate concern, needs
   deciding.

## Fix plan

Not designed here -- needs its own investigation pass (mirroring how
teenygrad-1nr.12's flash-attention investigation was scoped) before any
implementation: read `reduce_sum_forward`'s real body plus every other
`nn::tensor::reduction.rs` kernel, confirm the exact axis-index mapping
`TritonLowering` produces for `Op::ReduceSum`'s real (input, output) edge
shapes, and decide whether `TensorTileSpec` needs a new field (e.g. an
explicit per-axis input-to-output dim mapping) or whether `reduction_axis`
alone, finally consumed, is enough.

## Non-goals

- `Softmax`'s own internal reduction (it doesn't change rank -- output
  shape equals input shape -- tracked separately, teenygrad-1nr.14, as
  a same-rank whole-row-reduction case, structurally simpler than this).
- Any other still-missing op family -- tracked separately.
notes:
DECISION (teenygrad-1tl.9, PR pending): option 1 -- the fallback is genuinely
correct and no change to TensorTileSpec is needed. This issue was closed at P3
with a fix plan that still read "not designed here"; this is the decision it
asked for.

## The premise was wrong

This issue recorded that TensorTileSpec "cannot express a rank-changing
input/output pair". It can. The investigation this issue specified -- read
reduce_sum_forward's body and every other reduction.rs kernel, then decide
whether a new field is needed -- was done, and a hand-built spec of exactly
that shape resolves correctly:

  output tile [4]  ->  input [Some(4), None]

x is [n_outer, n_inner] rank 2, y is [n_outer] rank 1. The reduced axis has no
counterpart in the output, so it has no binding, and an axis with no binding
keeps its full extent. That is the TRUTH here, not a degenerate fallback: one
output row needs its whole input row. Name matching on n_outer carries the
block across the rank change.

## The secondary worry was overstated

"For a full reduction that is the entire tensor, which is correct but makes the
spec worthless for footprint." Only when n_outer == 1. These kernels use a
generic (outer, inner) decomposition, so a full reduction is just that case,
and the input tile genuinely IS the whole tensor. That is the cost model
correctly learning a full reduction cannot be tiled on its inner axis --
useful, not worthless.

## Consumer contract worth knowing

The reduced axis stays None even when the ConstLookup supplies n_inner, because
resolve_inputs only visits bound axes (same as GEMM's K, teenygrad-2sd1). A
footprint consumer must read None as "full extent" itself.

## Also settled

cum_sum/cum_prod were expected to be a route-3 reason. They are declarable:
rank-preserving, inner axis untiled on BOTH sides, which is how the spec says
the prefix dependency makes it untileable. The reason itself lives in a source
comment, since "untiled" says that an axis is not tiled, not why.
close_reason: Superseded by teenygrad-1tl.9, which covers the reduce_* family, the global pools and the cumulative scans. This issue's finding -- that TensorTileSpec cannot relate an input axis to 'no output axis' -- is carried over there as the decision the rung has to make: either the full-extent fallback is correct and should be stated, or the type needs changing.

title: feat: determine a fused virtual node's grid when constituent ops have incompatible native grids
description:
## Goal

Given a `VirtualNode` (`TraceEvent::VirtualNode`, `anduin/trace.rs`) --
several original DAG nodes `schedule_graph` decided to fuse into one
kernel launch -- there is currently no mechanism, and no design, for
determining *the grid* (CTA count/shape) that fused kernel launches with.

## Current state: every op computes its own grid independently, and they
don't agree

Every `RuntimeOp` implementation has its own `fn grid(&self, output_shape:
&[usize]) -> [u32; 3]` (`core/teeny-core/src/model/mod.rs:160`), computed
purely from that op's own real output shape and whatever `BLOCK_*` consts
got baked in at construction -- entirely independent of any other op,
because today every kernel is launched separately. Checked three real
kernels this session, all structurally different:

- `conv2d_forward`: flat 1-D `pid`, manually decoded into `(b, c_out, oh,
  ow_tile)`.
- `batch_norm_2d_nchw_forward_inference`: genuine 2-D grid `[C, B]` --
  channel on Axis::X, batch on Axis::Y.
- `silu_forward` (and every flat elementwise op, teenygrad-1nr's
  `flat_elementwise_tile_spec` sweep): flat 1-D `pid` over
  `n_elements / BLOCK_SIZE`, no `(b, c, h, w)` decomposition at all.

For the real, already-passing fusion test
(`conv2d_batchnorm_silu_schedule_fuses_the_three_compute_nodes_apart_from_input`),
`schedule_graph` groups exactly these three into one `SharedMemory`-level
`VirtualNode` -- but their three grids above don't correspond to the same
iteration space at all. There is no way to launch "one kernel" that is
simultaneously conv2d's `(b, c_out, oh, ow_tile)` grid, batchnorm2d's
`(c, b)` grid, and silu's flat element-block grid, without picking one as
the *anchor* and rewriting the other two's per-CTA index arithmetic to
derive the same logical tile position from the anchor's `pid` instead of
each independently calling `T::program_id`.

## Relationship to teenygrad-1nr.1

teenygrad-1nr.1 ("Rework `#[tiled_kernel]` API to compose `Tile<D>`
functions") already identifies the adjacent half of this problem --
"`program_id` doesn't compose today... the wrapper owns pid decode... the
composed functions must receive their tile position... instead of calling
`T::program_id` themselves" -- but its own text never says *which* op's
grid shape the wrapper's pid decode should be, or how the other fused
ops' differing natural grids get reconciled onto it. This issue is that
missing piece: teenygrad-1nr.1 solves *how a composed function receives*
a tile position once one is chosen; this issue is about *choosing* it
(and reindexing every non-anchor op's per-tile access pattern to match).

## Open questions (not resolved here)

1. **Which fused op is the anchor?** The one with no consumer inside the
   group (matches Welder's own model -- the group's boundary *output*
   edge's shape drives the grid, since every fused op must produce
   exactly enough of its own tile to feed the next), or something else
   (largest tensor, most CTAs, etc.)?
2. **How does a non-anchor op's per-tile index arithmetic get rederived
   from the anchor's `pid`?** Conv2d's own `(b, c_out, oh, ow_tile)`
   decode and batchnorm2d's own `(c, b)` decode don't share axes 1:1 --
   reconciling them needs an explicit mapping from the anchor's logical
   coordinates to each fused op's own real tensor coordinates, which
   nothing in `TileGraph`/`SubGraphTilingResult`/`TileConfig` represents
   today (those carry *shapes*, not *index/offset expressions*).
3. **Does `SubGraphTilingResult`'s existing `config: TileConfig` (resolved
   boundary-edge shapes) already carry enough information**, or does
   `DagCodegen`/`Trace::trace_graph`'s `VirtualNode`/`Allocate`/
   `LoadTiles`/`ComputeTile`/`StoreTiles` sequence need a new field
   (e.g. the chosen grid dimensions, or an explicit anchor `NodeId`) to
   avoid recomputing this from scratch at codegen time?
4. **Does every fused group even get a *single* grid**, or can a virtual
   node legitimately need more than one CTA per "logical tile" for some
   fused ops (e.g. a reduction inside the group needing extra CTAs along
   a reduction axis the anchor's own grid doesn't have)? Not yet
   surveyed against a fusion group containing a reduction op.

## Non-goals

- Implementing any of this -- investigation/design only, mirroring how
  teenygrad-1nr.12 (flash attention) was scoped: recorded, not built.
- The `Tile<D>` value-passing mechanism itself (shared-memory round-trip
  via `shared_alloc`/`shared_store_index`/etc.) -- already scoped under
  teenygrad-1nr.1, unaffected by this issue.
- `DagCodegen`'s own implementation -- still blocked on teenygrad-1nr.1
  regardless of how this issue resolves; this issue is about what
  `DagCodegen` (or whatever the codegen pass will look like) needs to
  *compute*, not about implementing that pass.
close_reason: Closed together with the teenygrad-1nr epic (Welder-style TileGraph scheduler)

comments.author: Arshad Mahmood
comments.text:
Read Welder's own §4.1 "Decide aligned computation parallelism" and §4.2
"Code Generation and Compilation" (osdi23-shi.pdf, pp. 707-708) -- this
directly answers (and partially reframes) the open questions above.

## Welder's actual mechanism (not "pick an anchor op")

1. Common thread-block size via GCD, not one operator's grid winning:
   "we determine the greatest common divisor among the tile numbers of all
   operators as the common thread-block size, if it is larger than the
   hardware parallelism (e.g., 128) and less than the maximum limitation
   (e.g., 1024)." Every operator's own tiles get bound to that shared
   thread pool ("we bind all operator-tiles at the register level to
   these threads").
2. TVM virtual threads absorb the remainder: "If a single thread needs to
   run multiple tiles, we use TVM's virtual thread to bind them, thus
   allowing concurrent data access over all memory banks and avoiding
   bank conflicts" -- i.e. when an operator has more tiles than the
   common count, that thread serializes over its extras, rather than
   forcing every operator to an identical tile count.
3. Register-level vs. shared-memory-level fusion use genuinely different
   mechanisms:
   - Register level: TVM's `compute_inline` schedule primitive --
     structural inlining, no separate kernel boundary at all.
   - Shared-memory level: Welder generates *separate standalone kernels*
     per connected part first, then composes them: rewrites each one's
     global-memory load/store into shared-memory accesses (adding fences
     for races, padding for bank conflicts), producing a "device
     function" folded into the final fused kernel.
4. Explicit blockIdx/threadIdx remapping between composed kernels:
   "Some operators cannot be directly connected to others and require
   remapping of their blockIdx and threadIdx values... The remapping
   relationship is deduced from their tensor expressions." ThreadIdx
   remapping specifically connects 2D thread blocks to 1D ones when one
   fused operator needs inter-thread reduction/TensorCore (2D,
   threadIdx.x + threadIdx.y) and another doesn't (1D, threadIdx.x
   only) -- valid as long as the total thread count matches.
5. Shared memory across the whole fused group (not just each kernel's
   own) is managed uniformly via liveness analysis over topological
   execution order -> alloc/free sequence -> best-fit offset assignment,
   respecting alignment (e.g. 32B for TensorCore).

## The real dependency this reveals

Point 4 is doing the actual hard work, and it isn't a standalone
algorithm portable on its own -- "deduced from their tensor expressions"
means Welder leans on TVM's symbolic compute-graph representation (every
operator is a TVM tensor expression the scheduler can introspect and
re-derive an index mapping for automatically). This codebase's kernels
are hand-written Rust functions with `T::program_id` calls baked directly
into the body -- there is no symbolic tensor-expression layer to deduce a
remapping from. Porting "compute a GCD-based common thread count" (points
1-2 above) is straightforward once teenygrad-1nr.1's Tile<D> composition
exists. Porting point 4 (or an equivalent) is not just an algorithm port
-- it needs either (a) building an equivalent symbolic-expression layer
this codebase doesn't have at all, or (b) a different, more constrained
approach specific to this codebase's real kernel shapes (e.g. hand-derived
remapping rules per op-pair, or restricting fusion to op combinations
whose grids are trivially reconcilable without remapping -- matching
grid dimensionality/axis order already).

Updated understanding of the 4 open questions above:
- Q1 (which op anchors the grid) -- answered: none does: the common
  thread count is derived from all of them (GCD), not any single one's
  native grid.
- Q2 (how does a non-anchor op's index arithmetic get rederived) --
  answered in principle (blockIdx/threadIdx remapping "deduced from
  tensor expressions"), but the *mechanism* Welder uses to deduce it
  isn't available in this codebase and would need its own design.
- Q3 (does SubGraphTilingResult/TileConfig carry enough info) -- no:
  neither the GCD-based common thread count nor any remapping
  relationship is represented anywhere in TileGraph/SubGraphTilingResult/
  TileConfig today; both would need new fields/passes.
- Q4 (does every fused group get one grid) -- refined: yes, one common
  thread-block size, but individual operators can still need more tiles
  than that count (handled via virtual threads, not a second grid).

comments.author: Arshad Mahmood
comments.text:
Checked the actual Welder source (../Welder, python/welder/) against the paper text and a document the user separately wrote analyzing Welder-TVM integration. Corrects/sharpens the "deduced from tensor expressions" line from the previous comment: it isn't one mechanism, it's two, cleanly split by fusion level.

## Register-level fusion: schedule/te_elementwise.py:9-39

Every non-output op in the fused group gets `sch[op].compute_inline()` -- literally substituted as a pure TE expression into the output op's compute body. Grid/block/vthread/thread axes are then split *only* off `sch[out].op.axis` (the single output tensor's own axes: `bx, _t = sch[out].split(axis, factor=config.block[i])` etc.), then `bind`-ed to blockIdx.x/vthread/threadIdx.x. This is where "grid computed from final output only" (the shape of claim in the user's own doc, and a common informal description of Welder) is actually true -- but only because `compute_inline` never gives the intermediate op its own grid to reconcile against in the first place. TVM's tensor-expression system automatically rewrites the intermediate's index arguments in terms of the output's iteration variables as part of inlining; there's nothing left to remap.

This is NOT portable to this codebase directly: it depends on kernels being pure, symbolically-composable index expressions (TVM TE), not hand-written procedural Rust with baked-in `T::program_id()` calls and side-effecting loads/stores.

## Shared-memory-level fusion: IRpass/rewrite_output_pass.py, rewrite_input_pass.py

This is the part that stays genuinely hard, and it is NOT a formula -- it's two TIR-level statement-rewrite passes:

1. Each connected sub-part is first scheduled and *lowered as if it were its own standalone kernel*, with its own real blockIdx.x binding (own grid).
2. `remove_blockIdx` (identical helper duplicated in both pass files) walks the already-lowered TIR body and substitutes every `blockIdx.*` Var to the constant `0` -- because the sub-kernel is no longer independently launched; it becomes a per-thread-block subroutine of the *outer* fused kernel's grid.
3. `remap_ndim` (rewrite_output_pass.py:63-71) explicitly decomposes a flat linear index back into the sub-kernel's own N-D buffer offset using that sub-kernel's own `tile_shape`/strides -- shape metadata carried over from the Python-level scheduling config, not derived symbolically at the TIR level.
4. RewriteInputPass does the mirror-image job on the consumer side: BufferLoad indices referencing a shared-input tensor get the same blockIdx-zeroing (`remove_blockIdx`, duplicated again), and redundant BufferStores to what's now a shared-memory-staged tensor get replaced with `tir.Evaluate(0)` (elided, since the producing sub-kernel's own pass already emitted the real store).

So "deduced from tensor expressions" (paper's own phrase) really means: schedule each part independently first, lower each to TIR, then run these two statement-substitution passes over the *lowered* IR using shape/stride metadata already known from scheduling -- not a general symbolic-graph inference step.

## Why this matters for this codebase specifically

The shared-memory-level mechanism operates on a *lowered IR's* statements (TIR BufferLoad/BufferStore/blockIdx variables), driven by already-known shape/stride metadata -- not by parsing source or re-deriving a symbolic graph from scratch. We already confirmed (session investigation, ../teeny/compiler/rustc_mlir/src/triton/*) that this codebase's kernels genuinely lower to real MLIR Triton-dialect ops (`tt.get_program_id`, `tt.load`, `tt.store`, built via `rustc_mlir/src/triton/tensor.rs`'s `OperationBuilder` calls). That means an *analogous* post-lowering MLIR pass is architecturally available here in a way hand-parsing Rust AST/MIR never was: schedule/lower each fused op's kernel body independently first (each with its own `tt.get_program_id` call), then run a pass that (a) substitutes a composed sub-kernel's `tt.get_program_id` results with a constant/derived-from-outer-grid value, and (b) rewrites its load/store index arithmetic using its own known tile shape/strides -- the direct MLIR analog of RewriteOutputPass/RewriteInputPass's `remove_blockIdx`/`remap_ndim`.

This is a materially better port target than either (a) building a from-scratch symbolic tensor-expression layer (previous comment's pessimistic conclusion) or (b) the constrained named-axis fusion-legality gate proposed as a stopgap -- it's a real, scoped, IR-level rewrite pass with a working precedent to copy the shape of, not an open research problem. Still non-trivial (needs each fused op's kernel body lowered separately first, before composition, which is its own design question against how `DagCodegen`/`Trace::trace_graph`'s VirtualNode sequencing works today) -- but it's the first port target in this whole investigation that isn't blocked on infrastructure this codebase fundamentally lacks.

Also worth flagging: the "single ceil(final_output/blockDim) formula, works for any fusion combination" claim in the separately-reviewed document is only true for the register-level/compute_inline case above; it does not hold for the shared-memory-level case, where each part still gets scheduled with its own axes/threads before blockIdx gets zeroed out post-hoc. Not portable as a general rule.

Still investigation/design only -- nothing implemented.

comments.author: Arshad Mahmood
comments.text:
Added the simplest test that shows the issue directly, rather than by inference from reading kernel source: `conv2d_batchnorm_silu_fused_group_has_no_single_compatible_grid` in kernels/teeny-kernels/src/graph/optimizer/anduin/mod.rs (next to the sibling fusion test).

Same conv2d -> batchnorm2d -> silu graph as the existing `conv2d_batchnorm_silu_schedule_fuses_the_three_compute_nodes_apart_from_input` test, but B=2 instead of B=1 so BatchNorm2d's [C, B] grid is visibly 2-D rather than collapsing to [C, 1] by coincidence. The test:

1. Confirms via `Anduin::schedule` that conv+batchnorm+silu (nodes [1, 2, 3]) still fuse into one SharedMemory-level VirtualNode at B=2 -- a real scheduler decision, not an assumption.
2. Pulls each of the three nodes' real `RuntimeOp` straight off the lowered `Dag` (`dag.node(i).value.runtime_op()`) and calls `.grid(&[2, 8, 32, 32])` on each -- the actual production grid() implementations (BatchNorm2dNchwInferenceRuntimeOp in nn/norm/batchnorm.rs:753, Conv2dForward in nn/conv/conv2d.rs:568, SiluForward in nn/activation/sigmoid.rs:392), not stubs.
3. Asserts conv_grid[1] == 1, silu_grid[1] == 1 (both flat 1-D), but bn_grid[1] > 1 (genuinely 2-D: [C=8, B=2, 1]).

This is real and passing today -- `./scripts/test.sh -p teeny-core -p teeny-kernels --lib` -> 79 passed (was 78), same 1 known pre-existing unrelated failure (two_pointwise_then_reduction_then_pointwise_preserves_chain, DagCodegen::virtual_node's todo!()). clippy: same 4 pre-existing warnings, no new ones. rustfmt clean.

comments.author: Arshad Mahmood
comments.text:
Consolidated per feedback: deleted the standalone `conv2d_batchnorm_silu_fused_group_has_no_single_compatible_grid` test and merged its grid assertion straight into the existing `conv2d_batchnorm_silu_schedule_fuses_the_three_compute_nodes_apart_from_input` test instead, right after its existing virtual-node fusion asserts. No separate graph/setup duplication now -- one test, one graph construction, covers both "these three fuse" and "their real grids don't agree."

comments.author: Arshad Mahmood
comments.text:
Extended the same test with what the CORRECT fused grid should be, not just that the three native grids disagree.

Reasoning, verified against a real precedent already in this codebase: BatchNorm2d here runs in inference mode (precomputed running mean/var -- no data-dependent reduction) and SiLU is pointwise, so both are pure per-element functions of Conv2d's own output value, evaluable entirely within whatever thread already computed that value -- neither needs a grid dimension of its own (this is the register-level/compute_inline case from the earlier TVM investigation: an op with no real compute-structural constraint just rides along on whichever fused op does have one). Conv2d is the only op in the group with a real constraint (each thread reduces over its own KHxKW input window), so the correct grid for the whole fused group is Conv2d's own native grid.

This isn't a novel claim -- it's exactly what `Conv2dBnSiluForward` (kernels/teeny-kernels/src/nn/fused/conv2d_bn_silu.rs) already does, hand-written, today: its doc comment states "Grid: pid = ((b*C_OUT+c_out)*OH+oh)*num_ow_tiles+ow_tile" -- identical to Conv2dForward's own standalone grid formula -- and its kernel body applies BN's affine (using precomputed bn_scale/bn_shift indexed by the same c_out the conv thread already decoded) and SiLU in registers before the one final store. Its own `grid()` impl (line 237-244) is byte-for-byte the same formula as Conv2dForward's.

Added to the test: constructs `Conv2dBnSiluForward::new(3, 3, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 16)` (same conv params as the graph, block_ow=16 matching the real Conv2d node's own construction in graph/mod.rs's `Op::Conv2d` arm) and asserts:
- `correct_fused_grid == conv_grid` (the correct answer is conv2d's own native grid)
- `correct_fused_grid != bn_grid` (batchnorm2d's standalone 2-D grid is provably NOT the right answer for the fused kernel -- it's an artifact of how BatchNorm2d happens to be scheduled alone, not a real requirement)

Both pass today, using the real existing hand-written kernel as ground truth. This makes the gap sharper: Anduin's scheduler has no mechanism to derive this even though the correct answer is knowable and already implemented by hand elsewhere in this codebase for this exact op combination. The general version of "which op anchors the grid" (not just for this specific elementwise-epilogue case) is still open -- see the earlier comments on register-level (compute_inline) vs shared-memory-level (RewriteOutputPass/RewriteInputPass) fusion.

Re-verified: cargo check clean; ./scripts/test.sh -p teeny-core -p teeny-kernels --lib -> 78 passed, same 1 known pre-existing failure; clippy same 4 pre-existing warnings; rustfmt clean.

comments.author: Arshad Mahmood
comments.text:
Implemented the metadata piece discussed for the register-level-fusion detection case (feature/3w0-tile-dsl-welder-scheduler): a new `GridSpec`/`GridAxisBinding`/`GridDim` sibling to `KernelTileSpec` (`core/teeny-core/src/model/grid_spec.rs`), declaring a kernel's real launch-grid decomposition (which hardware dim, block-tiled or one-CTA-per-index, axis identity for name-matching).

**Key generalization:** `#[tile(...)]` (teenygrad-1nr.18) is now repeatable per parameter (one axis per occurrence, declaration order = outermost-first) and applies to *any* `In`/`Out`/`InOut` parameter, not just `Tile`-typed ones. On a raw pointer parameter this is purely declarative -- no prelude, no body change at all -- which is what makes it usable on `conv2d_forward` today, well before the Tile<D>-composition rework (teenygrad-1nr.1) lands: `conv2d_forward`'s real hand-written `pid` decode is completely untouched, just annotated. `x_ptr`/`y_ptr` now carry real `#[tile(name=..,extent=..[,block=..])]` attributes; `Conv2dForward::tile_spec()`/`grid_spec()` reproduce the old hand-authored `CONV2D_TILE_SPEC` exactly (and now actually populate `untiled_dims`, previously left empty) plus the new 4-axis grid decomposition matching the real `(b, c_out, oh, ow_tile)` decode order. `CONV2D_LOOP_SPEC` (the accumulation-loop metadata from teenygrad-1nr.18) is layered on top at the `TritonLowering` call site since loop-carry isn't per-axis and `#[tile(...)]` doesn't attempt to derive it.

Verified against real hardware: all 9 `test_conv2d.rs` tests pass (including 6 real CUDA correctness tests), MLIR snapshots regenerated (content byte-identical, only the compiler's crate-disambiguator hash in the mangled symbol name shifted, as expected from any source edit to the crate) confirming the kernel body/compiled output is genuinely unchanged.

**Deliberately not done:** no consumer reads `GridSpec` yet (matches this issue's own request -- the ask was specifically for the *metadata*, not the reconciliation logic). The "is op B's grid a name-matching subset of op A's" check that would actually detect the register-level-fusion case mechanically is still open -- this only makes it checkable. Multi-axis `#[tile(...)]` on a `Tile`-typed (post-1nr.1) parameter is explicitly rejected with a clear error (needs N-axis auto-prelude codegen this macro doesn't have).

title: spec: generalize the Tile ABI to N-D/windowed/looped kernels, derive KernelTileSpec from the signature
description:
## Goal

Generalize the `In<Tile<T,D>>`/`Out<Tile<T,D>>` ABI that `#[tiled_kernel]`
supports for flat, single-axis elementwise kernels to multi-axis, windowed
and looped kernels -- and derive `KernelTileSpec` from the signature rather
than hand-authoring it beside the kernel.

## Status: item 1 landed, items 2-4 split out (2026-09-23)

The original scope was four items. The first shipped on 2026-09-01; the rest
are now their own issues, since this gates most of `teenygrad-1tl` and
splitting lets that ladder unblock in stages rather than all at once.

| item | issue | state |
|---|---|---|
| 1. per-axis `block`/`extent` on `Tile` params | -- | **done**, 2026-09-01 |
| 2a. N-axis prelude codegen | `teenygrad-1nr.18.1` | **done**, 2026-09-29 (PR #47) |
| 2b. windowed axis in the prelude | `teenygrad-1nr.18.2` | open |
| 3. wrapper-owned accumulation loop | `teenygrad-1nr.18.3` | open |
| 4. port conv2d end-to-end | `teenygrad-1nr.18.4` | open |

What item 1 delivered: a narrow `#[tile(block=.., extent=..)]` on `Tile`
params, driving the *naming* of the existing single-flat-axis prelude and
the generated `tile_spec()`. `relu_forward`/`silu_forward` are tagged and
their lowering arms use the derived spec. It did **not** generalize the
codegen, which is what items 2-4 are.

## The constraint every item inherits

Generated indexing belongs to the **wrapper**, never spliced into the kernel
author's body. The pre-2026 `#[tile(...)]` did exactly that and was deleted
at `84ca6eedf` because it broke composability when a kernel is called as a
tile-op from inside another kernel's body -- the same root problem as
`teenygrad-1nr.1`'s "`program_id` doesn't compose".

## Correction on record

The approved preview for item 1 assumed `matmul_forward` was "already
multi-axis, no loop needed". Inspection found otherwise: it uses a different
tensor-descriptor primitive, not `In<Tile<..>>`, and has a real internal
K-loop. Same for batchnorm2d and conv2d. So GEMM is further from the target
form than `teenygrad-1tl.10` implies, and that rung should re-check its
premise before being claimed.

## Boundary with teenygrad-1nr.1

`.1` composes *several* `#[tiled_kernel]` functions inside one wrapper for
fusion, moving `Tile<D>` values between them through shared memory. This
issue generalizes the *single-kernel* ABI. Both need the same "wrapper owns
indexing" primitive; neither subsumes the other.

## Out of scope

The `TileGraph` search and Anduin's `optimize` (parent issue). Multi-function
composition (`teenygrad-1nr.1`). Making the cost model consume loop carries
(`teenygrad-1nr.31`).
close_reason: Closed together with the teenygrad-1nr epic (Welder-style TileGraph scheduler)

comments.author: Arshad Mahmood
comments.text:
Implemented a first slice, scoped to relu/silu + conv2d (feature/3w0-tile-dsl-welder-scheduler):

**Landed:**
- Revived `TileCarryBinding`/`TileLoopSpec` on `KernelTileSpec` (`core/teeny-core/src/model/tile_spec.rs`), generalizing the original design's single `trip_count_param: &'static str` to `trip_count_factors: &'static [&'static str]` -- conv2d's real trip count (`(C_IN/G)*KH*KW`) mixes a runtime param with consts, not a single named param the way flash-attn's would be.
- `macros/teeny-macros/src/macros/tiled_kernel.rs`: revived a narrow `#[tile(block=..,extent=..)]` on `In<Tile<..>>`/`Out<Tile<..>>` params. Optional/additive -- a `Tile` param without it falls back to the pre-existing hardcoded `BLOCK_SIZE`/`n_elements` convention unchanged (every other Tile-ABI kernel, e.g. sigmoid/tanh/elu/selu/exp/logsigmoid, is untouched). When *every* tile param on a kernel declares it, the macro emits a `tile_spec(rank: usize) -> KernelTileSpec` method built from the attribute -- `rank` stays a runtime arg since it's a graph-node property, not part of the kernel signature (mirrors `flat_elementwise_tile_spec`'s own reasoning). Never re-splices index arithmetic into the kernel body -- avoids repeating `84ca6eedf`'s mistake.
- Tagged `relu_forward`/`silu_forward`; `Op::Relu`/`Op::Silu`'s lowering arms now call the macro-derived `tile_spec()` instead of the hand-authored `flat_elementwise_tile_spec` -- closes the gap where hand-authored specs had no compiler-enforced link to the real signature.
- `CONV2D_TILE_SPEC` now declares a real `loop_spec` describing `conv2d_forward`'s actual accumulation loop (`acc: [BLOCK_OW]` over `(C_IN/G)*KH*KW` iterations) -- previously totally undescribed (no field existed to put it in).
- Regression test (`kernels/teeny-kernels/src/graph/mod.rs::relu_silu_tile_spec_tests`) lowers real `Op::Relu`/`Op::Silu` and asserts the macro-derived spec matches the real signature.

**Correction from the original plan:** the approved preview said matmul_forward was "already multi-axis, no loop needed" -- turned out wrong on inspection: matmul uses a completely different tensor-descriptor primitive (not `In<Tile<..>>`) and has a real internal K-loop. So did batchnorm2d and conv2d. Re-scoped with the user to conv2d + relu/silu, accepting conv2d needs loop-carry metadata (this issue's TileLoopSpec revival) rather than avoiding it.

**Deliberately not done (still open):**
- N-axis / windowed auto-prelude codegen in the macro -- conv2d_forward itself is untouched (still hand-written pointer arithmetic + hand-authored `CONV2D_TILE_SPEC`, just now with `loop_spec` attached). The macro's `#[tile(...)]` mechanism only generalizes the *naming* of the existing single-flat-axis prelude, not multi-axis/windowed/looped codegen.
- `loop_spec` has no consumer -- `TileGraph::propagate`/`mem_traffic`/`mem_footprint` still treat a loop-carried kernel's inputs as fully materialized. Declaring the metadata doesn't fix that (documented explicitly on `TileLoopSpec` itself).
- teenygrad-1nr.1's actual scope (composable `Tile<D>->Tile<D>` functions, wrapper-owned `pid` decode, multi-function composition via shared memory) is untouched.

title: feat: N-axis auto-prelude — generate indexing for several declared tile axes
description:
## Goal

Generalize `#[tiled_kernel]`'s auto-prelude from one flat axis to N declared
axes.

## Item 2 of teenygrad-1nr.18

Split out so the ladder it gates can unblock incrementally. Item 1 of that
issue (per-axis `block`/`extent` association on `Tile` params) landed on
2026-09-01; this is the codegen half that was deliberately not done.

## Current behaviour

`macros/teeny-macros/src/macros/tiled_kernel.rs` emits exactly one axis'
worth of indexing:

```rust
let pid = HW::program_id(Axis::X);
let block_start = pid * BLOCK;
let offsets = HW::arange(0, BLOCK) + block_start;
let in_bounds = offsets.lt(EXTENT);
```

One `offsets`, handed to every `In<Tile<..>>`/`Out<Tile<..>>` param. Axis
discovery is a single `#[tile(block=..,extent=..)]`, or hardcoded
name-matching on `const BLOCK_SIZE` + `n_elements`.

That covers shape-preserving elementwise kernels and nothing else, which is
why every other kernel still hand-writes its pointer arithmetic.

## Scope

- Accept several `#[tile(...)]` attributes per parameter, one per axis,
  outermost first -- the declarative form already parsed for raw pointers
  (teenygrad-1nr.19), now driving codegen.
- Emit per-axis `offsets`/masks and combine them into the multi-dimensional
  index each tile param needs.
- Support axes on `Axis::Y`/`Axis::Z`, not just `X` -- `batchnorm.rs` and
  `channel_bias_add.rs` already use them by hand.
- An untiled axis (a `#[tile(...)]` with no `block=`) is one index per CTA,
  not a block -- it already means that in the generated `tile_spec()`, and
  the prelude must agree.

## Constraint carried from teenygrad-1nr.18

The generated indexing belongs to the **wrapper**, never spliced into the
kernel author's body. The pre-2026 `#[tile(...)]` did exactly that and was
deleted at `84ca6eedf` because it broke composability when a kernel is
called as a tile-op from inside another kernel's body -- the same root
problem as `teenygrad-1nr.1`'s "`program_id` doesn't compose".

## Done when

A kernel declaring two or more axes gets correct generated indexing, proven
against a real kernel whose hand-written arithmetic it replaces, with the
existing single-axis kernels byte-identical.
design:
Acceptance now met: channel_bias_add_forward is converted and is the real proof (f4b1b10f2), replacing the test-only probe kernel as the only evidence.

Its `while n_start < N` loop existed only because the grid covered channels alone, so each CTA walked N itself. With N declared as an axis the grid covers it and the loop is gone. The prelude's row-major stride derivation reproduces the kernel's hand-written addressing exactly: `offsets_n * C + c` became `__tile_range * (C) + tile_c`.

Verified structurally in PTX, not just in source: branches and basic-block labels drop 2 -> 0, one rem/div appears for the pid decode, and ctaid/loads/stores stay at 1/2/1 -- same memory traffic per CTA, no loop.

NOT verified numerically. The hardware tests fail with CUDA error 218 (PTX JIT compilation failed) on this machine both before and after the change -- an environment issue on the sm_120 card, cf. teenygrad-0mr. Anyone with working CUDA should re-run test_channel_bias_add --features hardware before trusting the conversion.

One capability added along the way that was not in the original scope: the prelude binds each axis's CTA index under a usable name (`#[tile(name = "C", ..)]` binds `tile_c`). Multi-axis kernels need it -- this one indexes its bias by channel, conv2d will need b/c_out/oh -- and without it a body would have to reach for a generated name it was never promised.

Still limited to ONE blocked axis. Two would need a 2-D index tile (expand_dims plus Tensor<i32,2> bounds); no kernel in the tree needs it yet.
notes:
Landed via PR #47, squash-merged into feature/anduin-v2 as bdf75537c on 2026-09-29.

Delivered:
- N-axis auto-prelude in tiled_kernel.rs: flat program_id decode innermost-first,
  row-major strides derived from the declared extents, tile_<name> index bindings,
  and broadcast subsets (a Tile param may declare a subset of the output's axes).
- Converted as real proof rather than a synthetic case: channel_bias_add_forward
  (with bias_ptr also a Tile) and batch_norm_2d_nchw_forward_inference.
- Both NCHW batchnorm tests now compare against PyTorch fixtures
  (fixtures/batchnorm_nchw) instead of values computed in the test. The backward
  one had used uniform inputs at B=1 with var=0 and eps=1, so rstd was exactly 1;
  that could not detect a wrong batch or channel stride and never exercised rsqrt.
- The multi-axis probe kernel moved into nn::tensor's cfg(test) module, so no
  test-only kernel file remains under src/.

Verified on hardware: RTX 5070 sm_120, CUDA 13.4, driver 610.43.02, from a clean
build (exit 0). Workspace 410 passed / 11 failed; teeny-kernels cuda+hardware
569/10; riscv+training 281/12. Zero CUDA runtime errors and zero ptxas errors.
All 11 test_batchnorm tests pass. The remaining failures are pre-existing: the
Anduin schedule todo! stubs, teenygrad-15k (RISC-V asin/acos/atan), and one
teenyc Triton ICE in test_conv2d_boundary.

Six sin/cos/tan CUDA asm snapshots were re-recorded for the CUDA 13.4 upgrade.
The only change in each is the removal of the nounroll pragma, which comes from
libdevice and so ships with the toolkit. Accepted on passing numerics rather than
on the diff alone.

Deliberately out of scope, and what still gates the ladder: window (the conv and
pool receptive field), divide_by, reduction_axis, flattened multi-dim dims, and
loop_spec are all expressible in KernelTileSpec but not yet derivable from the
tile attributes, which only accept block, extent, name and dim. The spec the
macro emits also hardcodes one dim per axis and gives every tensor the first tile
param's axis set. That is what teenygrad-1nr.18.2/.3 and the twelve conv/pool
conversions are waiting on.
close_reason: Landed via PR #47 (bdf75537c); verified on hardware under CUDA 13.4

title: feat: windowed axis in the auto-prelude — stride/pad/kernel consts drive the input read
description:
## Goal

Teach the auto-prelude that an axis can be read through a strided, padded
sliding window, so a conv or pool input read is generated rather than
hand-written.

## Part of item 2 of teenygrad-1nr.18

Split from `teenygrad-1nr.18.1` because the plain multi-axis case unblocks
the norms and shape-changing families on its own, while only conv and pool
need a window. Separating them lets those rungs land earlier.

## Scope

- Extend `#[tile(...)]` to name the three consts, e.g.
  `#[tile(name = "H", extent = H, window(stride = STRIDE_H, pad = PAD_H, kernel = KH))]`.
- Emit the windowed input indexing: for an output tile of `block` elements
  along the axis, the input region read is the receptive field
  `(block - 1) * stride + kernel`, with the origin shifted by `pad`.
- Emit the boundary mask for the edge tiles, whose region runs off the real
  extent at one or both ends.
- Have the generated `tile_spec()` emit a real `TileWindow` instead of the
  `window: None` currently hardcoded at `tiled_kernel.rs:835` and `:915`.
  `TileWindow` is presently constructed nowhere in the repo.

## The arithmetic

Forward, exact, one answer -- **not** an inverted extent. Padding shifts the
window's origin, it does not change its size, so an interior tile needs the
full receptive field. A 3x3 conv at `p=1, s=1` with a block of 8 reads
**10** input elements. `teenygrad-1nr.30` has the derivation and why
`Op::infer_input_shape` is the wrong tool.

## Done when

RE-SCOPED 2026-09-30. This issue owns the DECLARATION and the spec:

- a kernel declares a windowed axis on its signature;
- its `tile_spec()` carries a real `TileWindow`;
- `resolve_inputs` returns the receptive field for an interior tile.

The generated input READ moved to `teenygrad-y8aa`, because conv and pool never
read their receptive field in one access: conv2d loads a `BLOCK_OW` slice per
`(kh, kw)` and the field is the union over the loop. Generating a single
receptive-field load would produce an access pattern no kernel wants, and
generating the per-iteration read needs the loop index, which is y8aa'''s job.
close_reason: Declaration and spec delivered via PR #62 (30f588b97): window(stride,pad,kernel,output) emits a real TileWindow, proven on conv2d_forward with receptive fields of 10/10/17. Re-scoped; the generated read moved to teenygrad-y8aa.

title: feat: wrapper-owned accumulation loop — declare and generate a kernel's reduction loop
description:
## Goal

Generate the wrapper's accumulation loop for kernels that reduce over a
receptive field or a K range, using the carries `TileLoopSpec` already
declares.

## Item 3 of teenygrad-1nr.18

## Why it is separate

`TileLoopSpec`/`TileCarryBinding` landed with `teenygrad-1nr.18`'s first
slice, so the *metadata* exists: `CONV2D_LOOP_SPEC` described
`conv2d_forward`'s real loop (`acc: [BLOCK_OW]` over `(C_IN/G)*KH*KW`). What
never existed is codegen that reads it.

That metadata was deleted with the other hand-authored specs (see
`teenygrad-1tl`), on the grounds that a spec written beside a kernel drifts
from it. So this issue owns both halves now: deciding how a kernel
*declares* its loop on its own signature -- a `#[tile_loop(...)]`, or
something inferred -- and generating it.

Note the name `#[tile_loop(...)]` existed before and was removed at
`84ca6eedf` for splicing index arithmetic into kernel bodies. Reusing the
name is fine; reusing that behaviour is not.

## Scope

- A way for a kernel to declare its carried accumulators and trip count on
  its signature.
- Generated loop: initialise carries, iterate, thread them through, write
  the result once after the loop.
- Trip counts that mix runtime params with consts -- conv2d's is
  `(C_IN/G)*KH*KW`, which is why `trip_count_factors` is a list of names
  rather than one param.

## Not in scope

Making the cost model *consume* loop carries. `acc`/`m_i`/`l_i` never cross
a pointer parameter, so they are never a `TileEdge`, and
`mem_footprint`/`mem_traffic` are entirely `EdgeId`-keyed. That is
`teenygrad-1nr.31`.

## Done when

RE-SCOPED 2026-09-30, after the design analysis below. This issue now owns the
DECLARATION only:

- A kernel declares its carried accumulators and trip count on its own
  signature, and the generated `tile_spec()` reports a real `TileLoopSpec`.

Generating the loop moved to `teenygrad-y8aa`, sequenced behind
`teenygrad-1nr.18.2`. The original Done-when -- "gets it generated, proven
against a real kernel whose hand-written loop it replaces" -- is carried there
verbatim. The split is not a narrowing of ambition: generation is blocked on
loop-indexed operands and a `Carry` type, neither of which is a syntax
question, and the rungs waiting on this issue needed only the ability to state
a reduction.
design:
DESIGN ANALYSIS, 2026-09-30, grounded in conv2d_forward. Four hard constraints, then four options, then a recommendation.

=== THE CONSTRAINTS ===

C1. THE PRELUDE LOADS AN In<Tile> EXACTLY ONCE, BEFORE THE BODY. Verified from the generated source: `let x = Tile::<T,D>{ tensor: T::load(x.add_offsets(offsets), Some(in_bounds), ..), mask: Some(in_bounds) }` is emitted ahead of the author's first statement, at offsets derived from program_id alone. conv2d's x is read at offsets depending on (c_in, kh, kw) -- i.e. on the loop index -- and its w at w_idx likewise. A load-once-up-front form cannot express either.

C2. Tile IS DELIBERATELY MOVE-ONLY. tile.rs states it: no Clone/Copy, because teenyc's no_core device environment does not resolve Option<T::BoolTensor>: Copy even though T::BoolTensor: Copy holds. "Read .tensor/.mask once each and move them onward rather than reusing tile itself." A Tile parameter therefore cannot be re-read across loop iterations even if C1 were solved.

C3. THE LOOP MUST NOT BE SPLICED INTO A COMPOSABLE FUNCTION BODY. This is 84ca6eedf's lesson and the issue restates it. Note the precise shape of the lesson: the N-axis prelude DOES generate index arithmetic into the body (tile_<name> bindings, offsets, in_bounds) and that is accepted, because it is a wrapper concern. What was reverted was arithmetic that broke composition when a kernel is called as a tile-op from inside another kernel's body. So the constraint is not "generate no indices", it is "the loop belongs to the wrapper".

C4. THE TRAILING STORE IS OUTSIDE THE LOOP. conv2d accumulates into acc across (C_IN/G)*KH*KW iterations and stores once afterwards.

=== OPTION A: #[tile_loop(..)] that wraps the existing body ===

    #[tile_loop(count = (C_IN / G) * KH * KW, carry(acc = zeros[BLOCK_OW]))]

REJECTED on C4. Wrapping the body in a loop puts the trailing T::store inside it. Separating "loop part" from "epilogue" requires a delimiter inside the body, and a macro reading markers out of a body is exactly C3's failure mode. This is the option the issue's phrasing implies, and it does not survive contact with the kernel.

=== OPTION B: metadata-only #[tile_loop(..)], no codegen ===

Body untouched; the attribute exists so tile_spec() emits a real TileLoopSpec (carries and trip_count_factors).

This has direct precedent: teenygrad-1nr.19 did exactly this for #[tile(..)] on raw pointers, and conv2d_forward already carries that metadata-only form -- its own comment says "#[tile(...)] below is metadata-only -- it drives tile_spec()/grid_spec() generation ... but never touches this body".

Cheap, cannot regress 84ca6eedf, and satisfies what the scheduler actually asks of loop_spec: that a loop's existence and carried shape be queryable. It does NOT satisfy this issue's Done-when, which says the loop "gets it generated".

=== OPTION C: the kernel expresses one iteration; the wrapper owns the loop ===

The kernel body becomes the loop body -- a function of (carry, loop index) returning the updated carry -- and the macro generates: initialise carries, iterate, thread carries, store once after.

This matches the issue's own title ("wrapper-owned accumulation loop") and teenygrad-1nr.1's goal of composing Tile functions rather than pointer-in/pointer-out kernels. It satisfies C3 by construction: the loop is the wrapper, never spliced.

It needs two things that do not exist: a Carry type (none in the tree), and a way to express an operand whose tile depends on the loop index, per C1/C2. That second requirement is the same problem teenygrad-1nr.18.2 solves for windowed axes -- an input region computed from the output tile rather than loaded at a fixed offset.

=== OPTION D: declare the reduced axes and reuse the N-axis decode ===

conv2d's loop index decode

    let kw = idx % KW; let kh = idx / KW % KH; let c_in_local = idx / (KW * KH);

is structurally IDENTICAL to the flat program_id decode teenygrad-1nr.18.1 already generates: innermost-first division and modulo over declared extents. Declaring the reduction as three axes with extents (C_IN/G), KH, KW would let one mechanism serve both the grid and the loop, which is the most economical idea available here.

It is a decode mechanism, not a placement mechanism: it still needs Option C's structure to say where the loop goes, and it still needs loop-indexed operands.

=== RECOMMENDATION ===

B now, C as the target, with D as C's decode.

1. Land B: a metadata-only #[tile_loop(..)] so the nine accumulating kernels can DECLARE their carries and trip counts. That is what teenygrad-1tl.8/.9/.11 actually need to proceed -- they are blocked on being able to state a reduction, not on having a loop written for them. Precedent, cost and risk are all favourable.
2. Solve loop-indexed operands, which is teenygrad-1nr.18.2's windowed-axis work. C1 and C2 make this the real prerequisite, and it is currently sequenced after this issue rather than before.
3. Then C, as its own ABI issue, with D as the decode.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE ISSUE AS WRITTEN: its Done-when -- "proven against a real kernel whose hand-written loop it replaces", with conv2d named as the reference -- is not reachable yet. conv2d cannot take In<Tile> for x or w at all, because both are read at loop-dependent offsets and the prelude loads once (C1), and Tile is move-only (C2). That also puts teenygrad-1nr.18.4 ("port conv2d_forward to the Tile ABI end-to-end") behind .18.2 rather than behind this issue. Recommend re-scoping this issue to Option B and opening a separate issue for C.
notes:
SCOPING AUDIT, 2026-09-30, before implementation.

Surveyed every forward kernel with a `while`/`for` loop: 12 of them. They split into two kinds, and only one kind is this issue's business.

INDEPENDENT WALK (3) -- the loop steps a tile over an extent and nothing crosses iterations. Each iteration loads, computes and stores on its own:
  batch_norm_forward_inference   (walk var n_start)
  batch_norm_normalize_forward   (walk var n_start)
  nchw_bias_add_forward          (walk var hw_start)
These do NOT need a generated accumulation loop. They need grid coverage, which teenygrad-1nr.18.1 already provides -- exactly the conversion applied there to batch_norm_2d_nchw_forward_inference and channel_bias_add_forward, whose walks became [C * cdiv(HW, BLOCK_HW), B] grids. Dependency edges claiming these are blocked on this issue were wrong and are corrected.

ACCUMULATING (9) -- a carry is reassigned from itself inside the loop, so the iterations are not independent:
  batch_norm_stats_forward        acc_sum, acc_sum_sq
  group_norm_forward{,_inference} sum, var_sum
  instance_norm_forward{,_inference} sum, var_sum
  layer_norm_forward{,_inference} sum, var_sum
  rms_norm_forward                sq_sum
  maxpool2d_forward               acc
Note most of these ALSO have a walk variable (n_start, l_start). That is not redundant: a row reduction cannot distribute its row across CTAs because the mean needs the whole row, so the walk is intrinsic and the carries accumulate across it. Walk plus accumulate is the shape, and both halves have to be generated.

conv2d_forward is the reference the issue names and is a third shape again: a `for idx in 0..loop_bound` with loop_bound = (C_IN/G) * KH * KW, one carry `acc: [BLOCK_OW]` initialised to zeros, and a body that decodes idx into (c_in_local, kh, kw) by division and modulo -- structurally the same innermost-first decode the N-axis prelude performs on program_id.

DESIGN CONSTRAINT worth restating from the issue: #[tile_loop(...)] was removed at 84ca6eedf for splicing index arithmetic into kernel bodies. So the generated loop must supply the scaffold only -- initialise carries, iterate, thread carries through, write once after -- and leave the body to compute its own indices from the loop variable. That rules out generating the idx decode, even though it would be mechanical.

CONSEQUENCES for the blocked rungs:
- teenygrad-1tl.4's last kernel (nchw_bias_add) is an independent walk, so it is unblocked now. Edge removed.
- Two of teenygrad-1tl.8's population (batch_norm_forward_inference, batch_norm_normalize_forward) are independent walks too, so that rung is only partly behind this issue.
close_reason: Declaration delivered via PR #59 (cc7f23051): #[tile_loop(trip_count=[..])] + #[tile_carry(name=[..])], metadata-only, proven on conv2d_forward. Issue re-scoped to the declaration; loop GENERATION moved to teenygrad-y8aa behind 1nr.18.2, since it needs loop-indexed operands and a Carry type.

title: feat: port conv2d_forward to the Tile ABI end-to-end
description:
## Goal

Port `conv2d_forward` to `In<Tile<..>>`/`Out<Tile<..>>` end to end, deleting
its hand-written pointer arithmetic and loop.

## Item 4 of teenygrad-1nr.18

The proof that the generated machinery is enough for a real multi-axis,
windowed, looped kernel -- mirroring how `c69c08b63` proved the 1-D case
against `relu`/`sigmoid`/`tanh`/`elu`/`selu`/`exp`.

## Why conv2d

It is the only kernel in the tree using the metadata-only form: raw
`In<T::Pointer<D>>` params with declarative `#[tile(name = .., extent = ..)]`
(teenygrad-1nr.19), body untouched. Under the direction settled for
`teenygrad-1tl` -- every forward kernel takes `Tile` params, raw pointers
are not carried forward -- that form is a migration aid with exactly one
user, and this is where it is retired.

It also exercises all three generated pieces at once: four axes, a windowed
input read on H and W, and an accumulation loop over `(C_IN/G)*KH*KW`.

## Watch for

The generated `tile_spec()` must not regress what the declarative form
already produces. Today `x_ptr` is rank 4 with `axes: []` and
`untiled_dims: ["B","C_IN","H","W"]`, and `y_ptr` has one binding on dim 3
(`BLOCK_OW`/`OW`) with `untiled_dims: ["B","C_OUT","OH"]`. After the port,
`x_ptr`'s H and W should carry real `TileWindow`s -- strictly more than
today, never less.

`kernels/teeny-kernels/src/graph/mod.rs::conv2d_grid_spec_tests` pins both
`tile_spec()` and `grid_spec()` against the current signature and is the
regression net for this.

## Done when

`conv2d_forward` takes `Tile` params, declares its axes, window and loop,
has no hand-written indexing left, and its generated spec is at least as
descriptive as the one it replaces.
notes:
## PREMISE CORRECTED 2026-10-01 -- read before picking this up

Two of this issue's statements were true when written and are not now. Neither
changes the goal; both change what the goal is worth and how big it is.

### 1. conv2d is NOT the only user of the metadata-only form

The issue says: "It is the only kernel in the tree using the metadata-only
form... that form is a migration aid with exactly one user, and this is where it
is retired."

Current count of DECLARED forward kernels:

  route 1 (In<Tile<..>>/Out<Tile<..>> params):  77
  route 2 (tagged raw In<T::Pointer<D>> params): 49

The 49 are: all 13 convs and pools, the 12 pads, all 10 reduce_* plus the two
global pools and the two scans, layer/rms/instance/group norm,
batch_norm_stats, batch_norm_normalize, matmul, linear, transpose_2d, flatten,
conv2d_bias, conv3d.

They were declared across teenygrad-1tl.5 / .7 / .8 / .9 / .10, every one of
them route 2, because the whole conv/pool/pad/reduction/matmul population has
hand-written bodies with their own program_id and index arithmetic.

So retiring route 2 is a ~49-kernel programme and this issue is the FIRST of
those, not the last. The "one user, retire it here" framing would materially
understate the work to whoever picks this up. What this issue still is: the
PROOF that the generated machinery can carry a hard kernel, which is its stated
purpose and remains the valuable part.

Note also that teenygrad-1tl.10 carried its own stale correction in the other
direction -- a note claiming route 2 was "no longer available" because the epic
had settled on Tile params everywhere. That was wrong too. The epic's "Done
when" (no forward kernel still takes raw pointer params) is aspirational
relative to how the work actually went.

### 2. The "Watch for" bar is already met, so it is now a REGRESSION bar

The issue describes today as "x_ptr is rank 4 with axes: [] and untiled_dims:
[B,C_IN,H,W]" and asks that the port give H and W real TileWindows.

teenygrad-1tl.7 already did that. x_ptr now carries a window on BOTH spatial
axes -- H with block_const "1" (one scalar oh per program) and W with
BLOCK_OW -- and untiled_dims is ["B","C_IN"]. y_ptr is unchanged.

So the port must PRESERVE that, not achieve it. The assertions in
graph/mod.rs::conv2d_grid_spec_tests were rewritten in 1tl.7 and are the live
regression net; read them rather than this issue's description of the spec.

## Scope unchanged

Port conv2d_forward to Tile params end to end: delete the hand-written pointer
arithmetic and the accumulation loop, declare axes + window + loop, generated
spec at least as descriptive as the one it replaces. Four axes, a windowed read
on H and W, and a loop over (C_IN/G)*KH*KW -- all three generated pieces at
once.

## The blocker is a design project, not a small task

teenygrad-y8aa is dependency-ready (1nr.18.2, its stated real prerequisite, is
closed) but is the largest single piece of work left in this area:

- The prelude loads an In<Tile> exactly ONCE, before the body, at offsets from
  program_id alone. conv2d reads x at offsets depending on (c_in, kh, kw) and w
  at a w_idx likewise. A load-once-up-front parameter cannot express either, so
  y8aa needs LOOP-INDEXED OPERANDS.
- Tile is deliberately move-only -- kernels/teeny-triton/src/triton/tile.rs:48,
  no Clone/Copy, because teenyc's no_core device environment does not resolve
  Option<T::BoolTensor>: Copy. So a Tile cannot be re-read across iterations
  even if the above were solved.
- It needs a Carry type. None exists in the tree.
- Design is Option C: the kernel becomes a function of (carry, loop index)
  returning the updated carry, with the macro generating
  initialise / iterate / thread / store-once-after. The loop is then the
  wrapper by construction, which is what prevents 84ca6eedf recurring.

Do not size this issue from its title.
close_reason: Complete via PR #80. conv2d_forward's body is one statement; the grid decode, carry init, loop, index decode, both operand reads and the store are generated. Numerics pass on GPU against the PyTorch fixtures, padded case included. The spec is unchanged, which was this issue's bar -- all three conv2d_grid_spec_tests pass on the same assertions. Found three bugs no probe could: route-1 grid_spec was hardcoded to one axis (a 1nr.19 relic), an undeclared param reached the spec at rank 0, and the generated bounds check recomputed each coordinate twice. Note the premise correction recorded earlier: conv2d was NOT route 2's only user -- 49 declared forwards are route 2 against 77 route 1 -- so this is the first of that population to port, not the last.

title: feat: auto-prelude supports two or more blocked axes (2-D index tile)
description:
## Goal

Let the auto-prelude generate indexing for **two or more block-tiled axes**, so
a kernel can have a genuinely 2-D tile rather than one blocked axis and a set
of scalar indices.

## Current behaviour

`teenygrad-1nr.18.1` shipped N *declared* axes with exactly **one** blocked.
A second `block =` is rejected outright:

```
only one `#[tile(...)]` axis may carry `block = ..` today -- two blocked axes
need a 2-D index tile (`expand_dims` and `Tensor<i32, 2>` bounds), which is a
separate change
```

That was the right call at the time: every kernel in the tree has the
one-blocked-axis shape (conv 1/2/3d, the nine pools, batchnorm's flattened
`BLOCK_HW`), so nothing needed it.

## Why it is needed now

`teenygrad-1tl` settled on a direction that changes this: **every forward
kernel takes `In<Tile<..>>`/`Out<Tile<..>>`, and raw pointer parameters are not
carried forward.** GEMM's tile is `BLOCK_M x BLOCK_N` — two blocked axes — so
under that rule it *must* go through the prelude, and cannot.

Note `teenygrad-1tl.10` currently assumes the opposite. It says GEMM stays on
"route 2 throughout" because "GEMM uses a swizzled 2-D `pid` decode that the
flat `Axis::X` auto-prelude cannot generate", which was true when written but
routes around a prelude the epic has since made mandatory. That issue's
premise needs revisiting alongside this one.

## What it involves

- **A 2-D index tile.** Each blocked axis's `arange` has to be broadcast into
  its own dimension -- `expand_dims(offs_m, 1)` and `expand_dims(offs_n, 0)` --
  then combined by stride. The single-blocked case gets this for free because
  its range is already the tile.
- **The rank bound changes.** Every kernel declares
  `T::I32Tensor: types::Tensor<i32, 1>` in its where clause. A 2-D index tile
  needs `Tensor<i32, 2>`, so this is an ABI change visible in kernel
  signatures, not only in generated code.
- **A 2-D mask.** Today the mask is one axis's `range.lt(extent)`. With two it
  is the conjunction of both axes' comparisons, broadcast the same way.
- **Strides stay row-major from the declared extents**, as now. Nothing about
  the stride derivation needs to change; only how the ranges are shaped.

## Watch for

`teenygrad-1nr.18`'s own recorded correction says `matmul_forward` does **not**
use `In<Tile<..>>` at all -- it uses a different tensor-descriptor primitive
and has a real internal K-loop. So GEMM needs this issue *and*
`teenygrad-1nr.18.3` (the wrapper loop), and is further from the Tile ABI than
a blocked-axis count alone suggests. Do not size this from the macro change
and assume GEMM follows.

The single-blocked path must keep emitting what it emits today. Snapshots
embed `.loc` debug info, so even a semantically identical prelude with a
different statement count rewrites a pile of them -- see
`teenygrad-1nr.18.1`'s comment on why its one-axis case is kept verbatim.

## Done when

A kernel declaring two blocked axes gets correct generated indexing and mask,
proven against a real kernel whose hand-written arithmetic it replaces, with
the existing single-blocked kernels unchanged.
notes:
FEASIBILITY CHECK, 2026-09-30, before implementing. Two findings re-scope this issue.

1. THE RANK BOUND IS A NON-ISSUE. The issue says a 2-D index tile "needs `Tensor<i32, 2>`, so this is an ABI change visible in kernel signatures, not only in generated code". That is textually true and materially false. Every implementation of `Tensor<D, RANK>` in the tree is generic over RANK:

    impl<D: ty::Dtype, const RANK: usize> ty::Tensor<D, RANK> for LlvmTensor<D> {}
    impl<D: Dtype, const RANK: usize> Tensor<D, RANK> for DummyTensor {}
    impl<D: Dtype, const RANK: usize> Tensor<D, RANK> for SymTensor {}

core/teeny-core/src/graph/mod.rs:182 says so outright: "SymTensor satisfies Tensor<D, RANK> for any D and RANK -- shape is tracked [dynamically]". The tensor types are rank-erased and there is exactly one Triton impl (LlvmTriton). So `T::I32Tensor: types::Tensor<i32, 1>` already holds at rank 2, and no existing kernel signature needs touching. No where-clause churn, no ABI migration.

2. THERE *IS* A NEW ABI REQUIREMENT, but a different one. Two blocked axes need their two masks conjoined, so a kernel using them must declare `T::BoolTensor: BitAnd<Output = T::BoolTensor>`. conv2d_forward already declares exactly that for its own hand-written `ow_mask & h_in_bounds & w_in_bounds`, so the bound is established practice rather than new ground -- but it is a real signature requirement and the issue does not mention it.

SHAPE OF THE CODEGEN, settled by reading the existing prelude. Comparing against expand_dims on a bool tensor, it is cheaper to expand the ranges and compare afterwards, which avoids needing `expand_dims` over `BoolTensor`:

    let range_m = expand_dims(arange(0, BM) + idx_m * BM, 1);   // [BM, 1]
    let range_n = expand_dims(arange(0, BN) + idx_n * BN, 0);   // [1, BN]
    let in_bounds = range_m.lt(ext_m) & range_n.lt(ext_n);      // broadcasts
    let offsets = range_m * stride_m + range_n * stride_n + <scalar base>;

Generalises to K blocked axes: the range for blocked axis k is expanded at every other blocked dim. Strides stay row-major from the declared extents, exactly as now -- only the ranges' shaping changes, which matches what the issue predicted.

NOTHING IN THE TREE USES TWO BLOCKED AXES TODAY. GEMM is route 2 and conv/pool are raw-pointer, so this has to be proven against a test-only probe kernel -- the same approach teenygrad-1nr.18.1 took, whose probe now lives in nn::tensor's cfg(test) module.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAS TO CHANGE in tiled_kernel.rs: relax the `blocked.len() > 1` guard; turn `blocked_at` from one index into a list; emit one expanded range per blocked axis instead of one `__tile_range`; conjoin the masks; and sum the blocked terms into `offsets`. `param_offsets`' broadcast check also becomes "declares *all* the blocked axes" rather than "declares the blocked axis".
close_reason: Landed via PR #64 (two commits: trait plumbing c4d9bc5d1, prelude generalisation f9be4aa6c). The predicted Tensor<i32,2> blocker did not exist; the real ones were expand_dims over I32Tensor and tensor-add bounds.

title: feat: BatchNorm2d stops being a hard boundary -- flattened #[tile(dims = ..)] binding, and the lowering carries its spec
description:
The BatchNorm2d lowering (graph/mod.rs, Op::BatchNorm2d arm) builds its KernelExecutable with tile_spec: None, so TileGraph propagation treats every conv2d -> bn2d -> silu chain as a hard boundary at bn2d.

It cannot simply be wired to BatchNorm2dNchwForwardInference::tile_spec(): that kernel declares its tensor as rank 3 [B, C, HW] (BLOCK_HW on a flattened H*W axis), while the graph edge is rank 4 [B, C, H, W]. resolve_inputs rejects a rank-4 output tile against a rank-3 spec.

TileAxisBinding::dims and resolve_inputs already support a flattened binding (several real dims under one block, innermost carries the block, others 1). Only the macro lacks syntax: it emits exactly one dim per declared axis.

Fix: add a flattened-axis form to #[tile(...)] so one declared axis can span several real dims (spec rank = real rank, binding dims = [2, 3]) without changing the kernel's memory access; declare it on batch_norm_2d_nchw_forward_inference; set tile_spec in the lowering; test resolve_inputs against a rank-4 tile. Same gap noted on conv2d_bn_silu_gemm and batch_norm_stats_forward.
close_reason: Closed together with the teenygrad-1nr epic (Welder-style TileGraph scheduler)

title: feat: the BatchNorm1d/3d training nodes carry their tile specs (batch_norm_stats_forward, batch_norm_normalize_forward)
description:
In LoweringMode::Training, BatchNorm1d/3d lower to two forward DAG nodes (graph/mod.rs, the Training block before the main match): batch_norm_stats_forward then batch_norm_normalize_forward. Both are built with tile_spec: None, so both are hard boundaries for TileGraph propagation -- the same lowering gap teenygrad-1nr.18.6 closed for BatchNorm2d.

Both kernels already declare #[tile(...)] and generate tile_spec(); the lowering just does not attach it.

- BatchNorm1d: the edge is [N, C], matching the kernels' [N, C] view, so this should be wiring plus a test.
- BatchNorm3d: the edge is rank 5 [B, C, D, H, W] while the kernels address x as [N, C], so the spec's rank disagrees with the edge and resolve_inputs rejects it. Needs either a span-style declaration (teenygrad-1nr.18.6) or a different kernel view. Note batch_norm_stats_forward's N is reduce + walk, and span cannot combine with reduce.

Also check the stats node's packed [2*C] output (mean then rstd) against the spec's two separate outputs.

Backward kernels are out of scope (no tile metadata by design).
