title: bug: batch_norm_stats_forward's #[tile_carry] names carries its generated body does not have
description:
batch_norm_stats_forward (nn/norm/batchnorm.rs) declares
  #[tile_loop(trip_count = [N, BLOCK_N])]
  #[tile_carry(acc_sum = [BLOCK_N], acc_sum_sq = [BLOCK_N])]
but since its conversion to #[tile_reduce_pass] (teenygrad-3dp5) the generated body accumulates into SCALAR carries named sum and sum_sq (zeros(&[1])), per the reduce passes' into = sum / into = sum_sq. No variable acc_sum exists (see tests/snapshots/test_batchnorm__batch_norm_stats_source_*.snap).

So tile_spec().loop_spec reports two [BLOCK_N] carries that do not exist. Nothing consumes loop_spec yet, which is why nothing failed.

Fix: either derive the loop_spec from the reduce passes (each pass's into is a [1] carry, trip count over its walk axis) so it cannot drift, or at minimum correct the declaration to sum = [1], sum_sq = [1]. The former is better: a hand-written carry list beside generated carries is the same decoupling that got the hand-authored specs deleted. Check the other #[tile_reduce_pass] kernels (layer_norm, instance_norm, group_norm, rms_norm) for the same drift.
close_reason: Closed together with the teenygrad-1nr epic (Welder-style TileGraph scheduler)

title: feat: BatchNorm1d/3d inference stops being a hard boundary -- batch_norm_forward_inference takes the Tile ABI
description:
BatchNorm1d/3d in LoweringMode::Inference lower to batch_norm_forward_inference via make_float_kernel!(BatchNormForwardInference(64), node), which sets tile_spec: None. The kernel is a plain #[kernel] with raw pointers and a hand-written per-channel while loop over N, so it has no spec to attach either. Every BN1d/3d inference node is therefore a hard boundary for TileGraph propagation.

Sibling of teenygrad-1nr.18.6 (BatchNorm2d inference, PR #103) and teenygrad-1nr.18.7 (the BN1d/3d training nodes), which do not cover this kernel.

Shape of the work: convert to #[tiled_kernel] in the batch_norm_normalize_forward style (x/y [N walk, C block 1], per-channel operands [C block 1], #[tile_grid(order = [C])]), with running_mean/running_var as the statistics; attach the spec in the lowering. BatchNorm3d's edge is rank 5 while the kernel addresses [N, C], so it hits the same rank question as 1nr.18.7 (span cannot combine with a walked/reduced N today); BatchNorm1d's [N, C] edge should match directly. Verify numerics against the PyTorch fixture before re-recording snapshots.

title: feat: DagCodegen::virtual_node — open a fused virtual-node group
description:
## Goal

Implement `DagCodegen::virtual_node` in `kernels/teeny-kernels/src/graph/optimizer/anduin/codegen.rs` (currently `todo!()`).

## Context

`codegen()` replays a `Trace` produced by `Trace::trace_graph`. In every recursion frame the first event is `TraceEvent::VirtualNode { nodes, level }` — Welder §3.1/Fig. 5's *virtual node*: the set of original `NodeId`s the scheduler decided to fuse into one kernel boundary at `level`.

A virtual node is essentially a **sub-DAG of the original lowering `Dag`**: `nodes` is an ordered list of indices into the un-fused `Dag<Box<dyn ExecutableOp>>` passed to `DagCodegen::new`. Singleton groups (`nodes.len() == 1`) are valid — a node not fused with anything is still viewed from `level` as itself.

## Deliverable

Open a new in-progress fused group in `DagCodegen` state:
- record `nodes` and `level`
- initialize the builder that subsequent `allocate` / `load_tiles` / `compute_tile` / `store_tiles` calls will populate
- ensure nested virtual nodes (from recursive `trace_graph` frames) don't clobber each other

## Blockers

- teenygrad-1nr.1 — real kernel synthesis needs `Tile<D>` composition, not pointer-in/pointer-out splicing

## References

- `anduin/codegen.rs` (`ExecuteDevice::virtual_node`, `DagCodegen` stub)
- `anduin/trace.rs` (`TraceEvent::VirtualNode`, `Trace::trace_graph`)
- teenygrad-1nr.6 — structural trace/codegen scaffold (shipped)
- `TILE_GRAPH_SCHEDULING_PLAN.md` §3.3 / §4.2
close_reason: Closed together with the teenygrad-1nr epic (Welder-style TileGraph scheduler)

comments.author: Arshad Mahmood
comments.text:
Simple-case algorithm (flat unary elementwise virtual node):

Codegen is driven by each member's KernelTileSpec / GridSpec plus the schedule's resolved TileConfig — not the kernel constructor's default block size.

From the winning TileConfig on the virtual node's output edge:
- BLOCK_SIZE = the resolved TileDim::Fixed tile extent (scheduler's choice)
- n_elements = runtime i32 from tile_spec outputs extent_param (usually "n_elements", product of output shape)
- launch grid = cdiv(n_elements, BLOCK_SIZE) on the axis grid_spec() names (today GridDim::X)

virtual_node opens the fused group and records these values for wrapper emission.

The wrapper (not each compute_tile) owns the pid decode once:
  pid = program_id(X)
  offsets = arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE) + pid * BLOCK_SIZE
  in_bounds = offsets.lt(n_elements)

See anduin/codegen.rs module doc "Flat elementwise virtual nodes".

title: Propagate (Welder-style backward tile-shape inference) for TileGraph, via revived KernelTileSpec metadata
description:
## Goal

Implement Welder §3.1/§3.2's `Propagate` (backward tile-shape inference)
for `TileGraph` (`kernels/teeny-kernels/src/graph/optimizer/anduin/tile_graph/mod.rs`),
completing the last missing primitive from `TILE_GRAPH_SCHEDULING_PLAN.md`'s
gap analysis (`SetConnect`/`ExtractSubgraph`/`MemFootprint`/`MemTraffic`/
`Profiler` are already done). This unblocks `SubGraphTiling`/`GraphConnecting`
(Fig. 7), the two-step scheduler `Anduin::optimize` currently stubs with
`todo!()`.

## Design decision: revive `KernelTileSpec`, not a `TilePropagationKind` enum

Two approaches were evaluated (see `TILE_GRAPH_SCHEDULING_PLAN.md`'s
"`Propagate` implementation plan" section for the fuller writeup):

1. A `TilePropagationKind` enum (`Pointwise`/`Reduction`/`SlidingWindow`/
   `MatMul`/`Opaque`) with one hand-written backward-shape formula per
   category, tagged per `TritonLowering` match arm.
2. Reviving `KernelTileSpec`/`TensorTileSpec`/`TileAxisBinding`/`TileWindow`
   — declarative per-kernel, per-tensor, per-axis metadata that already
   existed on this branch's history and was fully implemented, tested, and
   then removed (`kernels/teeny-triton/src/tile.rs`,
   `kernels/teeny-kernels/src/graph/optimizer/propagate.rs`, deleted at
   `84ca6eedf^`; see `git show 84ca6eedf^:kernels/teeny-triton/src/tile.rs`
   for the full prior implementation, and `4859fc7fb`/`34af1e505`/
   `9f6874d56`/`65dfe6d5e` for the commits that built it up incrementally
   under the `teenygrad-3w0` epic).

**Decision: revive (2).** Its actual propagation algorithm
(`propagate_within_kernel`) isn't per-category formulas at all — it's name
matching: each axis declares an `extent_param` name, and any two axes
(across any tensors, any ops) sharing a name are the same free variable.
Seeding an output tile's axis values resolves every axis sharing those
names for free — this covers Pointwise and MatMul-shaped ops (e.g.
`matmul_forward`'s `a_ptr`/`c_ptr` both declaring an axis named `"M"`) with
*no* formula at all. Only the windowed/conv case needs actual arithmetic
(`TileWindow`'s `(block-1)*stride + kernel_size`), and that's one generic
formula driven by three declared const names, not a per-op-category Rust
function. This is a materially smaller and better-precedented surface than
five hand-written formulas.

## Why it was removed, and why that doesn't block reviving it

Two separate commits, for two different reasons — worth being precise
since only one of them actually indicts anything about this design:

- `431230501` removed Anduin's hand-coded fusion strategies
  (`PointwiseFuse`/`TileFuse`/`ReduceFuse`/`SharedTransposeFuse`) as
  pattern-matchers on specific `Op` shapes, not Welder's actual algorithm.
  At this point `propagate.rs` (the graph-walk half) was explicitly
  **kept** — its commit message: "it's real algorithm infrastructure, not
  a hand-coded pattern."
- `84ca6eedf` removed everything else. Real reason: the *separate*
  `#[tile(...)]` attribute macro also auto-generated index arithmetic
  **into the compiled kernel body itself**, which doesn't compose when a
  kernel is called as a tile-op from inside another kernel's body — index
  arithmetic belongs in a wrapper, not baked into each composed function
  (`teenygrad-1nr.1`'s design). Contributing factor: "this metadata had no
  consumer anywhere in the codebase, not even Anduin."

Neither reason indicts the *metadata + name-matching propagation* design
itself. This issue revives only that half — `KernelTileSpec` as pure,
declarative, hand-authored metadata consumed by `TileGraph::propagate`,
never driving kernel-body codegen. The `#[tile(...)]` attribute macro and
its auto-generated index-arithmetic prelude are explicitly **not** being
revived; specs are constructed by hand (plain `const` values) per op we
choose to cover, same as the original's actual coverage was hand-authored
per kernel (`#[tile(...)]` only *parsed* the declarations, it didn't derive
them).

## What Welder's own reference implementation does, and why we don't port it directly

Read against `../Welder/python/welder/{graph.py,shape_inference/{te.py,common.py}}`.
Welder's real `Propagate` walks a TVM tensor-expression (TE) — a symbolic
array-comprehension IR — extracting each input's *symbolic index
expression* from the op body, then runs backward interval-bound
propagation (`ConstIntBound`) over those expressions via TVM's arithmetic
analyzer. Fully generic (treats pointwise/reduction/conv identically) but
only because every op is already expressed in that symbolic form. We have
no TE-equivalent (`teeny-triton` kernels are opaque compiled source, not a
symbolic IR to walk) — building one would be materially bigger than this
feature. `KernelTileSpec`'s name-matching is the right-sized analogue:
hand-declared correspondence instead of derived-by-walking-an-expression-tree.

One thing the reference implementation confirms is *correct*, not a gap:
reduction axes with no output-side name correspondence (e.g. GEMM's `K`)
are supposed to stay unresolved by `Propagate` — Welder's own `raxis` is
resolved one layer upstream (TE construction), and its tiling *search*
(not `Propagate`) chooses the reduction tile size independently. The prior
`KernelTileSpec` implementation already got this right and tested it
(`propagate_within_kernel_gemm_resolves_m_and_n_not_k`) — this is not a
"partial reduction / rstep" non-goal to defer, it's the intended behavior.

## Scope

1. **Types** (revived, adapted for the `EdgeId`-arena `TileGraph`, in
   `core/teeny-core` since `ExecutableOp` needs to name them):
   `TileAxisBinding { dim, block_const, extent_param, window: Option<TileWindow> }`,
   `TileWindow { stride_const, pad_const, kernel_size_const }`,
   `TensorTileSpec { param, rank, axes, reduction_axis, untiled_dims }`,
   `KernelTileSpec { inputs, outputs, loop_spec: Option<TileLoopSpec> }`
   (`TileLoopSpec`/`TileCarryBinding` can be deferred — flash-attn-style
   loop-carried state isn't needed for a first cut).
2. **`ExecutableOp::tile_spec(&self) -> Option<KernelTileSpec>`** — new
   default method, `None` default (= hard boundary, matches the old
   `propagate_graph`'s "no spec = stop cleanly" behavior, and doubles as
   the `Opaque` case from the enum approach without needing a variant for
   it).
3. **`KernelExecutable` gains a `tile_spec: Option<KernelTileSpec>` field**,
   set at `TritonLowering` construction time (same reasoning as the
   `TilePropagationKind` plan: `&Op`'s static fields, e.g. conv's
   kernel/stride/padding, are in scope at each match arm before they're
   erased — no `RuntimeOp::as_any` addition needed). Tag a representative
   subset first (pointwise identity case, matmul/gemm's M/N-not-K case,
   one windowed/pooling case) rather than all ~40+ arms — coverage was
   always meant to be incremental (the original only ever covered
   `elu_forward`/`matmul_forward`/`conv2d_forward`/`flash_attention2_forward`).
4. **`TileOp` gains its resolved `tile_spec`**, populated in `from_dag`
   from `node.value.tile_spec()`.
5. **`TileGraph::propagate(nodes: &[NodeId], output_tiles: &HashMap<EdgeId, TileEdgeShape>) -> TileConfig`**
   — the graph-walk half (`propagate_graph`'s equivalent), reworked for the
   arena: walks `nodes` in reverse topological order; at each node with a
   declared `tile_spec`, resolves axis names from its already-known output
   tile (name-matching, `TileWindow`'s formula for windowed axes), and
   writes each resolved input tile into `TileConfig` keyed by that
   specific incoming `EdgeId` (not `NodeId` — preserves the same
   per-edge-can-differ property `TileEdge::memory_level` already has; see
   the plan doc for why this is a deliberate choice, not an oversight). A
   node with no `tile_spec`, or whose declared axis count doesn't line up,
   is a hard boundary — matches `propagate_graph`'s degrade-cleanly design,
   improved on the original since our arena already has precise per-`EdgeId`
   producer/consumer wiring (no more `inputs.len() == spec.inputs.len()`
   positional-correspondence assumption needed).
   `TileConfig { tiles: HashMap<EdgeId, TileEdgeShape> }` (already specified
   in the plan doc).

## Explicit non-goals (carried over, still real gaps)

- `Op::Custom`/`CustomOp` has no matching backward-shape contract — stays a
  hard boundary (`tile_spec() -> None`) until `CustomOp` itself grows one.
- Reshape/Transpose/Concat/Slice have no spec shape yet — hard boundary for
  now, plausible future extension.
- Coverage is opt-in per kernel by construction (same as the original) —
  most ops will have `tile_spec() -> None` until explicitly annotated.
  This issue does not attempt exhaustive coverage.
- `TileLoopSpec`/`TileCarryBinding` (flash-attn's loop-carried
  accumulators) deferred — no consumer needs them yet.
- `mem_footprint`/`mem_traffic` teaching them to accept a `TileConfig` for
  tiled-rather-than-full-shape accuracy is a separate follow-up, not
  included here.

## References

- `TILE_GRAPH_SCHEDULING_PLAN.md` — full design writeup, gap-analysis table,
  build order.
- `../Welder/python/welder/{graph.py,bestfit.py,shape_inference/{te.py,common.py,antares.py}}`
  — reference implementation read for this design.
- `git show 84ca6eedf^:kernels/teeny-triton/src/tile.rs` and
  `84ca6eedf^:kernels/teeny-kernels/src/graph/optimizer/propagate.rs` —
  full prior implementation being revived (deleted, not stubbed).
- Commits `34af1e505`/`9f6874d56`/`65dfe6d5e`/`4859fc7fb` (build-up),
  `431230501`/`84ca6eedf` (removal) — history of the prior attempt.
notes: Superseded by the v2 TileGraph rewrite (9b9f58b28), which deleted this implementation along with builder.rs, memory.rs, propagate.rs, search.rs and sub_graph_tiling.rs. The algorithm is being re-landed against v2 by teenygrad-1nr.25 - do not assume this code exists in the tree. Left closed because the design decisions recorded here still hold; only the code was removed.
close_reason:
Implemented, deviating from the issue's own TilePropagationKind-enum sketch:
revived KernelTileSpec (name-matching, not per-category formulas) after
finding a fuller, already-tested prior attempt in git history
(kernels/teeny-triton/src/tile.rs, deleted 84ca6eedf^). See
TILE_GRAPH_SCHEDULING_PLAN.md's "Propagate (shipped, teenygrad-1nr.2)"
section for the final design.

Shipped: core/teeny-core/src/model/tile_spec.rs (TileWindow/TileAxisBinding/
TensorTileSpec/KernelTileSpec), ExecutableOp::tile_spec() default method,
KernelExecutable.tile_spec field (threaded through all ~25 construction
sites), TileOp.tile_spec (from_dag), TileGraph::propagate + TileConfig
(EdgeId-keyed) in tile_graph/mod.rs, 5 new tests. Two ops tagged as a
first proof-of-concept slice: Op::Relu (RELU_TILE_SPEC) and
Op::MatMul/Op::Gemm (MATMUL_TILE_SPEC, M/N resolved, K correctly left at
full extent).

Deferred, as scoped: TileWindow not yet consumed by propagate (matches
the original's own scope -- it was never wired into propagate_within_kernel
either), coverage beyond Relu/MatMul, Op::Custom support, mem_footprint/
mem_traffic accepting a TileConfig.

cargo check --workspace --exclude teeny-cli clean; teeny-core + teeny-kernels
test suites pass (only the pre-existing Anduin::optimize todo!() failure,
unrelated); clippy clean.

## Goal

Implement `DagCodegen::compute_tile` in `kernels/teeny-kernels/src/graph/optimizer/anduin/codegen.rs` (currently `todo!()`).

At the top of the memory hierarchy, `Trace::trace_graph` emits `TraceEvent::ComputeTile { node }` for each original Dag node not handled by a child recursion. This is the register-level fusion step: inline one operator-tile into the virtual node's composed kernel body.

- handle grid compatibility between constituent ops (see teenygrad-1nr.17 when grids disagree)

- `DagCodegen::load_tiles` (inputs in workspace)

title: revive propagate/mem_footprint/mem_traffic on the v2 TileGraph
description:
## Goal

Bring `propagate`, `mem_footprint`, `mem_traffic`, `boundary_edges`, `extract_subgraph`,
`sub_graph_tiling` and `enumerate_subtiles` back onto the v2 `TileGraph`. Blocker for
every other issue in this group — they all describe changes to code that does not
currently exist in the tree.

## Current state

The v2 rewrite (`9b9f58b28`, "scaffold v2 TileGraph with incremental node wiring")
deleted the whole v1 submodule: `builder.rs`, `memory.rs`, `propagate.rs`, `search.rs`,
`sub_graph_tiling.rs` and most of `mod.rs`, under
`kernels/teeny-kernels/src/graph/optimizer/anduin/tile_graph/`. All recoverable with
`git show 9b9f58b28^:<path>`.

What survives in the tree is stubs plus doc comments that still describe the deleted
contracts:

- `anduin/schedule.rs`, `anduin/profile.rs`, `anduin/trace.rs` — one `todo!()` each.
- `anduin/codegen.rs` — five `todo!()`s.
- `anduin/mod.rs:117` — `todo!("teenygrad-1nr: implement Anduin::schedule")`.

Five lib tests fail on those stubs today
(`anduin::tests::*`, `anduin::codegen::tests::test_codegen_pointwise_virtual_node`).

v2 `TileGraph` (`tile_graph/mod.rs`) currently has `from_dag`, `add_placeholder`,
`add_ir_node`, `add_output`, `connect_inputs`, `set_port_metadata` and per-node
`shapes`/`dtypes` — but no edge arena, no `TileEdge`, no `TileDim`, no memory levels,
and no tile config.

## Scope

Re-land the deleted algorithms against v2's node/edge model. This is a port, not a
redesign: keep the v1 semantics except where `teenygrad-1nr.26`/`.27` explicitly
change them.

Note `teenygrad-1nr.2` (the original propagate issue) is CLOSED — it delivered the
code that `9b9f58b28` then deleted. This issue is the revival, not a reopen.

## Acceptance

- The five failing `anduin::*` lib tests pass again.
- `TileGraph::propagate` resolves the same tile config as v1 for the pointwise and
  conv+bn+silu graphs in `anduin/mod.rs`'s tests.
- No new `todo!()` left in `schedule.rs`/`profile.rs`/`trace.rs`.
notes:
In progress on feature/1nr.25-revive-propagate. Increment 1 of 5 landed as 5e1589ec3.

Sizing: 9b9f58b28 deleted ~3,230 lines across the v1 tile_graph submodule (builder 466, memory 424, mod 565, propagate 457, search 563, sub_graph_tiling 371, testing 174, types 213). v2 has 396 lines (mod 318, node 78) and, before this increment, no tile vocabulary at all.

The one structural decision the port turns on: in v1 an EdgeId identified a global edge held in an arena beside its producer and consumer, so TileConfig could be HashMap<EdgeId, _>. v2 has no arena -- edges live inside the nodes they touch and an EdgeId is a port index, so EdgeId(0) means something different on every node. Tiles are now keyed by ValueId (producing node + output port), which is what identifies a value in v2 and is already the pair v2 uses when wiring inputs. Reintroducing v1's arena alongside v2's embedded edges was rejected: two representations of the same wiring have to be hand-synced.

Memory level moved from the edge record to the config beside the shape, since v2's Edge is a Copy 4-tuple used as a map key and a level is a property of a scheduling decision, not of the wiring.

Increment 1 (done): types.rs ported -- TileDim, TileShape, to_tile_shape, shape_byte_size, TileConfig, SubGraphTilingResult, ValueId. Node gains tile_spec and from_dag carries each op's declared spec across; it already had the ExecutableOp and read shape/dtype from it while discarding the spec, so every node was a boundary regardless of what its kernel declared. NodeId/EdgeId gained Ord for deterministic config iteration. Eight tests, one following a declaration along its whole path from the kernel attribute to the node.

Remaining increments:
2. propagate (v1 propagate.rs, 457 lines) -- resolve_inputs already exists in teeny-kernels from 1iy.2, so this is the graph-walking half.
3. memory: mem_footprint, mem_traffic, boundary_edges (v1 memory.rs, 424 lines).
4. extract_subgraph, sub_graph_tiling, enumerate_subtiles (v1 search.rs 563 + sub_graph_tiling.rs 371).
5. the schedule.rs/profile.rs/trace.rs todo!()s, and the five failing anduin lib tests.

Workspace 414/11 -> 421/11 after increment 1; the five anduin stubs still fail on todo!() as expected.

The multi-input rung could not test it because propagate does not exist on v2 yet, so it needs a test when increment 2 lands.

title: feat: TileDim::Sym carries an optional max extent
description:
## Goal

Give `TileDim::Sym` an optional upper bound so a later consumer can ask for a
*pessimistic* extent instead of the single optimistic one baked in today.

```rust
enum TileDim {
    Fixed(usize),
    Sym { name: String, max: Option<usize> },
}
```

Mechanical type change only — **no behaviour change in this issue**. Every existing
`Sym`-handling site keeps its current answer by ignoring `max`. `teenygrad-1nr.27`
makes footprint actually read it.

## Why the bound has to live on the dim

A dynamic axis is not resolvable anywhere else in the pipeline:

- `to_tile_shape` (`9b9f58b28^:.../tile_graph/types.rs:51`) maps graph `Shape`'s
  `None` straight to `TileDim::Sym(format!("n{node}d{axis}"))` — the graph-level
  `Shape = Vec<Option<usize>>` carries no extent for a `None` slot at all.
- `enumerate_subtiles` explicitly cannot enumerate a `Sym` axis: *"A `TileDim::Sym`
  (dynamic) axis isn't enumerable this way and is left unchanged in every candidate."*
  So a dynamic dim stays `Sym` end to end.

## Scope

- Add the variant field, default `max: None` at every construction site.
- Update `to_tile_shape`, `shape_byte_size`, `score_candidate_tile`,
  `SearchAxis::ladder` and the `propagate` fallbacks to the new shape, all preserving
  today's answers.
- `Sym`'s `PartialEq`/`Hash` must key on `name` only — two references to the same
  axis must stay equal regardless of whether one carries a bound.

## Acceptance

- No behavioural diff: every `anduin::*` test result identical before and after.
- `max` is populated nowhere yet; that's `teenygrad-1nr.28`.

Blocked on `teenygrad-1nr.25`.

title: fix: mem_footprint under-counts dynamic axes, so dynamic-batch models always fuse
description:
## Problem

Three sites decide what an unresolved/dynamic tile axis is worth, and they disagree in
*direction*. The disagreement is not two independent choices — they compose on the same
axis, and the second silently cancels the first.

| site | dynamic / unresolved axis | direction |
|---|---|---|
| `propagate`, unresolved-axis fallback | **full extent** — *"never smaller than needed"* | over-estimate |
| `shape_byte_size` (`9b9f58b28^:.../types.rs:101`) | **1** — *"optimistic, never an overestimate"* | under-estimate |
| `score_candidate_tile` (`9b9f58b28^:.../search.rs:111-118`) | **1** | under-estimate |

`propagate` deliberately keeps an unresolved axis at full extent; `shape_byte_size`
then prices that full extent as 1.

## Why it matters

`9b9f58b28^:.../search.rs:107` is a hard fit check against real hardware, not a
heuristic:

```rust
if self.mem_footprint_with_config(nodes, &config) > capacity {
    return None;
}
```

`orin_nano`'s `SharedMemory` capacity is 96 KiB
(`testing/teeny-test/src/hardware_profile.rs`). Under-counting accepts a tile that
does not fit.

The batch axis is the structural worst case, because it can never be enumerated and is
therefore always priced at 1. For the conv+bn+silu group at `[N, 8, 32, 32]` f32:

```
N dynamic (Sym -> 1)   tile     32,768   peak(2 live)     65,536   FITS -> fuse
N = 2                  tile     65,536   peak(2 live)    131,072   too big -> no fuse
N = 64                 tile  2,097,152   peak(2 live)  4,194,304   too big -> no fuse

peak = 2 * 32,768 * N <= 98,304  =>  N <= 1.5
```

The group genuinely fits only at `N = 1`, and a dynamic batch reports exactly that —
so it always fuses. mnist's c1 output `[N, 6, 28, 28]` reads as 19% of shared memory
dynamically and 1225% at `N = 64`. This is the common path, not a corner:
`models/teeny-vision/tests/test_mnist_compile.rs:43` traces with
`vec![None, Some(1), Some(28), Some(28)]`.

## The optimistic convention is not simply wrong

For `mem_traffic` feeding `SimpleProfiler`'s *relative* ranking, a uniform under-count
largely cancels between candidates, and that intent is stated in still-live code at
`anduin/profile.rs:53-57`: *"optimistic, never pessimistic, about a candidate's cost,
same as `TileEdge::byte_size`'s dynamic-axis handling."*

The defect is that `shape_byte_size` is the shared core of **both** the comparative
question (traffic, ranking) and the absolute one (footprint vs. capacity). One
convention cannot serve both: ranking wants consistency, a fit check wants an upper
bound.

## Fix

Split the two questions rather than picking one global direction.

- **Footprint vs. capacity** takes an upper bound: `Sym { max: Some(n) }` prices as
  `n`; `Sym { max: None }` means *unknown extent*, which the fit check must treat as
  **does not fit** (refuse to place the group below `DeviceMemory`). That matches
  `propagate`'s own stance and is the only sound reading of an unbounded axis.
- **Traffic / score** keep `Sym => 1` unchanged, with the `profile.rs` comment updated
  to say *why* the two now differ.

Introduce a distinct entry point (e.g. `shape_byte_size_upper` vs.
`shape_byte_size_est`) so the choice is explicit at each call site rather than implied.

## Acceptance

- A group containing an unbounded `Sym` axis is never placed below `DeviceMemory`.
- A group whose `Sym` axes all carry `max` is judged against those bounds.
- Traffic/score numbers unchanged from v1 for fully-static graphs.
- Regression test: conv+bn+silu traced with `None` batch must NOT fuse at
  `SharedMemory` (today it does), while the same graph at `Some(1)` still does.

Blocked on `teenygrad-1nr.26`.
close_reason: Closed together with the teenygrad-1nr epic (Welder-style TileGraph scheduler)

title: feat: populate TileDim::Sym max extents from caller-supplied shape hints
description:
## Goal

Populate `TileDim::Sym { max }` so dynamic-shape models can fuse again.

## Why this is needed, not optional

`teenygrad-1nr.27` makes an unbounded `Sym` axis mean "does not fit". Nothing populates
`max` at that point, so *every* model traced with a dynamic dim — the idiom in this
repo, e.g. `models/teeny-vision/tests/test_mnist_compile.rs:43` — loses all
sub-`DeviceMemory` fusion. `.27` is the safe half; this is the half that restores
capability.

## Scope

Thread a caller-supplied hint into the pipeline and use it in `to_tile_shape`:

```rust
Anduin::schedule(&dag, &hardware, &ShapeHints { max_batch: 64, .. })
```

Open design points to settle in this issue:

- **Granularity.** A single `max_batch`, or a per-axis map keyed by the same
  `n{node}d{axis}` name `to_tile_shape` already generates? The latter is more general
  and costs little, since the name already exists.
- **Where it enters.** `GraphOptimizer::optimize`'s signature, `HardwareProfile`, or a
  new argument to `Anduin::schedule`. `optimize` is a trait method shared with future
  strategies, so adding there has the widest blast radius.
- **Default.** No hints supplied must stay safe — i.e. behave exactly as `.27`
  (refuse), never silently fall back to 1.

## Acceptance

- With a hint supplied, conv+bn+silu traced with `None` batch produces the same
  schedule as the same graph traced with that concrete batch.
- With no hint, behaviour is identical to `teenygrad-1nr.27`.

Blocked on `teenygrad-1nr.27`.

title: feat: #[tile(..)] can express a strided/padded window; populate it on conv/pool specs
description:
## Problem

`TileWindow` exists and is **never constructed anywhere in the repo**.

```rust
pub struct TileWindow {
    pub stride_const: &'static str,
    pub pad_const: &'static str,
    pub kernel_size_const: &'static str,
}
```

`core/teeny-core/src/model/tile_spec.rs:75`. Verified zero call sites outside its own
definition and the `pub use` in `model/mod.rs:31`. `#[tiled_kernel]` hardcodes
`window: None` at `macros/teeny-macros/src/macros/tiled_kernel.rs:835` and `:915`, and
the module doc already concedes it: *"carried over from the original for fidelity but
is **not yet consumed by `TileGraph::propagate`**"*.

## Consequence for conv today

`conv2d_forward` (`kernels/teeny-kernels/src/nn/conv/conv2d.rs:65-74`) declares:

```rust
#[tile(name = "H",  extent = H)]  #[tile(name = "W",  extent = W)]   x_ptr
#[tile(name = "OH", extent = OH)] #[tile(name = "OW", block = BLOCK_OW, extent = OW)] y_ptr
```

Propagation is pure name-matching — two axes sharing an `extent_param` are the same
free variable. `H`/`W` and `OH`/`OW` are different names and there is no window to
relate them, so seeding `OW` resolves nothing on `x_ptr`, and the input tile falls back
to its full extent. Conservative, but it means conv is effectively untileable.

## Scope

Two halves, deliberately in one issue because the syntax is unusable until something
emits it:

1. **Extend `#[tile(...)]`** to accept a window, naming the three const generics:
   `#[tile(name = "H", extent = H, window(stride = STRIDE_H, pad = PAD_H, kernel = KH))]`
   and have `#[tiled_kernel]`'s generated `tile_spec()` emit a real `TileWindow`
   instead of `None`.
2. **Populate it** on the windowed kernels: `conv1d_forward`, `conv2d_forward`,
   `conv3d_forward`, and the pooling kernels.

Naming question to settle here: should a windowed input axis reuse the *output* axis's
`extent_param` (so `x_ptr`'s spatial axis is named `OH`, and the window explains the
difference), or keep `H` and have the window carry both names? The first keeps
name-matching as the single resolution mechanism; the second is more literal about the
kernel signature.

## Acceptance

- `Conv2dForward::<f32>::tile_spec()` returns a spec whose `x_ptr` spatial axes carry
  `Some(TileWindow { .. })` naming `STRIDE_H`/`PAD_H`/`KH` (and the W equivalents).
- No consumer yet — `propagate` still ignores it. That's `teenygrad-1nr.30`.
- Existing specs without a window are byte-identical.
close_reason: Superseded by teenygrad-1tl.7, which absorbs both halves intact -- the #[tile(..) ] window syntax extension and the population across conv 1/2/3d plus the nine pools -- along with the naming question (reuse the output axis's extent_param, or keep H and let the window carry both names) and the acceptance criteria. teenygrad-1nr.30 has been re-pointed to block on 1tl.7.

title: EnumerateSubtiles (Welder §4.1 Roller-style tile-shape search) — power-of-2 candidates only
description:
## Goal

Implement Welder §4.1's `EnumerateSubtiles` — the expanding tile-shape
search `SubGraphTiling` (Fig. 7) calls per node to produce candidate
output-tile shapes. Each candidate gets fed through the now-shipped
`TileGraph::propagate` (teenygrad-1nr.2) into a `TileConfig`, filtered by
the now-shipped `MemFootprint`, and ranked by `MemTraffic`/`Profiler`
(teenygrad-1nr's earlier work) — this is the last missing input before
`SubGraphTiling`/`GraphConnecting` themselves can be built. See
`TILE_GRAPH_SCHEDULING_PLAN.md`, "Suggested implementation order" items 4-5.

## Design grounding: Welder's own reference implementation

Read against `../Welder/python/welder/policy/default.py`, not just the
paper text:

- **`get_base_tile`** — starts from an all-1s tile and grows one axis-factor
  at a time while `compute_workload_per_item` (which calls
  `node.propogate_inputs` — our `TileGraph::propagate`) doesn't get worse.
  Gives the smallest tile that avoids redundant computation; the search's
  starting point.
- **`DFS_smem_tile`** — the actual `EnumerateSubtiles`. From the base tile,
  an expanding search: per-axis candidate step values are
  `get_all_factors(n)` (every divisor of the axis extent), with a handful
  of powers of two (`[2, 4, 8, 16, 32]`) spliced in as extra candidates
  between the base tile and the top of the range (`default.py:64-70`).
  Explores neighboring tile shapes via a priority queue ordered by
  `(traffic + 1) * num_wave` (lower is better), bumping one axis to its
  next candidate step per step; each visited shape is validated against
  memory capacity; capped at 2000 visited tiles (`default.py:84`); returns
  valid candidates sorted by score, later truncated to top-K by the caller.

## Key deviation: power-of-2-only candidates, not arbitrary divisors

Welder's own candidate set is "any divisor of the axis extent," with
power-of-2 only as a secondary enrichment (explicitly, per its own comment
at `default.py:153-154`: "use factor first... for large prime number,
which is rare case, use power of 2"). **We can't use arbitrary divisors.**
Every `BLOCK_*`-style compile-time tile constant in this codebase is
already, pervasively, required to be a power of two — this isn't a new
constraint this issue introduces, it's already load-bearing throughout:

- `kernels/teeny-kernels/src/graph/mod.rs:1880` and `:2437` —
  `n_cols.next_power_of_two()` computed at `TritonLowering` time for
  softmax/reduction-shaped kernels.
- Doc comments stating the same requirement on real kernels:
  `nn/attention/flash_attn2.rs:29` ("HEAD_DIM must be a power of two"),
  `nn/norm/groupnorm.rs:30` ("BLOCK_NL must be ... a power of two"),
  `nn/activation/softmax.rs:35`, and the loss kernels
  `nn/loss/{embedding,nll,ranking}.rs` ("`BLOCK_SIZE` must equal
  `next_power_of_two(n_dim)`").

This traces back to Triton's own `tl.arange`/vectorized `tl.load`/`tl.store`
requiring power-of-2 extents. So this issue's `EnumerateSubtiles` must
restrict its per-axis candidate set to powers of two only —
`{1, 2, 4, 8, ..., next_power_of_two(extent)}` — not Welder's full divisor
set. This is actually a *smaller, simpler* search space (O(log extent)
candidates per axis instead of O(divisor count)), at the cost of needing
boundary masking when a candidate tile doesn't evenly divide the extent —
already an established, already-handled pattern in this codebase (the
`next_power_of_two` kernels above all do exactly this), not a new problem
to solve.

Existing hand-coded prior art this feature is aimed at eventually
generalizing (not touched by this issue — flagged for context only):
`pick_gemm_tile_sizes` (`kernels/teeny-kernels/src/graph/mod.rs:695`) picks
GEMM's `BLOCK_M`/`BLOCK_N`/`BLOCK_K` from a small hardcoded lookup table
over `{8, 16, 32, 64, 128}` based on `M`/`N`/`K`'s magnitude — a fixed
heuristic, not a footprint/traffic-driven search. Same category of
hand-coded pattern-matching the parent epic (`teenygrad-1nr`) already
flagged Anduin's old fusion strategies for.

## Scope

1. Per-axis candidate generation: the power-of-2 ladder
   `1, 2, 4, ..., next_power_of_two(extent)` for each axis of a node's full
   (untiled) shape — the direct analogue of Welder's `get_all_factors`
   candidate list, restricted as above. A `TileDim::Sym` (dynamic) axis
   isn't enumerable this way; treat it as a hard boundary (not tiled by
   this search), consistent with how dynamic axes are already handled
   elsewhere in `TileGraph` (`TileEdge::byte_size`, `mem_footprint`).
2. Base-tile selection: adapt Welder's `get_base_tile` to use our own
   `TileGraph::propagate` + `mem_traffic` (both shipped) in place of
   `compute_workload_per_item`.
3. Expanding search: adapt `DFS_smem_tile`'s priority-queue neighbor
   expansion, using `TileGraph::mem_footprint` (validity — must fit a
   target `MemoryLevel`'s capacity from `HardwareProfile`) and
   `TileGraph::mem_traffic`/`Profiler` (scoring), both already shipped, in
   place of Welder's `td.valid`/`td.traffic`.
4. Return candidate output-tile shapes (`TileEdgeShape`s, or a small
   ranked `Vec` of them) for `SubGraphTiling` (not yet built) to consume —
   this issue does not build `SubGraphTiling`/`GraphConnecting` itself.

## Explicit non-goals

- **Reduction-step (`rstep`) search** — Welder's `_assign_reduce_step`/
  `_expand_reduce_axis`, a related but separate concern.
  `TileGraph::propagate` (teenygrad-1nr.2) already documents reduction axes
  as always resolving to full extent; this issue doesn't change that. A
  follow-up issue if/when partial-reduction tiling matters.
- **Block/warp assignment, rasterization, output striding** — Welder's
  `assign_block_size`/`plan_rasterization`/`output_strides_map`
  (§4.2/§4.3 concerns), out of scope here.
- **Real-hardware validation loop** — `GraphConnecting`'s step 5 (Fig. 7),
  already flagged as separate in the parent epic.
- **Replacing `pick_gemm_tile_sizes`** — cited above as related prior art,
  not something this issue touches.

## References

- `../Welder/python/welder/policy/default.py` (`get_base_tile`,
  `DFS_smem_tile`, `get_node_reduce_step_candidates`,
  `compute_workload_per_item`) and `policy/common.py`
  (`get_all_factors`/`factorize`) — reference implementation.
- `TILE_GRAPH_SCHEDULING_PLAN.md` — tracking doc, gap analysis, "Suggested
  implementation order."
- teenygrad-1nr.2 (closed) — `TileGraph::propagate`/`TileConfig`, direct
  dependency of this issue's scoring step.
notes: Superseded by the v2 TileGraph rewrite (9b9f58b28), which deleted this implementation along with builder.rs, memory.rs, propagate.rs, search.rs and sub_graph_tiling.rs. The algorithm is being re-landed against v2 by teenygrad-1nr.25 - do not assume this code exists in the tree. Left closed because the design decisions recorded here still hold; only the code was removed.
close_reason:
Implemented as TileGraph::enumerate_subtiles (kernels/teeny-kernels/src/graph/optimizer/anduin/tile_graph/mod.rs).

Base-tile growth (per-axis greedy, mirroring Welder's get_base_tile) +
expanding neighbor search (mirroring DFS_smem_tile), scored by MemTraffic
per output element via propagate + the new mem_traffic_with_config, pruned
by the new mem_footprint_with_config against a capacity. Candidate steps
per axis restricted to the power-of-two ladder (1, 2, ..., next_power_of_two
(extent)) as specified -- confirmed grounded in real, already-load-bearing
codebase convention (next_power_of_two call sites in TritonLowering,
BLOCK_SIZE-must-be-a-power-of-two doc comments across flash_attn2/
groupnorm/softmax/loss kernels), not an invented constraint. Per the user's
clarification: this only constrains candidate *block sizes*, not literal
axis divisibility -- an axis whose extent isn't itself a power of two still
gets covered via a masked/partial last tile elsewhere (already how the
existing next_power_of_two kernels handle it), which this search never
needs to compute or represent itself, only propose the block size.

Prerequisite discovered during implementation: mem_footprint/mem_traffic
needed config-aware variants (mem_footprint_with_config/
mem_traffic_with_config) to score a candidate's *tiled* size rather than
the full untiled shape -- this was flagged as an open question in both this
issue and 1nr.4, now resolved and shared by both.

4 new tests: power-of-two-only candidates, capacity never exceeded, dynamic
axis left unenumerated/unchanged, results sorted ascending by score.

cargo check --workspace clean, teeny-kernels test suite passes (62 tests,
only the pre-existing unrelated Anduin::optimize todo!() failure), clippy
clean, fmt clean.

title: feat: propagate consumes TileWindow — resolve a windowed axis via its receptive field
description:
## Goal

Teach `TileGraph::propagate` to resolve a windowed axis, so an output tile on a conv or
pool node yields the real input region that feeds it instead of falling back to the
full extent.

## The arithmetic is the easy part

This is **not** inverting `infer_output_shape`'s floor division. Given an output tile of
`block` elements along a windowed axis, the input region read is the receptive field:

```
input_extent = (block - 1) * stride + kernel
```

Forward, total, exact, no ambiguity and no candidate set — unlike whole-tensor reverse
inference (see `teenygrad-3fy`, where `s > 1` gives `s` candidates). The two ask
different questions: `Op::infer_input_shape` asks *which input extent produced this
output extent*, which many extents satisfy; tiling asks *which input elements does this
output tile read*, which has exactly one answer.

Do **not** reach for `Op::infer_input_shape`/`window_in_dim` here. They return
`s * (out - 1) + k - 2p`, and that `- 2p` is correct only when the tile is the whole
output, the one case where both ends of the region sit on the tensor's padded edges. An
interior tile touches no padding, so it needs the full receptive field. A 3x3 conv with
`p = 1, s = 1` and a block of 8 reads **10** input elements; `window_in_dim` says 8 —
right for the whole tensor, short by the 1-element halo at each end for a tile.

Padding does not enter the *extent*; it shifts the origin. In unpadded input
coordinates, for an output tile `[o0, o0 + block)` against a real axis extent `In`:

```
lo     = o0 * stride - padding                             // may be negative
hi     = (o0 + block - 1) * stride + kernel - padding      // exclusive; may exceed In
extent = hi - lo = (block - 1) * stride + kernel           // constant across tiles
pad_lo = max(0, -lo)
pad_hi = max(0, hi - In)
real   = [max(0, lo), min(In, hi))                         // what is actually read
```

`pad_lo`/`pad_hi` non-zero is what "the tensor is not big enough for this tile" actually
means: it is the edge tiles' share of the op's own padding, not a shortfall to fix.
Interior tiles want *halo* — real neighbouring data, `kernel - stride` of overlap per
step when `kernel > stride`, which is the redundancy Welder-style scheduling trades
against footprint. Edge tiles want *fill*. Both surface as "elements beyond my tile" and
are not the same thing.

A trailing partial tile of `block' < block` outputs reads `(block' - 1) * stride +
kernel`, so the last tile's region is smaller, not larger.

## Sourcing: Welder §3.1

This is Welder's `Propagate`, and the paper (Shi et al., *Welder: Scheduling Deep
Learning Memory Access via Tile-graph*, OSDI '23, p. 704) specifies both the method and
the direction of error:

> Once connected, most tiles in a tile-graph are correlated, which can be automatically
> inferred by propagating an output tile shape to the entire graph. This is achieved by
> using a chain of shape inferences from the output nodes to the inputs. For each
> operator-tile, the **dependent region** of the input tensor can be accurately
> determined by **analyzing its tensor expression** tile size. In cases where the input
> region may contain irregular patterns such as sparse or noncontinuous access (e.g.,
> `Gather` or **Convolution with strides**), our expression analysis provides a
> **conservative upper bound** as the input tile shape.

Two things to take from it. The region comes from evaluating the access function forward
over an output index range — Figure 4(a) shows a 3x3 conv taking a `[3x3xC]` input tile
for a `[1x1xC]` output tile, i.e. `(block - 1) * stride + kernel`. And where the region
cannot be described exactly, the answer must err **large**.

That second point is why `Op::infer_input_shape` is disqualified rather than merely
inconvenient: it returns the *smallest* consistent input by design (`teenygrad-3fy.2`),
which is conservative in the wrong direction for sizing anything.

Footprint is the consumer that makes this a correctness issue rather than an accuracy
one — §4.1: *"we add an infinite penalty if the total memory footprint of a given tile
configuration exceeds the memory capacity"*, and Figure 7 skips any config where
`MemFootprint(g) > level.capacity`. An estimate that errs low silently selects a tiling
that does not fit.

Note also what `MemFootprint` covers (p. 704): *"allocating all data tiles in a
topological order"* with bestfit — intermediates included, not just the propagated input
tiles. Propagation feeds footprint; it is not the whole of it.

## Scope

In `propagate`'s input-tile loop, where an axis's `extent_param` currently either
resolves by name or falls back to the full shape, add a third path: if the axis carries
`Some(TileWindow)` and its driving output axis is resolved, compute the extent above and
write it onto the innermost dim (same convention as the existing resolved path, with
flattened outer dims collapsing to 1).

Points to settle:

- **Where the window's consts come from.** `TileWindow` names `const` generics
  (`STRIDE_H`, `KH`, ...), and this metadata has no per-node parameter-value lookup —
  the same limitation `TileAxisBinding::divide_by` hit, which was solved by making the
  divisor a plain number resolved at `tile_spec()`-construction time. The cheapest
  consistent answer is to do the same: have `tile_spec()` bake in concrete values,
  since `Conv2dForward` already owns `self.kh`/`self.stride_h`/`self.g`.

  Worth noting where this differs from Welder structurally: it reads index maps off the
  *tensor expression*, which names each operand, so it never has to ask how many inputs
  a node has or how each is accessed. `TileWindow` is us reconstructing that metadata
  op by op. The same missing information is what blocks multi-input reverse inference in
  `teenygrad-3fy.5`.
- **Which output axis drives it**, once input and output axis names differ — depends on
  the naming decision made in `teenygrad-1nr.29`.
- **Clamping — but decide *which* question you are answering.** The region a boundary
  tile covers runs off both ends of the real axis, and the two consumers of this number
  want different answers:

  | question | answer | used by |
  |---|---|---|
  | how many real elements does this tile load? | clamped, `min(In, hi) - max(0, lo)` | `mem_traffic`, occupancy |
  | how large is the tile's staging buffer? | unclamped, `(block - 1) * stride + kernel` | `mem_footprint`, `SharedMemory` placement |

  Clamping the *buffer* under-sizes it at the edges, which only stays correct while the
  kernel masks its reads against global memory rather than staging a padded halo. This
  bead assumes masking — say so where the clamp is applied, because the assumption is
  invisible at the call site and silently wrong if a kernel ever materialises padding.

  When in doubt, round **up**: Welder's rule for any region it cannot describe exactly
  is a conservative upper bound, and footprint is compared against a hard capacity.

## Acceptance

- Propagating a `BLOCK_OW`-sized output tile through `conv2d_forward` resolves `x_ptr`'s
  W axis to `(BLOCK_OW - 1) * STRIDE_W + KW`, clamped to `W`, not to full `W`.
- The resolved extent does not depend on `PAD_W`: a padded and an unpadded conv with the
  same kernel and stride resolve the same input extent for the same block.
- `mem_footprint` for a conv group shrinks accordingly, and a conv+bn+silu group that
  previously could not be placed at `SharedMemory` on a static shape now can.
- Unwindowed specs behave exactly as before.

Blocked on `teenygrad-1nr.25` and `teenygrad-1nr.29`.

title: feat: node-level resident working-set term so loop_spec reaches the cost model
description:
## Goal

Give the cost model somewhere to put a kernel's loop-carried working set.

## Split out of teenygrad-1nr.12

That issue's own investigation concluded it was three separable pieces. Item 1
(revive `TileCarryBinding`/`TileLoopSpec` + `KernelTileSpec::loop_spec`) landed
with `teenygrad-1nr.18`. This is **item 2**, recorded here so closing `.12`
into the `teenygrad-1tl` ladder does not lose it.

## The problem, in that issue's own words

`acc`/`m_i`/`l_i` are kernel-body-local variables, never materialized as a
`TileEdge` — they never cross a pointer parameter. But
`mem_footprint_with_config`/`mem_traffic_with_config` are entirely
`EdgeId`-keyed (`TileConfig == HashMap<EdgeId, TileEdgeShape>`). There is no
notion anywhere in the cost model of "per-CTA working-set bytes not tied to
any edge".

So consuming `loop_spec` for anything beyond documentation needs a genuinely
new cost-model term — e.g. a node-level resident-working-set contribution
added into `sub_graph_tiling`'s capacity check alongside the edge-based
footprint. Not a hook into the existing functions, which have nowhere to put
it.

## Why it matters

For flash attention the per-CTA working set is `O(HEAD_DIM)`
(`acc`/`m_i`/`l_i`), not `O(N_CTX x HEAD_DIM)`. Without this term, a node whose
pointers are untagged falls back to full shape and the scheduler sees a working
set orders of magnitude too large. Cost-model *accuracy* is the whole value
here — there is no block-size choice for a search to make (see the note on the
current kernel in `teenygrad-1nr.12`).

## Blocked on

`teenygrad-1nr.25` — the cost model this extends does not currently exist in
the tree.

## Done when

A node-level working-set term exists, `loop_spec` feeds it, and a test shows a
loop-carried kernel costed at its real per-CTA residency rather than its full
input shape.

title: feat: graph-level attention Op + TritonLowering arm, so flash attention is reachable from Anduin
description:
## Goal

Make attention reachable from the graph pipeline: an `Op` variant plus a
`TritonLowering` arm.

## Split out of teenygrad-1nr.12

**Item 3** of that issue's three-way split, recorded here so closing `.12` into
the `teenygrad-1tl` ladder does not lose it.

## The finding

There is no `Op` variant for flash / scaled-dot-product attention, and no
lowering case for it. `TileGraph::from_dag` only ever sees
`Dag<Box<dyn ExecutableOp>>` nodes that `TritonLowering` produced from a
graph-level `Op`. So a complete, fully-wired `FLASH_ATTN2_TILE_SPEC` has
nowhere to attach — there is no node for the scheduler to ever see.

This means `teenygrad-1tl.11` can declare the kernel's tile axes and loop
carries, and that declaration is still unreachable from Anduin until this
lands. Worth knowing before anyone reads `.11`'s completion as "flash attention
is now schedulable".

## Scope note

This is a graph/lowering addition, not a tile-spec or scheduling change — it
sits outside `teenygrad-1nr`'s usual scope and is filed here only because
`.12`'s investigation is where it was found. Retarget it if a graph-layer epic
is a better home.

## Done when

A graph-level attention `Op` exists, `TritonLowering` lowers it to
`flash_attention2_forward`, and a `TileGraph` built from a graph containing it
has a node carrying that kernel's spec.

title: sub_graph_tiling — Welder §3.2 SubGraphTiling (Fig. 7): per-level tile-config search and recursion
description:
## Goal

Implement Welder Fig. 7's `SubGraphTiling(g, level, c)` — the recursive
half of the two-step scheduler, called by `GraphConnecting`/`schedule_graph`
(the other new sibling issue) to search for good tile configs at each
memory level and recurse upward. This is the piece that actually consumes
`EnumerateSubtiles` (teenygrad-1nr.3, not yet built — this issue depends on
it) and the already-shipped `TileGraph::propagate`/`TileConfig`
(teenygrad-1nr.2), `mem_footprint`, `mem_traffic`, and `extract_subgraph`.

## The paper's pseudocode (Fig. 7, re-verified against `osdi23-shi.pdf`)

```
Func SubGraphTiling(g:Graph, level:Memory, c:Config)
  configs = PriorityQueue();
  for subtile : EnumerateSubtiles(g, c) do
    config = Propagate(g, subtile);
    if MemFootprint(config) > level.capacity
      continue;
    configs.push(config, priority=MemTraffic(g));
  results = Dict();
  for config : TopK(configs, k) do
    // return empty sub-graph at top level to exit recursion
    subgraphs = unique([ExtractSubgraph(node, level+1) for node in g.nodes()]);
    for subgraph : subgraphs do
      subgraph_configs = SubGraphTiling(subgraph, level+1, config)
      results[config].append(subgraph_configs);
  return results;
```

## Mapping onto what's already shipped

- `EnumerateSubtiles(g, c)` → teenygrad-1nr.3 (not yet built; this issue is
  blocked on it). `c` (the paper's `Config`, an accumulated tile-shape
  constraint threaded down from the level below) maps naturally onto our
  already-shipped `TileGraph::propagate`'s own
  `output_tiles: &HashMap<EdgeId, TileEdgeShape>` parameter — `c` *is* that
  seed, carried from one recursion level into the next.
- `Propagate(g, subtile)` → `TileGraph::propagate(nodes, &output_tiles)`,
  already shipped (teenygrad-1nr.2), returns our `TileConfig`.
- `MemFootprint(config) > level.capacity` → `TileGraph::mem_footprint(nodes)`
  (already shipped) compared against `HardwareProfile`'s per-`MemoryLevel`
  `capacity` field (`core/teeny-core/src/device/hardware.rs`). Note: our
  `mem_footprint` doesn't yet take a `TileConfig` for tiled-rather-than-full
  sizing (documented non-goal on that method today) — this issue may need
  to extend it, or accept the full-shape approximation for a first cut;
  flag this as an open decision to resolve during implementation, not
  something to silently paper over.
- `MemTraffic(g)` (priority) → `TileGraph::mem_traffic(nodes)`, shipped.
  Same tiled-vs-full-shape caveat as above.
- `ExtractSubgraph(node, level+1)` → `TileGraph::extract_subgraph(node, level)`,
  shipped, returns `Vec<NodeId>` (a node set into the same graph, not a
  rebuilt one — see its own doc comment).
- `level+1` walks `MemoryLevelKind`'s hierarchy — already `Ord`-derived
  fast-to-slow (`Register < ... < HostMemory`), so "the next level up" is
  the next-slower `MemoryLevelKind`, sourced from
  `HardwareProfile::memory_levels`.
- `TopK(configs, k)` — needs a `k` parameter; no existing analogue, new.

## Open questions to resolve during implementation (the paper's pseudocode
## is terse here — don't silently guess past these)

1. **Recursion termination.** The paper's own comment says "return empty
   sub-graph at top level to exit recursion" — i.e. termination happens
   when `ExtractSubgraph` at the top memory level returns nothing new to
   recurse into (the whole graph is already one node at that point), not a
   fixed depth bound. Confirm this against `HardwareProfile::memory_levels`'
   actual ordering before implementing the loop condition.
2. **What `results[config]` is keyed by.** `Config`/`TileConfig` isn't
   obviously a natural `HashMap` key (it's essentially
   `HashMap<EdgeId, TileEdgeShape>`) — decide a concrete return shape for
   the Rust port rather than transliterating `Dict` literally. A
   `Vec<(TileConfig, Vec<TileConfig>)>` (config paired with its recursively
   collected sub-results) is a plausible starting point.
3. **Tiled vs. full-shape footprint/traffic** — see above; whichever way
   this resolves should probably also update `mem_footprint`/`mem_traffic`'s
   own doc comments (they currently say "still to add" for exactly this).

## Naming

Prefer `TileGraph::sub_graph_tiling` (direct snake_case translation,
matching the established `extract_subgraph`/`mem_footprint` convention) —
not a literal `SubGraphTiling` Rust name.

## Non-goals

- `EnumerateSubtiles` itself — separate issue (teenygrad-1nr.3), this issue
  only *consumes* it.
- `GraphConnecting`/`schedule_graph`'s outer loop and real-hardware
  `Profile` scoring — separate sibling issue.
- Actually rewriting the `Dag` into fused kernels — blocked on
  teenygrad-1nr.1 (the `Tile<D>` composition rework), unrelated to this
  issue's scheduling-only scope.

## References

- `osdi23-shi.pdf`, Fig. 7 (`SubGraphTiling`/`ExtractSubgraph` pseudocode).
- `TILE_GRAPH_SCHEDULING_PLAN.md` — tracking doc.
- teenygrad-1nr.2 (closed) — `Propagate`/`TileConfig`.
- teenygrad-1nr.3 — `EnumerateSubtiles`, this issue's direct dependency.
notes: Superseded by the v2 TileGraph rewrite (9b9f58b28), which deleted this implementation along with builder.rs, memory.rs, propagate.rs, search.rs and sub_graph_tiling.rs. The algorithm is being re-landed against v2 by teenygrad-1nr.25 - do not assume this code exists in the tree. Left closed because the design decisions recorded here still hold; only the code was removed.
close_reason:
Implemented as TileGraph::sub_graph_tiling + SubGraphTilingResult
(same file as 1nr.3).

One documented deviation from the paper, per this issue's own open
questions: always re-derives each recursion level's candidates fresh from
that level's own root via enumerate_subtiles, rather than threading the
paper's `c` (config chosen one level down) into the next level's search --
the pseudocode doesn't specify enough to port that literally, and even
Welder's own shipped policy (policy/default.py's emit_config) searches
once from a single base tile rather than implementing this literal
recursive threading. Recursion terminates at the top of HardwareProfile's
declared memory hierarchy (via a new next_memory_level helper), bounded by
the number of distinct declared MemoryLevelKinds, so it always halts.

4 new tests: returned configs never exceed the level's capacity,
no-children at the top of the hierarchy, recurses one level when a higher
level exists (and stops there), top_k is respected.

Same verification as 1nr.3 (shared commit/PR).

title: schedule_graph — Welder §3.2 GraphConnecting (Fig. 7): per-edge memory-level search, replaces Anduin::optimize's todo!()
description:
## Goal

Implement Welder Fig. 7's `GraphConnecting(g, d)` — the outer scheduling
loop that decides, per edge, which memory level to connect it at. This is
the piece that finally replaces the `todo!()` in
`Anduin::optimize` (`kernels/teeny-kernels/src/graph/optimizer/anduin/mod.rs`).

## Naming: not `GraphConnecting`

`GraphConnecting` is the paper's name and is a poor fit as a Rust API name
(reads like a gerund/type, not an action). Use **`schedule_graph`** instead
(e.g. `TileGraph::schedule_graph(&mut self, hardware: &HardwareProfile, profiler: &dyn Profiler)`
or a free function taking `&mut TileGraph` — whichever reads better once
the signature is worked out) — cross-reference "Welder's `GraphConnecting`
(Fig. 7)" in doc comments for paper traceability, same as
`extract_subgraph`'s doc comment references `ExtractSubgraph`.

## The paper's pseudocode (Fig. 7, re-verified against `osdi23-shi.pdf`)

```
Func GraphConnecting(g:Graph, d:Device):
  for node : TopologySort(g.nodes()) do
    for edge : node.out_edges() do
      for level : d.MemLevels() do
        SetConnect(edge, level);
        s = ExtractSubgraph(node, 0);
        configs = SubGraphTiling(s, 0, tensor_shapes)
        if t = Min(d.Profile(configs)) < best_latency
          best_latency = t
          best_level = level
      SetConnect(edge, best_level);
```

## Mapping onto what's already shipped

- `TopologySort(g.nodes())` → `TileGraph::topological_sort`, shipped.
- `node.out_edges()` → `TileGraph::children`, shipped.
- `d.MemLevels()` → `HardwareProfile::memory_levels`, shipped
  (`core/teeny-core/src/device/hardware.rs`).
- `SetConnect(edge, level)` → `TileGraph::set_connect`, shipped.
- `ExtractSubgraph(node, 0)` → `TileGraph::extract_subgraph(node, level)`,
  shipped (`0` = the lowest `MemoryLevelKind`, i.e. `Register`, per
  `MemoryLevelKind`'s derived `Ord`).
- `SubGraphTiling(s, 0, tensor_shapes)` → the sibling issue this one
  depends on (teenygrad-1nr.4, `sub_graph_tiling`, not yet built).
- `d.Profile(configs)` → **not a direct match to what exists today.**
  `Profiler::profile(tile_graph, nodes, hardware) -> f64` (shipped) scores
  a *node set* against its full untiled shape, not a candidate `TileConfig`
  the way the paper's `Profile(configs)` does (profiling each of
  `SubGraphTiling`'s returned candidates, not the node set once). Extending
  `Profiler`'s signature to accept a `TileConfig` (or adding a second
  method) is likely needed here — flag as an open design question to
  resolve during implementation, not a silently-assumed fit.

## Scope: scheduling only, not kernel materialization

This issue produces a **schedule** — `TileGraph`'s edges left with their
best-found `connect_level`s (mutating the same structure
`extract_subgraph`/`set_connect` already operate on) plus whatever
`TileConfig`(s) `sub_graph_tiling` settled on. It does **not** rewrite the
`Dag` into actually-fused kernels. `Anduin::optimize`'s current signature
returns `(Dag<Box<dyn ExecutableOp>>, Vec<usize>)` — turning a finished
schedule into that rewritten `Dag` requires materializing real fused
Triton kernels, which the parent epic (teenygrad-1nr) already documents as
blocked on `teenygrad-1nr.1` (reworking `#[tiled_kernel]` to compose
`Tile<D>` functions instead of pointer-in/pointer-out kernels — `pid`
decode doesn't currently compose across a fused call). **Do not treat
wiring this into `Anduin::optimize`'s return value as in scope here**
unless teenygrad-1nr.1 has landed first; if it hasn't, this issue should
still land `schedule_graph` itself plus tests against `TileGraph` directly,
leaving the `Anduin::optimize` wiring as a follow-up.

## Non-goals

- `EnumerateSubtiles` (teenygrad-1nr.3) and `sub_graph_tiling`
  (teenygrad-1nr.4) themselves — direct dependencies, not this issue's
  scope.
- Real-hardware validation (compiling/running/timing each candidate) —
  `SimpleProfiler` is a structural stand-in; a real `Profiler` impl built
  on Table 1's `Allocate`/`LoadTiles`/`ComputeTile`/`StoreTiles` is
  separate, larger work (`anduin::profiler`'s own doc comment already
  flags this).
- Rewriting `Dag`/materializing fused kernels — blocked on
  teenygrad-1nr.1, see above.

## References

- `osdi23-shi.pdf`, Fig. 7 (`GraphConnecting` pseudocode), Table 1 (device
  interfaces `Profile` would be built from).
- `TILE_GRAPH_SCHEDULING_PLAN.md` — tracking doc.
- teenygrad-1nr (epic) — "Composition mechanism" section on why kernel
  materialization is separately blocked.
- teenygrad-1nr.4 — `sub_graph_tiling`, this issue's direct dependency.
notes: Superseded by the v2 TileGraph rewrite (9b9f58b28), which deleted this implementation along with builder.rs, memory.rs, propagate.rs, search.rs and sub_graph_tiling.rs. The algorithm is being re-landed against v2 by teenygrad-1nr.25 - do not assume this code exists in the tree. Left closed because the design decisions recorded here still hold; only the code was removed.
close_reason:
Implemented as schedule_graph in a new module,
kernels/teeny-kernels/src/graph/optimizer/anduin/scheduler.rs -- your
suggested name, used directly (not GraphConnecting).

One documented deviation, flagged as an open question in this issue and
now resolved: Profiler doesn't (yet) take a TileConfig, so rather than the
paper's literal Min(d.Profile(configs)) over every SubGraphTiling
candidate, this asks sub_graph_tiling for only its single best-ranked
candidate (top_k = 1) per memory level and profiles the *structural* cost
of the extracted subgraph at that level instead -- still responds
correctly to which level is being tried (extraction and each boundary
edge's bandwidth both depend on the tentative connect_level), so it's a
reasoned working stand-in, not a silent gap. Extending Profiler to score a
specific TileConfig directly remains a real, separate follow-up.

Scoping honored as written: scheduling only. schedule_graph mutates a
TileGraph's connect_levels in place; it does not rewrite the Dag into
fused kernels, and is not wired into Anduin::optimize's return value --
still correctly blocked on teenygrad-1nr.1 (Tile<D> composition rework).
anduin/mod.rs's module doc comment updated to reflect the current state
accurately.

3 new tests: every edge ends up at a declared level, the search actually
prefers the cheaper-scoring level (Register over DeviceMemory under a
bandwidth gap favoring Register), and an empty hardware profile leaves
connect_levels unchanged.

Same verification as 1nr.3/1nr.4 (shared commit/PR): cargo check
--workspace clean, full teeny-kernels test suite passes (62 tests, only
the pre-existing unrelated Anduin::optimize todo!() failure), clippy
clean, fmt clean.

title: Persist the winning tile-config and execute_graph — structural walk over §3.3's ExecuteGraph (Fig. 8)
description:
## Goal

Two related pieces, scoped together because the second needs the first:

1. **Fix the dropped-config bug**: `schedule_graph` (teenygrad-1nr.5)
   computes a `Vec<SubGraphTilingResult>` per candidate memory level but
   only keeps `connect_level` (`best_level`) — the actual chosen
   `TileConfig` (concrete tile shapes) is discarded every iteration, even
   for the winning level. Confirmed while discussing this issue: `TileGraph`
   has no field for it at all.
2. **`execute_graph`**: a *structural* implementation of Welder §3.3's
   `ExecuteGraph` (Fig. 8) — the recursive routine a scheduled tile-graph
   maps to execution through. Structural only: records a trace of
   `Allocate`/`LoadTiles`/`ComputeTile`/`StoreTiles` calls (Table 1) via a
   pluggable device trait, the same pattern `Profiler` already uses. Does
   **not** emit real code — that's still blocked on teenygrad-1nr.1 (see
   non-goals).

## What's actually worth persisting: a tree, not a flat map

`ExecuteGraph`'s own pseudocode (Fig. 8, re-verified against
`osdi23-shi.pdf` p.707) recurses through the memory hierarchy, allocating a
workspace *at each level* and recursing into that level's own subgraph:

```
ExecuteGraph(g, level, in, out):
  mem = Allocate(g.MemFootprint(), level)
  LoadTiles(mem, in)
  for n in g.nodes():
    if level == top: ComputeTile(n, mem.in[n], mem.out[n])
    else: ExecuteGraph(n.TileGraph(), level+1, mem.in[n], mem.out[n])
  StoreTiles(mem, out)
```

A single flattened "final tile shape per edge" would only capture the
bottom of the hierarchy and lose every intermediate level's own
workspace-sizing/config — exactly what `SubGraphTilingResult` (already
shipped, teenygrad-1nr.4) already represents as a tree. So the fix is to
*retain* that tree (already computed, currently thrown away), not to
flatten it into something new.

## Scope

1. **`TileGraph` gains storage for the resolved schedule** — a
   `resolved_tiling: HashMap<EdgeId, SubGraphTilingResult>` field (or
   equivalent), populated by `schedule_graph` from whichever level's
   `sub_graph_tiling` call won (cache it during the level loop instead of
   recomputing), with a `TileGraph::resolved_tiling(edge_id) -> Option<&SubGraphTilingResult>`
   accessor.
2. **`SubGraphTilingResult` needs a `nodes: Vec<NodeId>` field** — a real
   gap found scoping this issue: `children: Vec<SubGraphTilingResult>` is
   currently a flat list with no record of *which* node subgraph each
   child's config applies to, so the tree isn't walkable by anything that
   needs to know "which nodes does this level's config cover" (which
   `execute_graph` does, directly mirroring Fig. 8's `n.TileGraph()`).
   `sub_graph_tiling` already computes this (`subgraph`, the
   `extract_subgraph` result, per child) — it just needs to be attached to
   the result instead of discarded.
3. **`ExecuteDevice` trait** (`Allocate`/`LoadTiles`/`ComputeTile`/
   `StoreTiles`, Table 1), mirroring `Profiler`'s existing pluggable-trait
   pattern. A reference/test implementation records a trace (`Vec` of
   recorded calls) rather than doing anything real.
4. **`execute_graph`** — the structural walk implementing Fig. 8's
   recursion over a `TileGraph` + a `SubGraphTilingResult` tree +
   `ExecuteDevice`, terminating at `hardware`'s top declared memory level
   (mirroring `sub_graph_tiling`'s own termination, via the existing
   `next_memory_level` helper).

## Non-goals

- **Real code generation.** `ExecuteDevice`'s methods here just record a
  trace; a real implementation (emitting actual Triton/CUDA source,
  register-level `compute_inline`-style fusion, shared-memory load/store
  rewriting, block/thread index remapping) is §4.2's scope and overlaps
  heavily with teenygrad-1nr.1's still-open `Tile<D>` composition rework —
  explicitly deferred, per this session's scope decision (chose "storage
  fix + structural ExecuteGraph only" over including §4.2 or the
  best-fit shared-memory allocator now).
- **§4.1's hardware-aligned refinements** (coalescing/under-parallelism
  penalty factors, TensorCore axis binding) — the removed, real-hardware-
  calibrated `teenygrad-3w0` `CostModel` is a strong revival candidate for
  this, same pattern as `KernelTileSpec`, but deferred to its own issue.
- **Wiring `execute_graph`/the resolved schedule into `Anduin::optimize`'s
  return value** — still blocked on teenygrad-1nr.1 for the same reason
  `schedule_graph` itself is.

## References

- `osdi23-shi.pdf` p.707 (Fig. 8, `ExecuteGraph`; Table 1, device
  interfaces) and p.707-708 (§4.1/§4.2, read in full for this scoping
  discussion).
- `TILE_GRAPH_SCHEDULING_PLAN.md` — tracking doc.
- teenygrad-1nr.4/.5 (closed) — `sub_graph_tiling`/`schedule_graph`, this
  issue's direct dependencies.
- `kernels/teeny-kernels/src/graph/optimizer/anduin/profiler.rs` — the
  pluggable-trait pattern `ExecuteDevice` should mirror.
notes: Superseded by the v2 TileGraph rewrite (9b9f58b28), which deleted this implementation along with builder.rs, memory.rs, propagate.rs, search.rs and sub_graph_tiling.rs. The algorithm is being re-landed against v2 by teenygrad-1nr.25 - do not assume this code exists in the tree. Left closed because the design decisions recorded here still hold; only the code was removed.
close_reason:
Implemented both pieces.

1. Storage fix: TileGraph gained resolved_tiling: HashMap<EdgeId,
   SubGraphTilingResult> (record_resolved_tiling/resolved_tiling
   accessors). schedule_graph now caches the winning level's already-
   computed sub_graph_tiling result instead of discarding it after the
   is_empty() check.

2. SubGraphTilingResult gained a `nodes: Vec<NodeId>` field, as scoped --
   confirmed necessary (not just tidiness) once execute_graph needed to
   know which nodes each child covers to dispatch correctly.

3. New module anduin/execute.rs: ExecuteDevice trait (allocate/load_tiles/
   compute_tile/store_tiles, Table 1), mirroring Profiler's pluggable
   pattern; TraceDevice, a structural reference implementation that
   records a call trace; execute_graph, the recursive walk implementing
   Fig. 8 over a TileGraph + SubGraphTilingResult + ExecuteDevice,
   terminating at the top of HardwareProfile's declared hierarchy via the
   same next_memory_level helper sub_graph_tiling uses (now pub(crate)).

the code and TILE_GRAPH_SCHEDULING_PLAN.md: SubGraphTilingResult::children
can have one child cover several nodes (sub_graph_tiling's existing
dedup-by-subgraph behavior), so execute_graph dispatches once per child
(marking every node that child covers as executed) rather than
unconditionally once per node in the paper's literal `for n : g.nodes()`
loop -- falls back to compute_tile directly only for a node no child
covers. Caught and fixed one wrong test expectation while writing tests
for this (assumed two connected nodes would merge into one child at the
next level; the >-level semantics of extract_subgraph, already shipped
and tested, mean an edge left at its from_dag default doesn't qualify, so
they stay separate singleton children -- not a code bug, a test-authoring
mistake).

round-trip, schedule_graph populates resolved_tiling, and 3 execute_graph
tests (direct compute at the top level with an exact expected trace,
recursion + no double-execution via child coverage, fallback to direct
compute_tile when no child covers a node).

title: fix: TileGraph::propagate drops untiled_dims, truncating a partially-tiled spec's TileEdgeShape
description:
## Goal

`TileGraph::propagate` silently truncates the resolved `TileEdgeShape` for
any `KernelTileSpec` whose `TensorTileSpec.axes` covers fewer dims than its
declared `rank` (i.e. genuinely relies on `untiled_dims`, per that field's
own documented purpose in `teeny_core::model::tile_spec`) — instead of a
full-rank tile with the untiled dims falling back to their real full
extent, it silently drops them, producing a `TileEdgeShape` shorter than
the edge's real declared rank. That's handed straight to
`mem_footprint_with_config`/`mem_traffic_with_config` downstream with no
guard.

Found and reproduced while scoping tile specs for `Conv2d`/`BatchNorm2d`
(conv2d's real `conv2d_forward` kernel only block-tiles its width axis via
`BLOCK_OW`; channels/height/batch are grid-driven with no block-size
generic of their own — exactly the case `untiled_dims` exists to describe,
per `tile_spec.rs`'s own module doc comment, which uses conv2d as its
motivating example).

## Reproduction

`kernels/teeny-kernels/src/graph/optimizer/anduin/tile_graph/mod.rs::tests::propagate_of_a_partially_tiled_spec_should_not_drop_the_untiled_dims`
(already added, currently failing on `main`/this branch). Builds `a -> b`
where `b` declares a spec with `rank: 2` but only 1 `TileAxisBinding` (the
width axis) plus `untiled_dims: &["C"]`. Seeds `b`'s output tile at
`[Fixed(16), Fixed(8)]` (rank 2) and asserts the resolved `a -> b` edge is
also rank 2, width 16 / channels 8. Fails today: resolves to `[Fixed(16)]`
(rank 1) — the channels dimension vanishes entirely instead of falling
back to its full extent.

## Root cause

Two related bugs in `TileGraph::propagate`'s output-tile and input-tile
construction (`tile_graph/mod.rs`, in `propagate`'s node loop):

```rust
// Output-side: builds the extent_param -> TileDim map used to resolve inputs.
let resolved: HashMap<&'static str, &TileDim> = output_spec
    .axes
    .iter()
    .zip(output_tile.iter())          // <-- positional zip, ignores axis.dim
    .map(|(axis, dim)| (axis.extent_param, dim))
    .collect();

// Input-side: builds each parent edge's resolved tile.
let input_tile: TileEdgeShape = input_spec
    .axes
    .iter()
    .enumerate()                      // <-- iterates axes.len() times, not rank
    .map(|(axis_idx, axis)| { ... })
    .collect();                       // <-- result has length axes.len(), not rank
```

1. **Positional zip ignores `TileAxisBinding.dim`.** `axis.dim` is declared
   metadata but never actually consulted — `axes[i]` is paired with
   `output_tile[i]`/`full_shape[i]` purely by position. Works by
   coincidence today only because every existing spec
   (`RELU_TILE_SPEC`/`MATMUL_TILE_SPEC`/the test specs) happens to declare
   `axes` in the same order as the tensor's real dims, contiguously from 0,
   with `axes.len() == rank`.
2. **Input/output tile construction is sized off `axes.len()`, not
   `rank`.** When `axes.len() < rank` (a genuinely partial spec, relying on
   `untiled_dims` for the rest), the constructed `TileEdgeShape` is
   correspondingly shorter than the edge's real, declared rank —
   `rank`-many-dimensional data silently collapsed to `axes.len()`
   dimensions, dropping the untiled dims entirely rather than falling back
   to their full extent (the stated, documented behavior for an axis
   without an output-side counterpart, e.g. a reduction axis, one dim
   over).

`untiled_dims` itself is not read anywhere (`grep` confirms — always `&[]`
in every existing spec); `window`/`block_const` are similarly inert. This
issue is about the `rank`/`axes`/`dim` sizing and indexing logic, not about
literally consuming `untiled_dims`'s string list.

## Fix plan

In `TileGraph::propagate`'s node loop (`tile_graph/mod.rs`):

1. **Resolve by `axis.dim`, not position.** Replace the `.zip(output_tile.iter())`
   with an explicit index: `output_tile.get(axis.dim)`, skipping (not
   panicking) an axis whose declared `dim` is out of range for the actual
   `output_tile` (same "degrade to a hard boundary for this axis, don't
   guess" philosophy `propagate` already uses elsewhere).
2. **Build each input tile at full rank, not `axes.len()`.** Start from
   `full_shape.clone()` (the input edge's real, full-rank shape — already
   available as `full_shape` in this loop) instead of mapping over
   `input_spec.axes`. Then, for each `TileAxisBinding` in `input_spec.axes`,
   overwrite `input_tile[axis.dim]` with the resolved dim
   (`resolved.get(axis.extent_param)`) when present; leave it at its
   full-shape fallback (the clone's original value) otherwise. This makes
   an untiled dim behave exactly like today's already-correct "reduction
   axis with no output-side counterpart" case — full extent, not absent —
   and the result is always length `full_shape.len()` (== `rank`), never
   `axes.len()`.
3. **Correct the doc comments this fix changes the meaning of:**
   - `TensorTileSpec.rank`: currently says "Must equal `axes.len()`" —
     change to "the tensor's real, full rank; `axes` may cover fewer dims
     than this (see `untiled_dims`) — any dim with no `TileAxisBinding`
     keeps its full extent."
   - `TileAxisBinding.dim`: note it's now actually consulted (not just
     documentation) — each `axes` entry's `dim` must be `< rank` and
     entries should have distinct `dim`s (last-write-wins if not, but
     that's a spec-authoring bug, not something to silently normalize).
   - `tile_spec.rs`'s module doc comment / `untiled_dims`'s own doc
     comment: update "not yet consumed" framing — the *effect* `untiled_dims`
     describes (untiled dims keep their full extent) now genuinely holds,
     even though the string names in `untiled_dims` itself still aren't
     read (the fallback is structural, not name-driven).
4. **Un-break the reproduction test** — once the fix lands,
   `propagate_of_a_partially_tiled_spec_should_not_drop_the_untiled_dims`
   should pass unmodified; keep it as a permanent regression test.
5. **Re-verify existing propagate tests still pass** (`flat_unary_spec`/
   `gemm_shaped_spec`-based tests) — the fix must be a strict
   generalization, not a behavior change, for specs where `axes.len() ==
   rank` already (the only kind that existed before this issue).
6. **Follow-up, not in this issue's scope:** once this lands, real
   `KernelTileSpec`s for `Conv2d`/`BatchNorm2d` (partial-axis, relying on
   the now-correct untiled-dim fallback) become safe to author — tracked
   separately once this fix is in.

## Non-goals

- Actually reading/validating `untiled_dims`'s string list against real
  kernel param names — it stays documentation-only, same as `window`.
- Wiring up `TileWindow`-aware propagation (a windowed axis's input extent
  vs. output extent) — separate, already-flagged follow-up in
  `tile_spec.rs`'s own module doc comment.
- Writing the actual `Conv2d`/`BatchNorm2d` tile specs — follow-up once
  this fix exists.
notes: Superseded by the v2 TileGraph rewrite (9b9f58b28), which deleted this implementation along with builder.rs, memory.rs, propagate.rs, search.rs and sub_graph_tiling.rs. The algorithm is being re-landed against v2 by teenygrad-1nr.25 - do not assume this code exists in the tree. Left closed because the design decisions recorded here still hold; only the code was removed.
close_reason: Fixed: propagate now builds full-rank input/output tiles indexed by axis.dim, falling back to full extent for untiled dims instead of truncating the result.

comments.author: Arshad Mahmood
comments.text:
Implemented and verified.

Fix landed in TileGraph::propagate (kernels/teeny-kernels/src/graph/optimizer/anduin/tile_graph/mod.rs):
