   instead of `.zip(output_tile.iter())` -- indexes by each axis's declared `dim`, not
   position, so axes needn't appear in tensor-dim order and needn't cover every dim.
2. Each input's tile is now built by cloning `full_shape` (full rank) and selectively
   overwriting `input_tile[axis.dim]` for each `TileAxisBinding` present, instead of
   mapping over `input_spec.axes` alone (which produced a result of length `axes.len()`,
   not `rank`). A dim with no axis binding now correctly falls back to its full extent --
   the same fallback an unresolved reduction axis already got -- instead of being
   silently dropped from the result.

Doc comments updated to match (teeny-core's tile_spec.rs: TensorTileSpec::rank,
TileAxisBinding::dim, untiled_dims, module doc comment; teeny-kernels'
TileGraph::propagate doc comment).

Verification:
- The reproduction test (propagate_of_a_partially_tiled_spec_should_not_drop_the_untiled_dims)
  now passes unmodified, kept as a permanent regression test.
- All pre-existing propagate tests (flat_unary_spec/gemm_shaped_spec-based) still pass
  unchanged -- confirms this is a strict generalization, not a behavior change, for specs
  where axes.len() == rank already.
- Full suite: cargo check, ./scripts/test.sh -p teeny-core -p teeny-kernels --lib

title: feat: TileAxisBinding.dims (flattened multi-dim axes) + real BatchNorm2d KernelTileSpec
description:
## Goal

`BatchNorm2d`'s real kernel (`batch_norm_2d_nchw_forward_inference`,
`kernels/teeny-kernels/src/nn/norm/batchnorm.rs`) doesn't fit
`TensorTileSpec`'s current model even after teenygrad-1nr.7's fix. Its
grid is `[C, B]` (one CTA per channel×batch), and each CTA iterates the
*flattened* `H*W` range in `BLOCK_HW`-wide tiles — there is no single real
graph dimension (H alone, or W alone) that `BLOCK_HW` corresponds to; it's
a block over the *product* of two real dims. `TileAxisBinding` only
models one `dim: usize` per binding, so there's no way to say "this
binding's block spans a flattened combination of dims 2 and 3."

This is different from (and harder than) Conv2d's case (already safely
expressible after teenygrad-1nr.7 — Conv2d's `BLOCK_OW` genuinely covers
one real dim, width, alone).

## Fix plan

1. **`TileAxisBinding.dim: usize` -> `TileAxisBinding.dims: &'static [usize]`**
   (`core/teeny-core/src/model/tile_spec.rs`) — non-empty, outermost to
   innermost real axis order. The common single-axis case is
   `dims: &[N]`; a flattened case like batchnorm's `H*W` is `dims: &[H_dim, W_dim]`.
2. **`TileGraph::propagate` update** (`tile_graph/mod.rs`): resolve/write
   via `dims.last()` (innermost) for the actual block-sized `TileDim`
   value; every *other* dim in `dims` (the flattened-away outer ones)
   gets `TileDim::Fixed(1)` when the axis resolves, or -- like today --
   the untouched full-shape fallback when it doesn't. This is
   product-preserving: `shape_byte_size`/footprint/traffic multiply all
   axes together, so `[..., Fixed(1), ..., Fixed(1), BLOCK_HW]` yields
   the same total element count as the real number of elements one tile
   touches, even though it isn't a literal axis-aligned rectangular
   region once `BLOCK_HW` doesn't evenly divide the innermost dim's
   extent -- an approximation, not a new one: this codebase already
   documents equivalent simplifications elsewhere (masked/partial last
   tiles in `enumerate_subtiles`'s doc comment, `TileWindow` not yet
   consumed).
   - When `dims.len() == 1`, this reduces exactly to today's behavior --
     strict generalization, not a behavior change, for every existing
     single-axis spec.
3. **Update every existing spec** to the renamed field: `RELU_TILE_SPEC`/
   `MATMUL_TILE_SPEC` (`kernels/teeny-kernels/src/graph/mod.rs`),
   `flat_unary_spec`/`gemm_shaped_spec`/`partially_tiled_spec` (test
   specs in `tile_graph/mod.rs`).
4. **Add `BATCHNORM2D_TILE_SPEC`** (`graph/mod.rs`, alongside
   `RELU_TILE_SPEC`/`MATMUL_TILE_SPEC`): `x_ptr`/`y_ptr` both rank 4
   (NCHW), one axis `{ dims: &[2, 3], block_const: "BLOCK_HW",
   extent_param: "HW" }` (H, W flattened, W innermost -- matches NCHW's
   row-major layout, W the fastest-varying real axis), batch/channels
   (dims 0/1) left out of `axes` (untiled, full extent). Wire it into
   `Op::BatchNorm2d`'s `KernelExecutable` construction (`graph/mod.rs`,
   the `BatchNorm2dNchwInferenceRuntimeOp` forward-kernel arm only --
   *not* the generic `BatchNorm1d`/`BatchNorm3d`
   `BatchNormForwardInference` arm, a different kernel/shape entirely),
   same pattern as `Op::Relu`'s `exec.tile_spec = Some(RELU_TILE_SPEC)`.
5. **Regression test** in `tile_graph/mod.rs`, mirroring
   `propagate_of_a_partially_tiled_spec_should_not_drop_the_untiled_dims`'s
   pattern: a batchnorm-shaped spec (rank 4, one flattened `dims: &[2,3]`
   axis), seed a rank-4 output tile, assert the resolved input tile is
   `[B_full, C_full, Fixed(1), Fixed(resolved_HW)]` and total element
   count matches the real per-tile element count.

## Known limitation (flag, don't solve here)

`TileGraph::enumerate_subtiles`'s candidate search varies each axis's
ladder *independently* (`full_shape`'s own per-axis power-of-two ladder),
with no notion that two real dims are jointly driven by one flattened
binding. For a batchnorm-style node, this means the search doesn't know
to grow H and W *together* as a single `HW` candidate -- it would try
combinations that don't correspond to any real `BLOCK_HW` the kernel
could actually use. Teaching `enumerate_subtiles`/`sub_graph_tiling` to
respect a flattened axis's joint ladder is a real follow-up, out of
scope here: this issue is about `propagate` resolving a *given* (e.g.
seeded, or eventually correctly-enumerated) output tile correctly, not
about generating one.

## Non-goals

- Making `enumerate_subtiles` flattened-axis-aware (see above).
- `TileWindow`-aware propagation (separate, already-flagged follow-up).
- Any other op's tile spec beyond `BatchNorm2d` (e.g. `Conv2d`, which
  already fits cleanly under the pre-existing single-dim model and
  doesn't need this feature).
close_reason: Implemented: TileAxisBinding.dims supports flattened multi-dim axes; propagate resolves them product-preservingly; BATCHNORM2D_TILE_SPEC added and wired in; regression test passes.

Known limitation, documented, not solved here: enumerate_subtiles's candidate
search still varies every axis's ladder independently, with no notion that
two real dims are jointly driven by one flattened binding -- teaching the
search to respect that is a separate follow-up.

title: feat: TileGraph::enumerate_subtiles ignores flattened multi-dim tile_spec axes
description:
## Goal

`TileGraph::enumerate_subtiles` (Welder §4.1's `EnumerateSubtiles`) builds
its candidate output-tile search space by growing each *real* axis's own
power-of-two ladder independently (from `root`'s full shape), with no
awareness of `root`'s own `tile_spec` at all -- in particular, no
awareness of a `TileAxisBinding` whose `dims` spans more than one real
axis (teenygrad-1nr.8's flattened-axis support, e.g. NCHW batchnorm2d's
`H*W` loop, one `BLOCK_HW` covering `dims: &[2, 3]`).

For a node governed by a flattened-axis spec, this produces two related
problems, not just redundant search:

1. **Wasted/redundant search.** `TileGraph::propagate`'s resolution for a
   flattened axis only ever reads the candidate output tile's *innermost*
   spanned dim (see teenygrad-1nr.8's fix) -- the outer spanned dim's
   value is ignored entirely when resolving that axis. So
   `enumerate_subtiles` varying H and W independently produces many
   candidates that `propagate` treats identically for that axis (same W,
   different H all resolve the same way on any downstream input edge).
2. **Invalid/misleading candidates.** `score_candidate_tile`'s footprint/
   traffic numbers (`mem_footprint_with_config`/`mem_traffic_with_config`,
   via `shape_byte_size`) multiply *every* dim of a tile together --
   including the candidate output tile's own boundary-edge footprint,
   computed straight from the enumerated `TileEdgeShape` before
   `propagate` ever touches it. A candidate with, say, `H=4, W=8` reports
   a footprint as if the real kernel could materialize a 4-row-by-8-col
   output tile -- but the real `batch_norm_2d_nchw_forward_inference`
   kernel can only ever pick one flat `BLOCK_HW` count over the *combined*
   range; there is no real kernel configuration that produces an
   `H=4, W=8` *rectangular* output tile. So some fraction of the search
   space explores and scores candidates that aren't realizable by the
   kernel this spec describes at all.

## Fix plan (sketch -- not implemented in this issue)

1. When `root`'s `tile_spec` is present, drive `enumerate_subtiles`'s
   ladder construction from its *output* `TensorTileSpec.axes`
   (`self.node(root).tile_spec`, already available) instead of raw
   per-real-dim ladders:
   - For each `TileAxisBinding` in `axes`: build **one** ladder over that
     binding's combined logical extent (the product of its `dims`' real
     full extents -- `H * W` for a flattened pair, or just the one dim's
     own extent in the ordinary single-dim case), then when writing a
     candidate value into the `TileEdgeShape`, use the exact same
     "innermost dim gets the value, every other spanned dim gets
     `Fixed(1)`" convention `propagate` already applies -- so every
     enumerated candidate is one `propagate` (and the real kernel) can
     actually realize.
   - For a real dim covered by no axis binding at all (untiled, per
     `TensorTileSpec::untiled_dims`'s documented case): no ladder: `Fixed`
     at its full extent in every candidate, consistent with `propagate`'s
     existing fallback for untiled dims.
   - When `root` has **no** `tile_spec` (still the overwhelming majority
     of nodes -- coverage is opt-in), fall back to exactly today's
     per-real-dim ladder behavior. This must be a strict, behavior-
     preserving extension for every currently-covered case (`Relu`/
     `MatMul`, and any other single-dim-axes spec), the same bar
     teenygrad-1nr.7/.8 held themselves to.
2. Regression coverage: an `enumerate_subtiles` test using
   `batchnorm2d_shaped_spec`-style spec (or a shared helper with
   teenygrad-1nr.8's), asserting every returned candidate has the
   flattened dims' outer entries at `Fixed(1)` (never independently
   varied) and that the search doesn't score/return duplicate-effective
   candidates that only differ in an outer flattened dim's (unused)
   value.

## Non-goals

- Reworking `sub_graph_tiling`'s own candidate consumption -- it already
  just takes whatever `enumerate_subtiles` returns; no change expected
  there beyond receiving a smaller, now-valid candidate set.
- Any change to `propagate` itself (teenygrad-1nr.8 already landed the
  read/write convention this issue's fix needs to match).
- Extending `TileWindow` support into this search (separate, already-
  flagged follow-up in `tile_spec.rs`'s module doc comment).
notes: Superseded by the v2 TileGraph rewrite (9b9f58b28), which deleted this implementation along with builder.rs, memory.rs, propagate.rs, search.rs and sub_graph_tiling.rs. The algorithm is being re-landed against v2 by teenygrad-1nr.25 - do not assume this code exists in the tree. Left closed because the design decisions recorded here still hold; only the code was removed.
close_reason: Implemented: enumerate_subtiles now builds one SearchAxis per declared TileAxisBinding (combined-extent ladder for flattened multi-dim axes), falling back to per-real-dim ladders when no usable tile_spec exists. Reproduction test passes; no regressions.

title: teeny-llm: an OpenAI-compatible LLM serving stack
description: Umbrella for the teeny-llm apps (apps/teeny-llm: teeny-llm-core, teeny-llm-server, teeny-llm-chat): turning the crate split and FunctionGemma port (#169) into a stack that serves real models behind the OpenAI-compatible API. teeny-llm-core holds the models (one feature per model, shared kernels in teeny_llm_core::kernels, model-specific ones in the model's module) and the interfaces frontends use; the server and CLI should serve any model that implements them, rather than the placeholder EchoEngine. Each step is a child issue.

title: teeny-llm-core: a ChatModel trait covering the OpenAI chat completions API
description:
Define the trait each model in teeny_llm_core::models implements to serve chat completions, so the server and CLI can serve any of them (FunctionGemma first).

Design decisions (agreed with the user):
- Models implement it; frontends do not. A per-model ChatModel trait sits under the existing Engine: a generic adapter turns one or more ChatModels into an Engine (or its successor), so teeny-llm-server and teeny-llm-chat keep talking to Engine. Engine stays the frontend interface, ChatModel the model interface.
- Full API, with capabilities. The request and response types cover the whole OpenAI chat completions API, not a subset. Each model reports its capabilities, and anything it lacks is refused before generation with a specific error the server maps to an OpenAI-style 400 (never silently ignored).
- Async, object-safe. Models implement the trait directly and must be Send + Sync; it has to work behind Arc<dyn ChatModel>, so methods return boxed futures/streams (as Engine::generate_stream does) rather than native async fn. Each model owns its own threading and device: FunctionGemma's runner is synchronous and borrows the device, so its implementation will need a worker thread or similar internally.
- Core domain types. Rust-native types in teeny-llm-core (enums for roles, content parts, tool choice, response format, finish reasons), with no serde wire details. teeny-llm-server keeps its OpenAI wire types (src/openai) and maps to and from these.

Must cover, request side: messages with every role (developer, system, user, assistant, tool) and content parts (text, image URL/data with detail, input audio, file), assistant messages carrying tool_calls and refusals, tool messages carrying tool_call_id; tools (function name, description, JSON-schema parameters, strict); tool_choice (none, auto, required, a named function); parallel_tool_calls; response_format (text, json_object, json_schema with strict); sampling (temperature, top_p, presence/frequency penalty, logit_bias, seed, stop strings); max_completion_tokens (and legacy max_tokens); n; logprobs and top_logprobs; reasoning_effort; modalities/audio output where a model supports it; stream_options.include_usage; user/metadata passed through.

Must cover, response side: per-choice streamed deltas (role, content, tool-call deltas with index, id, name and incremental arguments, refusal), finish_reason (stop, length, tool_calls, content_filter), per-token logprobs with top alternatives, usage (prompt, completion, cached prompt tokens, reasoning tokens), and a non-streamed form assembled from the stream.

Capabilities a model declares: at least tool calling (and parallel), structured output (json_object, json_schema), input modalities, logprobs, n > 1, reasoning, context length and max output tokens.

Done when: the trait and types are in teeny-llm-core with docs; a validation layer checks a request against a model's capabilities and returns specific errors (naming the field and the model); the adapter to Engine exists; EchoEngine (or an echo ChatModel) implements it as the reference; unit tests (test_ prefix) cover validation and stream assembly. Wiring FunctionGemma and the server onto it are separate follow-up issues under this epic.
close_reason: Implemented in teeny_llm_core::chat (commit f521f0b5c on feature/llm-functiongemma, PR #169): ChatModel trait, ChatRequest/ChatStream types, Capabilities + validate(), collect(), ChatEngine adapter (Engine::chat_stream), EchoChatModel reference, 18 unit tests.

title: teeny-llm-core: an ImageModel trait for /v1/images (later)
description:
Image generation for diffusion-class models: the furthest from teenygrad's current kernels, so last.
Request: generations (prompt, n, size, quality, style, background transparency, output_format png/jpeg/webp, output_compression, moderation level, partial_images for streaming, user); edits (one or more input images, optional mask, prompt, input_fidelity); variations (one image, n, size).
Response: images as bytes (the server encodes b64_json, or serves URLs if it stores them), revised prompt where the model rewrites it, streamed partial images, usage (input text/image tokens, output tokens).
Capabilities: sizes, qualities, max n, edits, masks, variations, transparency, output formats, streaming partials, max prompt length.

Follow the ChatModel pattern (teeny_llm_core::chat, teenygrad-1oui.1): Rust domain request/response types with no wire format, a Capabilities struct the model declares, validate() refusing malformed or unsupported parameters with Error::InvalidParameter / Error::UnsupportedParameter naming the parameter (never silently ignored), an object-safe Send + Sync trait returning boxed futures/streams, a serving adapter, a reference fixture implementation, and test_-prefixed unit tests. The server mapping of the OpenAI wire types is part of the work. Image encoding/decoding is shared infrastructure, not per model.

JPEG/WebP refused by name.

title: teeny-llm-core: a shared Tokenizer helper trait
close_reason: Implemented in teeny_llm_core::tokenizer (commit 5e8b73876 on feature/llm-functiongemma, PR #169): Tokenizer + StreamDecoder traits, ByteTokenizer reference, HfTokenizer behind hf-tokenizer (DecodeStream for streaming), Error::Tokenizer; FunctionGemma's Chat uses it. Echo models still count words (a whitespace tokenizer cannot decode).

title: teeny-llm-core: a model factory (Model::load) and a multi-API ModelEngine
description:
Something that takes a models::Model (with its size/variant) and returns a live model, so frontends never handle weights, devices or kernels.

Design (discussed with the user):
- Model::load(self, &LoadOptions) -> Result<LoadedModel>. The match in Model::load is the only place that knows every model, each arm behind its feature like the enum; each model module owns its loading (functiongemma::load(opts)). A size variant is passed down as data (Model::Qwen3(size) => qwen3::load(size, opts)): one loader per family, hyperparameters from config.json.
- LoadOptions (#[non_exhaustive], Default): model_dir (else the HF cache via Model::locate), context_length (KV-cache size, at most spec().context_length), compile_cache (teenyc kernel cache); later device selection, dtype/quantisation, max concurrent requests.
- LoadedModel (#[non_exhaustive]): model, info (id = model.tag()), exact parameter count, the model's tokenizer (teenygrad-1oui.11), and an optional Arc per API trait it implements: chat (ChatModel) now, embedding (EmbeddingModel, .5) and completion (CompletionModel, .6) when those exist. One loaded model can serve several APIs from one set of weights.
- The factory hides threading: a model whose runtime is synchronous or device-bound (FunctionGemma's CompiledStep<'d>) starts a worker thread in load that opens the device, loads weights and compiles steps, waits for it to report ready (or its error), and returns a Send + Sync handle whose trait methods send requests over a channel and stream events back. Dropping the last handle closes the channel; the worker exits and frees the device.
- Loading is slow and blocking (seconds on CUDA, minutes compiling under qemu), so load is a plain blocking fn (the server calls it through spawn_blocking at startup), with an optional progress callback for boards.
- ModelEngine::new(Vec<LoadedModel>) generalises ChatEngine into one Engine routing chat, completions and embeddings by tag to whichever trait each model provides; short tags (functiongemma3) resolve to canonical ones (functiongemma3:270m) in requests, through Model's FromStr. Duplicate tags are refused.
- Echo stays outside the factory (not a Model variant): tests build a LoadedModel from EchoChatModel directly, so no factory trait is needed for test injection.

Decided for now: a free function (Model::load), not a ModelFactory trait (only worth it for out-of-crate models); each loaded model opens the device itself (sharing a device and its memory budget can come later via LoadOptions); eager loading at startup, failing fast.

Done when: Model::load, LoadOptions, LoadedModel and ModelEngine exist with docs; ModelEngine is tested over echo LoadedModels (routing by tag, short-tag resolution, duplicate refusal, an API a model lacks refused with a clear error); FunctionGemma's load arm is filled in by teenygrad-1oui.2, and the server/CLI consume Model::load in teenygrad-1oui.3.
close_reason: Commit d36b25968 (PR #169): Model::load, LoadOptions, LoadedModel, ModelEngine (replacing ChatEngine) with routing, short tags, duplicate/mismatch/missing-API refusal (Error::ModelLacksApi). No compile_cache option (teenyc reads only TEENYC_CACHE_DIR). FunctionGemma's arm refuses until .2.

title: FunctionGemma implements ChatModel
description:
Implement teeny_llm_core's ChatModel trait (teenygrad-1oui.1) for models::functiongemma, so it can be served through the Engine adapter.
- Capabilities: tool calling (parallel), text in and out, no images/audio, no json_schema enforcement, no logprobs or n > 1 unless added; context length from --context-style config.
- Threading: the runner is synchronous and borrows the device (CompiledStep<'d>), so the implementation owns the device, weights and session on a worker thread and feeds requests to it over a channel, streaming deltas back. One request at a time per loaded model, keeping the KV-cache prefix reuse between turns.
- Map messages and tools onto the chat template (assistant tool_calls, tool results), and parse_calls output into streamed tool-call deltas with finish_reason tool_calls.
- Honour stop strings and max tokens; greedy decoding for now, refusing sampling parameters it cannot apply.
- The examples/chat.rs modes could then run on the trait instead of their own Engine struct.
Tests (test_ prefix): request mapping and tool-call delta assembly without the weights; an ignored end-to-end test with GEMMA_MODEL_DIR.
close_reason: Commit b3acd56a4 (PR #169): models::functiongemma::serve (worker thread, FunctionGemmaChat, template_inputs, ReplyAssembler), wired into Model::load. End-to-end test is ignored (needs GEMMA_MODEL_DIR; weights not on the dev host, so not yet run). examples/chat.rs keeps its own engine for now: its serve page reports per-step timings the ChatModel does not expose.

title: teeny-llm-server and teeny-llm-chat serve ChatModels
description:
Serve real models through the ChatModel adapter (teenygrad-1oui.1) instead of EchoEngine.
- teeny-llm-server: map the full OpenAI chat completions wire types (src/openai/chat.rs) to and from core's chat types: tools, tool_choice, response_format, content parts, logprobs, n, stream_options.include_usage, tool-call deltas in SSE chunks, finish_reason tool_calls. Capability refusals become OpenAI-style 400s naming the parameter. Remove the current blanket rejections of options a model now supports.
- Model selection: load models by feature and command-line flags (e.g. --functiongemma <model dir>), listed by /v1/models.
- teeny-llm-chat: the same model loading, with tool calls shown in the transcript.
- teeny-llm-server and -chat currently take teeny-llm-core without default features; model features become theirs to enable (and CI must keep their test binaries free of libcuda).
Tests: the existing end-to-end API tests on an echo ChatModel, plus tool-call streaming.
notes: Model selection: take --model as a teeny_llm_core::models::Model tag (family:size, e.g. functiongemma3:270m, or the family alone for its default size), parsed by a clap PossibleValuesParser over Model::tags() with ignore_case, as examples/chat.rs does; --model-dir <folder> with Model::locate() falling back to the local Hugging Face cache. /v1/models should list Model::tag() ids and can describe them from Model::spec() (display name, architecture, context length, licence) plus the exact models::parameter_count() of the loaded weights. The echo placeholder is deliberately not a Model variant, so until a real model is served the server and CLI keep EchoEngine with no --model choice. teeny-llm-server and -chat need model features of their own that forward to teeny-llm-core's (they build it without default features today), so their Model enum is not empty.

title: Retire EchoEngine once ChatModels serve
description: When the server and CLI serve ChatModels (the frontend issue under teenygrad-1oui), replace EchoEngine with an echo ChatModel used only as the reference implementation and test fixture, and remove the Engine code paths nothing implements any more. Update README, CLAUDE.md and the book chapter, which describe EchoEngine as what the binaries run.

title: teeny-llm-core: an EmbeddingModel trait for /v1/embeddings
description:
Embeddings come from different models than chat (BERT-style encoders, e.g. the BERT-tiny already run through the ONNX corpus), so they need their own trait rather than Engine::embed's stub.
Request: model, inputs (strings, or pre-tokenized token-id arrays, one or many), dimensions (truncation, for models trained for it), encoding_format (float, base64: a frontend concern but validated), user.
Response: one vector per input in order, prompt token usage.
Capabilities: max input tokens per item, max batch size, native dimension and whether dimensions can be reduced, whether token-id input is accepted, pooling/normalisation documented.
Replaces Engine::embed's default and the server's current refusal of base64 and dimensions where a model supports them.

Follow the ChatModel pattern (teeny_llm_core::chat, teenygrad-1oui.1): Rust domain request/response types with no wire format, a Capabilities struct the model declares, validate() refusing malformed or unsupported parameters with Error::InvalidParameter / Error::UnsupportedParameter naming the parameter (never silently ignored), an object-safe Send + Sync trait returning boxed futures/streams, an adapter onto Engine (or a sibling serving trait) for the server, a reference echo/fixture implementation, and test_-prefixed unit tests. The server mapping of the OpenAI wire types onto it is part of the work.

title: teeny-llm-core: a CompletionModel trait for legacy /v1/completions

title: teeny-llm-core: a TranscriptionModel trait for /v1/audio/transcriptions and /translations (later)
