A server option to moderate chat input and output with a ModerationModel (finish_reason content_filter) can follow.

Follow the ChatModel pattern (teeny_llm_core::chat, teenygrad-1oui.1): Rust domain request/response types with no wire format, a Capabilities struct the model declares, validate() refusing malformed or unsupported parameters with Error::InvalidParameter / Error::UnsupportedParameter naming the parameter (never silently ignored), an object-safe Send + Sync trait returning boxed futures/streams, an adapter onto Engine (or a sibling serving trait) for the server, a reference echo/fixture implementation, and test_-prefixed unit tests. The server mapping of the OpenAI wire types onto it is part of the work.
close_reason: Commit 2df65de9b (PR #169): moderation module (categories, request, result, capabilities, validate, ModerationModel, EchoModerationModel), Engine::moderate, ModelEngine routing with default model choice, server /v1/moderations. Chat-side moderation option (content_filter) not done; follow-up.

title: spec: every forward kernel declares its tile axes via #[tiled_kernel]
description:
## Goal

Every **forward** kernel takes `In<Tile<..>>`/`Out<Tile<..>>` parameters and
declares its axes with `#[tile(...)]`, so `tile_spec()` is derived from the
signature rather than written beside it.

Backward kernels are **out of scope**. Some already carry `#[tiled_kernel]`
(`elu_backward`, `selu_backward`); they are not part of this epic and the
enforcement test must not demand axes from them.

## Direction, settled 2026-09-23

There is one target form, not a choice of two:

```rust
#[tiled_kernel]
pub fn foo_forward<T: Triton, D: Num, const BLOCK: i32>(
    #[tile(block = BLOCK, extent = n)] x: In<Tile<T, D>>,
    #[tile(block = BLOCK, extent = n)] y: Out<Tile<T, D>>,
    n: i32,
) { .. }
```

**Raw `In<T::Pointer<D>>`/`Out<..>` parameters are not carried forward.** The
metadata-only form (`#[tile(name = .., extent = ..)]` on a raw pointer,
teenygrad-1nr.19) was a way to describe a kernel without touching its body;
it is a migration aid, not the destination. `conv2d_forward` is currently its
only user and is therefore a kernel to convert, not a reference to copy.

## Measured starting point

| | count |
|---|---|
| forward kernels | 146 |
| using `#[tiled_kernel]` | 13 (incl. 2 backward) |
| declaring axes via `#[tile(...)]` | **3** |

`relu_forward` and `silu_forward` (`Tile` params, the target form), and
`conv2d_forward` (raw pointers, the form being retired).

The other nine `#[tiled_kernel]` forward kernels declare nothing. Those with
`Tile` params fall through to the implicit `BLOCK_SIZE`/`n_elements`
convention, which drives the auto-prelude and generates **no** `tile_spec()`
-- silently. Those without (`matmul_forward`, `flash_attention2_forward`) are
on the macro for dtype dispatch alone and have no tiling meaning yet.

## Hard prerequisite: teenygrad-1nr.18

The auto-prelude handles exactly one flat axis on `Axis::X`: it computes one
`offsets = arange(BLOCK) + pid*BLOCK` and hands it to every tile param. That
covers the elementwise families and nothing else. Conv, pool, the norms,
GEMM and attention need multi-axis, windowed and looped preludes, which is
`teenygrad-1nr.18`'s scope.

So the ladder splits in two:

- **Rungs that need only what exists**: the elementwise families.
- **Rungs blocked on `teenygrad-1nr.18`**: everything else.

Sequencing the elementwise rungs first is therefore not just
simplest-first, it is what is possible today.

## Ordering

| rung | family | fwd kernels | needs 1nr.18 |
|---|---|---|---|
| recipe + enforcement | -- | -- | no |
| unary flat elementwise | activations, unary math, elementwise losses | ~53 | no |
| multi-input flat elementwise | `elemwise_binary`, `elemwise_add`, `where`/`clip` | ~18 | no |
| mixed-extent operands | bias-add, embedding, NLL/BCE/ranking losses | ~16 | yes |
| statically-indexed shape changers | 12 pads, upsample, transpose, cat/chunk, flatten | ~18 | yes |
| windowed | conv 1/2/3d, 9 pools | 13 | yes |
| row reductions + norms | LayerNorm/InstanceNorm/RmsNorm/GroupNorm/BatchNorm, softmax | ~9 | yes |
| rank-changing reductions | `reduction.rs` | 14 | yes |
| matmul family | Gemm, Linear | ~3 | yes |
| loop-carried | flash attention 2 | 1 | yes |
| fused composites | `nn/fused/*` | 3 | yes |

## Relationship to teenygrad-1iy

`teenygrad-1iy` delivered the verification half -- `KernelTileSpec::validate`
and `resolve_inputs` -- so a spec is testable the moment it is written. Its
per-family issues were closed into this ladder. What remains there is
`1iy.6`, the data-dependent (`Gather`/`Scatter`) fallback, which has no
kernels to convert and so is not a rung here.

## Done when

- Every forward kernel takes `Tile` params and declares its axes, or has a
  recorded reason it cannot.
- No forward kernel still takes raw pointer params.
- A test enumerates every forward `#[tiled_kernel]` with `Tile` params and
  asserts it declares axes and that the derived spec validates.
notes:
## CORRECTION to this epic's closing note, 2026-10-02

The closing note justified leaving 51 forwards on raw pointers by calling route 2
"a legitimate terminal state rather than a migration aid: it declares a real
tile_spec that resolve_inputs consumes, which is what teenygrad-1nr.25 needs."

That is right about SHAPE PROPAGATION and wrong about FUSION, and the second is
anduin's whole point:

  - resolve_inputs/propagate read KernelTileSpec and never a parameter's type,
    so route 2 really is sufficient to decide what tile a node needs;
  - FusionCore -- what lets anduin emit ONE kernel for several nodes, by
    splicing their bodies -- is derived from the auto-prelude's bindings, and
    the auto-prelude runs only for In<Tile<..>>. Its own doc: "input_ident is
    the name the auto-prelude binds the loaded input tensor to".

So a route-2 kernel can be chosen for a fused group and then cannot be generated
into one. Tiles are the inter-kernel mechanism, so the conversion is on the path
to fusion working, not tidying. The "sequence after teenygrad-1nr.25" line is
withdrawn too: .25 revives shape propagation, which route 2 already feeds, while
fusion needs the Tile ABI. Parallel tracks.

The epic's own work stands -- 133/133 accounted for, audited by a test -- and
closing it on that goal was right. What was wrong was the characterisation of
what remained.

## The remainder now has a home

teenygrad-3rk6, an epic, with the population split by WHY each kernel is still
route 2 rather than treated as one lump:

  26  single read at program_id offsets -- convertible today (teenygrad-1a1j)
  20  reads inside a loop -- needs the generated loop (teenygrad-3dp5),
      13 of them also an epilogue hook (teenygrad-3dbg)
   5  TMA descriptors -- `Tile` does not model make_tensor_descriptor;
      deliberately left unimplemented for now

So "cannot be converted" was too strong for 46 of the 51: half is simply undone
and the middle group is blocked on one concrete feature.

Separately, teenygrad-1cli: FusionCore extraction is stubbed to unconditional
None behind a comment saying `#[tile(...)]`'s attrs "no longer exist" -- which
this epic made false by putting them on 129 kernels. That stub is five of the
eleven pre-existing workspace failures.
close_reason:
Complete: all twelve rungs closed, and the closing audit shows no forward kernel
unaccounted for.

  in-scope forward kernels            133
    route 1  In<Tile<..>> conversion   78
    route 2  metadata on pointers      51
    recorded reason, no spec            4
    unaccounted                         0
  excluded by scope (losses)            9
  total forwards in tree              142

The audit is a TEST, not a count --
test_the_closing_audit_leaves_no_forward_kernel_unaccounted_for in
tests/test_tile_declarations.rs -- so it cannot rot.

Done-when, item by item:

1. "Every forward kernel takes Tile params and declares its axes, or has a
   recorded reason it cannot." MET, on the second half: 129 declare, 4 carry a
   recorded reason (channel_cat, channel_chunk, upsample_nearest2d,
   conv2d_bn_silu_gemm).

2. "No forward kernel still takes raw pointer params." NOT MET, and deliberately
   not pursued. 51 declare via the metadata-only form on tagged pointers.
   teenygrad-1nr.18.4 showed why: it was filed believing conv2d was route 2's
   only user, which was true when written and is not now -- that population grew
   to 51 across rungs .5/.7/.8/.9/.10, every one of them a hand-written body
   with its own program_id. Porting them is a programme of its own and is now
   teenygrad-fc9t, which also lists the five macro gaps the conv2d port
   surfaced (chiefly: generate has no epilogue hook, so any kernel with work
   between its loop and its store cannot use it).

   Route 2 is a legitimate terminal state rather than a migration aid: it
   declares a real tile_spec that resolve_inputs consumes, which is what
   teenygrad-1nr.25 needs. Closing on the epic's goal rather than on this
   aspiration.

3. "A test enumerates every forward #[tiled_kernel] with Tile params and asserts
   it declares axes and that the derived spec validates." MET --
   test_every_tile_param_forward_kernel_declares_its_axes and
   test_the_backfilled_kernels_generate_validating_specs.

Scope note: inference kernels only, decided 2026-10-01. The nine undeclared loss
kernels are excluded; nine others in nn/loss were already declared by .4 and
stay, so that family is deliberately half-declared.

Three premise corrections made along the way, each recorded on its issue:
1nr.16's claim that TensorTileSpec cannot express a rank-changing pair (it can);
1tl.10's note that route 2 was no longer available (it was, and is what the epic
used); and y8aa's constraint C2 as a teenyc limitation (it was a missing
impl<T: Copy> Copy for Option<T> in this project's own device prelude).

title: feat: the #[tiled_kernel] conversion recipe, plus a test that a converted kernel really declares its axes
description:
## Goal

Write down the one conversion recipe, and add the test that stops a
converted kernel from silently declaring nothing.

## Why this is first

Nine forward kernels carry `#[tiled_kernel]` and declare no axes. For the
ones with `Tile` params that failure is invisible: the implicit
`BLOCK_SIZE`/`n_elements` convention drives the auto-prelude, the kernel
compiles, the tests pass, and `tile_spec()` is simply absent. Every rung of
this epic can make the same mistake dozens of times over.

## The recipe

One target form (see the epic). `relu_forward` is the worked example:
delete `pid`/`block_start`/`offsets`/`in_bounds`, change
`x_ptr: In<T::Pointer<D>>` to
`#[tile(block = BLOCK_SIZE, extent = n_elements)] x: In<Tile<T, D>>`,
replace the `T::load(...)` call with `x.tensor`, and pass `x.mask` to
`T::store`.

## The enforcement test

Scope it to what the rule can actually mean:

- **In scope**: a **forward** kernel with `In<Tile<..>>`/`Out<Tile<..>>`
  params. It must declare `#[tile(...)]` on every one, and the derived
  `tile_spec()` must `validate()`.
- **Out of scope**: backward kernels (`elu_backward`, `selu_backward` carry
  `#[tiled_kernel]` and `Tile` params today and are not this epic's
  business), and kernels still on raw pointers -- those are simply
  unconverted, which is the normal state until their rung lands.

`#[tiled_kernel]` alone must **not** be the trigger: `matmul_forward` and
`flash_attention2_forward` use it for dtype dispatch with plain
`In<T::Pointer<D>>` params and no tiling meaning at all. Keying the test off
the attribute would fail them for a non-defect.

A `#[tiled_kernel]` forward kernel with `Tile` params and no `#[tile(...)]`
should fail with a message naming the kernel, not pass quietly.

## Backfill

Seven forward kernels need `#[tile(...)]` added, all flat and
single-axis, so all are mechanical:

`elu_forward`, `selu_forward`, `sigmoid_forward`, `log_sigmoid_forward`,
`tanh_forward`, `elemwise_exp_forward` -- plus `conv2d_forward`, which is
the one raw-pointer user and belongs to `teenygrad-1tl.7` rather than here,
since converting it to `Tile` params needs the multi-axis prelude from
`teenygrad-1nr.18`.

So: six here, and the test must tolerate `conv2d_forward` still being on raw
pointers until `.7`.

## Done when

The test exists and passes, the six backfilled kernels generate validating
specs, and the recipe is written where the next rung's author will find it.
notes:
Implemented on feature/1tl.1-tiled-kernel-recipe, PR #53 (base feature/anduin-v2), 2026-09-29.

All three Done-when criteria met:
- tests/test_tile_declarations.rs exists and passes. It parses the crate's own src/ with syn, because an undeclared kernel has no tile_spec() to assert against -- the omission is invisible at the type level. Verified it actually fails by reverting tanh_forward's declaration; it names the kernel, file and parameters and points at the recipe.
- The six backfilled kernels generate validating specs: a second test asserts each tile_spec(rank) describes one flat axis over ranks 1..=4 and validates.
- The recipe is at contributing/TiledKernelRecipe.md, named by the test's failure message and linked from the macro's module doc.

Scope held as written: the rule keys off Tile params on a forward kernel, not off the attribute, so matmul_forward and flash_attention2_forward (dtype dispatch, raw pointers) are not flagged; backward kernels and raw-pointer conv2d_forward are out of scope.

Two additions beyond the issue text. The recipe documents the multi-axis form as well as relu_forward's flat one, since rungs .4/.5/.8 need it and channel_bias_add_forward plus batch_norm_2d_nchw_forward_inference are now worked examples including the broadcast-subset case. It also tabulates what the attributes cannot express against the rung that unblocks each. Separately, the macro module doc claimed the attribute does not add N-axis prelude codegen, which stopped being true at 1nr.18.1; corrected.

Testing on RTX 5070 sm_120 / CUDA 13.4: workspace 410/11 -> 412/11, cuda+hardware 569/10 -> 571/10, riscv+training 281/12 -> 283/12. Exactly the two new tests, failure sets unchanged, no snapshots moved.
close_reason: Landed via PR #53 (226853ba5) into feature/anduin-v2; enforcement test verified against a deliberate regression

title: feat: declared tile axes for the matmul family (Gemm, Linear, QLinearMatMul)
description:
## Goal

Declared tile axes for the matmul family.

## Population

`nn/mlp/linear.rs`, the GEMM in `math/gemm.rs`, and whatever
`QLinearMatMul`/transpose-aware `Gemm` variants `TritonLowering` reaches.

## What is different

This is the only family whose inputs need genuinely *different* tiles from
each other, and `MATMUL_TILE_SPEC` already demonstrates the shape: `a_ptr`
takes `M`, `b_ptr` takes `N`, and `K` — shared by both, present on neither
output — is left unresolved by design.

~~Route 2 throughout: GEMM uses a swizzled 2-D `pid` decode that the flat
`Axis::X` auto-prelude cannot generate.~~

**Premise corrected 2026-09-27.** That was true when written, but this epic has
since settled on every forward kernel taking `In<Tile<..>>`/`Out<Tile<..>>`,
with raw pointer parameters not carried forward. So route 2 is no longer
available to GEMM, and the prelude has to grow instead. Two pieces are needed
and both are now filed:

- `teenygrad-1nr.18.5` -- two or more blocked axes, i.e. the `BLOCK_M x BLOCK_N`
  2-D index tile. The prelude currently rejects a second `block =` outright.
- `teenygrad-1nr.18.3` -- the wrapper-owned loop, for GEMM's K reduction.

Also note `teenygrad-1nr.18`'s recorded correction: `matmul_forward` does not
use `In<Tile<..>>` at all today. It uses a different tensor-descriptor
primitive and has a real internal K-loop, so it is further from the Tile ABI
than a blocked-axis count suggests.

## The thing to get right

Leaving `K` unresolved is correct for `Propagate`, but it means both input
tiles come back at full `K`. For a 1024-cubed f32 GEMM at a 64x32 output tile
that is 256KiB + 128KiB — more than an A100 SM's shared memory, so every GEMM
looks unfusable. The `K` block is a tiling-search decision that needs a
channel into `resolve_inputs` that does not exist yet; `ConstLookup` is the
only way in today and is the wrong one, since it is documented as supplying
full extents and has `divide_by` applied to it.

Declaring the axes here does not depend on that being fixed. Sizing anything
from the result does. Record the dependency rather than working around it.

## Done when

The family has generated specs, `MATMUL_TILE_SPEC`'s hand-authored version is
retired or recorded as still needed, and the `K`-block channel is filed as its
own issue against `resolve_inputs` if it is not already.
close_reason: Complete via PR #69. matmul_forward and linear_forward declare their axes; no QLinearMatMul kernel exists in the tree and MATMUL_TILE_SPEC was already retired. K is reduced and unbound by design, so both operands resolve to full K. The K-block channel is filed as teenygrad-2sd1, and the gap is sharper than described: not a missing const, since resolve_inputs only visits bound axes. Both kernels now emit no grid_spec, via the new #[tile_grid(swizzled)] -- a GROUP_M grouping is not the mixed-radix decode GridAxisBinding::dim documents. The issue's own 2026-09-27 'route 2 no longer available' correction was itself stale; route 2 is what the whole epic has used.

title: feat: declared tile axes and loop carries for flash attention 2
description:
## Goal

Declared tile axes for `flash_attention2_forward` — the one kernel whose
output is produced by a loop carrying accumulator state.

## What is different

`TensorTileSpec` describes tensors sliced by `(block, extent)`. Flash
attention's `acc`/`m_i`/`l_i` are kernel-body-local, shaped by const generics,
and updated in place across a `for k_row in 0..n_ctx_k` loop. That is what
`TileLoopSpec`/`TileCarryBinding` exist for.

`flash_attn2.rs` already carries `#[tiled_kernel]` but no `#[tile(...)]`, so it
generates no spec today. It also uses `Axis::Y`, so route 2.

## Read this before treating completion as "flash attention is schedulable"

Absorbed from `teenygrad-1nr.12`, which this rung supersedes:

- **It is not reachable from the pipeline.** There is no `Op` variant for
  flash / scaled-dot-product attention and no `TritonLowering` arm, and
  `TileGraph::from_dag` only ever sees nodes `TritonLowering` produced. So the
  spec this rung writes has nowhere to attach until `teenygrad-1nr.32` lands.
- **The cost model cannot consume `loop_spec`.** `acc`/`m_i`/`l_i` never cross
  a pointer parameter, so they are never a `TileEdge`, and
  `mem_footprint`/`mem_traffic` are entirely `EdgeId`-keyed. A node-level
  working-set term is `teenygrad-1nr.31`.
- **There is no block-size choice for a search to make.** The current kernel's
  grid is `(N_CTX_Q, BH, 1)` with `for k_row in 0..n_ctx_k` — one row at a
  time, no `BLOCK_KV` const generic anywhere in the signature. So even a fully
  wired `TileLoopSpec` feeds cost-model *accuracy* here, not a search.
- The original pre-revival design left `q_ptr`/`k_ptr`/`v_ptr`/`o_ptr`/`l_ptr`
  **entirely untagged** (`spec.inputs.len() == 0`), putting all the metadata in
  `loop_spec`. Worth deciding deliberately whether to follow that precedent
  rather than inheriting it.

So the deliverable is: the loop's existence and its carried shapes become
queryable, and the distance to a costable, reachable kernel is the two issues
named above.

## On where loop metadata is declared

`CONV2D_LOOP_SPEC` is the existing hand-authored example — attached at the
`TritonLowering` call site rather than declared via `#[tile(...)]`, because
loop-carry metadata is not per-axis and the attribute does not attempt to
derive it. Check whether that split still holds or whether the macro should
grow a `#[tile_loop(...)]` — bearing in mind the old attribute of that name was
removed at `84ca6eedf` for splicing index arithmetic into kernel bodies, which
is not what this would do.

## Done when

`flash_attention2_forward` has a spec with its three carries declared, and the
decision on tagging its pointer params is recorded either way.
close_reason: Complete via PR #70. flash_attention2_forward reports a TileLoopSpec: trip count n_ctx_k, carrying acc/m_i/l_i at [HEAD_DIM]. The untagged pointers are forced, not inherited: every tensor has BH as dim 0 and BH is the grid extent of Axis::Y, never a kernel parameter. Two blockers had to give -- the macro silently ignored loop attributes on an untagged kernel (loop_spec rides inside tile_spec, only generated when a param was tagged), and validate() rejected a spec with no outputs; it now makes one narrow exception for no-tensors-plus-a-loop. Also fixed a latent asymmetry: 1tl.7's unblocked-window fix had landed on only one of the macro's four binding-emission sites.

title: feat: fused composites and the final forward-kernel coverage audit
description:
## Goal

Close out the sweep: the fused composites, and anything the earlier rungs did
not reach.

## Population

`nn/fused/conv2d_bn_silu.rs`, `conv2d_bn_silu_tiled.rs`,
`conv2d_bn_silu_gemm.rs` (3 forward), plus any forward kernel not claimed by
rungs 2-11.

## Why last

A fused kernel's spec is the composition of its parts' specs — conv's window,
batchnorm's per-channel reduction, silu's identity — so it cannot be written
honestly until those three are settled on their own rungs.

There is a second question here that the other rungs do not raise: these
kernels exist because the scheduler could not yet fuse them itself. Once
`propagate` is back (`teenygrad-1nr.25`) and the conv/norm/elementwise specs
are real, a hand-fused `conv2d_bn_silu` is either redundant or a benchmark
baseline. Deciding which is part of this rung.

## Final audit

Re-run the count this epic opened with. Every forward kernel should be in one
of three buckets, with none unaccounted for:

- route 1 (full conversion), or
- route 2 (metadata-only), or
- a recorded reason it has no spec.

## Done when

The three fused kernels are resolved, the audit shows no unaccounted forward
kernel, and the epic's opening table can be restated with the new numbers.
notes:
Scope note (2026-10-01): the epic is now INFERENCE KERNELS ONLY, so this rung's
"final forward-kernel coverage audit" must audit against the in-scope population
(133), not all 142 forwards. The nine undeclared loss kernels are excluded by
decision, not missing -- see teenygrad-1tl's scope note.

Audit should expect, at the time this rung runs:
- 125+ of 133 declared
- channel_cat, channel_chunk, upsample_nearest2d undeclared WITH a recorded
  reason on the kernel (teenygrad-1tl.5) -- these are complete, not gaps
- nine loss forwards declared and nine excluded, i.e. nn/loss deliberately
  half-declared
- prelu_forward and log_softmax_forward: orphans that belonged to no rung's
  population. Whatever picks them up, the audit is the backstop that was
  always going to find them -- worth declaring before this rung rather than in
  it.
close_reason: Complete via PR #81. conv2d_bn_silu and conv2d_bn_silu_tiled declared (the tiled one with two blocked axes, a 2-D carry, and a stated grid order -- the second real user of #[tile_grid(order=..)]); conv2d_bn_silu_gemm carries a recorded reason (implicit-GEMM view: flattened spatial M and a strided allocation width, neither expressible per-axis, plus it would need #[tile_grid(swizzled)]). All three metadata-only: the bn affine and SiLU sit between loop and store, which #[tile_loop(generate)] has no epilogue hook for. Audit landed as a TEST so it cannot rot: 133 in-scope forwards, 78 route 1, 51 route 2, 4 recorded reasons, 0 unaccounted, 9 losses excluded by scope. Second question decided: benchmark baseline, not redundant -- propagate is not back (1nr.25 in progress), and even once it is these are the reference its output must match or beat.

title: feat: convert the unary flat elementwise kernels to #[tiled_kernel] (~53 kernels)
description:
## Goal

Route 1 (full conversion) for every unary, shape-preserving, single-extent
kernel — the largest rung and the one with no design content at all.

## Population (~53 forward kernels)

- `nn/activation/*` — 27 forward, of which `relu`/`silu` are already done and
  `elu.rs`/`tanh.rs`/`sigmoid.rs` are part-way (`#[tiled_kernel]`, no `#[tile]`).
  Includes `leaky_relu`, `hardtanh`, `softshrink` etc. that take an extra
  scalar parameter — the prelude does not care, extra scalars pass through.
- `nn/tensor/elemwise_unary.rs` — 22 forward.
- `nn/loss/elementwise.rs` — 4 forward.

## Why it is purely mechanical

Every one has the same body shape: compute `offsets`, load, one expression,
store. The auto-prelude generates exactly that. `leaky_relu_forward` is the
representative before/after.

The spec that falls out is the identity: input and output share one
`extent_param`, so `resolve_inputs` round-trips an output tile to the same
input tile. That is the assertion for the whole rung.

## Watch for

- A kernel whose real extent parameter is not called `n_elements`, or whose
  block const is not `BLOCK_SIZE` — give it an explicit
  `#[tile(block=.., extent=..)]` rather than renaming the parameter.
- A kernel that reads its input more than once, or at an offset — that is not
  this rung.
- `rank` is not baked into a generated spec; it is supplied per node, the same
  way `flat_elementwise_tile_spec` does it. Converting these kernels should
  let `flat_elementwise_tile_spec`'s `Box::leak` hand-rolled path start
  retiring.

## Done when

Every kernel in the population is on route 1 or has a recorded reason, the
enforcement test from the recipe subtask passes over all of them, and
`resolve_inputs` identity round-trip tests cover a representative handful.
notes:
Implemented on feature/1tl.2-unary-flat-elementwise, 2026-09-29.

Population: 53 forward kernels, as estimated. 8 were already converted (relu, silu, elu,
selu, sigmoid, log_sigmoid, tanh, elemwise_exp -- the last six backfilled by 1tl.1).
38 converted here. 7 excluded with reasons; the issue's population list was over-inclusive.

Excluded, with the rung each belongs to:
- prelu_forward: two inputs (x, slope) -> 1tl.3 (or .4 if the slope is treated as broadcast).
- softmax_forward, log_softmax_forward: row-wise over n_cols with _n_rows as the first i32,
  not flat single-extent. 1tl.8 already names softmax in its own title.
- l1_loss_forward, mse_loss_forward, huber_loss_forward, smooth_l1_loss_forward: two inputs
  (x, target) -> 1tl.3.

The 38 were perfectly uniform, which is what made a scripted conversion safe: every one had
the identical four-line canonical prelude, every one bound `let x = T::load(..)`, and every
one bound `let y` for its result. That last point is the trap -- `y` collides with the new
Out parameter -- so the transform renames the local to `out`. Three kernels in extra.rs
(swish, thresholded_relu, shrink) have no D generic and take Tile<T, f32>. The approach was
validated on misc.rs alone, numerics confirmed, before the other 33 were touched.

Net -813 lines (233 insertions, 1046 deletions): each kernel loses its prelude, its
eight-argument T::load and its six-argument masked T::store.

FINDING 1 -- the Done-when criterion as written is not true. "resolve_inputs round-trips an
output tile to the same input tile" holds only at rank 1. Above that it is the
product-preserving identity: the flat spec declares one binding whose dims spans every
dimension, so resolution puts the whole element count on the innermost dim and a bare 1 on
the rest, exactly as TileAxisBinding::dims documents. ReluForward at rank 2 takes [8, 9] to
[1, 72]. Probed across ranks 1-4; also confirmed that one unresolved output dim unresolves
the entire flattened axis ([8, None] -> [None, None]), since a partial element count cannot
be split back across dims. The new test in graph/tile_resolve.rs asserts what actually
holds, over four representative kernels and ranks 1-4.

FINDING 2 -- the declarations are not yet read by the graph layer, so this rung delivers no
scheduling benefit on its own. The note about retiring flat_elementwise_tile_spec's
Box::leak path is stale: that function no longer exists. What exists is exec_from in
graph/mod.rs, which hardcodes `let tile_spec = None`, and only three ops override it (Relu,
Silu, and one fixed-rank op). So all 38 kernels now declare their axes correctly and
TileGraph::propagate still treats every one of them as a hard boundary. Wiring exec_from to
pass the macro-derived tile_spec(shape.len()) is about 20 mechanical call sites and is what
makes this rung pay off; exec_from's own doc comment already states every caller is shaped
for it. Not done here because it is outside this issue's Done-when -- worth its own issue or
folding into 1tl.12.

Testing on RTX 5070 sm_120 / CUDA 13.4, all three configs converged with zero pending
snapshots and failure sets exactly at baseline: workspace 412/11 -> 413/11, cuda+hardware
571/10 -> 572/10, riscv+training 283/12 -> 284/12. The +1 in each is the new round-trip
test. Zero numeric regressions: the only non-snapshot failures are the pre-existing Anduin
todo! stubs, the four fusion_core stubs, and teenygrad-15k's three RISC-V trig ICEs.
Snapshot churn was 36 source/asm pairs per config, accepted only after numerics passed.
close_reason: Landed via PR #54 (a98d2f94b); 38 converted, 7 deferred with reasons, verified on hardware under CUDA 13.4

title: feat: convert the multi-input flat elementwise kernels to #[tiled_kernel] (~18 kernels)
description:
## Goal

Route 1 for the flat elementwise kernels with more than one input — the first
rung that produces a multi-operand `KernelTileSpec`.

## Population (~18 forward kernels)

`nn/tensor/elemwise_binary.rs` (16: `add`/`sub`/`mul`/`div`/`pow`/`fmod`/
`min`/`max`/`mean`/`sum`/`clip`/`where`/the four comparisons),
`nn/tensor/elemwise_add.rs`. `clip` and `where` are ternary.

## What is new here

The auto-prelude already supports this — it computes **one** `offsets` and
hands it to every `In<Tile>`/`Out<Tile>` param — so the conversion itself is
no harder than the unary rung. What is new is the spec: `inputs` gains one
`TensorTileSpec` per operand, all sharing the single `extent_param`.

This is the first real exercise of `resolve_inputs`' multi-input path against
a generated spec. `MATMUL_TILE_SPEC` covers the distinct-names case; this
covers the all-operands-share-one-name case, where every input tile should
come back identical to the output tile.

## Precondition to check

All operands must be the same shape — the shared `offsets` makes that a
correctness requirement, not a style choice. A binary op that broadcasts
belongs on the mixed-extent rung, not here. Audit the population for this
before converting, and record any that are secretly broadcasting.

## Also relevant

`TileGraph::propagate` zips `spec.inputs` positionally against a node's parent
edges. Two consequences worth a test here, since this is the first family
where they can bite:

- Operand order must match parent-edge order.
- `x + x` dedups to one parent edge against two spec inputs, which the v1
  walk treated as a hard boundary.

## Done when

Every kernel in the population is converted, each spec declares one input per
operand, and `resolve_inputs` returns N identical tiles for an N-operand op.
notes:
Implemented on feature/1tl.3-multi-input-flat, PR #56, commit 21fba9599.

17 kernels converted: 16 in elemwise_binary.rs plus elemwise_add_forward. Each operand declares the shared axis; the spec gains one TensorTileSpec per operand, all naming n_elements.

Precondition audit (the issue's own requirement) came back clean: every kernel in the population uses a single offsets for all loads and the store, so none is secretly broadcasting and none belongs on 1tl.4. Correction to the issue text: elemwise_clip_forward is described as ternary but is unary at the pointer level, its bounds being f32 scalars rather than tensors. It converts identically either way.

The rung's characteristic assertion is in graph/tile_resolve.rs: for two and three operands every input tile resolves identically, and to the same product-preserving shape the unary family gives. It also pins operand order to the signature, since propagate zips spec.inputs positionally against parent edges -- a drift there is invisible for add and very visible for sub.

NOT covered here, and carried to teenygrad-1nr.25: the issue flags that x + x dedups to one parent edge against two spec inputs, which v1's walk treated as a hard boundary. That is propagate behaviour and propagate does not exist on the v2 TileGraph yet, so it cannot be tested from this rung.

Snapshots: 69 re-recorded after numerics passed -- 17 kernels x 4 variants, plus teeny-compiler's elemwise_add_forward_sm90 PTX snapshot. That last one sits outside kernels/ and outside -p teeny-kernels, so a kernels-scoped acceptance pass misses it and the failure only appears in a full workspace run. Four snapshot directories exist in this workspace; cargo insta accept --workspace is what covers them.

Testing on RTX 5070 sm_120 / CUDA 13.4, zero pending snapshots repo-wide: workspace 414/11 -> 415/11, cuda+hardware 573/10 -> 574/10, riscv+training 285/12 -> 286/12. Zero numeric regressions.

GAP FOUND LATER (route audit, 2026-09-30): four kernels that belong to this rung were never converted. l1_loss_forward, mse_loss_forward, huber_loss_forward and smooth_l1_loss_forward are flat, same-offset, two-operand -- exactly this rung's shape. They were deferred out of 1tl.2 as 'multi-input, belongs to 1tl.3', but this rung's population was defined by FILE (elemwise_binary.rs, elemwise_add.rs) rather than by shape, so they were never picked up and it closed without them. They remain unconverted and need a follow-up; nothing blocks them.
close_reason: Landed via PR #56 (e9c6f6a6c); 17 kernels converted, precondition audit clean, x+x dedup case carried to teenygrad-1nr.25

title: feat: tile axes for mixed-extent operand kernels (bias-add, embedding, NLL/BCE/ranking losses)
description:
## Goal

Kernels whose operands are real tensors of *different* extents — a per-channel
bias, an embedding table, a per-sample target vector.

## Population (~16 forward kernels)

`nn/tensor/channel_bias_add.rs` (2), `nn/loss/embedding.rs` (2),
`nn/loss/nll.rs` (3), `nn/loss/bce.rs` (6), `nn/loss/ranking.rs` (3).

## Why this rung exists

The auto-prelude computes one `offsets` from one extent and applies it to
every tile param, so an operand with a different extent **cannot** go through
route 1. These are route 2 (metadata-only) unless the kernel is restructured,
which is out of scope here.

The design question this rung has to settle, and the reason it sits before the
windowed rung: what does the spec say about an operand that does not receive
the output's block? A bias of shape `[C]` against an output tiled on `HW` gets
no block on any axis — it falls back to full extent, which is correct and
conservative, but it should be *declared* that way rather than achieved by
omission.

`teenygrad-1iy.3` raises the same question as "broadcasting: an operand
broadcast along an axis does not get the output's block on that axis.
Establish what the spec says here." Settle it on this rung and record the
answer there.

## Note on `channel_bias_add`

It uses `Axis::Y`, so it is doubly disqualified from route 1 — the prelude is
`Axis::X` only. Worth confirming whether its grid axes should be declared via
`#[tile(dim = Y)]` (teenygrad-1nr.19 supports `dim=`).

## Done when

Every kernel in the population has a generated spec, the broadcast/mixed-extent
convention is written down, and `resolve_inputs` tests assert the
non-block operand comes back at full extent.
notes:
PARTIALLY DELIVERED by PR #57 (commit 0a0e06f74), 2026-09-29. Stays OPEN: one kernel of the population still has no spec.

The issue's premise was stale in three ways, all because 1nr.18.1 landed after it was written -- it says these kernels cannot go through route 1, that the prelude is Axis::X only, and that channel_bias_add is doubly disqualified. Broadcast subsets and dim = Y both exist now, and channel_bias_add_forward was converted by .18.1 itself.

Population of 16, classified by reading the bodies rather than by file:
- 1 already converted: channel_bias_add_forward.
- 9 flat SAME-extent with a single offsets -- converted in PR #57: bce.rs (bce_loss, bce_with_logits, soft_margin, kl_div, poisson_nll, gaussian_nll), margin_ranking, hinge_embedding, multilabel_soft_margin. These are 1tl.3's shape, not mixed-extent; they were outside 1tl.3 only because its population was defined by file.
- 5 row-wise reductions (row_offs/tgt_off offsets, T::sum, no canonical prelude) -- these belong to 1tl.8 and should be moved there: nll_loss, cross_entropy, multi_margin, cosine_embedding, triplet_margin.
- 1 loop-carried: nchw_bias_add (a `while` over two offset expressions) -- blocked on 1nr.18.3, edge added.

So only two members were genuinely mixed-extent and one was already done. The conversion script independently confirmed the split by refusing exactly the three row-wise kernels in the files it touched.

THE DESIGN QUESTION IS SETTLED, and settling it exposed a defect rather than a convention gap. #[tiled_kernel] gave every tensor the FIRST tile parameter's axis list (spec_axes = all_tile_param_attrs[0]), so channel_bias_add_forward's (C,) bias reported rank 2 with N blocked -- an axis it does not have. A scheduler reading that would size the bias tile along a nonexistent dimension. The prelude was always correct, which is why the kernel is numerically fine; only the metadata lied.

Each parameter now reports its own declared axes. bias is rank 1, axes empty, untiled ["C"], and resolves to its own full extent. The convention: an operand declares exactly the axes it has; one sharing no blocked axis carries no binding and falls back to full extent -- correct and conservative, and now declared rather than achieved by omission. Recorded on 1iy.3, which raises the same question. Asserted in graph/tile_resolve.rs::test_a_broadcast_operand_resolves_to_its_own_full_extent.

That macro fix is also a precondition for 1tl.7, where a conv input's axes differ from its output's -- previously noted there as a limitation, now understood as a correctness bug and fixed.

TO CLOSE THIS RUNG: convert nchw_bias_add once 1nr.18.3 lands, and move the five row-wise kernels to 1tl.8's population.
close_reason: Landed fully via PR #58 (03a375e0f): nchw_bias_add converted as an independent walk, needing only 1nr.18.1's grid coverage rather than the accumulation loop. Nine flat kernels landed in PR #57 with the broadcast convention and the per-parameter-axes macro fix; five row-wise kernels moved to 1tl.8.

title: feat: tile axes for statically-indexed shape changers (12 pads, upsample, transpose, cat/chunk, flatten)
description:
## Goal

Kernels where the output index maps to a *different* input index by a fixed,
data-independent rule — padding, nearest-neighbour upsampling, transpose,
concat/chunk, flatten.

## Population (~18 forward kernels)

12 pads (`constant`/`reflection`/`replication`/`circular`, 1d/2d/3d),
`upsample_nearest2d`, `transpose`, `channel_cat`, `channel_chunk`,
`mlp/flatten`.

## Why they are a rung of their own

The mapping is affine and known at compile time, but it is not the identity,
so route 1's shared `offsets` is wrong for them. Route 2 (metadata-only)
throughout.

Each sub-family asks the same question differently:

- **Pad** — an output tile overlapping the pad region reads *fewer* input
  elements than its own width, and an interior tile reads exactly its width.
  This is the one case where the input region is smaller than the output tile,
  the opposite of the windowed rung.
- **Upsample** — one input element feeds `scale^2` output elements, so an
  output tile of `block` needs `ceil(block / scale)` input elements. A
  genuinely different arithmetic from `TileWindow`'s receptive field.
- **Transpose** — axes permute, so the output's axis `i` block belongs on the
  input's axis `perm[i]`. Name-matching handles this correctly *if* the axes
  are named consistently; it is a good test that the naming convention holds
  when dim order does not.
- **Cat/chunk** — the output axis is a concatenation of several inputs' axes.
  A tile may span a seam. Likely a recorded route-3 reason rather than a spec.

## Done when

Each sub-family has a spec or a recorded reason, and the pad and upsample
arithmetic is either expressible in the existing types or the gap is written
up as a follow-up on `teeny_core::model::tile_spec`.
notes:
Rung complete via PR #67 (after #66's pads). All 17 accounted for: 14 declared,
3 with a recorded reason on the kernel itself.

Declared: 12 pads (#66), transpose_2d, flatten.
Recorded reason: channel_cat, channel_chunk, upsample_nearest2d.

Both of this rung's open questions are answered:
- Pad arithmetic IS expressible in the existing types -- padding is a window of
  stride = 1, kernel = 1.
- Upsample arithmetic is NOT, provably: the receptive field is minimised at
  block, and upsample needs less. 12l6 holds the analysis.

The naming-convention question this rung raised is settled affirmatively by
transpose: name matching alone carries a block across permuted dim order, so no
permutation field is needed.

New macro gap found and fixed here: grid_spec() took the output's TENSOR DIM
order, but GridSpec::axes is documented as outermost-to-innermost decode order.
transpose is the first kernel where those differ (output [N, M], decodes pid_m
outer), and the generated grid was silently reversed. #[tile_grid(order = [..])]
now states it. Worth checking any future kernel whose pid decode does not walk
the output's dims in order.
close_reason: Complete via PR #66 (12 pads) and #67 (transpose, flatten, three recorded reasons). All 17 accounted for: 14 declared, 3 with a reason recorded on the kernel itself. Pad arithmetic IS expressible (a window of stride 1, kernel 1); upsample's provably is not, and 12l6 is now decided as route 3 since upsample is the only shrinking map in the tree. The naming-convention question is settled affirmatively by transpose: name matching alone carries a block across permuted dim order.

title: feat: allow #[tile(...)] on both Tile-typed and raw-pointer params in one kernel
description:
## Goal

Let one kernel carry `#[tile(...)]` on both `In<Tile<..>>`-typed parameters and
raw-pointer parameters.

## Current behaviour

`macros/teeny-macros/src/macros/tiled_kernel.rs` rejects the combination
outright:

> this kernel mixes `#[tile(...)]`-tagged `In<Tile<..>>`/`Out<Tile<..>>`
> parameters with `#[tile(...)]`-tagged raw pointer parameters -- not
> supported in one kernel yet (teenygrad-1nr.19)

So each kernel is all-route-1 or all-route-2. That is why `conv2d_forward`
declares its *output* axes on a raw pointer with `block = BLOCK_OW` rather
than using a `Tile`-typed output: one tagged raw-pointer input forces the
whole signature onto route 2.

## Why it is worth lifting

A conv, a norm or a GEMM has one output with a flat, blocked innermost axis —
exactly what the auto-prelude generates — alongside inputs whose access is
hand-written. Today the prelude has to be hand-written too, purely because of
the mixing rule.

## Not a blocker

Every rung of this epic can be completed without it, via route 2. Filed so the
constraint is visible rather than rediscovered, and so the boilerplate it
forces can be quantified once a few of the later rungs are done.

## Done when

Either the restriction is lifted with a test covering a mixed signature, or
there is a recorded reason the two preludes cannot coexist.
close_reason: Moot under the direction settled 2026-09-23: every forward kernel takes In<Tile<..>>/Out<Tile<..>>, and raw pointer params are not carried forward. The restriction this issue proposed lifting -- that one kernel cannot mix #[tile(...)]-tagged Tile params with #[tile(...)]-tagged raw pointers -- only bites when both forms coexist in a signature, which the target form never does. If a kernel genuinely cannot take Tile params, that is a recorded reason on its own rung, not a case for mixing.

title: feat: declared tile axes with real TileWindows for conv 1/2/3d and the nine pools
description:
## Goal

Declared tile axes for the sliding-window kernels — the first rung whose specs
need `TileWindow`, and the first where the input tile is *larger* than the
output tile.

## Population (13 forward kernels)

`conv1d`, `conv2d`, `conv3d` (`conv2d_forward` is the reference), and the nine
pools (`maxpool`/`avgpool`/`lppool`, 1d/2d/3d).

## `#[tile(...)]` cannot express a window at all today

Absorbed from `teenygrad-1nr.29`, which this rung supersedes. `TileWindow` is
**never constructed anywhere in the repo** — `#[tiled_kernel]` hardcodes
`window: None` at `macros/teeny-macros/src/macros/tiled_kernel.rs:835` and
`:915`. So this rung is two halves, and they have to be one issue because the
syntax is unusable until something emits it:

1. **Extend the attribute** to name the three const generics, e.g.
   `#[tile(name = "H", extent = H, window(stride = STRIDE_H, pad = PAD_H, kernel = KH))]`,
   and have the generated `tile_spec()` emit a real `TileWindow`.
2. **Populate it** on all 13 kernels.

## Why the current conv2d declaration resolves nothing

`conv2d_forward` declares `#[tile(name = "H", extent = H)]` on `x_ptr` and
`#[tile(name = "OH", extent = OH)]` on `y_ptr`. Propagation is pure
name-matching, `H` and `OH` are different names, and there is no window to
relate them — so seeding `OW` resolves nothing on `x_ptr` and the input falls
back to full extent. Correct, but conv is effectively untileable.

**Naming question to settle here:** should a windowed input axis reuse the
*output* axis's `extent_param` (so `x_ptr`'s spatial axis is named `OH` and the
window explains the difference), or keep `H` and have the window carry both
names? The first keeps name-matching as the single resolution mechanism; the
second is more literal about the signature.

## The arithmetic

`(block - 1) * stride + kernel` — forward, exact, one answer. It is **not**
`Op::infer_input_shape`'s inverse: padding shifts the window's origin, it does
not change the extent, so an interior tile needs the full receptive field.
`teenygrad-1nr.30` has the derivation and the worked counter-example (3x3,
`p=1`, `s=1`, block 8 reads 10).

`CONV1D_TILE_SPEC`/`CONV3D_TILE_SPEC` currently declare `x_ptr` with
`axes: &[]` — no bindings at all. Retire those hand-authored consts rather
than keeping them alongside generated specs.

## Hard dependency on const values

A windowed axis only resolves if `resolve_inputs`' `ConstLookup` can supply
`stride`/`kernel`. Nothing can build one at graph level today — `ExecutableOp`
exposes `tile_spec()` and no companion for parameter values. Without that,
every window declared here silently falls back to full extent. Declaring is
still worth doing first; the resolution path is `teenygrad-1nr.30`'s problem.

## Acceptance

- The attribute accepts a window and the generated `tile_spec()` emits one.
- `Conv2dForward::<f32>::tile_spec()` returns a spec whose `x_ptr` spatial axes
  carry `Some(TileWindow { .. })` naming `STRIDE_H`/`PAD_H`/`KH` and the W
  equivalents; all 13 kernels likewise.
- Existing specs without a window are byte-identical.
- `resolve_inputs` tests assert the receptive field for an interior tile
  against hand-computed values with an explicit const table.
- The hand-authored conv consts are retired.
notes:
Window coverage complete via PR #65: all 13 kernels declare a window on every
spatial axis (1-D 1, 2-D 2, 3-D 3). conv2d_bias_forward, conv3d_forward and the
three 3-D pools were undeclared entirely and now carry axes + windows.

Mechanism, correcting this issue's premise: the dependency on 1nr.18.5 was
mis-specified. This whole family is route 2 -- hand-written bodies with their
own program_id/arange -- so generalising the auto-prelude could never reach
them. What was actually needed was for the macro to emit a binding for an axis
that declares a window but no block, with block_const "1". That is truthful
about the body: the pid decode yields one scalar oh, and one output row reads
KH input rows == (1-1)*stride+kernel.

Found en route: conv2d's H window had been written since 1nr.18.2 and silently
discarded -- asserted and documented as "dropped", which is why it survived.
And resolve_inputs' const fallback applied window arithmetic to an axis's FULL
extent, yielding more than the extent and claiming a read past the tensor;
an unresolved windowed axis now stays at full extent.

Also: the recorded blocker "avgpool3d has no obvious input D" was wrong. The
parameter is Dv, spelled to avoid colliding with the dtype generic D.

Still open on this rung, per the issue's own text: these windows do not
*resolve*, because nothing builds a ConstLookup at graph level (1nr.30), and a
windowed axis resolving against an untiled output variable gets no block.
Giving one a real block means rewriting the pid decode -- 1nr.18.4, a port.
close_reason: Landed via PR #65 (merge 17b68c66d). All five acceptance items met: the attribute emits a real TileWindow, all 13 kernels declare one per spatial axis (1-D 1 / 2-D 2 / 3-D 3), specs without a window are byte-identical (zero snapshot changes), resolve_inputs asserts the receptive field against an explicit const table, and the hand-authored conv consts are gone. Window *resolution* is not part of this rung: the issue defers it to 1nr.30, which is itself blocked by this one, so holding this open deadlocked both.

title: feat: declared tile axes for row reductions and norms (LayerNorm/InstanceNorm/RmsNorm/GroupNorm/BatchNorm/softmax)
description:
## Goal

Declared tile axes for kernels that reduce a whole row before writing it back
at the same rank — the norms and softmax.

## Population (~9 forward kernels)

`nn/norm/layernorm.rs`, `instancenorm.rs`, `rmsnorm.rs`, `groupnorm.rs`,
`batchnorm.rs` (4 forward), `nn/activation/softmax.rs`.

## What is new

The reduced axis cannot be tiled: a row's mean needs the whole row. So the
spec's job here is to say which axis is *not* available for tiling
(`reduction_axis`), and to leave the rest correctly propagating.

Three existing pieces of the type all land on this rung at once, which is
exactly the combination `teenygrad-1nr.15` was filed about after `.10` and
`.11` were built but "never combined or tried together against the real
kernel":

- `reduction_axis` — the row axis.
- `divide_by` — GroupNorm's `channels_per_group = C / G`.
- flattened `dims` — BatchNorm2d's single `BLOCK_HW` spanning dims 2 and 3.

## GroupNorm cannot use a `const` spec

`divide_by` is a plain number fixed at spec-construction time, but `G` is a
runtime parameter. So `GroupNormForward::tile_spec()` has to be built per
instance from its own data, not returned from a shared `const`. Check whether
the generated `tile_spec()` can express that at all — if it cannot, that is a
finding for the macro, and the honest answer may be that GroupNorm stays
hand-authored.

`batchnorm.rs` uses `Axis::Y`, so route 2 regardless.

## Done when

Each kernel has a spec declaring its reduction axis, `BATCHNORM2D_TILE_SPEC`'s
hand-authored version is either retired or recorded as still necessary, and
the GroupNorm `divide_by` question has a written answer.
notes:
INCREMENT 1 delivered on feature/1tl.8-row-reductions. Two of the three Done-when items answered; declarations partly done.

=== MACRO CAPABILITY (the blocker) ===
Before this, the macro hardcoded `reduction_axis: None` at four sites and `divide_by: None` at three, so a reduction axis could not be declared at all. Added `#[tile(extent = N, reduce)]`, emitted in both the Tile and raw-pointer paths. More than one `reduce` per tensor is rejected, since `reduction_axis` holds a single index.

=== A GAP FOUND BY TRYING IT ON A REAL KERNEL ===
`TileCarryBinding::shape_consts` was documented as holding names of `const {NAME}: i32` generics. Every row reduction in the tree accumulates into `T::zeros::<D>(&[1])` -- a scalar -- and there is no const named `1`. So the names-only contract could describe conv2d's `acc: [BLOCK_OW]` and NONE of the nine reductions. Proving `#[tile_loop]` on conv2d alone (teenygrad-1nr.18.3) did not surface this; it is exactly what teenygrad-1nr.15 warned about, these pieces having been built but never combined against a real kernel.

I first declared LayerNorm's carries as `[BLOCK_N]`, which compiled and validated and was simply wrong. Caught by checking the body before declaring the next kernel rather than pattern-matching from the first.

Fixed by widening the contract: an entry is now a const name OR a decimal integer literal. No type change was needed -- `shape_consts` is already `&[&'static str]`, so `"1"` fits. Two facts checked first: `validate()` rejects an empty shape, so "empty means scalar" was unavailable; and nothing consumes `shape_consts` anywhere, so the contract is documentation-only and widening it breaks no consumer. The doc now states a consumer must try an integer parse before a name lookup.

=== DECLARED (3 of 14) ===
layer_norm_forward, layer_norm_forward_inference, rms_norm_forward. Each: x/y rank 2 with reduction_axis = Some(1) on the N axis, weight/bias [N], saved stats [M], scalar carries, trip_count [N, BLOCK_N] for cdiv(N, BLOCK_N). LayerNorm's three outputs (y, mean, rstd) combine with a reduction axis and a declared loop for the first time.

Verified metadata-only: the source snapshots pass unchanged despite the `#[kernel]` -> `#[tiled_kernel]` switch.

=== VERIFIED CARRY SHAPES FOR THE REST, so nobody re-derives them ===
  rms_norm_forward                 sq_sum [1]                         BLOCK_N    DONE
  layer_norm_forward{,_inference}  sum [1], var_sum [1]               BLOCK_N    DONE
  instance_norm_forward{,_inf}     sum [1], var_sum [1]               BLOCK_L
  group_norm_forward{,_inf}        sum [1], var_sum [1]               BLOCK_NL
  batch_norm_stats_forward         acc_sum [BLOCK_N], acc_sum_sq [BLOCK_N]  <- const-shaped, the odd one out
  softmax_forward                  NO CARRIES -- loads its whole row in one tile, so it needs a
                                   reduction axis and no loop declaration at all
  batch_norm_forward_inference     INDEPENDENT WALK -- grid coverage only, see 1nr.18.3's audit
  batch_norm_normalize_forward     INDEPENDENT WALK -- same
  the five row-wise losses         moved here from 1tl.4; each has a per-row target operand
                                   alongside the reduced data

=== ANSWER: GroupNorm's divide_by ===
Cannot be expressed, and the issue's suspicion was right. `G` is a runtime `i32` PARAMETER, not a const generic (confirmed: `group_norm_forward<T, D, const BLOCK_NL: i32>(... , _N: i32, C: i32, L: i32, G: i32, ...)`). `divide_by: Option<usize>` is fixed at spec-construction time, and the generated `tile_spec()` returns `&'static` data, so it cannot carry a per-instance divisor.

Three ways forward, none taken here:
  (a) GroupNorm declares no divide_by. Its channel axis then falls back to full extent C rather than C/G -- conservative, correct, less precise. Cheapest, and consistent with the "never smaller than needed" philosophy elsewhere.
  (b) The generated tile_spec() grows a parameter for runtime divisors. There is precedent: the flat path already emits `tile_spec(rank: usize)`.
  (c) GroupNorm stays hand-authored -- rejected, since eliminating hand-authored specs is the point of this epic.
Recommend (a) now and (b) if a consumer ever needs the precision.

=== ANSWER: BATCHNORM2D_TILE_SPEC ===
Already retired. It survives only in a doc comment in anduin/mod.rs, which claimed BatchNorm2d "gained" it -- the const was deleted with the other hand-authored specs. Corrected to record that history. Same stale-reference pattern as CONV2D_LOOP_SPEC and flat_elementwise_tile_spec.
close_reason: Complete via PR #68. All seven forward kernels declare their axes (the issue's ~9 over-counted; batchnorm has two forwards, not four). BATCHNORM2D_TILE_SPEC is retired. The GroupNorm divide_by question has a written answer in groupnorm.rs, and it is no: divide_by is fixed at spec-construction time while G is a runtime param and tile_spec() returns &'static data, so C falls back to full extent. Two premises were stale and retired rather than acted on: batchnorm contains no Axis::Y, and the divide_by answer predated this rung. batch_norm_normalize needed #[tile_grid(order = [C])] -- the first kernel needing that attribute for selection rather than ordering, since its grid is [C] while its output is [N, C].

title: feat: declared tile axes for rank-changing reductions (reduce_* family, global pools, cumulative scans)
description:
## Goal

Declared tile axes for the kernels in `nn/tensor/reduction.rs`, where the
output has a *different rank* from the input.

## Population (14 forward kernels)

`reduce_sum`, `reduce_mean`, `reduce_max`, `reduce_min`, `reduce_prod`,
`reduce_l1`, `reduce_l2`, `reduce_log_sum`, `reduce_log_sum_exp`,
`reduce_sum_square`, `global_avg_pool`, `global_max_pool`, `cum_sum`,
`cum_prod`.

## The known blocker

`teenygrad-1nr.16` already records that `TensorTileSpec` cannot express a
rank-changing input/output pair: the input's reduced axis has no counterpart
in the output, so name-matching has nothing to match it against and it falls
back to full extent. For a full reduction that is the entire tensor, which is
correct but makes the spec worthless for footprint.

This rung's job is to establish whether the answer is:

1. the fallback is genuinely correct and the spec should say so explicitly, or
2. `TensorTileSpec` needs a way to relate an input axis to "no output axis",
   which is a change to the type in `teeny-core`.

`cum_sum`/`cum_prod` are rank-*preserving* but sequentially dependent — every
output element depends on all preceding ones along the scan axis. Those are
probably a recorded route-3 reason, and worth separating from the true
reductions early.

## Done when

Each of the 14 has a spec or a recorded reason, and `teenygrad-1nr.16` has a
decision rather than a description.
close_reason: Complete via PR #71. All 14 declared. Settles teenygrad-1nr.16 as option 1: the fallback is genuinely correct and TensorTileSpec needs no new field -- a rank-changing pair resolves by name matching, and the reduced axis having no binding IS the truth, since one output row needs its whole input row. cum_sum/cum_prod turned out declarable rather than route 3. BLOCK_INNER deliberately not bound to the reduced axis: it is the load width, not a tiling.

title: refactor: align emit_bin and emit_asm semantics across CUDA and RISC-V backends (asm=PTX, bin=SASS)
description:
Context

CompilerOptions (force, emit_asm, emit_bin) landed in ed5065739 and LlvmCompiler honours it
uniformly: emit_bin maps to --emit=obj and emit_asm maps to --emit=asm, for every target
triple. But the two backends do not mean the same thing by those two outputs.

RISC-V

- emit_bin yields a linked RISC-V ELF shared library. teeny_riscv::device::program opens it
  and resolves the entry point (it cannot be dlopened on a non-RISC-V host).
- emit_asm yields .s RISC-V assembly text.
- The two artifacts are genuinely different, and bin is the one that executes.

CUDA

- The artifact returned by teeny_cuda::compiler::compile_kernel is consumed as PTX:
  teeny_test::load_program_from_ptx takes the bytes directly, and the re-export doc in
  drivers/teeny-cuda/src/compiler/mod.rs describes compile_kernel as compiling to PTX.
- The real device binary (cubin/SASS) is produced separately and later by PtxCompiler
  (nvptxcompiler) at load time, not by the emit options at all.
- So on CUDA both emit flags currently land in the same region (PTX), and the artifact
  corresponding to the RISC-V bin (device machine code) is never an emit output.

Proposal

Define the two outputs consistently across backends:

- emit_asm == human-readable target assembly: PTX on CUDA, .s on RISC-V.
- emit_bin == loadable device machine code: SASS/cubin on CUDA, linked .so on RISC-V.

On CUDA that means emit_bin should run the PTX-to-cubin step (nvptxcompiler, already
wrapped by PtxCompiler) as part of compilation and cache the cubin alongside the PTX,
rather than deferring it to load time.

Open questions, to confirm when implementing

- What --emit=obj actually produces for the nvptx64-nvidia-cuda triple has NOT been
  verified byte-for-byte: the teenyc cache (TEENYC_CACHE_DIR, default /tmp/teenyc_cache)
  was empty when this issue was written. Confirm whether that .o holds PTX text or a real
  object before settling the mapping.
- Compiling SASS ahead of time pins the artifact to one SM version, whereas PTX is portable
  and JITs at load. Decide whether emit_bin on CUDA should be capability-specific, and how
  that interacts with the cache key (which already folds in target_cpu and ptx_version).
- teeny-cuda AOT packaging (drivers/teeny-cuda/src/compiler/aot.rs) may assume the artifact
  is PTX. Check it before changing what compile_kernel returns.

Related

- teenygrad-261 (builder API for compiler and options) would supply the entry point through
  which these are selected.
- teenygrad-3fc records RISC-V snapshots having captured raw ELF bytes, which is the same
  class of confusion between asm and bin.

title: teeny-riscv: RISC-V driver crate mirroring teeny-cuda
description:
Add a new drivers/teeny-riscv crate so teenygrad can target RISC-V vector kernels through the mlir/Triton compiler backend's RISC-V path, mirroring the structure of drivers/teeny-cuda (see its src/ layout: compiler/{target,options,driver,graph,aot}.rs, device/{context,mem,buffer,program}.rs, runtime/, model/, testing/, buffer.rs, context.rs, mem.rs, program.rs).

Context / what this builds on:
- The ../rust compiler fork (teeny) now has a real (if minimal) RISC-V codegen path: a dedicated `riscv64-generic` target spec with default_codegen_backend=mlir, a TargetBackend::Riscv dispatch, and a RiscvBackend that synthesizes a placeholder no-arg `void @kernel()` function, compiles it through LLVM's real RISC-V backend, and links it into a shared library via ld.lld.
- compiler/teeny-compiler/src/compiler/backend/llvm/compiler.rs's LlvmCompiler was generalized (branch feature/riscv-target-support, not yet merged to main) to accept .with_target_triple(...) instead of hardcoding "nvptx64-nvidia-cuda", so a RISC-V caller can already do .with_target_triple("riscv64-generic").with_target_cpu("spacemit-k3" | "generic-rvv1.0" | ...).

What teeny-cuda does that teeny-riscv needs an equivalent of:
- compiler/target.rs: a Capability-style enum enumerating supported chips (e.g. SpacemitK1, SpacemitK3, GenericRvv1_0) with Display/FromStr, and a Target type implementing teeny_core::compiler::Target::target_cpu().
- compiler/driver.rs + compiler/graph.rs + compiler/aot.rs: wiring the FXGraph compiler pipeline to LlvmCompiler for this target, AOT packaging support.
- compiler/options.rs: RISC-V-specific compile options analogous to CudaCompileOptions-level knobs (whatever ends up mattering once real codegen exists -- vector width/extension selection likely, once the chip-name-to-LLVM-cpu/feature mapping referenced below exists).

What's structurally different from teeny-cuda (open design questions to resolve during implementation, not now):
- teeny-cuda's device/{context,mem,buffer}.rs wrap the CUDA driver API (device selection, device memory allocation, kernel launch via a real GPU driver). RISC-V kernels run on the host CPU via a dlopen'd shared library, not a discrete accelerator device -- there is no CUDA-driver-API equivalent to wrap. The execution model is presumably: dlopen the compiled .so, resolve the kernel symbol, call it directly against host memory, but this needs real design work once the kernel ABI (arguments, not just a no-arg placeholder) exists on the compiler side.
- No device/buffer.rs or device/mem.rs equivalent may be needed at all if kernels operate directly on host-owned buffers; teeny-cpu (if one exists) may be a closer structural model than teeny-cuda for the device/buffer/mem layer specifically -- worth comparing both before committing to a layout.

Blocking/known gaps on the compiler side (from teeny's teenyc-wue, teenyc-j3a):
- No mapping yet from Triton-side chip identifiers (spacemit-k3, generic-rvv1.0) to real LLVM RISC-V cpu/feature strings -- the backend currently ignores the requested cpu and always codegens for a generic RV64 target.
- No real MIR/Triton-to-LLVM-IR lowering -- every kernel compiles to the same placeholder no-op function regardless of source, so there is no real kernel argument/ABI to call into yet.
- The compiled shared library's bytes (getBIN()) aren't even retrieved by the compiler's own Rust side yet (rustc_codegen_llvm's compile_module only reads get_asm()) -- needed before teeny-riscv can get a .so path/bytes back from LlvmCompiler::compile() at all.

Given those compiler-side gaps, real end-to-end RISC-V kernel execution isn't possible yet -- this epic should start with the crate scaffold + Target/Capability types + wiring LlvmCompiler with the riscv64-generic target, exercised against the current placeholder no-op kernel (dlopen + call, verifying the linked .so loads and runs), and defer real kernel compilation/argument-passing until the compiler-side gaps above are closed.
notes:
First milestone done (2026-09-04, commit ce7dc92c0 on feature/riscv-target-support): drivers/teeny-riscv crate scaffold with compiler::target::{Capability, Target} (GenericRvv1_0, SpacemitK1, SpacemitK3), compiler::TARGET_TRIPLE, and runtime::KernelLibrary (libloading-based dlopen/dlsym wrapper). tests/test_compile_riscv.rs compiles a real kernel (ReluForward, reused as-is since RiscvBackend ignores incoming module content today) via LlvmCompiler targeting riscv64-generic and checks the ELF header.

Verified genuinely end-to-end beyond the automated test: installed a fresh teenyc (../teeny/x.py install, picking up this session's riscv64-generic target + RiscvBackend + getBIN fixes), then cross-compiled a dlopen/dlsym C harness for riscv64-linux-gnu and ran it under qemu-riscv64 against the .so teeny-riscv's own test produces -- loads, resolves riscv_kernel, calls it, returns successfully.

Deliberately did NOT build: device/context/mem/buffer layer (no CUDA-driver-API equivalent needed/designed yet -- RISC-V kernels run via dlopen'd .so on host CPU), compiler/driver.rs graph-level wiring, real kernel argument passing. Blocked on teenyc-wue's remaining gaps (#1 chip-name-to-LLVM-cpu mapping, #3 real MIR lowering) for anything beyond the placeholder no-op kernel.
close_reason: Done or will not be done (closed by owner, 2026-11-26)

title: test(riscv): gate integration tests behind riscv+qemu features, run via QEMU emulator driver
description:
Add integration test coverage for teeny-riscv that actually executes a compiled RISC-V kernel, gated behind two new Cargo features on drivers/teeny-riscv: `riscv` (already-implied by the crate, but kept explicit so the test is opt-in) and `qemu`. Tests under this cfg (`#[cfg(all(feature = "riscv", feature = "qemu"))]`) run only when both are enabled, since qemu-riscv64 + a riscv64-linux-gnu cross toolchain aren't available in every dev/CI environment.

Context: teenygrad-1zd's notes record that this was already verified manually — a cross-compiled dlopen/dlsym C harness for riscv64-linux-gnu, run under `qemu-riscv64` against the `.so` teeny-riscv's own `tests/test_compile_riscv.rs` produces (via `LlvmCompiler` targeting `riscv64-generic`) — loads, resolves `riscv_kernel`, calls it, and returns successfully. This issue is to automate that manual step as a real (non-manual) integration test.

Scope:
- A `QemuDriver` (or similar) in teeny-riscv's `testing`/`runtime` layer that: locates `qemu-riscv64` and a riscv64-linux-gnu cross toolchain (erroring clearly, not skipping silently, when the `qemu` feature is on but the tools are missing), cross-compiles a small dlopen/dlsym host harness (or reuses/generalizes teenygrad-1zd's manual C harness), and runs it under `qemu-riscv64` against a `.so` produced by `LlvmCompiler` targeting `riscv64-generic` (same path `tests/test_compile_riscv.rs` already exercises for the ELF-header-only check).
- Wire the new integration test(s) into `drivers/teeny-riscv/tests/` alongside `test_compile_riscv.rs`, feature-gated so `cargo test -p teeny-riscv` alone (no features) still passes without qemu/the cross toolchain installed.
- Document the required host setup (qemu-user riscv64 package, riscv64-linux-gnu-gcc or equivalent) in the crate's README or a doc comment, and note the feature flags in `./scripts/test.sh` / CI docs if CI is expected to opt in.

Out of scope: real kernel argument passing / non-placeholder kernel bodies (blocked on teenyc-wue's remaining compiler-side gaps, per teenygrad-1zd) — this issue only needs to prove the dlopen-under-qemu execution path for the existing placeholder no-op kernel, same as the manual verification did.
close_reason: Done: RISC-V tests run under QEMU via the riscv/qemu features (closed by owner, 2026-11-26)

title: RISC-V kernel .so calls libm without listing it as a dependency
description:
Kernels lowered through TritonCPU call libm (CpuBackend's math_to_libm; e.g. tanh_forward's .so imports expf), but teeny's RiscvBackend::makeBIN links them with ld.lld -shared and no libm, so the .so has no DT_NEEDED entries (llvm-readelf -d shows none). dlopen(RTLD_NOW) then fails with an undefined symbol: 23 teeny-kernels hardware tests failed this way under QEMU before the launcher was changed.

teeny-riscv's QEMU trampoline now loads libm.so.6 with RTLD_GLOBAL before dlopen()ing the kernel, but a native RISC-V loader (or any other consumer of the .so) would still hit it.

Fix belongs in teeny: link libm into the kernel library (e.g. add DT_NEEDED libm.so.6 in RiscvBackend::makeBIN), then drop the preload from the trampoline.

title: bug: Softmax/LogSoftmax lowering - wrong grid above rank 2, unmasked row load/store, axis dropped, importer clamps negative axis (GH #152)
description:
GitHub #152 (reporter: realitymatrix). Partial fix in open PR #153.

## Verified on current main: four independent faults
1. **Grid**: `SoftmaxRuntimeOp::grid` (`kernels/teeny-kernels/src/nn/activation/softmax.rs:162`) returns `output_shape[0]`. The row count is the product of every axis except the last, so above rank 2 most rows are never written and stay zero. LogSoftmax has the same fault with `first()` (`nn/activation/extra.rs:819`).
2. **Unmasked load/store**: BLOCK_SIZE = n_cols.next_power_of_two(), and `softmax_forward` loads and stores without a mask. For a row width that is not a power of two, the extra lanes read the next row (corrupting this row's max and sum), overwrite the next row's first elements, and run past the end of the buffer on the last row. log_softmax_forward has the same fault. This even breaks a 2-D last-axis softmax such as [4,6].
3. **Axis dropped**: the `Op::Softmax { .. }` and `Op::LogSoftmax { .. }` arms (`graph/mod.rs:1756`, `:2308`) ignore dim/axis and always normalise over the last axis.
4. **Importer**: `onnx.rs:282` maps `axis.max(0) as usize`, so any negative axis becomes 0. The default is 1 regardless of opset, but opset 13 and later use -1. `Op::Softmax.dim` is a `usize`, whereas `LogSoftmax.axis` is an `i64`. Related: the LogSoftmax importer defaults to -1 even for opset <13, where ONNX's default is 1.

Real-world impact: FoundationStereo's disparity softmax over [1,9,96,128] axis 1 leaves 110464 of 110592 elements zero.

## Plan
1. Review and merge PR #153. It fixes items 1, 2 and 4 (adds `rows_and_cols`, a masked load with a -1e30 sentinel, `dim: i64`, and an opset-aware default), and refuses a non-innermost axis instead of computing over the wrong one. It re-blesses softmax/log_softmax source snapshots, so check them in all four configs.
2. Full fix for item 3: transpose dim innermost, apply softmax, transpose back. This is blocked on Op::Transpose lowering (separate bead) and reuses `reduce_transpose_perm` from #151 / PR #154.

## Acceptance
These six models match numpy and have no exact zeros: [6,4] -1, [4,8] -1, [4,6] -1, [1,3,2,4] -1, [6,4] axis 0, [1,3,2,4] axis 1. Do the same for LogSoftmax.

title: teenyc invocation fails: -Zcodegen-backend requires nightly, but toolchain is stable
description: LlvmCompiler::compile() calls teenyc with -Zcodegen-backend=mlir but teenyc is now distributed on the 'stable' channel (see spinorml-cdn/teeny naming work), so it refuses with 'the option Z is only accepted on the nightly compiler'. Fix: set RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP=1 on the Command instead of switching the whole distribution to nightly.

Verified: -Zcodegen-backend=mlir now accepted against the stable-teenyc-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu CDN toolchain; test_batch_norm_training_graph compiles past the flag (fails later on an unrelated sm_120/PTX-version mismatch on this RTX 5070 dev box); a clean AOT compile via teeny-cli targeting sm_87 (Jetson) succeeds end-to-end with no errors.

title: refactor: builder API for compiler and CompilerOptions, replacing positional flags in compile_kernel
description:
Context

compile_kernel(kernel, target, force, debug) in both driver crates takes two positional
bools whose meaning is invisible at the call site. CLAUDE.md explicitly calls this out:
use enums or structs instead of bool parameters when the meaning is unclear at call sites.

teeny_core::compiler::CompilerOptions (force, emit_asm, emit_bin) landed in ed5065739, but
it is only reachable by constructing an LlvmCompiler directly. Both driver wrappers
hardcode CompilerOptions::default().with_force(force), so emit_asm and emit_bin cannot be
selected through the normal entry point.

LlvmCompiler already has a partial builder: with_target_triple, with_target_cpu,
with_ptx_version, with_log_level. The compiler half is therefore half-built; the options
half and the driver-level entry point are not.

Proposal

Replace the positional-flag compile_kernel with a builder that composes the compiler and
its options in one place, so a call site reads as named intent rather than two bare bools.

Constraints

- Roughly 100 files under kernels/teeny-kernels/tests call
  compile_kernel(&kernel, &target, true, false). Migration needs either a compatibility
  shim or a mechanical sweep; pick one deliberately.
- Both driver wrappers (teeny-cuda, teeny-riscv) intentionally share a signature so
  teeny-runtime can re-export whichever backend is active. Any new API must preserve that.
- debug is not part of CompilerOptions today; it toggles a thread-local tracing subscriber
  via with_pipeline_logging. Decide whether it belongs in the builder.

Related

teenygrad-3fc wants RISC-V snapshots re-recorded via --emit=asm. That needs asm-only
compiles reachable from the driver layer, which this issue would provide.

title: feat(macros): bring conv2d's weight into its tile spec (P5)
description:
## Problem
conv2d's weight `w` (`[C_OUT, C_IN/G, KH, KW]`) has `#[tile_loop_scalar(..)]` but no `#[tile(..)]`. Its second extent is `C_IN / G`, and `#[tile(extent = <ident>)]` can only name an identifier. So `w` is missing from `conv2d_forward`'s tile spec. Its reads are left out of the scheduler's traffic and footprint (ANALYSIS.md §12.2 P5).

The footprint effect is small: one scalar per iteration. The traffic is under-counted by `C_IN/G · KH · KW` elements per unit. This came out of teenygrad-3f4z (requirement 5), which landed P4 and P6 for conv2d and left this part.

## Requirements
- Let `#[tile(extent = ..)]` name an expression or a derived param, so `w` can declare `[C_OUT, C_IN/G, KH, KW]`. Alternatively, derive `w`'s spec from its `#[tile_loop_scalar(index = [..])]`. Either way, never write it by hand.
- `w`'s C_OUT axis binds at block 1, like the output's (P4). Its `(c_in_local, kh, kw)` dims are walks with chunk 1 (P6), so a unit holds one weight element per iteration and reads one `c_out` slice in total.
- The same applies to conv1d, conv3d and the fused conv kernels.
- Tests: conv2d's spec has two inputs, `w`'s region per unit is `[Tiled len 1, Chunk 1, Chunk 1, Chunk 1]`, and a lone conv's traffic includes the slice.

## Related
teenygrad-3f4z, teenygrad-1l7i
close_reason: Implemented in 68d1a0073

title: RISC-V compile_kernel returns a shared object named .o (#120)
description: teeny_riscv::compiler::compile_kernel returns <cache>/<kernel>_<hash>.o, but on RISC-V that file is a linked ELF shared object (teenyc's RiscvBackend links with ld.lld -shared and hands the bytes back as --emit=obj). The .so the reporter saw next to it is not ours: it is reproduced exactly by riscv64-linux-gnu-gcc -shared on the .o (6968 bytes, only __cxa_finalize/_ITM_* dynsyms, 0 vector instrs), i.e. a second link done outside teenygrad. Fix: name the cached RISC-V binary .so so the returned path's extension matches the file, and document it on compile_kernel. CUDA unchanged.
