title: Kernel compile cache races when two threads compile the same hash concurrently
description:
teeny-compiler's kernel cache (default_cache_dir(), see compiler/teeny-compiler/src/compiler/mod.rs) is a shared scratch/object-cache directory keyed by kernel content hash. Under cargo test's default parallelism (or any concurrent use), two threads/processes compiling the SAME kernel hash at the same time race on that shared directory -- one invocation's write/rename can collide with another's, producing spurious 'could not copy ... No such file or directory' failures. scripts/test.sh's clean-cache-dir workaround only makes failures reproducible from a known state, it does not fix the underlying race, and running everything single-threaded (the current safe workaround) fully serializes ALL compilation, not just colliding ones.

Fix: per-hash advisory file locking (flock on <cache_dir>/<hash>.lock) scoped to the specific hash being compiled, so unrelated hashes still compile fully in parallel and only two racers on the identical hash serialize. Combine with atomic cache writes (compile to a unique temp path in the same directory, e.g. <hash>.o.tmp.<pid>, then rename() into <hash>.o -- POSIX rename is atomic on the same filesystem) so a reader never observes a partial/missing file even at the edges of the lock window.

Design:
1. Acquire flock() on <cache_dir>/<hash>.lock before compiling a given hash. Different hashes use different lock files and proceed fully in parallel; only concurrent compiles of the IDENTICAL hash serialize on that one lock.
2. After acquiring the lock (i.e. after any wait for a prior holder to release it), re-check whether the cache entry now exists BEFORE compiling. If the thread that held the lock finished compiling that hash while we were waiting, reuse its output rather than recompiling -- this double-checked-locking / compile-once check is the main point of taking the lock at all, not just avoiding the file-corruption symptom but avoiding wasted duplicate compilation work.
3. Make the actual cache write atomic regardless: compile/write outputs to a unique per-process temp path in the same directory (e.g. <hash>.o.tmp.<pid>), then rename() into the final <hash>.o path. This guarantees no reader ever sees a partial file even if locking has any edge-case gap.
4. Release the lock only after the atomic rename completes (or after confirming a cache hit in step 2).
5. flock is process-scoped and released automatically on process exit, so a crashed holder doesn't leave a stale lock -- no separate stale-lock cleanup needed.

Acceptance criteria:
- Two concurrent processes compiling the SAME kernel hash: only one actually invokes teenyc; the other blocks on the lock, then reuses the first one's cache output without recompiling.
- Two concurrent processes compiling DIFFERENT kernel hashes: both compile fully in parallel, no serialization.
- cargo test (default parallelism, no --test-threads=1, no scripts/test.sh cache-clear workaround) passes reliably without the 'could not copy ... No such file or directory' race.
- Killing a process mid-compile (holding the lock) does not deadlock subsequent compiles of that hash.
close_reason: Implemented per-hash flock (fd-lock crate) + double-checked cache-hit skip + atomic rename (.o and .mlir sidecar) in LlvmCompiler::compile. Verified: 8-way same-hash race dedups to ~1x compile time; different hashes stay fully parallel; full workspace suite passes with 0 failures under default cargo test parallelism (release/0.1.3, commit 43f0c0f9d).

title: feat: the auto-prelude reads a reduced axis in full (no output counterpart)
notes:
## The gap, measured

Converting reduce_sum_forward to In<Tile<..>> fails at the prelude's own
validation:

  error: `x` declares an axis the output does not, so the prelude cannot place
  it. An input axis must either match an output axis by name, or be left off
  entirely (which broadcasts it).

A reduced axis has no output counterpart BY CONSTRUCTION -- that is what
reduction means -- and it must be read IN FULL, not broadcast. So the prelude's
two options are both wrong for it, and `#[tile(.., reduce)]` already says which
axis it is.

## Who needs it (12)

  10  reduce_sum, reduce_mean, reduce_max, reduce_min, reduce_prod, reduce_l1,
      reduce_l2, reduce_log_sum, reduce_log_sum_exp, reduce_sum_square
   2  global_avg_pool, global_max_pool

All identical in shape: x is [n_outer, n_inner], y is [n_outer], one program per
row, and the read is `arange(0, BLOCK_INNER) + row * n_inner` masked to
n_inner.

## What it has to generate

For an axis carrying `reduce`:

  - a range of its block width, masked to its extent -- the kernels write
    `arange(0, BLOCK_INNER)` with `.lt(n_inner)`;
  - that range as the innermost term of the row-major offset, with the outer
    axes contributing `row * n_inner`;
  - and NOT a grid axis: the grid is over the output's axes only, which is
    already true since grid_spec is built from the output.

## One declaration consequence worth deciding

teenygrad-1tl.9 deliberately did NOT bind BLOCK_INNER to the reduced axis,
reasoning that it is a load width rather than a tiling -- and its tests assert
`untiled_dims == ["n_inner"]`. Route 1 needs a block to know the load width, so
converting flips that: `#[tile(block = BLOCK_INNER, extent = n_inner, reduce)]`.

That is the same tension softmax already sits on: softmax is route 1 and blocks
its reduced axis, while the route-2 norms do not. The two conventions follow the
two routes, so this is consistent rather than a contradiction -- but 1tl.9's
assertions will need updating, and the reasoning recorded there should be
amended rather than silently contradicted.
close_reason: Complete via PR #82. The prelude generates a rank-reducing axis's read: a range of its block width, masked to its extent, as the innermost term of the row-major offset. All ten reduce_* plus both global pools converted to In<Tile<..>>. Scoped to rank-reducing axes (reduced AND absent from the output) so softmax/log_softmax, which are rank-preserving, keep the kernel's own range and are untouched. fill = zeros|neg_inf|pos_inf|one is part of the feature: masked lanes take part in the reduction, so the fill must be the reduction's identity. Added a partial-tile fixture test (n_inner 40 vs BLOCK_INNER 64) because nothing exercised a masked lane -- INNER == BLOCK_INNER everywhere -- and it caught a tolerance bug on reduce_prod immediately. Also fixed a latent bug in reduce_log_sum_exp, whose second load filled 0.0 and so let a masked lane contribute exp(0-m). teenygrad-1tl.9's reasoning amended in place rather than contradicted.

title: feat(lowering): attach conv2d's derived grid spec so Anduin can schedule it
description:
## Problem
`TritonLowering` lowers `Op::Conv2d` with `exec.tile_spec = Some(Conv2dForward::<f32>::tile_spec())` (kernels/teeny-kernels/src/graph/mod.rs, the Conv2d arm, ~line 1532) but never sets `exec.grid_spec`. `OpMeta::new` (anduin/tile_graph/mod.rs:77) returns `None` for an op without both specs, so conv2d enters the Anduin scheduler with no meta and is always scheduled `Opaque`. It can never anchor or join a fused group.

`Conv2dForward::<f32>::grid_spec()` already exists. It is derived by `#[tiled_kernel]` (commit 3ef6d8b773), and `conv2d_grid_spec_tests` (graph/mod.rs ~3770-3810) checks that it follows the kernel's real pid decode `(b, c_out, oh, ow_tile)`. It is just never attached.

## Requirements
1. Set `exec.grid_spec = Some(Conv2dForward::<f32>::grid_spec())` next to the tile spec in the Conv2d arm. Do the same for any other Conv2d path that sets a conv2d tile spec (check the bias / `Conv2dBiasForward` arm too). Only attach it where the kernel's spec and grid are true of the node: ungrouped vs grouped `G`, and static vs dynamic batch. Otherwise leave both `None` and add a comment saying why.
2. The GridSpec must agree with the launch grid `RuntimeOp::grid(concrete_shape)` actually uses. Add a test that lowers a conv (B=2, C_in=3, C_out=8, 32x32, 3x3, s1, p1) and checks that the product of the GridSpec's axis unit counts equals the product of `runtime_op().grid(&[2, 8, 32, 32])`, axis by axis in pid-decode order.
3. Update `test_w7_conv_batchnorm_silu_fuses_batchnorm_and_silu_through_the_real_lowering` (anduin/schedule/mod.rs). It currently asserts `g.nodes[conv.0].meta.is_none()` ("conv2d has no grid spec"). After this change conv has meta. The schedule under `TeenygradCaps` is still expected to be `[Opaque(conv), Tiled{bn, silu}]`, because conv -> bn cannot fuse (bn is not a rider; see the fusion issue). Update the assertion and its comment.
4. Check that adding `grid_spec` changes no generated kernel source. Kernel snapshots must still converge in all four configs (see the snapshot-verification memory: default features is the easy miss).

## Acceptance
- conv2d has an `OpMeta` in `TileGraph::from_dag`.
- New grid-agreement test passes.
- W7 updated and passing.
- `./scripts/test.sh --workspace --no-fail-fast` shows no new failures (known: the 5 Anduin `todo!` tests and teeny-triton `test_tile_layout_boundary_type_param_conv2d`).

## Context
Found by `test_conv2d_batchnorm_silu_schedules_as_one_tiled_kernel` (umbrella issue). Experiment: with this grid spec plus a fuse-anything capability set, conv/bn/silu do fuse, but the tiling is wrong for the reasons in the P3 and P4 issues.
close_reason: Implemented in 1064a280a

title: feat: convert the optimizer step kernels to the Tile ABI (~18 kernels)
description:
## Goal

Convert the optimizer step kernels to `In<Tile<..>>`/`Out<Tile<..>>`/`InOut<Tile<..>>`
with declared tile axes, the same route-1 treatment `teenygrad-1tl.2`/`.3` gave
the flat elementwise families.

## Why they are not in teenygrad-1tl

That epic is scoped to *forward* kernels. An optimizer step is neither forward
nor backward, so no rung claims these -- they were simply never counted. Found by
the route audit recorded on `teenygrad-1tl`.

## Population (~18 kernels)

`optim/sgd.rs` (sgd_step, sgd_momentum_step, sgd_nesterov_step),
`optim/adam.rs` (adam_step, adamw_step), `optim/adamax.rs`, `optim/adagrad.rs`
(adagrad_step, adadelta_step), `optim/asgd.rs`, `optim/nadam.rs`,
`optim/radam.rs` (radam_adaptive_step, radam_sgd_step), `optim/rmsprop.rs`
(rmsprop_step, rmsprop_momentum_step), `optim/rprop.rs`, and `optim/muon.rs`
(muon_update, muon_ns_xtx, muon_ns_step).

## Why they are straightforward

Verified on `sgd_step`: `params_ptr` (`InOut`) and `grad_ptr` are read at the
*same* `offsets = T::arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE) + block_start`, with one store back to
params. That is exactly `teenygrad-1tl.3`'s shape -- several operands sharing one
extent -- so the existing conversion recipe applies unchanged and each spec is
the identity.

None of the four route blockers applies to the flat ones: no in-kernel loop, no
data-dependent offset, no rank change, and one shared offsets expression.

## Watch for

- `InOut<T::Pointer<..>>` params. `Tile` has been used behind `In`/`Out` so far;
  check whether `InOut<Tile<..>>` is supported by the prelude, since an optimizer
  reads and writes the same buffer. This is the one genuinely new thing here.
- `muon_frob_norm_sq` is excluded: it reduces to a scalar, so it is blocked by
  (c), a rank-changing output.
- `teenygrad-0mr` is an open correctness bug against `muon_ns_xtx` on sm_120,
  reproducing bit-identically as of 2026-09-29. Convert it, but do not expect the
  numerics to start passing, and do not treat its failure as caused by the
  conversion.

## Done when

Every flat optimizer step takes `Tile` params with declared axes, the
`test_tile_declarations` guard covers them, and numerics are unchanged (except
`muon_ns_xtx`, which fails for `teenygrad-0mr`'s reasons either way).
close_reason: Won't do: the TileGraph / Tile ABI / Anduin approach is abandoned (closed by owner, 2026-11-26)

title: feat: a channel for the K block into resolve_inputs, so a GEMM's operand tiles are not full-K
notes:
## The gap

A matmul's K axis is shared by both operands and present on neither output, so
it is left unresolved by design (declared that way in teenygrad-1tl.10). Both
input tiles therefore come back at FULL K.

For a 1024-cubed f32 GEMM at a 64x32 output tile that is 256KiB + 128KiB --
more than an A100 SM's shared memory. So every GEMM looks unfusable and the
cost model will reject fusions that are in fact fine.

## What it is NOT

Not a missing const. resolve_inputs only visits an axis that HAS a
TileAxisBinding, and K deliberately has none -- binding it would advertise a
per-tile extent nothing honours. So supplying K and BLOCK_K through the
ConstLookup changes nothing. That is asserted directly in
test_matmul_family_takes_different_operand_tiles_and_leaves_k_unresolved.

ConstLookup is the wrong way in regardless: it is documented as supplying full
extents, and divide_by is applied to whatever it returns.

## What is needed

The K block is a tiling-SEARCH decision, not a property of the kernel: the
searcher picks BLOCK_K and resolution needs to be told. So this is a new input
to resolve_inputs rather than a new field on the spec -- the spec side already
says everything needed. TensorTileSpec::reduction_axis identifies which axis it
is per operand, and TileLoopSpec::trip_count_factors already names K and
BLOCK_K.

## Done when

A GEMM's operand tiles come back at the searcher's chosen BLOCK_K rather than
full K, with the 1024-cubed case above as the test, and divide_by is not
involved.

Filed from teenygrad-1tl.10, whose acceptance asks for exactly this issue.
Referenced from gemm.rs and from the test named above.

title: teeny-quant: safetensors model quantization crate for deployment
description: New utilities/teeny-quant crate (lib + bin, same shape as teeny-cli) that quantizes safetensors model checkpoints for deployment. Initial validation target is Ultralytics YOLO models (safetensors in, safetensors out). Two tracks: (1) weight-only PTQ (INT8/INT4/FP8) that only needs the safetensors weight tensors and is unblocked today; (2) static activation quantization that needs a calibration forward pass, run by parsing the model's ONNX export through teeny-onnx into a teeny_core::graph::Graph and executing it via teeny-compiler's ndarray backend (avoids adding an external onnxruntime dependency). title: perf: LLM inference performance (multi-user throughput, CUDA + SpacemiT K3, 1-8B dense models)
description:
Umbrella for the inference performance work identified by comparing teenygrad's LLM path with llama.cpp/ggml and vLLM.

Targets: CUDA and RISC-V (SpacemiT K3) ranked separately; multi-user throughput serving; 1-8B dense decoder models.
Constraints: kernels stay in the Triton DSL (#[kernel] + teenyc); teenyc fork changes are in scope; fusion should be compiler-driven (egg rewrite rules); the no_std path must be preserved.

Baseline (FunctionGemma 270M, f32): RTX 5070 ~850-940 tok/s pp, ~80 tok/s tg; K3 8x X100 ~67 tok/s pp, ~11 tok/s tg.
Main overheads today: cuCtxSynchronize after each of ~390 launches/token, full host KV cache uploaded every step, activation BufferPool recreated and zero-filled every run, f32 weights duplicated per CompiledStep, per-row dot-product linear kernel with no tensor cores, single-request FIFO serving with host greedy sampling.

Suggested order: Tier 0 + CUDA overhead removal -> bf16 + generic models -> serving stack -> quantization -> fusion/autotuning.

See INFERENCE_PERF_ROADMAP.md (repo root) for context and the llama.cpp/vLLM comparison.
