title: feat: LLM fusion rewrite rules in the graph optimiser (norm+mul, residual+norm, QKV/gate-up merge, GEMM epilogues, rope+kv store)
description:
compiler/teeny-compiler/src/fxgraph/rules is empty, and the LLM path's only fusions are hand-written (gelu_mul, Gemma rmsnorm). Fusion for the LLM path is to be driven by egg rewrite rules over the graph, replacing the discontinued Anduin approach.
Rules to add (compiler-driven, not hand-fused):
- RMSNorm -> mul(weight); residual add + RMSNorm.
- Horizontal merge of linears sharing an input: Q/K/V -> one GEMM, gate/up -> one GEMM.
- GEMM epilogues: SwiGLU/GeGLU, residual add, bias.
- RoPE + KV cache store.
- Load-time constant folding of norm weights (e.g. Gemma 1+w).
Also needed: a graph-level attention op so fused attention kernels (FlashAttention, teenygrad-35vc.25) are reachable from the optimiser, and a way to enable the optimiser in the LLM lowering path (runner.rs calls TritonLowering::new() with none).
Acceptance: fewer launches per decode step and lower step time on both backends, measured with teenygrad-35vc.1.

See INFERENCE_PERF_ROADMAP.md (repo root) for context and the llama.cpp/vLLM comparison.

title: perf: enable the Anduin optimiser in the LLM lowering path
description:
runner.rs ~114 calls TritonLowering::new() with no optimiser, so none of the Anduin fusion applies to LLM graphs.
Scope: lower LLM steps with TritonLowering::with_optimizer, make the custom LLM ops (linear, attention, rmsnorm, rope, gelu_mul) Tile-ABI-aware so they participate, and measure launches/step and step time before/after.
Related: teenygrad-3rk6 (Tile ABI conversion), teenygrad-3q7w (register budget).

See INFERENCE_PERF_ROADMAP.md (repo root) for context and the llama.cpp/vLLM comparison.
close_reason: Anduin fusion work discontinued; LLM fusion is tracked by teenygrad-35vc.13 (egg rewrite rules)

title: feat: kernel autotuning per (shape bucket, device), cached with the kernel cache
description:
GEMM tiles come from the fixed pick_gemm_tile_sizes heuristic (kernels/teeny-kernels/src/graph/mod.rs ~2232-2264); LLM block sizes are hand-picked constants; num_warps/num_stages cannot be set.
Scope: expose num_warps/num_stages in the DSL; search configs per (op, shape bucket, device) at first use or AOT, persist results keyed alongside the SHA256 kernel cache; teeny-bench mode to regenerate.
Acceptance: tuned configs reused across runs; measurable gain on linear/attention shapes for 1-8B models.

See INFERENCE_PERF_ROADMAP.md (repo root) for context and the llama.cpp/vLLM comparison.

title: feat: bf16/f16 kernels - #[kernel] cannot monomorphise f16/bf16, and runtime buffers are f32-only
description:
The LLM runs entirely in f32 because teenygrad cannot yet build or run bf16/f16 kernels.

Already fixed upstream: teenyc's T::cast(..., bitcast=true) used to emit arith.sitofp. Since teeny b59c418f8b4 (2026-11-24, teenyc 1.100.0, the installed toolchain) it emits tt.bitcast, and <<, >> and ^ work on tensors, so bf16 weights can be widened to f32 in a kernel (shift into the high half, bitcast).

Remaining, all in teenygrad:
- #[kernel] maps Float to f32/f64 only and treats f16/bf16 as marker-only (macros/teeny-macros/src/macros/kernel.rs, all_dtypes_for_bound ~197).
- teeny-triton defers BF16: it needs a KernelArg impl strategy for non-native types (kernels/teeny-triton/src/triton/llvm/triton/num.rs:17).
- f16/bf16 storage with f32 accumulation in linear, attention and the norms.
- Runtime buffers typed by dtype rather than f32 words (testing/teeny-test/src/model.rs ~170-181).

Why: decode is memory-bandwidth-bound on both targets, so halving weight bytes is the largest kernel-level win.
Acceptance: bf16 FunctionGemma and a 1B model match the f32 reference within tolerance; apps/teeny-llm/docs/functiongemma.md bug 3 row updated to say BF16 weights are back.

See INFERENCE_PERF_ROADMAP.md (repo root) for context and the llama.cpp/vLLM comparison.

title: feat: quantized-weight inference (W8A16, grouped W4A16, GGUF Q8_0/Q4_K) with dequantization inside the matmul
description:
teeny-quant (utilities/teeny-quant) produces INT8/INT4/FP8 compressed-tensors checkpoints, but nothing in the inference path consumes them and no dequant kernels exist.
Scope: loader support for compressed-tensors and GGUF Q8_0/Q4_K; quantized linear kernels that dequantize in registers for GEMV (decode) and GEMM (prefill), backend-specific fast paths tracked separately (CUDA, K3 IME).
Acceptance: an 8B model at ~4.5 bpw runs with perplexity close to llama.cpp's for the same format.
Related: teenygrad-303 (teeny-quant epic).

See INFERENCE_PERF_ROADMAP.md (repo root) for context and the llama.cpp/vLLM comparison.

title: feat: quantized KV cache (q8 / fp8) with dequantization inside attention
description:
KV is f32 only. Store K/V as q8_0-style blocks or fp8 with per-block scales; quantize on write, dequantize in the attention kernel (llama.cpp -ctk/-ctv q8_0).
Why: ~2x (vs f16) concurrent sequences per GB, which directly raises serving throughput.

See INFERENCE_PERF_ROADMAP.md (repo root) for context and the llama.cpp/vLLM comparison.

title: perf(cuda): remove cuCtxSynchronize after every kernel launch; use a dedicated stream
description:
CudaDevice::launch (drivers/teeny-cuda/src/device/mod.rs ~387-400) launches on the null stream and calls cuCtxSynchronize() after every kernel: ~390 full syncs per decode token.
Scope: launch on a per-model stream, synchronise only when outputs are read or errors must be surfaced (keep a debug env flag for sync-after-launch).
Acceptance: one sync per step in steady state.

See INFERENCE_PERF_ROADMAP.md (repo root) for context and the llama.cpp/vLLM comparison.

title: perf: dedicated inference runtime with a static activation memory plan, replacing teeny_test::RuntimeModel in the LLM path
description:
The LLM runs through testing/teeny-test/src/model.rs RuntimeModel, which by its own header is for cross-backend correctness, not speed.
Problems: a new BufferPool is created on every run() (model.rs ~768) so activations are cuMemAlloc'd every step; every acquire zero-fills via a host upload (model.rs ~280-287); each CompiledStep uploads its own copy of all weights, and tied lm_head reloads embed_tokens (runner.rs ~75-84), so the embedding sits on device ~4x.
Scope:
- Compute a static activation memory plan at compile time (liveness-based offsets into one arena, like ggml-alloc); no per-step alloc, no zero-fill unless an op needs it.
- Share weight storage across compiled graphs and tied parameters.
- Persistent input/output buffers written in place; outputs read only on demand.
- Keep the planning logic no_std friendly (arena + offsets, no std collections in core).
Acceptance: zero device allocations per step in steady state; device weight footprint = 1x model size.

See INFERENCE_PERF_ROADMAP.md (repo root) for context and the llama.cpp/vLLM comparison.

title: perf(cuda): stop allocating/freeing TMA scratch around each launch
description:
Kernels needing scratch get cuMemAlloc + cuMemsetD8 + cuMemFree around every launch (drivers/teeny-cuda/src/device/mod.rs ~353-410). Allocate scratch from the inference runtime's arena (or a persistent per-kernel buffer) instead.

See INFERENCE_PERF_ROADMAP.md (repo root) for context and the llama.cpp/vLLM comparison.

title: perf(cuda): CUDA graph capture per batch/token bucket in the inference runtime
description:
Graph capture exists (LoadedModel::capture_graph, drivers/teeny-cuda/src/model/mod.rs ~1231-1640) but only tests use it. Capture one CUDA graph per shape bucket in the inference runtime and replay it each step, updating only small inputs (token ids, positions, block tables) in place.
Requires static memory plan, no per-launch allocations, and stream-based launches.

See INFERENCE_PERF_ROADMAP.md (repo root) for context and the llama.cpp/vLLM comparison.

title: perf(cuda): pinned host staging buffers and async copies overlapping compute
description:
All copies are synchronous cuMemcpyHtoD_v2/DtoH_v2 from pageable memory (drivers/teeny-cuda/src/device/mem.rs ~51,65). Use cuMemAllocHost staging buffers and cuMemcpyAsync on the model stream; overlap the next step's input upload and the previous step's token download with compute.

See INFERENCE_PERF_ROADMAP.md (repo root) for context and the llama.cpp/vLLM comparison.

title: perf(cuda): tensor-core GEMM for prefill and batched decode in the LLM path
description:
linear4_forward (apps/teeny-llm/src/kernels/linear.rs) is a per-row dot product with no tiling and no MMA. teeny-kernels already has a TMA + T::dot tiled matmul_forward (math/gemm.rs) that the LLM path does not use.
Scope: bf16 inputs with f32 accumulation via T::dot, tiles for M in [1..512], split-K for skinny decode shapes, epilogue hooks for fused activations/residuals; route LLM linears through it.
Acceptance: prefill GEMMs reach a reasonable fraction of peak tensor-core throughput on RTX 5070.

See INFERENCE_PERF_ROADMAP.md (repo root) for context and the llama.cpp/vLLM comparison.

title: perf(cuda): quantized GEMV/GEMM (int4/int8 dequant in registers feeding MMA)
description:
CUDA fast path for quantized-weight inference: MMVQ-style GEMV for small batch, MMQ-style GEMM for prefill/large batch, int8 dot or dequant-to-bf16 MMA, all in the Triton DSL.

See INFERENCE_PERF_ROADMAP.md (repo root) for context and the llama.cpp/vLLM comparison.

title: perf(cuda): tiled FlashAttention-2 for prefill and flash-decoding (split-KV) for long-context decode
description:
flash_attention2_forward (kernels/teeny-kernels/src/nn/attention/flash_attn2.rs) processes one query row per program and loops over keys one at a time. Implement block-tiled FA2 with T::dot for prefill, and a split-KV decode kernel with a reduction pass for long contexts; both over paged KV.

See INFERENCE_PERF_ROADMAP.md (repo root) for context and the llama.cpp/vLLM comparison.

title: feat(cuda): FP8 and NVFP4/MXFP4 matmuls on Blackwell via dot_scaled
description:
The DSL declares dot_scaled with E4M3/E5M2/E2M1 (kernels/teeny-triton/src/triton/mod.rs ~96-108, 290) but only a kitchen-sink test uses it. Make it lower and run through teenyc on sm_120 (RTX 5070), and add FP8 / NVFP4 / MXFP4 weight formats to the loader.

See INFERENCE_PERF_ROADMAP.md (repo root) for context and the llama.cpp/vLLM comparison.

title: feat(cuda): multi-GPU tensor parallelism (later)
description:
teeny_runtime::open() picks the first device; there is no peer copy or collective support. Tensor-parallel linears and attention heads with all-reduce. Not needed for 8B bf16 on a single 12 GB+ card; low priority.

See INFERENCE_PERF_ROADMAP.md (repo root) for context and the llama.cpp/vLLM comparison.

title: perf(riscv): zero-copy device buffers on unified memory
description:
On the K3, host and device memory are the same physical DRAM, but uploads/downloads are still memcpys competing for the ~21-24 GB/s bus (apps/teeny-llm/docs/functiongemma.md: ~22 ms of a 170 ms step was host copies). Make RISC-V device buffers aliasable from the host so inputs/outputs, weights (incl. mmap) and the KV cache need no copies.

See INFERENCE_PERF_ROADMAP.md (repo root) for context and the llama.cpp/vLLM comparison.

title: perf(riscv): map spacemit-k1/k3 capabilities to real target features (VLEN, zvfh/zvfbfmin, IME)
description:
Kernels are built for a fixed zvl128b f32 baseline (functiongemma.md ~148-149, 204-205) and the capability enum (generic-rvv1.0, spacemit-k1, spacemit-k3) is not mapped to LLVM features (compiler/teeny-compiler/src/compiler/target.rs ~17-25). Pass the correct -march/-mattr per capability, include it in the kernel cache key, and update stale comments calling RISC-V a stub/RV64GC baseline.

See INFERENCE_PERF_ROADMAP.md (repo root) for context and the llama.cpp/vLLM comparison.

title: perf: device-resident KV cache (DeviceKvCache) with in-kernel K/V writes
description:
HostKvCache keeps K/V in host Vec<f32> (support/teeny-kvcache/src/host.rs); each step uploads every layer's whole [capacity, row] buffers as graph inputs (runner.rs ~266-271, model.rs ~751-763), ~38 MB/token at 1k ctx, and reads new rows back to append them.
Scope:
- DeviceKvCache implementing the KvCache trait, allocated once on the device.
- Attention / a fused rope+store op writes new K/V rows into the cache in-kernel (llama.cpp set_rows); no per-step transfers.
- PastLen / positions passed as small device scalars.
- On unified-memory targets (K3) the same backend must avoid any copy.
Acceptance: per-step host<->device traffic independent of context length (tokens in, token ids/logits out only).

See INFERENCE_PERF_ROADMAP.md (repo root) for context and the llama.cpp/vLLM comparison.

title: perf(riscv): lower T::dot to the SpacemiT IME matrix extension in teenyc
description:
The K3's IME matrix unit is unused (functiongemma.md ~149). Lower int8 (and f16 where supported) T::dot tiles to IME instructions in teenyc so DSL kernels stay portable. Reference: llama.cpp ggml/src/ggml-cpu/spacemit/ime1_kernels.cpp and ime2_kernels.cpp.

See INFERENCE_PERF_ROADMAP.md (repo root) for context and the llama.cpp/vLLM comparison.

title: perf(riscv): on-the-fly int8 activation quantization and IME-friendly repacking of Q4/Q8 weights
description:
Follow llama.cpp's CPU pattern: quantize activations to int8 blocks per step, repack Q4/Q8 weights once at load time into the tile layout the IME kernels consume (cf. ggml/src/ggml-cpu/spacemit/repack.cpp, ggml-cpu/repack.cpp). Kernels written in the Triton DSL on top of the IME-lowered dot.

See INFERENCE_PERF_ROADMAP.md (repo root) for context and the llama.cpp/vLLM comparison.

title: perf(riscv): measure and tune batched decode on the K3
description:
Decode on the K3 is memory-bandwidth-bound, so batching several sequences should add throughput at little cost per token. Once the scheduler and batched attention land, measure tok/s vs batch size on the K3, tune linear block sizes / program ordering for batched shapes, and document results.

See INFERENCE_PERF_ROADMAP.md (repo root) for context and the llama.cpp/vLLM comparison.

title: perf(riscv): topology-aware threading (cluster pinning, X100/A100 split per op, L2-aware partitioning)
description:
The native launcher hands out program ids from a flat atomic counter (drivers/teeny-riscv/src/native.rs ~297-414); TEENY_RISCV_AI_THREADS just moves the last N threads to A100 cores.
Scope: pin threads to clusters; per-op placement (e.g. GEMM/IME work on A100 cores, other work on X100); partition weight rows so each cluster keeps its slice hot in L2 across steps.

See INFERENCE_PERF_ROADMAP.md (repo root) for context and the llama.cpp/vLLM comparison.

title: perf(riscv): TCM / scratchpad-aware tiling on SpacemiT
description:
If the K3 exposes tightly coupled memory to user space, stage weight/activation tiles there for IME kernels. Reference: llama.cpp ggml/src/ggml-cpu/spacemit/spine_tcm.h and spine_mem_pool.cpp. Start with an investigation of availability and API.

See INFERENCE_PERF_ROADMAP.md (repo root) for context and the llama.cpp/vLLM comparison.

title: perf: move per-step host work off the model worker hot path
description:
RoPE tables, KV append, argmax and detokenisation run single-threaded on the model worker (serve.rs / runner.rs); at ~11 tok/s on the K3 this is a noticeable share of each step. Largely solved by device RoPE, device KV and device sampling; remaining host work (detokenise, stop strings, streaming) should run on a separate thread, overlapped with the next step.

See INFERENCE_PERF_ROADMAP.md (repo root) for context and the llama.cpp/vLLM comparison.

title: feat: DSpark speculative decoding (semi-autoregressive drafter + confidence-scheduled verification)
perf: dynamic or bucketed token/batch dimensions for compiled LLM steps
description:
Steps are compiled only for T=16 (CHUNK, serve.rs ~53) and T=1; prompt remainders run one token at a time (runner.rs ~228-241), so a 71-token prompt is ~half the rate of a 64-token one.
Scope: either symbolic token/batch dims through lowering and kernels, or a set of compiled buckets (1,2,4,...,512) with padding to the next bucket. Bucket choice must also suit CUDA graph capture (one graph per bucket).
Acceptance: prompt throughput roughly monotonic in prompt length; no single-token prefill path.

See INFERENCE_PERF_ROADMAP.md (repo root) for context and the llama.cpp/vLLM comparison.

title: perf: compute RoPE cos/sin on device (or cache a full-context table) instead of rebuilding host tables each step
description:
runner.rs ~262-264 builds four RoPE tables on the host and uploads them every step. Compute cos/sin in the rope kernel from position ids, or precompute one table for max context at load and index it.
Acceptance: no per-step RoPE uploads; identical outputs vs current path.

See INFERENCE_PERF_ROADMAP.md (repo root) for context and the llama.cpp/vLLM comparison.

title: feat: generic decoder model builder (Llama/Qwen/Gemma/Mistral) plus mmap safetensors and GGUF loading
description:
Only FunctionGemma 270M exists, and Weights::load reads the whole file with std::fs::read and converts every tensor to f32 (runner.rs ~38-71).
Scope:
- One parameterised decoder builder: GQA, SwiGLU/GeGLU, RoPE variants (theta, scaling, partial), sliding-window layers, tied embeddings, pre/post norms, qk-norm.
- Load safetensors via mmap (reuse utilities/teeny-data safetensors loader), keeping the native dtype; no host f32 conversion.
- GGUF reader (metadata + tensors, incl. quantized types) to reach pre-quantized models.
- Target first models: Llama-3.2-1B/3B, Qwen2.5/3 1.5-8B, Gemma-3 1-4B.
Acceptance: a 1B and an 8B model load and match HF reference logits within tolerance.

See INFERENCE_PERF_ROADMAP.md (repo root) for context and the llama.cpp/vLLM comparison.

title: feat: paged KV cache with a block manager
description:
vLLM-style paged KV: fixed-size blocks, per-sequence block tables, on-demand allocation and freeing.
Scope: block allocator + block tables in teeny-kvcache; attention reads K/V through block-table indirection.
Prerequisite check: verify the Triton DSL / teenyc lowers gather-style loads (computed pointers from a block table) efficiently on CUDA and RISC-V.
Acceptance: many concurrent sequences share one KV pool with no per-sequence max-context reservation.

See INFERENCE_PERF_ROADMAP.md (repo root) for context and the llama.cpp/vLLM comparison.

title: feat: variable-length batched attention kernels (paged decode + packed prefill)
description:
gqa_attention_forward (apps/teeny-llm/src/kernels/attention.rs) runs one program per (token, head) and loops over keys one at a time; it serves one sequence.
Scope:
- Decode kernel over paged KV with per-sequence lengths (GQA, sliding window, softcap).
- Prefill kernel over cu_seqlens-packed sequences with causal masking.
- Both expressed in the Triton DSL.
Acceptance: correctness vs reference for mixed-length batches; scales with batch size.

See INFERENCE_PERF_ROADMAP.md (repo root) for context and the llama.cpp/vLLM comparison.

title: feat: continuous batching scheduler with chunked prefill
description:
Today a single worker serves requests strictly FIFO, one at a time (serve.rs ~65-125), and n>1 is refused (max_choices: 1).
Scope:
- Step-level scheduler: admit/retire sequences every step, mix prefill chunks and decode tokens under a token budget per step (chunked prefill).
- Pre-emption (recompute or swap) when KV blocks run out.
- Support n>1 choices.
- Streaming per sequence through the existing ChatModel / ModelEngine interfaces.
Acceptance: aggregate tok/s increases with concurrent clients; no head-of-line blocking from long prompts.

See INFERENCE_PERF_ROADMAP.md (repo root) for context and the llama.cpp/vLLM comparison.

title: test_qemu_relu still calls the placeholder riscv_kernel symbol with no arguments
description:
Found 2026-09-11 running the RISC-V suite one test binary at a time against teenyc from teeny feat/triton-riscv-rvv @ 9f48d7207fa: TEENYC_PATH=<teeny>/build/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/stage1/bin/teenyc INSTA_FORCE_PASS=1 cargo test -p teeny-kernels --no-default-features --features riscv,training --test <name> -- --test-threads=1. Overall: 69 binaries, 63 passed; 245 tests passed, 15 failed.

Failing test (1): drivers/teeny-riscv/tests/test_qemu_relu.rs::compiled_kernel_loads_and_runs_under_qemu (cargo test -p teeny-riscv --features qemu --test test_qemu_relu).

Error:
  qemu-riscv64 harness exited with exit status: 1: stderr=dlsym(riscv_kernel) failed: /tmp/teenyc_cache/relu_forward_<hash>.o: undefined symbol: riscv_kernel

Cause: the test and teeny-test's riscv::qemu harness were written for teeny's old placeholder RiscvBackend, which ignored the kernel and emitted a no-argument void @riscv_kernel(). teenyc now really lowers the kernel through TritonCPU: the compiled .so exports the kernel's entry point (llvm-nm -D shows T relu_forward_entry_point), and its signature is the kernel's own arguments followed by six program-context arguments that TritonCPU's FuncOpToLLVM appends: pid x/y/z (i32), then grid/num_programs x/y/z (u32) (see teeny issue teenyc-34n). The C harness in testing/teeny-test/src/riscv/qemu.rs dlsym()s argv[2] and calls it as void(*)(void), so even with the right name it would run the kernel with garbage arguments.

Fix: resolve the real entry-point symbol, and have the harness allocate input/output buffers and call it with the kernel's arguments plus pid=0 and grid=1 per axis (single block), then check the output. Related: teenygrad-1zd.1 (RISC-V integration tests via QEMU).
close_reason: Fixed in e5ed60b17: teeny-test's QEMU harness calls the real kernel entry point with its arguments plus TritonCPU's six program-context arguments, once per block; test_qemu_relu checks ReluForward's output against host relu over 2548 elements, including the mask.

comments.author: Arshad Mahmood
comments.text: 2026-09-11: Fixed (uncommitted). teeny-test's riscv::qemu harness now runs a real pointwise kernel: QemuTestEnv::run_pointwise_kernel(so_path, symbol, block_size, n_elements, x, y) writes x/y to f32 files, and the C harness dlopen()s the .so and calls the entry point as void(float *x, float *y, int32_t n, int32_t pid_x, pid_y, pid_z, uint32_t grid_x, grid_y, grid_z) once per block (pid 0..blocks-1, grid = blocks x 1 x 1), then writes y back. qemu-riscv64 runs with -cpu max for RVV. The old no-argument run_kernel is gone (test_qemu_relu was its only caller). test_qemu_relu now compiles ReluForward (BLOCK_SIZE 1024), calls kernel.entry_point_name() (relu_forward_entry_point) over 2548 elements (2 full blocks + 500), and asserts y[i] == max(x[i], 0) for i < n and that padding past n keeps its sentinel. Passes: cargo test -p teeny-riscv --features qemu --test test_qemu_relu (1 passed, ~2 s under QEMU).

title: feat: the graph layer consumes the tile specs its kernels declare (exec_from)
description:
## Goal

Make the graph layer read the tile specs the kernels now declare. Without this,
every conversion rung in teenygrad-1tl accumulates declarations that nothing
consumes.

## The gap

After 1tl.1 and 1tl.2, 46 forward kernels declare their tile axes and
`#[tiled_kernel]` generates a `tile_spec()` for each. `TileGraph::propagate`
reads three of them.

`exec_from` in `kernels/teeny-kernels/src/graph/mod.rs` hardcodes:

    let tile_spec = None;

and 20 `Op` arms route through it -- Elu, Selu, Celu, Gelu, Mish, Hardtanh,
Relu6, Hardsigmoid, Hardswish, Hardshrink, LeakyRelu, Threshold, Softsign,
Softshrink, Softplus, Sigmoid, LogSigmoid, Tanh, Tanhshrink, Silu. Only Relu and
Silu end up with a spec, and both do it by overriding the field after the call.
So `propagate` treats the other 18 as hard boundaries even though each kernel
can describe itself precisely.

`exec_from`'s own doc comment already states that every caller is one of the
flat single-BLOCK_SIZE elementwise activations, which is exactly the shape whose
`tile_spec(rank)` is derivable.

Note the doc comment also refers to a `flat_elementwise_tile_spec` fallback.
That function no longer exists; the reference is stale and should go.

## Approach

Give `exec_from` a required `tile_spec: KernelTileSpec` parameter and pass
`XForward::<f32>::tile_spec(node.shape.len())` at each call site. Required
rather than `Option` so a future caller has to decide rather than silently
inheriting `None`; a caller that is not flat elementwise should not be using
`exec_from` at all, which its doc already says.

`tile_spec(rank)` is dtype-independent -- block/extent names and dims do not
vary with `D` -- so the `::<f32>` monomorphization is safe for any node dtype.
This is the reasoning already written out at the Op::Relu arm.

Relu's and Silu's post-hoc `exec.tile_spec = Some(..)` overrides then become
redundant and should collapse into the normal path.

## Done when

- `exec_from` requires a spec and no arm sets `tile_spec` after the fact.
- A test asserts that every Op in the list above lowers to a `KernelExecutable`
  with `tile_spec.is_some()`, so the next conversion rung cannot regress it.
- The stale `flat_elementwise_tile_spec` reference is gone.
close_reason: Landed via PR #55 (300effc22); exec_from now requires a spec, 20 call sites wired, guard test verified against a deliberate regression. No behaviour change until propagate is revived (teenygrad-1nr.25).

title: Technical debt
description: Umbrella for cleanup work that doesn't change behaviour: naming and layout consistency, stale comments, and conventions that should be written down so new code follows them. Each item is a child issue.

title: Name all tests consistently with a test_ prefix, and record the convention in CLAUDE.md
description:
Test function names are inconsistent: across the workspace, 424 #[test] functions use the test_ prefix and 405 don't. For example, core/teeny-core/src/graph/mod.rs's tests module uses test_ (test_sequential_graph_extraction, test_traced_avgpool2d_records_padding), while the sibling graph/{constant,einsum,matmul,reduce,resize}.rs test modules use descriptive names without it (a_u64_above_i64_max_is_out_of_range_not_wrapped, plans_a_batched_outer_contraction).

Convention: every test function is named test_<what it checks>, keeping the descriptive part, e.g. test_u64_above_i64_max_is_out_of_range.

Done when:
1. Every #[test] function in the workspace has the test_ prefix. Rename only, with no behaviour change; renaming insta-snapshot tests also renames their .snap files, so move those with git mv rather than regenerating them.
2. CLAUDE.md's Testing section states the convention, so new tests follow it.
3. All four snapshot configs still pass with the same test counts: --workspace, -p teeny-kernels with cuda,hardware, -p teeny-kernels default features, -p teeny-kernels --no-default-features --features riscv,training.

title: Benchmarks for critical kernels (matmul/linear, attention, norms) on CUDA and RISC-V
Move custom-op output dtype into CustomOp::infer_output_dtype and drop record_custom's dtype parameter
description:
Problem: a custom op's output shape comes from the op (CustomOp::infer_output_shape), but its output dtype comes from the caller, through SymTensor::record_custom's third parameter, dtype: Option<DtypeRepr> (core/teeny-core/src/graph/tensor/mod.rs). With None, the node takes the primary input's dtype via dtype.unwrap_or(self.dtype). So every call site has to know what dtype the op produces, although that is a property of the op, just as its shape is.

The unwrap_or itself is fine: it defaults an optional argument and hides no error. The issue is where the decision lives.

Evidence that the override isn't needed:
- No code in this workspace calls record_custom.
- Its only external user is vision-rs (depends on teeny-core 0.3.1 from crates.io), which calls it 5 times in src/models/yolo/yolo26/blocks/c2psa.rs, for PsaPackQkvOp, FlashAttn2PsaOp lo and hi, PsaMergeAttnOp and PsaExtractVOp. All 5 pass None.
- The kernels book's one example (books/kernels/src/in-a-model/graph-op.md) also passes None.

Do NOT remove record_custom. It is public API that vision-rs depends on, it is the only practical way to record a CustomOp through SymTensor (the alternative is Graph::add_node with manual node-id bookkeeping), and the book chapter 'Your Kernel as a Graph Op' is built around it.

Suggested approach:
1. Add a defaulted method to CustomOp in core/teeny-core/src/graph/mod.rs:
       /// The output dtype given the input dtypes; by default the first input's.
       fn infer_output_dtype(&self, input_dtypes: &[DtypeRepr]) -> DtypeRepr {
           input_dtypes[0]
       }
   Ops that change dtype, such as a comparison producing bool or a cast, override it.
2. Change record_custom to (&self, data: CustomData, other_inputs: &[&SymTensor]) -> Self. It builds the input dtypes the same way it builds the input shapes, and asks data.infer_output_dtype for the result.
3. Update the Op::Custom doc comment in graph/mod.rs, which currently says shape and dtype must be supplied via Graph::add_node or record_custom.
4. Update books/kernels/src/in-a-model/graph-op.md: drop the third argument from the example and the 'an output dtype, or None' bullet, add infer_output_dtype to the 'Implementing CustomOp' trait listing, and update OUTLINE.md's Uses line for chapter 20.
5. Add teeny-core tests: the default infers the first input's dtype, and an override (e.g. a bool-producing op) is recorded on the node.

Compatibility: this is a breaking signature change to a published crate, so it ships in a minor release. vision-rs then needs a one-line change at each of its 5 call sites (delete the None argument) when it picks up that release. Adding infer_output_dtype is not breaking, because it has a default.

title: Replace ConstantTensor's to_i64_vec/to_f64_vec with one generic to_vec::<T>() built on num_traits::NumCast
description:
Problem: core/teeny-core/src/graph/constant.rs has to_i64_vec and to_f64_vec, which repeat the same pattern (match on the source dtype, decode little-endian chunks, convert each element). Every new target type (usize for shapes, i32, f32, ...) would add another copy. A generic version needs a generic 'as T', which Rust has no trait for.

Options for a generic 'as T':
- 'as' itself: a primitive cast, unusable in generic code.
- TryFrom/From: std has no float<->int TryFrom, and From covers only lossless widenings (no i64 -> f64).
- num_traits::AsPrimitive<T>: exactly 'as' as a trait, so it wraps silently. Measured: u64::MAX.as_() gives -1i64, the bug we just removed. Rejected.
- num_traits::NumCast: a checked 'as' returning Option. Use this. num-traits 0.2.19 is already a workspace dependency and works with default-features = false, which teeny-core needs because it is no_std.

NumCast behaviour (measured with num-traits 0.2.19):
- u64::MAX -> i64: None. -1i64 -> usize: None. 300i64 -> u8: None. NaN -> i64: None.
- 2.7f32 -> i64: Some(2), silent truncation. -0.5f64 -> u32: Some(0), silent truncation.
- i64::MAX -> f64: Some(9.22e18), rounded.
- 1e40f64 -> f32: Some(inf), not None.
- half::f16 -> f64 works through half's num-traits feature (half 2.7.1 is already a workspace dependency).

Suggested design (prototyped; it compiles and matches today's behaviour):
    /// An element type a constant can be decoded into.
    pub trait ConstantElement: NumCast + Copy {
        const NAME: &'static str;   // for error messages
        const FROM_FLOAT: bool;     // false for integers: refuse floats, don't truncate
    }
    pub fn to_vec<T: ConstantElement>(&self) -> Result<Vec<T>, ConstantReadError> {
        match self.dtype {
            DtypeRepr::Bool | DtypeRepr::U8 => self.decode_cast(|[b]: [u8; 1]| b),
            DtypeRepr::I32 => self.decode_cast(i32::from_le_bytes),
            // ...one line per source dtype...
            DtypeRepr::F32 if T::FROM_FLOAT => self.decode_cast(f32::from_le_bytes),
            _ => Err(ConstantReadError::UnsupportedDtype { dtype: self.dtype, target: T::NAME }),
        }
    }
decode_cast<const W, S: NumCast + Copy + Debug, T> decodes each element as its source type S, then calls T::from(s), turning None into OutOfRange { index, value, target }. to_i64_vec and to_f64_vec stay as one-line wrappers (self.to_vec()), so callers are unchanged.

Prototype results:
- u64 [1, MAX] as i64: OutOfRange at index 1.
- f32 as i64: UnsupportedDtype.
- i32 as f64: widened.
- bool as i64: works.
- i32 [3, -1] as usize: OutOfRange { index: 1, value: "-1" }.

What it adds:
- to_vec::<usize>() refuses negatives, which suits shape vectors. It can replace the manual usize::try_from after to_i64_vec in teeny-onnx's Split handling (support/teeny-onnx/src/onnx.rs, expand_split).
- Each new target type costs one small impl ConstantElement.
- F16 and BF16 decoding, refused today, comes almost free through half.

Decisions to make:
1. Float to integer: NumCast truncates. FROM_FLOAT keeps today's rule of refusing a float tensor read as integers. If integral floats such as 2.0 should be accepted instead, the check becomes 'accept if s.fract() == 0'.
2. Float overflow: f64 -> f32 gives inf, not None. A float target needs an extra check, treating a finite source with a non-finite result as OutOfRange. That matters only once an f32 target exists.
3. The OutOfRange error: its value: u64 field must become generic, since a failing value may be -1i32 or NaN. The prototype formats the value into a String, which keeps the 'messages include the values' rule.
4. Precision loss into floats (i64 -> f64 above 2^53) stays allowed and documented, as now.

When: worth doing once a third conversion is needed, usize being the most likely. With only i64 and f64 it's roughly a wash in lines of code; the gain is that each source dtype is listed once instead of once per method.

Done when:
- to_vec::<T>() exists and to_i64_vec/to_f64_vec are wrappers around it.
- The existing ConstantTensor tests in graph/constant.rs pass unchanged, apart from the OutOfRange value field.
- New tests cover a usize target, including refusing negatives, and whichever of decisions 1-3 are adopted.

title: Remove the activation misc modules: move LeakyRelu, Threshold, Softsign, Softshrink and Softplus into named modules
description:
Problem: nn/activation/misc.rs is a catch-all ('Other activations that don't fit the other modules'), and it exists in two crates with the same five activations:
- core/teeny-core/src/nn/activation/misc.rs: the layer structs LeakyRelu, Threshold, Softsign, Softshrink and Softplus, whose eager call() is still todo!().
- kernels/teeny-kernels/src/nn/activation/misc.rs: their Triton kernels and ops (LeakyReluForward/Backward, ThresholdForward/Backward, SoftsignForward, SoftshrinkForward, SoftplusForward, the *ForwardDispatch types, the *Op structs and LeakyReluRuntimeOp), tested by kernels/teeny-kernels/tests/test_misc_acts.rs with insta snapshots tests/snapshots/test_misc_acts__*.snap (source and asm, cuda and riscv).
Goal: no misc module in either crate.

Decision 1, scope (unresolved; the user wanted to clarify before choosing):
- (a) Both crates, with the same layout in each. Recommended, so the two activation trees keep mirroring each other.
- (b) teeny-core only. teeny-kernels then keeps misc.rs, and the layouts diverge until it's done separately.

Decision 2, layout (unresolved):
- (a) Recommended: LeakyRelu and Threshold join Relu in relu.rs (Threshold(0, 0) is ReLU). Softsign, Softshrink and Softplus go in a new soft.rs, mirroring the existing hard.rs (Hardtanh, Hardsigmoid, Hardswish, Hardshrink, Relu6).
- (b) One module per activation: leaky_relu.rs, threshold.rs, softsign.rs, softshrink.rs, softplus.rs.

References to update:
- teeny-core: nn/activation/mod.rs (module list and doc comments; relu.rs's doc already says 'ReLU and leaky ReLU'); graph/tensor/layers.rs (the misc:: import); graph/mod.rs, the five Op variant doc comments that point at nn::activation::misc::* (around lines 814-833).
- teeny-kernels: nn/activation/mod.rs; graph/mod.rs (the misc:: import block near line 48); tests/test_misc_acts.rs.
- Other consumers: none found in vision-rs, vision-rs-utils or drone-rs. The module paths are public API of published crates, so this is a breaking path change for a minor release.

Snapshot handling (if teeny-kernels is in scope):
- Insta names snapshots after the test file, so renaming or splitting test_misc_acts.rs (e.g. into test_relu.rs / a new test_soft_acts.rs) renames its .snap files. Move them with git mv rather than regenerating them.
- Moving the kernel structs may change kernel source or asm (e.g. module paths or .loc lines), so expect snapshot drift. Verify numerics on GPU first, then converge snapshots jointly across all four configs: --workspace; -p teeny-kernels --features cuda,hardware; -p teeny-kernels default features; -p teeny-kernels --no-default-features --features riscv,training. Pass counts should not change.

Related: teeny-kernels also has nn/activation/extra.rs ('Additional activation kernels: Swish, PRelu, LogSoftmax, Hardmax, ThresholdedRelu, Shrink'), another catch-all with no teeny-core counterpart. It's a candidate for the same treatment (e.g. ThresholdedRelu next to Threshold, Shrink next to Softshrink/Hardshrink, LogSoftmax in softmax.rs), but that is out of scope here unless decided otherwise.

Done when: neither crate has an activation::misc module, all references are updated, and the four snapshot configs pass with unchanged test counts.

title: teeny-onnx: add a from_bytes import entry point and read model files whole instead of streaming
description:
## Background

`support/teeny-onnx/src/onnx.rs` is fully synchronous. Its only I/O is opening and reading the model file:

- `Onnx::from_path`, `Onnx::from_path_with_tensors` and `Onnx::import_from_path` each `std::fs::File::open` the path and pass the unbuffered `File` to the matching `*_from_reader`.
- `Onnx::import_from_reader(&mut impl Read)` wraps the reader in `protobuf::CodedInputStream` and parses the whole `ModelProto` in one call.
- Tensors whose data is stored externally (`data_location == EXTERNAL`) are refused in `tensor_data` rather than loaded. The model file is the only thing read.
- The crate doesn't depend on tokio, and every current caller is synchronous: the tests in `kernels/teeny-kernels/tests/` and `support/teeny-onnx/tests/`.

## Why not make the import async

We looked at this and decided against it:

1. **The work is CPU-bound, not I/O-bound.** The read is one sequential file read. The cost is the protobuf parse, the tensor conversion and building the graph. An async read wouldn't stop the parse from blocking an executor thread, so an async caller would still need `spawn_blocking` around the whole import.
2. **The protobuf crate has no async parser.** `parse_from` takes a blocking `Read` or a byte slice, so an async version could only read the bytes into memory and then do the same synchronous parse.
3. **`tokio::fs` is blocking I/O on tokio's thread pool.** An async wrapper would amount to `spawn_blocking(|| Onnx::import_from_path(p))`, which callers can already write.
4. **It would tie the crate to one runtime.** A synchronous parser that takes a reader works with tokio, smol (both used in the workspace) or no runtime at all.

The idiomatic shape is a synchronous parser, with async callers choosing where it runs.

## Proposed changes

1. **Add `Onnx::from_bytes` / `Onnx::import_from_bytes(&[u8])`** (and `_with_tensors` if wanted). They would use `ModelProto::parse_from_bytes`.
   - The tests already fake this with `Onnx::import_from_reader(&mut &bytes[..])`; switch them over.
   - Callers can then get the bytes however they like (tokio, smol, HTTP, a memory map) and parse them.
2. **Read the whole file, then parse the bytes.** In the `*_from_path` functions, use `std::fs::read(path)` followed by `import_from_bytes`, instead of streaming from an unbuffered `File`.
   - The parsed proto holds every byte anyway, so streaming saves no memory.
   - Parsing from a slice avoids `CodedInputStream`'s refill path.
   - Put the path in the I/O error. A bare `io::Error` from `File::open` doesn't say which file.
3. **Optional, later: an async convenience behind a `tokio` feature.** For example, `import_from_path_async`, which runs the sync import under `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`.
   - Only add it once something async actually loads models; nothing does today.
   - Keep tokio out of the default features.
4. **Future, if external data is supported.** Weights in sidecar files are the one place I/O would become real work, since large exports keep their weights there. Use a memory map or parallel reads, not async. Resolve `location` relative to the model file's directory.

## Acceptance

- `import_from_bytes` exists, and the existing tests use it in place of the `&mut &bytes[..]` reader trick.
- The path-based entry points read the whole file and parse the bytes, and an open or read error names the path.
- No change to the import's output.
- The `teeny-onnx` tests pass, and so do the `teeny-kernels` ONNX tests (`./scripts/test.sh -p teeny-onnx -p teeny-kernels`).

title: einsum_plan: limit only the output rank; operands can be EINSUM_MAX_RANK + 1
description:
## Problem

`einsum_plan` (`core/teeny-core/src/graph/einsum.rs`) refuses any operand whose rank is above `EINSUM_MAX_RANK` (4), as well as any output above it:

- operand check: `if shape.len() > EINSUM_MAX_RANK` inside the per-operand loop;
- output check: `if out_labels.len() > EINSUM_MAX_RANK` just after it.

Only the output limit is imposed by the kernel. `einsum_forward` (`kernels/teeny-kernels/src/math/einsum.rs`) takes 3 pointers plus 16 scalars:

- `n_elements`, `k`, `a_step`, `b_step`;
- three length-4 vectors: the output extents `s0..s3`, and A's and B's per-output-coordinate strides `a0..a3` / `b0..b3`.

That is 19 of the 20 arguments the ABI allows. The vectors are indexed by *output* coordinate. An operand's own rank never reaches the kernel: its strides are worked out on the host by `contiguous_strides` and then projected onto the output labels.

The planner already refuses partial reductions (`PartialReduction`) and requires exactly one contracted label (`ContractedLabels`). So every operand label is either an output label or the single contracted label, which means:

```text
operand rank <= output rank + 1 <= EINSUM_MAX_RANK + 1
```

An equation like `abcde,ae->abcd` (rank-5 A, rank-4 output, contract over `e`) fits the kernel exactly, but it is refused with `RankTooHigh { rank: 5 }`.

## Suggested fix

1. Drop the per-operand `RankTooHigh` check. Keep the output check, which is the real kernel limit, and leave the operand ranks to the structural checks that follow.
   - Alternatively, keep an operand check at `EINSUM_MAX_RANK + 1` as a safety net, with a comment explaining the bound.
2. Update the `EINSUM_MAX_RANK` doc comment to say the limit applies to the output rank.
3. Tests:
   - `test_rejects_what_it_cannot_express` currently asserts that `abcde,ae->abcd` is `RankTooHigh`. Change it to plan successfully, and check its strides: A's contract stride is 1, and `a_strides` are `[16, 8, 4, 2]` for a `[2,2,2,2,2]` A.
   - Add a case with a rank-5 *output*, which must still be `RankTooHigh`.
   - Add an end-to-end kernel test in `kernels/teeny-kernels/tests/test_einsum.rs` for the rank-5-operand form, checked against a CPU reference, so the projection is exercised on the device.

## Priority

Low. No export seen so far needs it: FoundationStereo's equation is `aijk,aijh->ajkh`, which is rank 4 everywhere. This just removes a limit the kernel doesn't actually have.

title: EinsumRuntimeOp: replace silent 'as i32' casts with checked conversions and a clear error
description:
## Problem

`EinsumRuntimeOp` (`kernels/teeny-kernels/src/math/einsum.rs`) turns the host-side plan into the kernel's `i32` scalars with plain `as` casts. These wrap silently above `i32::MAX` (2^31 - 1):

- `EinsumRuntimeOp::new`: `plan.k as i32`, `plan.a_contract_stride as i32`, `plan.b_contract_stride as i32`.
- `pad_left`: `*v as i32` for the output extents and both stride vectors. The plan holds these as `i64`/`usize`.
- `pack_args`: `self.kernel_scalars(n as i32)`, where `n` is the output's element count, a `usize`.

The kernel itself also computes offsets in `i32`: `a_base + c * a_step` and `b_base + c * b_step`, built from the per-coordinate strides. So even when every scalar fits, an operand whose largest element offset is at least 2^31 overflows inside the kernel.

A wrapped value doesn't fail. It produces a negative or truncated extent or stride, so the kernel reads the wrong elements or, under the masked load, zeros. The result is silently wrong output, not an error.

Today's exports are well below the limit. FoundationStereo's einsum operands are `[1, 224, 120, 160]`, about 4.3M elements.

## Suggested fix

1. Do the checked conversion where the plan becomes the runtime op. `EinsumRuntimeOp::new` currently returns `Option<Self>`; make it return a `Result` with a specific error.
   - Convert `k`, the contraction strides, the extents, the strides and the element count with `i32::try_from`.
   - Also check that each operand's maximum element offset fits. That is `sum((extent - 1) * |stride|)` over the output axes, plus `(k - 1) * |contract_stride|`; it's simpler to check each operand's element count, since contiguous inputs bound the offset by it.
   - The error should name the value, the operand and the limit, e.g. "Op::Einsum: operand 0 has 3,000,000,000 elements, beyond the 2^31 - 1 the kernel's i32 offsets can address".
2. Move `pad_left` from `as` to the checked conversion. Alternatively, have `new` validate first, so `pad_left` takes already-checked values.
3. `pack_args` can't return an error. Its `n as i32` should be covered by checking the output element count in `new`; then the cast there is known to be safe and can say so (or use `expect` with that reason).
4. `einsum_executable` (`kernels/teeny-kernels/src/graph/mod.rs`) maps the `None` from `new` to a rank error. Propagate the new error instead, so the message says which limit was hit.
5. Tests: a unit test that a plan whose `k` or element count is above `i32::MAX` is refused with the new error. The values can be built directly in an `EinsumPlan`, with no allocation. And a test that a plan just under the limit is accepted.

## Related

Other kernels in `kernels/teeny-kernels/src/math/` very likely have the same `as i32` pattern for extents and strides. Audit them in the same change, or file a follow-up. The fix should only affect values that would have wrapped, never valid ones.

## Priority

Low today, but it should be fixed before any model with an operand over about 2.1G elements is lowered through einsum. Wrong output with no error is the worst way for it to fail.

title: Executors launch empty grids for zero-element outputs; CUDA rejects them (skip the launch instead of per-op .max(1))
description:
## Problem

A node whose output has a zero-length extent gets an empty grid, `[0, 1, 1]`, from the usual `ceil(n / block_size)` formula. No executor checks for that before launching.

- **CUDA:** a launch with no blocks is rejected (`cuLaunchKernel` returns `CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE`) and the model run fails. `kernels/teeny-kernels/tests/test_fs_zero_extents.rs` documents exactly this: the FoundationStereo 96x128 export fails at `/cost_agg/conv3_up/conv/Slice_1`, shape `[0, 112, 6, 8]`, with a grid of `[0, 1, 1]`.
- **RISC-V:** an empty grid launches nothing, and the run carries on.

## Current state

Each op handles this or doesn't, on its own. 8 of the 44 `RuntimeOp`s with a `grid` clamp it with `.max(1)`:

- `pad_nd`, `conv_transpose2d`, `broadcast_binary`, `scatter`, `grid_sample`, `resize`, one op in `activation/misc.rs`;
- and the slot calculation in `gather`.

The other ~36 don't, and `EinsumRuntimeOp` is among them.

`.max(1)` is only safe for a kernel whose every load and store is masked by `p < n`. With `n = 0` the one block then does nothing. A kernel with an unmasked access, or one that divides by an output extent, would misbehave on that block instead. So a per-op clamp is not a general fix.

## Suggested fix

Skip the launch in the executor when the output has no elements, or equivalently when any grid component is 0. A zero-element output has nothing to write, so skipping is exact rather than an approximation.

Launch sites in `drivers/teeny-cuda/src/model/mod.rs`:

- forward: around lines 637/641, 801/805, 1329, 1407 and 1450/1454 (`grid` / `grid_for_launch`);
- backward (training): around 1144/1146 (`backward_grid` / `backward_grid_for_launch`). A zero-element *input* gradient also gives an empty backward grid.

The `teeny-test` executor (`testing/teeny-test/src/model.rs`) launches through `Device::launch` and needs the same guard.

Things to check while there:

1. **Zero-byte allocation.** The executor allocates `n_elems * elem_bytes` for the output, and `cuMemAlloc` of 0 bytes is also an error on CUDA. Either skip allocating, or give the node a valid placeholder pointer that downstream nodes never read (they also see zero elements).
2. **Multi-launch ops** (`n_launches() > 1`). Check each launch's grid individually, since one chunk can be empty while others aren't. Concat with a zero-length input is the obvious case.
3. **Remove the per-op `.max(1)` clamps** once the executor guards, or leave them and say why. Keeping both hides which layer is responsible.

## Tests

- A graph with a zero-extent node (e.g. a `Slice` that selects nothing) feeding a consumer, run on CUDA and on qemu. It should complete, and the consumer's result should match a reference.
- Re-run `test_fs_zero_extents` and the FoundationStereo 96x128 CUDA run that fails today.

## Related

`EinsumRuntimeOp` now takes its launch count from the plan rather than the resolved output shape (feature/fs-structural-lowerings). `tile`, `strided_copy` and `gather` still compute `n` from the runtime `output_shape` in `pack_args`/`grid`, the same pattern einsum had. They're worth reviewing against their stored plans when this is done.

title: ScatterND/ScatterElements kernels store at unchecked model-controlled indices (out-of-bounds write)
description:
## Summary

`scatter_nd_forward` and `scatter_elements_forward` (`kernels/teeny-kernels/src/nn/tensor/scatter.rs`) use index values taken from the model as the store offset, without checking them against the axis. An out-of-range index writes outside the output buffer. Both kernels are new on `feature/fs-structural-lowerings` (b1af14680 ScatterND, 9924115c9 ScatterElements); neither exists on `main`.

The security review of PR #164 rated this 7 of 10, just under its reporting bar of 8. That was only because exploiting it needs a specific deployment. The missing bound itself is certain.

## Where

- `scatter_nd_forward`: the offset is computed at `scatter.rs:125` (`dst = dst + (coord + wrapped) * stride;`) and stored to at `scatter.rs:138`.
- `scatter_elements_forward`: the offset is computed at `scatter.rs:208-210` (`along`, `dst`) and stored to at `scatter.rs:221`.
- Lowering: `kernels/teeny-kernels/src/graph/mod.rs:4544-4550`, through `scatter_elements_executable` (around line 930) and `scatter_nd_executable` (around line 1064).
- ONNX mapping: `support/teeny-onnx/src/onnx.rs:1306-1309` maps `ScatterElements` and `ScatterND` straight onto these ops.

## The defect

Each kernel loads an `i64` index and casts it to `i32` with `T::cast::<i64, i32>`. A large value wraps silently. If the result is negative, the axis extent is added once. The result then becomes the destination offset:

```rust
let coord = T::cast::<i64, i32>(coord, None, false);
let wrapped = T::where_(coord.lt(0), extent, T::full::<i32>(&[BLOCK_SIZE], 0));
dst = dst + (coord + wrapped) * stride;
...
T::store(out_ptr.add_offsets(dst), v, Some(in_bounds), ...)
```

`in_bounds` is `p < n_elements`, a check on the lane number only. Nothing tests `0 <= coord + wrapped < extent`:

- **In the kernel:** no mask, clamp or `where_` on the store.
- **On the host:** the lowering checks shapes, rank, axis, dtype (indices must be I64) and operand count. It never looks at index values, even when they're a constant known at lowering time.

`Gather` handles the same problem: `GatherRuntimeOp` rejects any index outside `[-dim, dim)` on the host (`GatherError::IndexOutOfRange`, `kernels/teeny-kernels/src/nn/tensor/gather.rs`). So this is a gap compared with an existing check in the same crate, not a missing hardening measure.

## Impact

Someone loads an untrusted `.onnx` file with a `ScatterND` or `ScatterElements` node. Its indices come from a `Constant` (copied to the device unchanged) or from a small computation, and its update values are chosen by the attacker.

- **Native riscv64 backend** (`drivers/teeny-riscv/src/native.rs`): the compiled kernel is loaded with `libloading` and run inside the host process, directly on host memory. Each lane writes an attacker-chosen value up to about 2^31 elements either side of the output buffer. That corrupts the host process's heap, which is a standard building block for code execution. Severity: HIGH on that deployment.
- **CUDA:** the write lands in device memory and overwrites other tensors in the context, such as weights or another model's activations, so outputs can be silently tampered with. Severity: MEDIUM.
- **qemu-user** (RISC-V on a non-riscv host): confined to the emulated process.

Even without an attacker, an exporter bug or an index computed out of range silently corrupts memory instead of failing.

## Suggested fix

1. **Bound the store in both kernels** (required). After the negative wrap, AND `0 <= idx && idx < extent` into the store mask, per indexed axis for ScatterND. An out-of-range index then writes nothing. This is the only fix that also covers indices computed at runtime, which the module comment says FoundationStereo's are.
   - ONNX treats out-of-range indices as invalid, so dropping the write is conformant.
   - Bounding the final `dst` against the output's element count is a cheap extra guard.
2. **Catch the 64-to-32-bit wrap.** Check the `i64` value before the cast, or do the range check in `i64`, so a value like `2^32 + 1` can't wrap into range and pass the check.
3. **Validate on the host when indices are constant.** When the indices operand is in the lowering's `ConstantMap`, check its values at lowering time the way `GatherRuntimeOp` does, and refuse with an error naming the node, the index and the extent. This gives a clear error for the common case on top of the kernel guard.
4. **Audit the other data-indexed kernels** for the same pattern: anything that turns a loaded value into a store or load offset. GatherND and grid_sample were checked in the review and are fine (host check and masked loads respectively).

## Tests

- **A graph test per op** (ScatterND, ScatterElements): the indices include one value at or above the extent, one below `-extent`, and one large `i64` that would wrap in `i32`. Put a guard region next to the output buffer and assert that it's untouched and that the in-range updates landed. Run on CUDA (`cuda,hardware`) and on qemu (`qemu,hardware,training`).
- **A lowering test** that constant out-of-range indices are refused with the new error.
- The existing `test_scatter_nd.rs` cases must still pass; snapshots will change for the masked store, in all four snapshot configurations.

## Priority

P1. It's a memory-corruption path reachable from an untrusted model file, introduced on this branch. It should be fixed before PR #164 merges, or as the first follow-up.
close_reason: Fixed in b0eea55c7 on feature/fs-structural-lowerings: kernels mask out-of-range indices (checked in i64 before the narrowing cast); constant indices validated on the host. Tests in test_scatter_nd.rs, run on CUDA and qemu.

title: feat: an epilogue hook for #[tile_loop(generate)] -- work between the loop and the store
notes:
## DONE -- PR #86 (2026-10-05). Option C, as the issue predicted.

`#[tile_carry(acc = [..], finish = <expr>)]` emits `let acc = <expr>;` between the loop and the store. The epilogue is a declared expression over the carry, not a second spliced body, so the loop body stays the only place author code is spliced -- which is what teenygrad-1nr.18.3's C3 asked for. Option A (a marker in the body) is the failure mode that analysis rejected; option B was not needed.

A `finish` without `generate` is rejected: the epilogue is only emitted by the generator, so it would be silently dropped.

Acceptance bar met: avgpool2d_forward and conv2d_bias_forward both take `generate`, bodies down to `acc = acc + input;` and `acc = acc + x * w;` respectively, numerics passing against their existing fixtures.

## The test asserts the ORDER, not just the numerics

An epilogue placed before the loop divides the zeroed carry; placed after the store it is dead code. BOTH still compile, and avgpool's numerics catch the first but not the second. test_the_epilogue_sits_between_the_loop_and_the_store checks loop < finish < store in the generated source.

That is teenyc-u9z's lesson applied: a generated-code feature needs its generated code examined.

## What this does NOT cover, found while doing it

conv2d_bias's epilogue LOADS a bias, and that operand cannot be a route-1 tile. An input axis must match an output axis on extent AND block; the output's C_OUT is unblocked, so the bias's must be too -- but a route-1 input derives its tile shape from a blocked axis, so it must have one. A read-once operand indexed by an unblocked axis and broadcast over the blocked one has no expression today.

The kernel converted anyway because `finish` takes an arbitrary expression, so the load sits there with bias_ptr left untagged (as conv2d_forward leaves w_ptr). Filed as a separate gap -- it recurs for conv1d/conv3d bias and the norms' affine parameters.

The norms remain the harder case this issue already flagged: their epilogue is a second pass over the row, not an expression over the carry, so `finish` does not reach them.

title: feat: convert the 20 loop-reading kernels to In<Tile<..>> (convs, pools, norms, flash attention)
notes:
## Population (20) -- reads inside the loop

Each loads inside its accumulation loop, so it needs the generated loop and its
loop-indexed operand attributes (teenygrad-y8aa), not a load-once prelude.

  convs    conv1d, conv2d_bias, conv3d, conv2d_bn_silu
  pools    avgpool/maxpool/lppool x 1d/2d/3d  (9)
  norms    layer_norm, rms_norm, instance_norm, group_norm
  batchnorm  batch_norm_stats, batch_norm_normalize
  attention  flash_attention2

conv2d_forward is already done and is the worked example
(teenygrad-1nr.18.4).

## Blocked on teenygrad-3dbg

13 of the 20 have an epilogue between the loop and the store, which
#[tile_loop(generate)] cannot express yet. The pools and convs are the clean
cases; the norms' epilogue is a second pass over the row and may need more than
the hook.

## Three further gaps, all found by conv2d's port

- MULTI-CARRY / MULTI-OUTPUT. generate takes exactly one carry and one
  Out<Tile>. batch_norm_stats has two carries and two outputs; flash attention
  has three carries. Pairing carry to output needs a declaration that does not
  exist.
- NON-ZERO CARRY INIT. Carries initialise to zeros; flash attention's `m_i`
  starts at negative infinity.
- EXTENTS THAT ARE NOT PARAMETER NAMES. `extent = <ident>` cannot express
  `C_IN / G`, which is why conv2d's `w` stays out of its spec. Any kernel whose
  operand extent is an expression hits this.

So flash_attention2 and batch_norm_stats are the two that need more than the
epilogue hook, and are worth sequencing last.

## Done when

All 20 take Tile parameters with their loops generated, and numerics pass. Every
one of them has fixture tests, which is the point: unlike teenygrad-y8aa's
probes, this rung can actually verify the generated addressing computes the right
answer.

## PROGRESS: 5 of 20 (2026-10-05)

  conv2d_bias, avgpool2d      PR #86 (with teenygrad-3dbg's epilogue hook)
  avgpool1d, avgpool3d        PR #88
  maxpool1d                   PR #88

Two more gaps closed on the way, both in PR #88:

  CARRY INIT. `#[tile_carry(.., init = <expr>)]` replaces the hardcoded zeros.
  This was listed above as 'NON-ZERO CARRY INIT' and attributed to flash
  attention's m_i; the three max-pools need it just as much, and it is done.

  A DECLARED READ FILL. The generated per-iteration read hardcoded a zeros
  fill -- the identity for a SUM, wrong for a max. It now reads the operand's
  own `#[tile(.. fill = ..)]`, the same key the prelude's reduced-axis load
  uses.

## Owed test, do not skip it

maxpool1d's `fill = neg_inf` is NOT observable: removing it leaves every test
passing. That is structural -- no padding and no declared `bounds` means the
read's mask equals the output tile's in_bounds, so every masked lane is an
out-of-range OUTPUT lane that the masked store discards.

maxpool2d and maxpool3d DO pad, so they bounds-check input coordinates that
belong to STORED output lanes. There a zeros fill corrupts the answer. Whoever
converts them owes a test with a padded window over all-negative input, which
would fail today if the fill were wrong.

## Remaining 15, in the order they look cheapest

  maxpool2d, maxpool3d    need `bounds` for their padding; owe the fill test
  lppool1/2/3d            need the loop-invariant constants (p_vec, inv_p_vec,
                          eps_vec) somewhere: the author's body IS the loop
                          body, so there is no prologue hook. Inlining per
                          iteration is correct but recomputes -- a prologue hook
                          is the fourth gap of this shape, after finish and init.
  conv1d, conv3d          analogues of conv2d_bias
  conv2d_bn_silu          bn affine then SiLU in finish
  layer/rms/instance/group norm   epilogue is a SECOND PASS over the row, which
                          `finish` does not reach -- still the hard case
  batch_norm_stats        two carries, two outputs
  batch_norm_normalize    -
  flash_attention2        three carries; `init` is now available for its m_i

## STATE 2026-10-05 (end of session): 7 of 20 on trunk

  conv2d_bias, avgpool2d      PR #87 (re-land of #86)
  avgpool1d/3d, maxpool1d     PR #89 (re-land of #88)
  conv1d, conv3d              PR #90

All verified on trunk: workspace 445/11, cuda+hardware 608/10, default 320/10,
riscv 315/12, teeny-compiler 7/0.

### maxpool2d is NOT a copy of maxpool1d -- looked, did not convert

Its loop is shaped differently from every pool converted so far. It pre-clamps
the H range (`ih_lo`), decodes `ih_local = ih_lo + iter / KW` rather than
taking kh as a loop axis, and builds its own `valid_mask` from
`iw_range.ge(0) & iw_range.lt(W)`. So `axes = [kh = KH, kw = KW]` does not
describe it, and converting means either restructuring the decode to the
standard form or teaching the generated decode about a clamped base.

Do this one with the owed fill test in the same change: a padded window over
all-negative input, which would fail today if the read's fill were zeros rather
than neg_inf.

### Design question for the next session, worth answering before more kernels

Three gaps closed so far -- `finish` (3dbg), `init` and the declared read fill
(this rung) -- are all the SAME shape: a value the generated loop hardcoded that
actually belongs to the kernel. lppool needs a fourth (a prologue, for its
loop-invariant p_vec/inv_p_vec/eps_vec) and batch_norm_stats/flash_attention a
fifth (multi-carry, multi-output).

Adding keys one kernel at a time is working but may be the wrong shape. One pass
giving the generated loop a general per-carry 'init / prologue / body / epilogue'
vocabulary would subsume all five. It would churn the four kernels already using
`generate`, so it needs the user's call first -- raised, not decided.

## 9 of 20 -- PR #91 (2026-10-05). The owed fill test found a real bug.

maxpool2d and maxpool3d convert. The owed test is written and it did its job.

### The declared read fill was DEAD CODE

PR #88/#89 added `fill` to the generated per-iteration read. The lookup searched
`prelude_in_params`, which EXCLUDES loop-indexed operands by design -- and a
loop-indexed operand is exactly what that read loads. The lookup always returned
None; the read always fell back to zeros. The feature never did anything.

No landed kernel computed wrong answers: every loop-tile kernel so far wants
zeros (the sum identity) except maxpool1d, whose fill is unobservable. Latent,
not actively wrong -- but shipped as working when it was not.

Found by test_maxpool2d_padded_forward_fills_with_negative_infinity, which
failed first time with gpu=0, expected=-1. Writing down that the test was owed,
rather than treating the previous rung as finished, is what caught it.

### maxpool2d's H window is masked now, not clamped

Its body opened with two `while` loops walking kh past the top edge and kh_hi
back from the bottom, so the trip count was `(kh_hi - kh) * KW` -- a runtime
value differing per oh, divergent across a warp. For a MAXIMUM, clamping and
masking-with-neg_inf are equivalent, so the loop is now the constant KH * KW
with bounds + fill at the edges. Both while loops and the data-dependent trip
count are gone.

Worth noting for the remaining pools: a data-dependent trip count is NOT
expressible by `#[tile_loop(generate)]` at all. maxpool2d only converted
because its clamping could be re-expressed as masking. A kernel whose trip
count genuinely varies per program would need a different answer.

### Remaining 11

  lppool1/2/3d            prologue hook for p_vec/inv_p_vec/eps_vec
  conv2d_bn_silu          bn affine then SiLU in finish
  4 norms                 epilogue is a second pass over the row
  batch_norm_stats        two carries, two outputs
  batch_norm_normalize    -
  flash_attention2        three carries; init now exists for m_i
close_reason: Anduin fusion work discontinued; closed with the Anduin-related issues

title: spec: flash_attention2 needs multi-carry, multi-output and a prologue
description:
Measured 2026-10-06. flash_attention2_forward needs THREE features plus a
signature change -- the largest remaining piece in teenygrad-3dp5, and the one
kernel where forcing the declaration vocabulary may not pay.

## It is not a multi-pass kernel

teenygrad-3rk6.2's #[tile_reduce_pass] does not fit. A pass emits
`carry = carry + (acc_expr)`. Flash attention's loop is an ONLINE softmax:

    let m_new = T::maximum(m_i, qk);
    let exp_diff = T::exp(m_i - m_new);
    let p = T::exp(qk - m_new);
    l_i = exp_diff * l_i + p;        // RESCALE then add
    acc = exp_diff * acc + p * v_vec;
    m_i = m_new;                     // replace

Three interdependent carries, shared per-iteration intermediates, and updates
that rescale rather than accumulate. That is the #[tile_loop(generate)] shape --
the author's body IS the loop body -- not the pass shape.

## What generate is missing for it

1. THREE CARRIES. `generate` enforces exactly one.
2. TWO OUTPUTS WITH DIFFERENT EPILOGUES. `o = acc / l_i` is a [HEAD_DIM] row;
   `l = T::sum(m_i + T::log(l_i), Some(0), false)` is a scalar derived from two
   OTHER carries. `generate` emits one store from one carry.
3. A PROLOGUE. `q_vec` is loaded once before the loop. The author's body is the
   loop body, so there is nowhere for a loop-invariant load to live. lppool1/2/3d
   need exactly this too, for their p_vec/inv_p_vec/eps_vec.

## And a signature change before even route 2

Its grid is (pid_m, pid_bh) over Y, so q/k/v are [BH, n_ctx, HEAD_DIM]. There is
NO `bh` parameter -- the signature has n_ctx_q, n_ctx_k, softmax_scale, neg_inf.
`extent = ..` names a parameter, so the batch-head axis cannot be declared at
all without adding one. Even metadata-only #[tile(..)] tags need that.

Today it carries #[tiled_kernel] purely for dtype dispatch, which
test_tile_declarations.rs records as deliberate.

## Sequencing note

The PROLOGUE is the higher-leverage feature: it unblocks lppool1/2/3d (three
kernels) on its own and is one of flash attention's three needs. Multi-carry and
multi-output are wanted by flash attention alone right now.

## Coverage is already good here

Unlike the norms, test_flash_attention2_forward exists and asserts BOTH outputs
(expected_forward_o.bin and expected_forward_l.bin). So a conversion would be
verifiable from the start -- the first kernel in this epic where that was true
without new test work.
close_reason: Anduin fusion work discontinued; closed with the Anduin-related issues

title: feat(anduin): model reduction loops (P6 rsteps, conv2d's tile_loop) so group footprints are not over-estimated
description:
## Problem
The scheduler over-estimates the per-unit footprint (peak level-1 / shared-memory bytes) of any group containing a reduction or a looping kernel. That makes it reject or mis-rank tilings that the real kernel runs in a small working set. In the conv-block experiment (teenygrad-1l7i), the fused conv/bn/silu group's footprint was 90112 B for only 2 units. The hand-fused `Conv2dBnSiluForward` holds one `[BLOCK_OW]` accumulator plus one input row chunk per iteration.

Causes, in the order they inflate the number:

1. **No rsteps (ANALYSIS.md §12.2 P6).** `initial_rsteps` and `expand_rsteps` (anduin/schedule/tiling.rs ~123-135) are no-ops: `BTreeMap::new()` and an empty body. Every reduce dim therefore propagates as `DimSpan::Full`, and `lens_fp` charges the whole reduced extent as resident at once. For conv2d that is the whole `C_IN x H x W` input per unit. For softmax's max/sum, the whole row. A16's "Fallbacks while P6 and P8 are unmet" documents this as conservative, which it is, but it is also wrong by orders of magnitude for conv.
2. **The scheduler ignores the kernel's own loop metadata.** conv2d already declares its reduction loop via `#[tile_loop(trip_count = [C_IN, G, KH, KW], axes = [c_in_local = (C_IN / G), kh = KH, kw = KW], generate)]`, `#[tile_carry(acc = [BLOCK_OW])]` and `#[tile_loop_tile(..)]` on `x` (nn/conv/conv2d.rs ~57-115). It surfaces as `KernelTileSpec::loop_spec: Option<TileLoopSpec>` (core/teeny-core/src/model/tile_spec.rs ~279). Nothing under anduin/ reads `loop_spec`; the only mentions are two test fixtures setting it to `None`. `TileLoopSpec::trip_count_factors` is documented as "documentation only... no consumer computes the actual trip count".
3. **conv2d's output binds only OW (P4 for conv2d itself).** `y` is `#[tile(name="B", extent=_B)] #[tile(extent=C_OUT)] #[tile(extent=OH)] #[tile(block=BLOCK_OW, extent=OW)]`. B, C_OUT and OH are grid-decoded but unbound, so they are `Full`, and a conv-anchored unit spans every (b, c_out, oh). This is the same defect teenygrad-yf8f fixes for BatchNorm2d.
4. **conv2d's weight is not in the spec (P5).** `w` carries `#[tile_loop_scalar(..)]` but no `#[tile(..)]`, because its second extent `C_IN / G` cannot be named by `extent = <ident>`. Its reads are missing from traffic and footprint. That is an under-estimate, but it skews the same comparison.

## Requirements
1. **P6 metadata in teeny-core.** Give a reduction binding (or a `TileLoopSpec` axis) what A12 needs: the reduce-extent name whose `extent_param` does not occur in the output, and the allowed chunk values (a searchable rstep const, or "factors of the extent"). Decide whether this extends `TensorTileSpec`/`TileAxisBinding` (as ANALYSIS.md §12.3 proposes) or is read from `loop_spec`. Prefer reusing `loop_spec` where a kernel already loops, since it is derived from the body's actual loop. Either way, derive it in `#[tiled_kernel]`; never hand-author it (tile-dsl-guide gotcha #2).
2. **Distinguish "walks inside the unit" from "reads whole".** A kernel that loops over its reduction (conv2d: `c_in_local`, `kh`, `kw`) holds one iteration's chunk resident, i.e. `DimSpan::Chunk`. A single-block reduction (the `Reduce*` kernels with `BLOCK_INNER` >= row, `reduce_block` in graph/mod.rs) really does hold the whole row, so `Full` is correct there. The metadata must say which one it is; footprint must not shrink for a kernel that does not actually chunk.
3. **Implement `initial_rsteps` and `expand_rsteps`** per ANALYSIS.md §12.4 (Welder `_assign_reduce_step` / `_expand_reduce_axis`): candidates `factors(E_k)` (or powers of two below `E_k` when factors give only two and `E_k > 64`), greedy start by coalescing similarity, then expansion under `min(capacity_per_cu / units_per_cu, capacity_per_owner)`. Fill `GroupSchedule.rstep`, `op_trips` (operands re-read once per chunk) and `trips`, so traffic stays correct as the footprint shrinks.
4. **Bind conv2d's B, C_OUT and OH** with block literal 1 (gotcha #4), matching its pid decode `(b, c_out, oh, ow_tile)`. Check that the derived grid spec, generated prelude and snapshots are unchanged in all four configs.
5. **Bring conv2d's weight into the spec**, either by letting `extent` name an expression or derived param (`C_IN / G`), or with another derived form. Its region is one `(c_out)` slice per unit, walked over `(c_in_local, kh, kw)`.
6. **Tests (anduin/schedule):**
   - A singleton conv2d (2x3x32x32 -> 8 channels, 3x3, s1, p1) tiles with a footprint of O(BLOCK_OW·(chunk) + halo) bytes, not O(C_IN·H·W). Assert a concrete upper bound computed from the kernel's real per-iteration working set.
   - Matmul-style: an `rk` rstep gives `op_trips[A] = op_trips[B] = ceil(K/rk)` and `trips = 1` (ANALYSIS.md §12.4 example).
   - A single-block reduce keeps `Full` and its footprint is unchanged (requirement 2).
   - D1 softmax still schedules as one group and its existing traffic assertions still hold.
   - Extend `test_conv2d_batchnorm_silu_schedules_as_one_tiled_kernel` (teenygrad-1l7i) to bound the fused group's footprint.
7. Update ANALYSIS.md: §12.2's preconditions status (P6), A16's fallbacks paragraph, and the "no consumer computes the trip count" note on `TileLoopSpec`.

## Acceptance
A conv-anchored tiling's footprint is within a small constant of the real kernel's working set. Single-block reductions are unchanged. No regressions in `./scripts/test.sh --workspace --no-fail-fast` (known failures: the 5 Anduin `todo!` tests and teeny-triton `test_tile_layout_boundary_type_param_conv2d`).

## Related
teenygrad-1l7i (umbrella; this is a quality blocker for it), teenygrad-yf8f (the same P4 fix for BatchNorm2d), teenygrad-a19a (P3: needed so the windowed H/W axes are Tiled with a halo rather than Full, which is the other half of conv's footprint).
close_reason: P4 in 758a97e2e, P6 in 737c64764; conv weight (P5, requirement 5) split to teenygrad-27hr

title: RISC-V asm snapshots hold raw ELF bytes of the old placeholder .so; switch to --emit=asm and re-record
description:
Found 2026-09-11 running the RISC-V suite one test binary at a time against teenyc from teeny feat/triton-riscv-rvv @ 9f48d7207fa: TEENYC_PATH=<teeny>/build/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/stage1/bin/teenyc INSTA_FORCE_PASS=1 cargo test -p teeny-kernels --no-default-features --features riscv,training --test <name> -- --test-threads=1. Overall: 69 binaries, 63 passed; 245 tests passed, 15 failed.

All 228 *_asm_riscv.snap files in kernels/teeny-kernels/tests/snapshots were recorded from teeny's old placeholder RiscvBackend: each is the linked ELF shared object stored as a Debug string (it contains only the stub riscv_kernel symbol and a LLD 22.1.6 comment), not assembly. With real lowering almost every RISC-V asm snapshot changes; the run above left 212 pending .snap.new files (not accepted, INSTA_FORCE_PASS=1). Because the output is binary, the new snapshots cannot be reviewed meaningfully either.

teeny now honours --emit=asm for the MLIR backend (teeny commit dee040602a5): with it, teenyc writes RiscvBackend's assembly text to the requested output instead of the .so.

Proposed: have the RISC-V snapshot path (teeny_runtime::compile_kernel / read_compiled_asm for the riscv backend) compile with --emit=asm, or disassemble the .so, so snapshots show RVV assembly; then delete the pending .snap.new files, re-record and review. Consider doing this after the tensordesc and acos/asin/atan fixes so their snapshots are recorded once.
close_reason: Both halves are done. (1) The --emit=asm switch landed: read_compiled_asm now reads the cached .s for RISC-V, so the snapshots hold readable RVV assembly rather than the placeholder .so's ELF bytes -- verified on this branch, e.g. test_avgpool1d__avgpool1d_forward_asm_riscv now opens with .attribute/.file/.text/.globl and real mnemonics, no ELF magic. That was commit 6ee517f56, shipped via #40 (e19795dbf). (2) Re-recording is done for everything that can be reviewed: PR #49 accepted 284 of 430 pending snapshots, gated on the kernel's own numeric test passing on the target the snapshot records -- CUDA numerics for *_asm_cuda, QEMU numerics for *_asm_riscv. This issue's own advice was to re-record after the tensordesc and acos/asin/atan fixes so it happens once; that is exactly why 144 snapshots are still held: 20 binaries fail RISC-V numerics (teenygrad-1gw softmax NaN, teenygrad-15k libdevice, teenygrad-203 libm) and 5 fail on CUDA (teenygrad-5sk tensordesc ICE, plus the trig mov-mismatch recorded on teenygrad-dd1). Those get recorded when their underlying bug is fixed, tracked there rather than here.
