RISC-V *_asm_riscv snapshots now regenerate as RVV assembly (e.g. test_relu: 2351 lines, 2034 instructions). test_compile_riscv still gets an ELF .so. Full run then regenerated pending snapshots for both backends (not accepted); re-recording is still to do, ideally after teenygrad-5sk and teenygrad-15k.

title: spec: reverse shape inference — Op::infer_input_shape for Graph nodes
description:
## Status: parked, 2026-09-22

`.1` is merged. `.2` is written and tested but **parked unmerged** on the branch
`feature/infer-input-shapes` (renamed from `feature/3fy.2-conv-pool-spatial-dims`,
commit `f261abe48`); PR #42 was closed by that rename and carries the same explanation.
`.3`, `.4` and `.5` are not started.

Parked because reverse inference is not needed for anduin, and — more importantly — it
is the wrong tool for the tile propagation it was expected to feed:

- `Op::infer_input_shape` has no callers outside `teeny-core/src/graph/`, and
  `kernels/teeny-kernels/src/graph/optimizer/anduin/` uses neither it nor the window
  helpers.
- Welder (Shi et al., OSDI '23, §3.1) propagates a tile shape by analysing the
  *dependent region* from the tensor expression — receptive field,
  `(block - 1) * stride + kernel` — and demands a **conservative upper bound** wherever
  a region cannot be described exactly. This epic inverts whole-tensor extents and
  returns the *smallest* consistent input, which errs in the opposite direction and
  would under-size buffers that are checked against a hard capacity. Tile propagation
  lives in `teenygrad-1nr.30`, which now sources that requirement from the paper.

What it is still good for, and why the branch is kept rather than deleted: whole-tensor
questions. Sizing a model to a required output (composing the reverse through a conv/
pool backbone — e.g. a ResNet-50 spatial chain reverses from 7x7 to 193, the smallest of
the 32 inputs in `193..224` that produce it), concretising dynamic `None` dims so a graph
is static enough to schedule, and validating a graph against a required output.

**What stays in `feature/anduin-v2` regardless of this parking**, because PR #41 merged
it and it is not separable without a large revert:

- `Layer::call`, `Op::infer_output_shape` and `window_out_dim` are all fallible now,
  along with the 43 `nn` stubs, `sequential!`, teeny-vision and its example.
- `CustomOp::infer_input_shape` is a **required** trait method, so an out-of-tree custom
  op (vision-rs) must implement it whether or not this epic resumes.

## Goal

A reverse counterpart to `infer_output_shape` — given a node's output shape, recover
what it implies about its inputs — reporting per *dimension* what is known, bounded, or
lost, rather than per op.

```rust
impl Op {
    pub fn infer_input_shape(&self, output: &Shape) -> Result<Option<Vec<Shape>>>;
}
```

Separate from the Anduin tile work (`teenygrad-1nr.*`): that needs *tile* propagation,
which is receptive-field arithmetic and never inverts anything. This is whole-tensor
inference, useful for re-targeting a traced model to a new input size and for
validating a graph against a required output.

## Why per-dimension

Classifying whole ops as invertible/not is too coarse. Of **243** `Op` variants, **174**
are shape-preserving, so the inverse is the identity. Of the remaining **69**, most lose
exactly *one* dimension and keep their rank:

| op | recoverable | lost |
|---|---|---|
| `GlobalAvgPool`/`GlobalMaxPool` | N, C, and rank | trailing spatial dims |
| `MatMul`/`QLinearMatMul` | batch dims + M | K only |
| `Gemm{trans_a,trans_b}` | M (transpose-aware) | K only |
| `ArgMax`/`ArgMin{axis,keepdims}` | every dim but `axis`; rank | `axis` only |
| `Concat{axis}` | every dim but `axis`; rank | per-input `axis` extent (sums to output) |
| `Split{axis,num_outputs}` | rank, and the axis up to a fan-in | the remainder of an uneven split |
| `TopK` | everything | nothing (forward is `input.clone()`) |
| `Reduce*` with `keepdims: true` | everything | nothing (forward is `input.clone()`) |

The genuine total-loss set is only four shapes: `Flatten`, `Reshape`, `Reduce*` with
`keepdims: false`, and `Custom`.

## The representation already exists

`Shape = Vec<Option<usize>>`, and `infer_output_shape` already uses `None` as "unknown
dim" throughout — `unwrap_or(None)` in the `MatMul` and `Gemm` arms,
`try_fold(..).map(Some).unwrap_or(None)` in `Concat` and `Flatten`. A reverse pass
emitting `None` for a lost dim is the established idiom, not a new concept. The outer
`Option` is only needed for the four total-loss shapes.

## Decisions taken while building

These supersede the original sketch above where they differ.

- **An associated function, not a free one.** `Op::infer_input_shape(&self, output)`,
  mirroring `Op::infer_output_shape`. Singular: it returns the shapes of one node's
  inputs. Both are `pub` on `Op`, and the op set now lives in
  `core/teeny-core/src/graph/op.rs`, not `graph/mod.rs`.
- **Fallible.** `Result<Option<Vec<Shape>>>` separates three outcomes: `Err` when the
  output could not have been produced by this op at all, `Ok(None)` when the op has no
  inverse, and `Ok(Some(shapes))` otherwise. `infer_output_shape` became fallible at the
  same time — a window that cannot fit its padded input is an error, not a panic.
- **Ambiguity resolves to the smallest exact fit.** Where floor division gives a fan-in
  (conv, pool, `Split`), the reverse returns the smallest input producing that output —
  the one that divides evenly, with no remainder for the forward pass to drop. Stated on
  the method as a convention rather than an inverse. For `stride == 1` it *is* the exact
  inverse.
- **The `CustomOp` reverse hook shipped in `.1`, not `.4`.** `CustomOp::infer_input_shape`
  is a **required** trait method with no default, so an out-of-tree op must implement it
  deliberately; `Op::Custom` delegates to it. `CustomOp::infer_output_shape` became
  fallible to match.
- **Unimplemented variants panic** with `unimplemented!` naming the variant, rather than
  returning `Ok(None)`. `None` means "no inverse exists" and must not be overloaded with
  "not written yet".

## Known blocker: multi-input arity

`infer_input_shape` returns one shape *per input*, but an `Op` variant does not record
how many inputs its node has. `Add`, `Concat`, `MatMul` and the like therefore cannot
report a correct-length result from the output shape alone, however much is known about
the individual dimensions. This is a gap in the IR, not in the arithmetic.

The convolutions escape it only because a node records just the data input — the kernel
and bias come from the variant, not from sibling edges.

Resolving this gates `.3` and much of `.5`. Carried in `teenygrad-3fy.5`.

## Sub-issues, simplest first

1. `.1` identity and exact-from-config ops — **closed**, PR #41
2. `.2` floor-ambiguous conv/pool spatial dims, plus `Split` — PR #42
3. `.3` partially-determined ops (one dim to `None`) — needs the arity question settled
4. `.4` total-loss ops: `Flatten`, `Reshape`, `Reduce*` with `keepdims: false`
5. `.5` exact-from-config remainder, and the multi-input arity question

All against `core/teeny-core/src/graph/op.rs`.
close_reason: Not doing. Reverse shape inference is not needed for anduin, and is the wrong tool for the tile propagation it was expected to feed: Welder propagates a dependent region and requires a conservative upper bound, while this returns the smallest consistent input extent. PR #43 removed the shipped parts from feature/anduin-v2; the code is preserved on feature/infer-input-shapes. Kept closed rather than deleted because the analysis (the 243-variant classification, the per-dimension recoverability table, the multi-input arity gap) explains the decision and is cited by teenygrad-1nr.30.

title: feat: reverse inference for identity and exact-from-config ops
description:
## Scope

The easy two-thirds of reverse inference. Establishes the signature, module layout and
test harness that `teenygrad-3fy.2/.3/.4` extend.

### Identity (174 of 243 `Op` variants)

Every arm of `infer_output_shape` (`core/teeny-core/src/graph/mod.rs:1656`) returning
`input.clone()` / `input.to_vec()` — all activations, `BatchNorm*`, `LayerNorm`,
`RmsNorm`, `GroupNorm`, `InstanceNorm*`, `Add`, `Mul`, `Attention`, `ChannelBiasAdd`,
`Softmax`, `Unique`, `OneHot`. Reverse is the identity.

Also exactly identity despite not being literal `input.clone()` arms: `TopK` (forward
already returns the input shape as an approximation) and `Reduce*` with
`keepdims: true`.

### Exact from op config

- `Linear { in_features, .. }` — last dim to `in_features`.
- `ChannelChunk { c_total, .. }` — carries `c_total` alongside `chunk_c`, so the input
  channel count is exact.
- `Transpose { perm }` — inverse permutation; also the `perm.is_empty()` reverse case.
- `UpsampleNearest2d { scale_h, scale_w }` — divide; always exact, since forward
  multiplied.
- The 12 pad variants (`Constant`/`Reflection`/`Replication`/`Circular` x 1d/2d/3d) —
  subtract the pads.
- `Conv1d/2d/3d { in_channels }` — **channel dim only**. Spatial dims are emitted as
  `None` here and filled by `teenygrad-3fy.2`, so this issue can land conv partially
  without waiting.
- `SpaceToDepth { blocksize }` — **channel dim only** (`c_out / blocksize^2`, exact).
- `ConvTranspose` — see the divisibility caveat in Design.

## Corrections to the original scope (2026-09-19)

Three ops filed here belong elsewhere; established by reading the forward arms.

| op | why | moves to |
|---|---|---|
| `SpaceToDepth`/`DepthToSpace` spatial dims | forward integer-divides (`h / blocksize`), same floor fan-in as conv | `teenygrad-3fy.2` |
| `DepthToSpace` channel dim | forward is `c / blocksize^2` — also floor | `teenygrad-3fy.2` |
| `ChannelCat { c_total }` | multi-input; per-input channel counts individually unknown, only their sum is known | `teenygrad-3fy.3` |

`ConvTranspose` stays here, but its forward is injective-**not**-surjective (linear in
`h`, no floor), so the reverse is exact only when it divides evenly — see Design.

## Related bug found while scoping (not fixed here)

`Op::ConvTranspose`'s forward arm underflows `usize`, and the `window_out_dim` guard
added in `225a808ea` does **not** cover it:

```rust
(h - 1) * stride_h - 2 * padding_h + kernel_h + output_padding_h
```

Rust evaluates left-to-right, so the subtraction lands before `+ kernel_h`. For
`h=2, s=1, p=2, k=5` that is `1 - 4` -> underflow, though the true result is `2`.
Reachable: `support/teeny-onnx/src/onnx.rs:378` constructs this op from ONNX import.
Should be its own bug issue.
design:
# Implementation plan

## Step 0 — signature and placement

**Arity is a property of the node, not the op.** `SymTensor::record`
(`core/teeny-core/src/graph/mod.rs:2412`) is unary — it passes `vec![self.node_id]` —
and `infer_output_shape` already takes `inputs: &[&Shape]`. `Op::Add`/`Op::Mul` never
appear in a `teeny-core` recording path at all; they arrive from ONNX import. So the
reverse cannot derive its own arity and must be told:

```rust
// core/teeny-core/src/graph/reverse.rs  (new, sibling of graph/compiler.rs)
pub fn infer_input_shapes(op: &Op, output: &Shape, arity: usize) -> Option<Vec<Shape>>;

impl Graph {
    /// Arity read from `self.nodes[node].inputs.len()`.
    pub fn infer_input_shapes(&self, node: usize) -> Option<Vec<Shape>>;
}
```

New module rather than growing `graph/mod.rs` — the inference region there is already
~2400 lines in a 105 KB file. Requires bumping `infer_output_shape` to `pub(super)`
for the round-trip tests.

Contract: outer `None` = "no inverse exists for this op". `Some` with `None` dims =
"partially determined". This is already the file's idiom — the forward pass uses
`None` for unknown dims throughout (`unwrap_or(None)` in the `MatMul`/`Gemm` arms,
`try_fold(..).map(Some).unwrap_or(None)` in `Concat`/`Flatten`).

## Step 1 — identity, and the one structural decision

The 174 shape-preserving variants **must not be retyped**. Extract the existing arm's
op list into a macro consumed by *both* directions so they cannot drift:

```rust
macro_rules! shape_preserving_ops {
    () => { Op::Relu | Op::Elu { .. } | Op::Selu | /* ... */ | Op::InstanceNorm3d { .. } };
}
```

This is the highest-value choice in the issue. It also means this issue **edits
`infer_output_shape`**, a slightly wider blast radius than "add a new function" — a
deliberate inclusion, flagged as open decision 3 below.

Multi-input shape-preserving ops (`Add`, `Mul`, `Attention`, `ChannelBiasAdd`) return
`vec![output.clone(); arity]`.

**Exhaustiveness: no `_ => None` catch-all.** List the ~45 not-yet-covered variants
explicitly in a `None` arm. With 243 variants, a catch-all means a newly added op
silently returns `None` forever; an exhaustive match fails the build and forces a
decision. The "uncovered ops return `None`" requirement holds either way — this makes
it deliberate rather than accidental.

## Step 2 — exact-from-config

`Linear`, `ChannelChunk`, `Transpose`, `UpsampleNearest2d`, the 12 pads, plus the
channel dim of `Conv1d/2d/3d` and `SpaceToDepth`. No arithmetic risk beyond the pad
subtraction (guard it the way `window_out_dim` guards its own).

## Step 3 — `ConvTranspose`

```
h = (h_out + 2*pad - kernel - output_padding) / stride + 1
```

`Some` iff it divides evenly, `None` for that dim otherwise. Guard the subtraction.

## Step 4 — tests

Table-driven, in the new module:

- **Round-trip:** `infer_input_shapes(op, &infer_output_shape(op, &[&input]), 1)
  == Some(vec![input])`, over a spread of input shapes per covered op. Use ~10
  representatives for the identity families rather than all 174 — the shared macro is
  what covers the rest.
- **Dynamic dims:** a `None` in the output round-trips to `None`, never a panic (e.g.
  `Linear` on `[None, 128]`).
- **Uncovered:** every op in the `None` arm returns `None`.
- **`ConvTranspose`:** one divisible case (`Some`) and one non-divisible (`None` for
  that dim).

## Open decisions

1. **Broadcasting.** `Op::Add => input.clone()` assumes none, and
   `vec![output; arity]` inherits that assumption. Fine today, but both directions have
   to change together if broadcasting is ever modelled. Wants a comment saying so.
2. **`Transpose` with an out-of-range `perm`.** Forward silently yields `None` via
   `unwrap_or(None)`; the reverse cannot distinguish that from a genuine dynamic dim.
   Reject the perm, or mirror the silence?
3. **Does the `shape_preserving_ops!` refactor belong in this issue** or in a separate
   prep issue, given it modifies the forward path?
acceptance_criteria:
- Round-trip holds for every covered op:
  `infer_input_shapes(op, &infer_output_shape(op, &[&input]), 1) == Some(vec![input])`.
- Conv ops return the channel dim exactly and `None` for spatial dims (filled later by
  `teenygrad-3fy.2`), rather than returning outer `None`.
- `ConvTranspose` returns `Some` for divisible configurations and `None` for that dim
  otherwise; no `usize` underflow on any input.
- A `None` (dynamic) dim in the output round-trips to `None` without panicking.
- Ops not yet covered return outer `None`, never a fabricated shape, so
  `teenygrad-3fy.2/.3/.4` are purely additive.
- The match over `Op` is exhaustive with no `_` catch-all: adding a new `Op` variant
  fails to compile until a reverse arm is chosen for it.
- Forward and reverse share one `shape_preserving_ops!` list; no op name is written
  twice.
notes: Superseded by PR #43: the code this delivered was removed from feature/anduin-v2 and now exists only on the parked branch feature/infer-input-shapes. Left closed rather than reopened - the work was done, the decision to drop it is recorded on teenygrad-3fy.
close_reason: done

comments.author: Arshad Mahmood
comments.text:
Landed on feature/3fy-infer-input-shapes (46b90f71f, d4af7e084, f4effd25e).

Delivered: the signature, module layout and test harness this issue was meant to establish, plus every identity arm that can be done from an output shape alone — the 31 activations/norms, the 38 single-input unary element-wise math ops, Op::Input, and Op::Custom delegating to CustomOp::infer_input_shape.

Signature differs from the epic: it is a method, Op::infer_input_shape(&self, output: &Shape) -> Result<Option<Vec<Shape>>>, matching the forward pass which is also now a method and fallible. The CustomOp reverse hook, which the epic assigned to 3fy.4, landed here too.

Not delivered, split into teenygrad-3fy.5: the whole exact-from-config half (Linear, ChannelChunk, Transpose, UpsampleNearest2d, the 12 pads, conv channel dims, SpaceToDepth channel dim, ConvTranspose), and the multi-input identity arms — blocked because an Op variant does not record its node's input count, so a one-shape-per-input result cannot be the right length.

title: feat: reverse inference for floor-ambiguous conv/pool spatial dims
description:
## Problem

Conv and pool spatial dims go through floor division, so the inverse is a *set*, not a
value:

```
out = floor((in + 2p - k) / s) + 1
```

The fan-in is exactly `s`. Verified by exhaustive enumeration:

| k, s, p | inputs producing `out = 8` |
|---|---|
| 3, 1, 1 | `[8]` |
| 3, 2, 1 | `[15, 16]` |
| 3, 3, 0 | `[24, 25, 26]` |
| 5, 4, 1 | `[31, 32, 33, 34]` |

## Closed forms

Both checked exhaustively for `out` in `1..200`:

- `s == 1` — unique: `in = out + k - 2p - 1`
- `s > 1` — smallest input producing `out`: `in = s * (out - 1) + k - 2p`

## Scope

Cover the spatial dims of `Conv1d/2d/3d` and all nine pooling variants
(`AvgPool`/`MaxPool`/`LpPool` x 1d/2d/3d), plus `Split { num_outputs }`, which has the
same floor fan-in (`out[ax] * num_outputs` recovers the input only when it divided
evenly).

Design point to settle: what to return when `s > 1`.

- **smallest exact fit** (`s*(out-1) + k - 2p`) — one concrete answer, matches the
  "the model was probably sized to fit" assumption, and is what a re-targeting caller
  wants;
- **`None`** for that dim — honest but discards information the caller usually has
  enough context to use;
- a range/bounds type — most faithful, but a new type in a `Shape` that has no room
  for one.

Recommend smallest-exact-fit, documented as a convention, with `s == 1` noted as
genuinely unique.

Note `window_out_dim` (added in `225a808ea`,
`core/teeny-core/src/graph/mod.rs:1656`) is now the single forward implementation for
all of these, so the reverse belongs beside it and inherits the same `op`/`axis`
naming for its messages.

## Acceptance

- For `s == 1`, round-trip is exact for every covered op.
- For `s > 1`, the returned input re-runs forward to the original output.
- The guard cases `window_out_dim` rejects (kernel wider than padded input, zero
  stride) are unreachable in reverse and must not panic.

Blocked on sub-issue 1.
notes: Superseded by PR #43, same as teenygrad-3fy.1: the code exists only on feature/infer-input-shapes (commit f261abe48). PR #42 was closed, not merged.
close_reason: Implemented in PR #42: reverse inference for the three convolutions, the nine pooling variants and Split, taking the smallest exact fit where floor division gives a fan-in. Both directions now share one window_shape core.

title: feat: reverse inference for partially-determined ops (one dim to None)
description:
## Scope

Ops where rank survives and exactly one dimension is unrecoverable. Each returns a
`Shape` with `None` in that slot and concrete values elsewhere — the same convention
`infer_output_shape` already uses via `unwrap_or(None)`.

| op | output | reverse |
|---|---|---|
| `MatMul`/`MatMulInteger`/`QLinearMatMul` | `[.., M, N]` | A = `[.., M, None]`, B = `[.., None, N]` |
| `Gemm { trans_a, trans_b }` | `[M, N]` | transpose-aware, K to `None` |
| `ArgMax`/`ArgMin { axis, keepdims }` | axis reduced or removed | re-insert `None` at `axis` |
| `Concat { axis }` | summed along `axis` | every other dim exact; `axis` to `None` per input |
| `GlobalAvgPool`/`GlobalMaxPool` | `[N, C, 1, 1]` | `[N, C, None, None]` |

Two things make this more than mechanical:

- **Arity.** These are the first multi-input ops in the reverse direction, so
  `infer_input_shapes` must return one `Shape` per input, and the caller has to know
  which is which. `Concat` is variadic — its input count is not recoverable from the
  output at all, so the signature needs the arity passed in or taken from the
  `GraphNode`.
- **Constraints, not just values.** `Concat`'s per-input `axis` extents are individually
  unknown but must sum to the output's. Worth deciding whether this API drops that
  (simplest), or returns it so a caller re-solving a whole graph can use it.

## Acceptance

- Every covered op returns the right arity with `None` in exactly the lost slot.
- Rank is always preserved.
- Re-running forward on a reverse result where the caller has filled the `None`s
  reproduces the original output.

Blocked on sub-issue 1.
close_reason: Not doing: reverse shape inference is not needed for anduin, and is the wrong tool for tile propagation (Welder needs a dependent region with a conservative upper bound, not an inverted extent). Never started. See the parked note on teenygrad-3fy.

title: feat: total-loss ops (Flatten, Reshape, keepdims-false reductions)
description:
## Scope

The three shapes where the output genuinely determines nothing useful.

| op | why |
|---|---|
| `Flatten` | `[N, C*H*W]` — N survives, the rest cannot be factored, and the input rank is unknown |
| `Reshape` | arbitrary; the target shape is the op's input, not something the output implies |
| `Reduce*` with `keepdims: false` | the arm collapses to `vec![Some(1)]` and the `Op` variant carries **no `axes` field**, so even the rank is gone |

`Custom` was originally the fourth. It is **done**: `CustomOp::infer_input_shape` shipped
in `.1` as a *required* trait method with no default, so an out-of-tree op has to
implement it rather than silently inheriting `None`, and `Op::Custom` delegates to it.

## Work

- Return `Ok(None)` for the three, documented per-op with *why*, so callers can
  distinguish "no inverse exists" from "not implemented yet". Today they fall into the
  `unimplemented!` catch-all in `Op::infer_input_shape`, which is the correct holding
  position — `None` must not be overloaded to mean "not written yet".
- Consider whether `Reduce*` should gain an `axes` field. The forward arm already
  admits it is guessing — *"Without axis info at static-inference time, approximate:
  keepdims=true -> same rank, keepdims=false -> reduce all -> scalar"* — so this is a
  pre-existing gap in the **forward** direction that reverse inference merely exposes.
  That is arguably its own issue; flag it rather than fixing it here.

## Acceptance

- Each of the three returns `Ok(None)`, never a fabricated shape.
- The doc comment on `Op::infer_input_shape` states the contract: `Ok(None)` means "no
  inverse exists", `Ok(Some)` with `None` dims means "partially determined", `Err` means
  "this output could not have been produced by this op".

All against `core/teeny-core/src/graph/op.rs`.

Blocked on sub-issues 1, 2 and 3.
close_reason: Not doing: same reason as teenygrad-3fy.3. Never started. The CustomOp reverse hook this once owned was removed from anduin-v2 by PR #43.

title: feat: reverse inference for exact-from-config ops, and the multi-input arity question
description:
## Scope

Split out of `teenygrad-3fy.1`, which landed the signature, module layout, test
harness and the identity arms. What remains is the "exact from op config" half,
plus the identity arms that could not be done because they are multi-input.

## Exact from op config (none done)

- `Linear { in_features, .. }` — last dim to `in_features`.
- `ChannelChunk { c_total, .. }` — exact input channel count.
- `Transpose { perm }` — inverse permutation, plus the `perm.is_empty()` case.
- `UpsampleNearest2d { scale_h, scale_w }` — divide; exact, forward multiplied.
- The 12 pad variants (`Constant`/`Reflection`/`Replication`/`Circular` x 1d/2d/3d)
  — subtract the pads.
- `Conv1d/2d/3d { in_channels }` — channel dim only; spatial dims emit `None`
  and are filled by `teenygrad-3fy.2`.
- `SpaceToDepth { blocksize }` — channel dim only (`c_out / blocksize^2`).
- `ConvTranspose` — exact only when the stride divides evenly; see the
  divisibility caveat in `teenygrad-3fy`.

## The multi-input blocker

`Op::infer_input_shape` returns one shape per input, but an `Op` variant does
not record how many inputs its node has. From the output shape alone there is
no way to return a correct-length result for a multi-input op, so these were
left `unimplemented!` even though their forward arm is `input.clone()`:

- `Add`, `Attention`, `ChannelBiasAdd`
- the 25 binary/variadic element-wise ops (`Mul`, `Sub`, `Div`, `Pow`, `Mod`,
  `ElemMin/Max/Mean/Sum`, the comparisons, `And`/`Or`/`Xor`)
- ops the forward groups under "unary" that are not: `PRelu`, `Clip`,
  `Dropout`, `ReverseSequence`, `Trilu`, `CumSum`, `CumProd`,
  `QuantizeLinear`, `DequantizeLinear`, `RotaryEmbedding`,
  `MultiHeadAttention`, `FlexAttention`, `LinearAttention`,
  `CausalConvWithState`, `OneHot`
- `Pad`, which the forward treats as identity but which changes shape

Resolving this needs an arity source — either passing the node's input count
in, or an `Op::arity()`. Worth deciding before `teenygrad-3fy.3`, which hits
the same wall with `Concat`.

## Not identity despite an identity forward arm

The 21 "structural" ops (`Reshape`, `Squeeze`, `Unsqueeze`, `Slice`, `Gather`,
`Tile`, …), the 6 `Einsum`/`Det`/`Col2Im`/`ConvInteger`/`DeformConv`/
`QLinearConv` group, the 26 sequence/loop ops, `Unique`, and the 5
`Stft`/window ops all return `input.clone()` forward only as an approximation
when the real shape is not statically known. Their reverse is not the
identity; `Reshape` in particular is total-loss and belongs to
`teenygrad-3fy.4`.

## Done when

Every op in "exact from op config" reverses exactly, and the arity question
above has an answer.
close_reason: Not doing: same reason as teenygrad-3fy.3. Never started. The multi-input arity finding it carried is preserved in the parked note on teenygrad-3fy, since it is a real gap in the IR regardless of this epic.

title: feat(anduin): charge parameters many units share once per kernel, not once per unit
description:
## Problem
The traffic model has no cache. Every unit's operand read is charged in full from device memory, and each contiguous run is inflated to a whole read transaction (128 B).

For the conv block (teenygrad-1l7i), each unit reads one channel of BatchNorm2d's four [C] parameters. That is 4 B each, charged as 128 B: 262,144 B of the 983,040 B total (27%). The real reads are shared by the 64 units on the same channel and served from L1/L2. conv2d's weight slice (27 floats, read by the 64 units of its output channel) is over-charged in the same way.

This skews the ranking against any tiling or fusion that reads small, broadcast parameters per unit, which describes most normalization and bias epilogues.

## Requirements
- A reuse or cache term in A10's traffic. One simple form: when an operand's region doesn't depend on some grid axes (it is broadcast over them), charge its distinct bytes once per kernel, or once per wave, rather than once per unit. A fuller form: an L2 level in the hierarchy with a capacity and hit model.
- Keep it conservative where reuse isn't assured, e.g. when the operand is larger than L2.
- Tests: the conv block's BN-parameter traffic falls to roughly its tensor size (4 x 8 x 4 B, plus transaction rounding). D1 softmax and the existing traffic assertions still hold, or are updated with a reason.

## Related
teenygrad-1l7i, ANALYSIS.md §12 A10
close_reason: Anduin fusion work discontinued; closed with the Anduin-related issues

title: Tensor-core (TF32) implicit-GEMM conv kernel for KxK convolutions
description:
## Problem

conv2d_bn_silu_tiled_forward (kernels/teeny-kernels/src/nn/fused/conv2d_bn_silu_tiled.rs)
is the dominant kernel in YOLO26n inference -- 49.7% of total GPU time on an RTX 5070
(Nsight Compute, batch=1, 640x640) -- and uses plain FP32 CUDA-core FMA via an
outer-product accumulation scheme (acc += w_row[:, None] * x_col[None, :]), not tensor
cores.

Profiling ONNX Runtime's CUDA execution provider running the same model (nsys, kernel
name breakdown) shows cuDNN dispatching TF32 tensor-core kernels for the equivalent
convolutions (cutlass_tensorop_s1688fprop_optimized_tf32_..., sm80_xmma_fprop_implicit_gemm_...,
multiple cutlass_80_tensorop_s1688gemm_* tile-size variants auto-selected per shape).
This is the best-evidenced explanation for vision-rs's own YOLO26n bench being ~3x
slower end-to-end than ONNX Runtime (9.1ms vs 3.0ms/image) on the same hardware --
see conversation history / benchmark reports for the full profiling trail (Nsight
Compute occupancy analysis, coalescing/bank-conflict check, then this kernel-name-level
confirmation).

## Why this kernel specifically

conv2d_bn_silu_gemm_forward (the sibling kernel handling 1x1/stride=1/pad=0 convs) already
uses T::dot::<f32,f32>(w_tile, x_tile, acc, Some(InputPrecision::IEEE), None) -- teeny-triton's
tensor-core-accelerated matmul primitive -- and its own doc comment notes "~8x throughput
vs direct scalar accumulation" on sm_87+. That 1x1 case works because a 1x1 conv is
literally Y[N,M] = W[N,K] @ X[K,M] with no spatial kernel window, so X drops directly into
a clean 2-D GEMM operand.

conv2d_bn_silu_tiled_forward handles the general KxK (e.g. 3x3) case, where there's no such
direct 2-D view -- this is exactly why it doesn't already use T::dot(). The fix is an
*implicit-GEMM* formulation (same technique cuDNN's implicit_convolve_sgemm /
xmma_fprop_implicit_gemm kernels use): treat the reduction dimension as C_IN * KH * KW
instead of just C_IN, looping over each (kh, kw) kernel-window offset and doing a
T::dot() accumulation against an appropriately shifted/masked X tile for that offset,
summing into the same [BLOCK_N, BLOCK_M] accumulator across all (kh, kw, k-tile)
combinations. The boundary/padding masking logic already exists in the current direct
kernel and should carry over largely unchanged -- what's new is composing it with
tile-based descriptor loads instead of per-thread scalar loads, and replacing the
outer-product accumulation with T::dot() calls.

## Scope / open questions to resolve during implementation

- Tensor-core tile-size constraints: T::dot()'s TF32 path likely requires BLOCK_M/BLOCK_N/
  BLOCK_K to be multiples of some minimum (the existing GEMM kernel uses 32/32/32 --
  confirm the actual minimum, e.g. tied to the "1688" MMA shape naming seen in the
  profiled cuDNN kernels, and whether smaller KH*KW*C_IN reduction tiles for early/thin
  layers can still hit those minimums).
- Dispatch boundary: where does this fit relative to the existing use_gemm/use_tiled
  logic in graph/mod.rs? Likely a new case between them (KxK, non-depthwise, groups=1,
  large-enough C_IN/C_OUT to tile efficiently), falling back to the existing
  outer-product kernel for shapes too small to benefit (e.g. very low C_IN making even
  one BLOCK_K tile mostly padding). Depthwise/grouped convs should stay on the direct
  kernel regardless -- cuDNN's own profile shows it also falls back to a direct kernel
  (conv2d_grouped_direct_kernel) for those, not tensor-core GEMM.
- Precision matching: the existing GEMM kernel's comment flags "IEEE precision required
  to match cuDNN's float32 accumulation" as something that had to be empirically nailed
  down -- expect the same validation work here (compare against the existing
  conv2d_reference()/bn_affine_silu_reference() pure-Rust reference in
  tests/test_conv2d_bn_silu_tiled.rs, same pattern the existing tiled-kernel test uses).
- This kernel would also want the sm-count-based adaptive tile-size selection
  (see the sibling commit adding Options::sm_count/pick_adaptive_block_n) once it
  exists, but that's a follow-up, not part of this issue -- tensor-core tile
  constraints may also change what "adaptive" means here (larger minimum tiles).

## Expected impact

conv2d_bn_silu_tiled_forward is 49.7% of total GPU time. If a tensor-core reformulation
gets even roughly the same ~3-4x speedup ONNX Runtime's tensor-core kernels show over
plain FP32 CUDA-core convolution, that alone is a projected ~35% reduction in total
end-to-end inference latency for YOLO26n -- by far the largest lever identified from
this session's profiling work.

## Testing

Follow the existing test_conv2d_bn_silu_tiled.rs pattern: numeric correctness against
the pure-Rust conv2d_reference()/bn_affine_silu_reference() functions, plus a source
snapshot test. Re-run the Nsight Compute + bench_all.py (vision-rs-utils) comparison
against PyTorch/ONNX Runtime/TensorRT afterward to confirm the projected latency win
actually materializes.
close_reason: No longer relevant.

title: feat(anduin): give conv2d an output-channel block knob so a unit reuses its input across channels
description:
## Problem
The scheduled conv block (conv2d -> batchnorm2d -> silu, teenygrad-1l7i) gives each unit one (b, c_out, oh). conv2d's C_OUT axis is bound at the fixed block "1" (P4, derived by `#[tiled_kernel]` from the prelude), so the scheduler has no knob for it. Each unit therefore re-reads its input window once per output channel.

In the 2x3x32x32 -> 8-channel test, x accounts for 589,824 B of the 983,040 B traffic, against a 24,576 B tensor. That is about 24x: 8x from output channels and 3x from the H window. The hand-tuned `Conv2dBnSiluTiledForward` (nn/fused/conv2d_bn_silu_tiled.rs) avoids the 8x by tiling C_OUT by BLOCK_N with a 2-D carry `acc = [BLOCK_N, BLOCK_OW]`.

## Requirements
- A conv2d variant whose C_OUT is a real blocked axis (`block = BLOCK_N`), with a derived spec and grid. Either:
  - port `conv2d_bn_silu_tiled`'s approach to plain conv2d on the Tile path, which needs a multi-blocked-axis `#[tile_loop_tile]` (teenygrad-y8aa); or
  - let the lowering offer both kernels and the scheduler pick one.
- The scheduler searches BLOCK_N alongside BLOCK_OW (A4/A5 knobs).
- BN and SiLU still ride on the anchor: BN's [C] params become `Tiled{len: BLOCK_N}`.
- Tests: the conv block's x traffic falls by about BLOCK_N, with no region Full on B or C, and the existing acceptance test's other checks still hold.

## Related
teenygrad-1l7i (where this was measured), teenygrad-y8aa

title: Stale insta snapshot tests across kernels crate (kernel.source()/MLIR dumps)
description:
Nearly every kernel.source()/MLIR-dump insta snapshot test in teeny-kernels and teeny-triton (hundreds of tests: activations, losses, optimizers, pooling, normalization, GEMM, flash-attn2/PSA snapshots, kitchen_sink, etc.) fails when run with --no-fail-fast, e.g.:

The diffs are purely cosmetic (line wrapping, and in at least one case an unused-parameter rename B -> _B, plus an entry_point -> kitchen_sink_entry_point symbol rename) — not functional regressions.

Confirmed NOT a numeric/correctness issue: all 180 real GPU-execution (_cuda-suffixed) tests in the same run pass (the only non-ok one, test_muon_ns_xtx_cuda, is a pre-existing #[ignore] tracked separately as teenygrad-0mr). Also worth enabling --no-fail-fast in whatever CI/dev workflow runs this suite so a single stale snapshot doesn't mask the rest of the suite (this is how the breadth of the staleness went unnoticed).

title: test_anduin_conv_bn_silu_mlir snapshot is nondeterministic (volatile Rust-mangled symbol names)
description:
test_anduin_conv_bn_silu_mlir (kernels/teeny-kernels/tests/test_anduin_conv_bn_silu.rs:131) snapshot-asserts the joined MLIR text for the Conv2d/BatchNorm/SiLU pipeline via insta::assert_debug_snapshot!. It fails intermittently against the committed snapshot.

Root cause confirmed by repeated reruns with a cleared $TEENYC_CACHE_DIR: the mangled Rust symbol name embedded in each kernels MLIR (e.g. conv2d_forwards private tt.func symbol) changes on every single invocation even with byte-identical source and no code changes -- three consecutive runs produced three different hashes (_RINvCs6ayRZh6PIkJ_79conv2d_forward, _RINvCs5c5VyB5fJan_79conv2d_forward, _RINvCsfg0brKrY9wV_79conv2d_forward). Re-blessing the snapshot does not fix it; the next run goes stale again immediately.

This is a different root cause from the (already-closed) staleness issues teenygrad-3in/teenygrad-2dv/teenygrad-nov.18, which were one-time snapshot drift from a cargo fmt pass and were fixed by re-blessing once. Here the snapshot can never be stable as currently captured.

By contrast, kernels/teeny-kernels/tests/test_anduin_pointwise.rs::test_anduin_pointwise_relu_sigmoid_mlir snapshots a PointwiseFuse-fused kernels MLIR the same way (assert_debug_snapshot! on raw mlir text) and is stable across repeated reruns -- so the volatility is specific to how conv_bn_silu compiles its three kernels (conv2d_forward, batch_norm_2d_nchw_forward_inference, silu_forward) as separate compilation units, not inherent to every MLIR snapshot in this test style. Worth comparing how PointwiseFuse assigns its fused kernels crate/module identity vs. how the plain per-op lowering path (TritonLowering::lower_unary_op / the main op table) assigns conv2d_forward etc theirs, to find what makes the latter volatile.

Suggested fix direction: normalize/strip the volatile hash segment from mangled symbol names before snapshotting (regex substitution in the test), or track down and fix whatever makes the underlying crate-hash/disambiguator nondeterministic for these individually-compiled kernels so the mangled name is content-addressed like PointwiseFuses.

Not blocking: test_anduin_conv_bn_silu_matches_pytorch (the numerical-correctness test in the same file) passes reliably every run. Only the text-snapshot comparison is affected.

Found while investigating pointwise-fusion (teenygrad-1bf.1) test coverage; confirmed not covered by any existing open or closed beads issue, including all children of teenygrad-1bf.
close_reason: Closing without a fix: investigation (see comments) traced the mangling mechanism end-to-end and found it provably deterministic given identical kernel source, and could not reproduce the reported hash variability in this environment. Moot regardless -- case 8 (teenygrad-1bf.8) doesn't yet do Conv2d+BatchNorm2d+Silu fusion for these ops, so this test's code path is going to be rewritten as part of that work rather than debugged as-is.

comments.author: Arshad Mahmood
comments.text:
**Investigation: traced the mangling mechanism end-to-end; could not reproduce the reported variability**

## The mechanism, confirmed deterministic by source inspection

Traced the full causal chain from kernel source to the mangled `Cs<hash>_` segment, using the actual `teeny` rustc-fork source at `/home/arshadm/Workspace/projects/spinorml/teeny` (the source behind the installed `stable-teenyc` toolchain — not vendored into this repo, but present locally):

1. `Kernel::id()`'s default impl is `sha256(self.source())` (`core/teeny-core/src/device/program.rs:191-199`) — a pure content hash. **Not overridden** by `ForwardKernelAdapter` (`drivers/teeny-cuda/src/compiler/graph.rs:41-60`), the adapter actually used for `conv2d_forward`/`batch_norm_2d_nchw_forward_inference`/`silu_forward` — its `source()` returns `self.0.forward_kernel_source()` verbatim, no extra hashing/randomization layered on.
2. `LlvmCompiler::compile` (`compiler/teeny-compiler/src/compiler/backend/llvm/compiler.rs:169-183`) computes `effective_id = sha256(kernel.id() + target_cpu + ptx_version)`, and `kernel_file_name = "{kernel.name()}_{effective_id}"` — this becomes the `.rs` filename, and since **no `--crate-name` flag is ever passed** to `teenyc` (`compiler.rs:227-246`), rustc infers the crate name from the file stem. So the crate name is a pure function of `(kernel.source(), kernel.name(), target_cpu, ptx_version)`.
3. **No `-C metadata` flag is ever passed either** — confirmed by reading every `cmd.arg(...)` call in `compiler.rs:227-249`. This matters because Cargo normally injects `-C metadata` (hashed from package+features+profile) specifically to make crate disambiguation independent of directory/build-graph position; without it, the disambiguator falls back to whatever `StableCrateId::new` computes from crate name alone.
4. `StableCrateId::new(crate_name, is_exe, metadata, cfg_version)` (`teeny`'s `compiler/rustc_span/src/def_id.rs:159-205`, unmodified from upstream rustc in this area) is a `StableHasher` over: the crate name string, the **sorted+deduped** `-C metadata` list (empty here), `is_exe` (always `false`, `--crate-type=lib` is hardcoded), and the rustc version string (`sess.cfg_version`, a compile-time constant of the `teenyc` binary). No entropy source, no PID/timestamp/pointer-address involvement anywhere in this function.

So: the entire chain **`source() → id() → effective_id → crate name → Cs<hash>_`** is, per source, a pure function of `kernel.source()` (holding `target_cpu`/`ptx_version` fixed, which are also constant for a single machine/run). There's no code path here through which the same source could legitimately produce a different disambiguator.

## Empirical reproduction attempt: fully deterministic, could not trigger the bug

- Ran `test_anduin_conv_bn_silu_mlir` twice, each as a fully separate `cargo test` process with a **freshly emptied `$TEENYC_CACHE_DIR`** (via a throwaway `git worktree` of `feature/fusion-case-8-conv-bn-silu-epilogue` @ `e4545e0a8`, its current tip). Both runs produced byte-identical `.rs` source and `.mlir` output for all three kernels (`conv2d_forward`, `batch_norm_2d_nchw_forward_inference`, `silu_forward`), including identical `Cs<hash>_` segments.
- Extracted the real captured `conv2d_forward` source from the cache and invoked the actual `teenyc` binary directly 30 times with the same flags `LlvmCompiler::compile` uses (15 sequential, 15 launched concurrently as background jobs, to specifically probe for a threading/scheduling-dependent race) — **all 30 produced the identical `Cs<hash>_` segment.**
- Could not reproduce the reported hash variability under any of these conditions.

## A discrepancy worth flagging: the test as it currently exists can't reach the snapshot step at all

At `feature/fusion-case-8-conv-bn-silu-epilogue`'s current tip (`e4545e0a8` — the only commit that has ever introduced or touched this test file on this branch), `test_anduin_conv_bn_silu_mlir` fails **before** the MLIR-snapshot code is ever reached:
```
assertion `left == right` failed: expected Anduin to fuse Conv2d+BatchNorm2d+Silu into a single node
  left: 4
 right: 2
```
This matches the test's own module doc-comment ("Currently failing by design: case 8... is not implemented yet"). Since `assert_eq!` panics unconditionally on mismatch, execution never reaches the `mlir_blobs`/`assert_debug_snapshot!` lines this issue describes — meaning whoever observed the 3-different-hashes symptom must have been running against a state where Anduin's case-8 fusion collapsed the graph to 2 nodes (i.e. `dag.len() == 2` passed), which isn't the state of any commit currently reachable in this repo's git history for this branch. Likely an uncommitted local WIP state of Anduin that predates `e4545e0a8` or was never pushed.

## Practical implication

Given the mechanism is provably deterministic for identical `(source(), name(), target_cpu, ptx_version)`, and I couldn't reproduce it in this environment, the most likely explanations left are:
1. **The "byte-identical source" claim needs re-verification, not assumption.** `LlvmCompiler::compile` never deletes the `.rs` file it writes to `$TEENYC_CACHE_DIR` after a successful compile — the next time this reproduces, `diff` the three retained `.rs` files directly (don't eyeball them) before concluding the hash algorithm is at fault. If they're byte-identical and the `Cs<hash>_` still differs, that would be a real, reproducible rustc-fork bug worth filing upstream in `teeny` with a minimal repro; if they differ even subtly, the actual bug is upstream of compilation, in whatever generates `forward_kernel_source()`/`kernel.name()` for Anduin's fused-epilogue candidate path specifically (not yet implemented on this branch, so not inspectable here).
2. **`target_cpu`/`ptx_version` stability.** `effective_id` folds these in; worth confirming they're actually pinned (not autodetected from GPU enumeration order, which could vary run to run on a multi-GPU machine) whenever this is next investigated.
3. Given the state needed to reproduce this (a working case-8 fusion) doesn't exist in the repo yet, this may simply not be reproducible again until `teenygrad-1bf.8` lands enough of Anduin's fusion for `dag.len() == 2` to actually hold — at which point, capture the retained `.rs`/`.mlir` files from each of the 3 (or more) runs before re-diagnosing, rather than only comparing the final mangled names.

Not making a fix or closing this — no root cause was confirmed, only that the previously-assumed mechanism (rustc-level hash randomness) is not supported by the source, and isn't reproducible under controlled testing in this environment.

title: refactor(core): remove reachable panics from teeny-core's public API
description:
## Problem

`teeny-core` still aborts the process on ordinary bad input. `Layer::call`,
`Op::infer_output_shape` is now fallible
(`46b90f71f`, `d4af7e084`, `f4effd25e`), but only *window geometry* errors
travel as `Result`. Everything else panics.

This matters more since `Op::infer_output_shape` became `pub`: a caller
outside the crate can trigger each of these with a wrong-rank argument.

## Confirmed reachable panics

Verified by running `catch_unwind` probes against the lib, not by reading:

| Site | Trigger | Panic |
|---|---|---|
| `graph/op.rs:1549` | `Op::Relu.infer_output_shape(&[])` | `inputs[0]` index out of bounds |
| `graph/op.rs:1588` | `Op::Linear` on a rank-0 shape | `input[..input.len() - 1]` usize underflow |
| `graph/op.rs:1628` | `Op::Conv2d` on a rank-2 shape | `input[2]` index out of bounds |
| `graph/op.rs:2202` | `Op::SpaceToDepth { blocksize: 0 }` | `h / blocksize` divide by zero |

## Full inventory (lib code, tests excluded)

**Positional indexing — 63 sites, all in `infer_output_shape`.** Every arm
reads `input[0..4]` with no rank check; conv/pool/norm arms assume rank 3-5.
The dominant class.

**Arithmetic — 2 unguarded divides.** `SpaceToDepth` (`op.rs:2202-2203`) and
`DepthToSpace` (`op.rs:2208`) divide by `blocksize` without a zero check.
`Op::Split` (`op.rs:2061`) *does* guard, with `num_outputs.max(&1)`, so the
gap is local rather than systemic. Multiplications (`c * blocksize *
blocksize`, `Flatten`'s `acc * d`) can overflow and wrap silently in release
— the failure mode `window_out_dim`'s own comment warns about.

**`todo!()` — 43, all eager `Layer::call` stubs in `nn/*`.** Honest
"backend not written" placeholders, but they abort. Now that `call` returns
`Result` these can be a proper `Err`, which also makes the eager path's
incompleteness visible instead of fatal.

**`unimplemented!()` — 0.** This inventory counted one, `Op::infer_input_shape`'s
catch-all, which PR #43 removed along with the rest of reverse shape
inference (`teenygrad-3fy`, not doing).

**New since the audit:** `window_out_shape` (`op.rs`) now indexes the input
shape on behalf of all twelve conv/pool arms, so the wrong-rank panics they
each had are consolidated into one place. That makes the fix below cheaper,
not smaller: one guard replaces twelve.

**`assert!` — 4, all genuine.** `graph/mod.rs:190` (`topological_sort`,
"graph contains a cycle") and `utils/dag.rs:61,62,126` (self-loop, invalid
node index, cycle). `Graph::topological_sort` and `Dag::add_edge` are both
`pub`.

**Safe, no action:** `op.rs:2250`'s `.unwrap()` is guarded by `len() >= 2` on
the line above. `inputs[1]` in `Gemm`/`MatMul` sits behind `inputs.len() >=
2`; `out[ax]` in `Concat`/`Split`/`Reduce*` uses `rem_euclid` after a rank
check. No `panic!`, `unreachable!`, `expect()` or `debug_assert!` in lib code.

## Suggested approach

1. A checked accessor — `Op::dim(&self, shape, index) -> Result<Option<usize>>`
   returning a new `Error::UnexpectedRank { op, index, rank }` — retires the
   63 indexing sites and the `inputs[0]` case together. The op's name can come
   from its `Debug` form, truncated at the first space, so no 243-arm match is
   needed; build it only on the error path.
2. `Error::ZeroBlockSize` for the two divides.
3. Decide separately on the `todo!()`s and on `topological_sort` /
   `Dag::add_edge`, since making those fallible changes more public
   signatures.

A prototype of 1 and 2 was written and passed (77 reads guarded, 54 tests
green) but was set aside to keep it out of the branch it was found on. Note
the line numbers in this inventory predate PR #41 and PR #43 and will have
moved; the categories and counts still hold for the forward path.

## Done when

No panic reachable from `teeny-core`'s public API by argument alone, and the
four probes above return `Err`.

title: feat(anduin): cap a unit's tile at a register budget so wide rows aren't one huge program
description:
## Problem
The tile search keeps only one per-unit size limit: the footprint must fit level l+1's capacity (shared memory). For the conv block on an 8192-wide image (`test_a_wide_conv_block_tiles_its_rows_with_a_halo`), it picks `BLOCK_OW = 4096`. That gives a 64 KiB footprint and one unit per compute unit. At width 4096 it takes the whole row.

In Triton those tensors live in registers, not shared memory, so a 4096-element f32 tile per program would spill and run poorly. The model has nothing that penalizes it. `reg_est` exists only for thread-level tilings (A13), which are not implemented. The key is `(traffic + 1) · waves`, and larger tiles always cut traffic.

## Requirements
- A per-program register budget, e.g. a cap on the elements of the largest live tensor per unit, or `reg_est` applied at the block level. It goes in the hierarchy or the caps, not hard-coded, and is calibrated against Triton's practical limits (num_warps x 32 threads x registers).
- Tilings over the budget are rejected (or penalized), so the search settles on a moderate BLOCK_OW, e.g. <= 1024 for f32.
- Tests: the 8192-wide conv block picks a BLOCK_OW at or under the cap. The 32-wide block is unchanged. D1 softmax is unchanged unless its rows exceed the cap, in which case say what happens.

## Related
teenygrad-1l7i, ANALYSIS.md §12 A10/A13 (reg_est)

title: spec: convert the 51 route-2 kernels to the Tile ABI, so anduin can fuse them
notes:
## Goal

Convert the 51 forward kernels that declare their tile axes via the
metadata-only form on raw pointers to In<Tile<..>>/Out<Tile<..>>, so anduin can
FUSE them and not merely schedule them.

## Why this is not tidying

teenygrad-1tl left 51 of 133 forwards on tagged raw pointers, and its closing
note called that "a legitimate terminal state" on the grounds that route 2
declares a real tile_spec. That reasoning holds for shape propagation and fails
for fusion:

  - resolve_inputs/propagate read KernelTileSpec and never a parameter's type,
    so route 2 is enough to decide WHAT tile a node needs;
  - FusionCore -- what lets anduin emit ONE kernel for several nodes, by
    splicing their bodies -- is derived from the auto-prelude's bindings, and
    the auto-prelude runs only for In<Tile<..>>.

So a route-2 kernel can be chosen for a fused group and then cannot be
generated into one. Tiles are the inter-kernel mechanism; this epic is on the
path to fusion working at all. teenygrad-1cli carries the FusionCore half, which
is separately stubbed behind a now-false comment.

## Population, by why each kernel is still route 2

Measured from the tree, not estimated.

  RUNG 1 (teenygrad-1a1j) -- 26, convertible today, no blocker.
    A single read at program_id offsets, which is exactly what the auto-prelude
    emits. 12 pads, 10 reduce_*, 2 global pools, 2 scans.

  RUNG 2 (teenygrad-3dbg) -- the epilogue hook.
    #[tile_loop(generate)] emits the store immediately after the loop, so any
    kernel with work between the two cannot use it. 13 of rung 3's 20 are in
    that position. conv2d_forward only escaped it by having no epilogue.

  RUNG 3 (teenygrad-3dp5) -- 20, loop-reading, blocked on rung 2.
    Reads inside their accumulation loop, so they need the generated loop
    (teenygrad-y8aa's machinery) rather than a load-once prelude. Convs, pools,
    norms, both batchnorm halves, flash attention.

  OUT OF SCOPE for now -- 5, TMA descriptors.
    matmul, linear, transpose_2d, flatten, conv2d_bn_silu_tiled use
    make_tensor_descriptor rather than add_offsets. `Tile` does not model that
    primitive, so these are a genuine modelling gap rather than undone work.
    Deliberately left unimplemented; file separately if and when wanted.

## Done when

Rungs 1 and 2 and 3 are closed, the 46 non-TMA kernels take Tile parameters,
and teenygrad-1tl.12's closing audit test shows route 2 down to the 5 TMA
kernels. The audit is already a test, so it will report this without new work.

## Worked example

teenygrad-1nr.18.4 ported conv2d_forward end to end: its body is now
`acc = acc + x * w;` and everything else is generated. Numerics pass against its
PyTorch fixtures. That is the shape every rung-3 conversion should take, and the
source of the four gaps rung 2 and the TMA note record.

title: feat: a read-once broadcast operand (bias-shaped) for route-1 kernels
description:
Found while doing teenygrad-3dbg (PR #86).

A bias is read ONCE, before the loop, indexed by one UNBLOCKED output axis and broadcast over the blocked one. That operand cannot be a route-1 In<Tile<..>> today:

  - the prelude requires an input axis to match an output axis on extent AND block (tiled_kernel.rs, the 'declares an axis the output does not' check);
  - conv2d_bias's output declares C_OUT unblocked, so the bias must declare it unblocked too;
  - but a route-1 input derives its tile shape from a blocked axis, so it must have one. With none, the macro panics: 'checked above: exactly one axis carries block = ..'.

So the two requirements are mutually exclusive for this shape.

## Workaround in place

conv2d_bias_forward converted anyway: bias_ptr stays untagged and the load sits inside the `finish` expression teenygrad-3dbg added. x, w and y are tiles. That is the same partial state conv2d_forward is in with w_ptr, and it is why #86 did not block on this.

## Who needs it

conv1d_bias, conv2d_bias, conv3d_bias (the bias add), and the affine parameters of layer/rms/instance/group norm, which have the same shape: one value per channel, broadcast across the block.

## Shape of the work

Probably a declaration saying 'this axis indexes the operand but is not blocked in it', letting the tile be [1] and broadcast. Check against the existing broadcast rule -- an axis LEFT OFF already broadcasts, so the gap is specifically an axis that indexes without blocking, which is not the same thing.
close_reason: Anduin fusion work discontinued; closed with the Anduin-related issues

title: spec: multi-pass kernels (the norms) -- a declared reduction pipeline before the map pass
description:
Option C, chosen 2026-10-05: anduin does need to fuse the norms, so they must become route 1. Scoped from what the five kernels actually do, not from a guess.

## Why the other options were rejected

A (keep adding keys) reaches 6 of teenygrad-3dp5's remaining 11 and never reaches the norms.
B (unify finish/init/prologue into one per-carry vocabulary) converts ZERO additional kernels -- multi-pass is not a key-shaped problem -- and would churn the nine kernels already using `generate`. Dropped.

## The measured shape

layer_norm_forward is THREE passes over the same axis, with scalar work between them and three outputs:

  pass 1   carry `sum`,     accumulate T::sum(x_tile)            -> mean_1 = sum * n_inv
  pass 2   carry `var_sum`, accumulate T::sum(diff*diff)         -> rstd_1 = rsqrt(var_sum*n_inv + eps)
           store mean_1, store rstd_1   (one element per row)
  pass 3   NO carry -- stores y per tile                          (a MAP, not a reduction)

rms_norm_forward is the same with one reduce pass instead of two. instancenorm, groupnorm and batch_norm_normalize are the same family (3, 3 and 2 stores respectively).

The last pass is a MAP over the axis. That is the 'second pass over the row' earlier notes kept referring to, now pinned down.

## Why the final pass is the right cut

FusionCore's contract (kernels/teeny-triton/src/fusion_core.rs, module docs) is: the auto-prelude binds the loaded input, the body's statements compute, and the body ends in a plain T::store which gets stripped to leave a splice-ready core.

That describes a norm's FINAL MAP PASS exactly. So fusion needs the map pass to be route 1; the preceding reduction passes only need to RUN, not to be fusable. That is the cut this design takes, and it is why the whole kernel does not need a general multi-pass body mechanism.

It also means the author's body stays exactly one spliced region -- the map pass -- so teenygrad-1nr.18.3's C3 (the loop belongs to the wrapper) still holds, and option A of that analysis (markers in the body) is still avoided.

## Design

A repeatable function-level attribute, declared in execution order, running BEFORE the author's body:

    #[tile_reduce_pass(
        over = N,            // axis walked in blocks; the block comes from the operand's blocked axis
        read = x,            // which Tile operand this pass reads
        into = sum,          // the carry
        acc = <expr>,        // added each iteration; may name the read tile
        finish = <expr>      // optional scalar after the loop; may name 
    )]

Emitted per pass:

    let mut <into> = zeros::<D>(&[1]);
    let mut __tile_pass_n = 0;
    while __tile_pass_n < (<over>) {
        let <read> = load(<operand> + row_base + __tile_pass_n + arange(0, BLOCK), mask, fill);
        <into> = <into> + (<acc>);
        __tile_pass_n += BLOCK;
    }
    let <into> = <finish>;          // rebinding, as  on a carry already does

Later passes may name earlier passes' carries: pass 2's `acc` references `mean`, which is pass 1's finish. Sequential by declaration order, so this falls out.

The author's body is the final map pass, wrapped in the same block walk with the trailing store generated -- which is what `#[tile_loop(generate)]` already does, so that machinery is reused rather than duplicated.

Rank-reduced outputs (mean, rstd, rrms: one element per row) are declared as Out params with their own axes, and the macro stores the matching carry after its pass.

## Staging

  1. rms_norm_forward   one reduce pass, one scalar output, one map pass. The
                        smallest complete instance -- it exercises the pass
                        loop, the scalar store and the generated map in one
                        kernel.
  2. layer_norm_forward two reduce passes, an inter-pass reference (pass 2 reads
                        pass 1's mean), two scalar outputs.
  3. instancenorm, groupnorm, batch_norm_normalize.

Verify numerics on GPU before touching any snapshot at every stage; each of these has fixture tests, which is the point of this rung.

## Risks

- The block walk is a `while` over a runtime extent, so the trip count is
  runtime -- fine here (it is `cdiv(N, BLOCK_N)`, uniform across the warp)
  but it is NOT the fixed `axes`/`count` form `generate` uses today. The pass
  loop and the map loop therefore need a second loop form, not the existing one.
- A pass reads the SAME operand the map pass reads, so one Tile parameter is
  now loaded more than once. That breaks the current one-load-per-parameter
  assumption, which is exactly why the norms could not be route 1 before.
  The prelude must not ALSO emit its own load for such an operand.
- Three of the five write 3 outputs. `generate` currently insists on exactly
  one Out<Tile>; that check has to learn about the scalar outputs.

        read = x,            // which Tile operand this pass reads
        into = sum,          // the carry
        acc = <expr>,        // added each iteration; may name the read tile
        finish = <expr>      // optional scalar after the loop; may name the carry
    )]

Emitted per pass:

    let mut CARRY = zeros::<D>(&[1]);
    let mut __tile_pass_n = 0;
    while __tile_pass_n < (OVER) {
        let READ = load(OPERAND + row_base + __tile_pass_n + arange(0, BLOCK), mask, fill);
        CARRY = CARRY + (ACC);

    }

3. instancenorm, groupnorm, batch_norm_normalize.

## Risks

- The block walk is a while loop over a runtime extent, so its trip count is runtime. Fine here (it is cdiv(N, BLOCK_N), uniform across the warp) but it is NOT the fixed axes/count form the generate flag uses today. The pass loop and the map loop therefore need a second loop form, not the existing one.

- A pass reads the SAME operand the map pass reads, so one Tile parameter is now loaded more than once. That breaks the current one-load-per-parameter assumption, which is exactly why the norms could not be route 1 before. The prelude must not ALSO emit its own load for such an operand.

- Three of the five write 3 outputs. The generate flag currently insists on exactly one Out<Tile>; that check has to learn about the scalar outputs.


## STAGE 3 PROGRESS -- PR #94 (2026-10-05)

instance_norm_forward converts: layer_norm's shape over L with one more gridded
axis, so the statistic is per (sample, channel).

Two bugs ALREADY IN THE TREE surfaced while doing it:

1. param_offsets picked a multi-blocked parameter's range BY BLOCK VALUE
   (.position(|&k| axes[k].block == axis.block)), so a statistic blocked at 1 on
   two gridded axes took slot 0 twice -- offset came out
   __tile_range_0 * C + __tile_range_0, the channel index used as the sample
   index. Latent only because every other multi-blocked kernel spells its blocks
   differently (BLOCK_M vs BLOCK_N). Third bug in teenygrad-1nr.18.5's path.

2. The pass store used broadcast_to where the rank differs. A statistic's
   address tile is [1, 1] against a [1] carry, and broadcasting cannot change
   rank -- it needs expand_dims per extra dimension.

instance_norm's weight/bias stay raw pointers: teenygrad-3rk6.1's gap, worse
here because with two gridded block-1 axes the prelude's load is rank 2 while
the map pass works in rank-1 blocks.

### Method note that paid off

I wrote the numerics test and confirmed it passed against the UNCONVERTED kernel
before changing any declaration, so a later failure could only be the
conversion. It then caught all three problems. Worth repeating for the rest.

### Remaining two, and they are NOT alike

batch_norm_normalize_forward is a MAP with no reduction pass at all: just a
walked store loop, with mean/rstd as [C] INPUTS. The multi-pass dispatch fires
on a non-empty pass list, so it never triggers. Needs the dispatch to fire on a
walked axis alone -- small, and the existing test_batch_norm_forward_training
already covers it numerically.

group_norm_forward does NOT fit the current vocabulary. It walks
group_size = (C / G) * L -- a FLATTENED span of two axes -- from
group_start = n * C * L + g * (C / G) * L, and indexes mean/rstd by the flat
pid rather than by (n, g). pass_offset models one walked axis with row-major
others; nothing describes a flattened pair, nor a grid axis (G) that is not a
tensor axis. This is a new gap, not an extension: either a declared flattened
axis, or group_norm stays route 2.


## ALL FIVE NORMS CONVERTED -- stage 3 complete (2026-10-05)

  rms_norm              PR #92
  layer_norm            PR #93
  instance_norm         PR #94
  batch_norm_normalize  PR #95
  group_norm            PR #96

group_norm took option 3 of the three offered: restructured to declare
[N, G, group_size] instead of [N, C, L], so the walked span is ONE axis rather
than a flattened (C / G) * L. Having done it, the flattening was a workaround
for not being able to express a split axis -- option 1 would have baked that
into the vocabulary for one kernel.

### Vocabulary this rung added

  #[tile_reduce_pass(over, read, into, acc, finish, store, fill)]
  #[tile(.., walk)]              axis walked in blocks, neither gridded nor
                                 loaded whole; carries `block` as its STEP
  tile_walk / tile_walk_mask     the map block's coordinate and mask, for a
                                 body needing a computed gather

### Bugs found, all pre-existing or introduced here and caught by tests

  param_offsets picked a multi-blocked range BY BLOCK VALUE, so two axes
    blocked at 1 collided on slot 0 (#94). Third bug in teenygrad-1nr.18.5's
    path.
  The pass store used broadcast_to where the RANK differs; needs expand_dims
    (#94).
  pass_offset ignored the walked axis's own stride, wrong whenever that axis is
    not innermost (#95).
  The rank mode was decided by all_tile_param_attrs[0], which excludes walked
    operands (#95).
  A walked axis looked like a tiled one in THREE places -- untiled_dims (#93),
    blocked_positions (#92) and grid_spec (#95). The grid one shipped in three
    PRs: anduin would have launched cdiv(extent, block) times too many
    programs. All three are the same cause, `walk` carrying `block` as its step
    while every site keyed on block.is_some(). Auditing the sites when the flag
    was introduced would have found all three at once.
  Masked lanes contributed mean^2 to the variance -- a per-pass `fill` fixes it
    (#93). The hand-written body had a comment warning about exactly this.

### Method that worked, worth keeping

Four of five norms had NO numerics test for the kernel being converted, only a
source snapshot. From layer_norm onward I wrote the test and confirmed it passed
against the UNCONVERTED kernel first, so a later failure could only be the
conversion. That found the mean^2 bug, the slot collision, the rank confusion
and the stride omission. Deleting a declaration to see whether anything notices
is one test run and caught three more.

### STILL UNVERIFIED

FusionCore is stubbed to unconditional None (teenygrad-1cli). The norms are
route 1 and their map pass has the shape FusionCore's contract describes, but
that anduin actually fuses them is structurally true and empirically untested.
Five kernels now rest on it.

title: Regression tests and snapshot update for teenyc-2ef (scalar divisibility hint, issue #133)
description:
Companion to teeny's teenyc-2ef (tt.divisibility=16 on scalar kernel args miscompiles integer division and bounds masks on CUDA, GitHub #133). Once a teenyc with that fix is released:
- Add kernels/teeny-kernels/tests/test_div_probe.rs (the reporter's probe from realitymatrix/teenygrad feature/fs-structural-lowerings), not ignored: y[i] = i / d for d in 2..=13 must be exact on cuda,hardware.
- Add a bounds-mask test: a masked store with n_elements not a multiple of 4 (e.g. 30) into a buffer with guard values past n, asserting the guards are untouched and every element < n is written.
- Add a strided_copy test with an innermost extent not a multiple of 4 (e.g. transpose of [5, 5] / [rows, 5] for rows 2..=13); current fixtures only use multiples of 4, which is why test_strided_copy passes.
- Update the CUDA asm snapshots: masks and scalar arithmetic will no longer be vectorised in groups of 4, so many *_asm_cuda snapshots change; check the diffs are only that.
A local branch feature/scalar-divisibility-133 holds the probe file (untracked).
close_reason: Done in #134 (div probe + 109 CUDA snapshots) and #135 (bounds-mask and transpose regression tests), both on release/0.3.1
