Both need BLOCK_SIZE 1024 to trigger; both fail on teenyc d6e7f420547 (mask overruns to next multiple of 4, confirmed) and pass on 18d0e121498. Close the bead when #135 merges.

title: spec: tile-based DSL over teeny-triton + Welder-style tile-graph scheduler
description:
## Goal

Design (and eventually implement) a tile-based DSL layered on top of `teeny-triton`'s
existing `Triton` trait, where a kernel declares each tensor argument's *tile shape*
(in terms of `BLOCK_*` consts and grid axes) plus the total tensor shape, and the
generated code derives the index/offset/mask boilerplate and `RuntimeOp::grid()`
automatically. This is a prerequisite for a second, larger goal: a
Welder-style (OSDI'23, Shi et al., "WELDER: Scheduling Deep Learning Memory Access
via Tile-graph", https://www.usenix.org/conference/osdi23/presentation/shi)
tile-graph scheduler that decides *which* ops fuse and at *which* memory level,
driven by an analytic memory-traffic cost model instead of hand-written allowlists.

This issue is a design spec, in the same spirit as `teenygrad-1bf` (which specs a
`TritonFusionBackend` for graph-level fusion) but one layer lower: `teenygrad-1bf`
specs the fusion *decision/lowering* trait; this issue specs the *kernel-authoring*
abstraction that both today's hand-written kernels and a future Welder-style
scheduler would sit on top of. See "Relationship to teenygrad-1bf" below.

## Motivating problem

Every hand-written Triton-DSL kernel in `teeny-kernels` repeats the same
pid-decode -> offset -> mask -> load/store boilerplate, with zero structured
metadata about tile shape available outside the kernel body:

- `kernels/teeny-kernels/src/nn/activation/elu.rs` (`elu_forward`) — flat 1D:
  `pid -> block_start = pid*BLOCK_SIZE -> offsets = arange(BLOCK_SIZE)+block_start
  -> mask = offsets.lt(n_elements)`.
- `kernels/teeny-kernels/src/math/gemm.rs` (`matmul_forward`) — 2D swizzled:
  `group_id`/`pid_in_group`/`pid_m`/`pid_n` GROUP_M swizzle for L2 locality,
  `make_tensor_descriptor`/`load_tensor_descriptor` per operand, K-dim reduction
  loop accumulating via `T::dot`.
- `kernels/teeny-kernels/src/nn/conv/conv2d.rs` (`conv2d_forward`) — flat
  pid decoded into `(b, c_out, oh, ow_tile)`, masked sliding-window loads over
  `(C_IN/G)*KH*KW` combinations, weight broadcast-load.
- `kernels/teeny-kernels/src/nn/attention/flash_attn2.rs`
  (`flash_attention2_forward`) — 2-axis grid `(q_row, batch_head)`, online-softmax
  accumulator state threaded through a `for k_row in 0..n_ctx_k` loop.

None of this is expressed as data — it's all inline `T::` calls. The only
structured per-kernel metadata that exists today is `KernelIo`
(`kernels/teeny-triton/src/kernel_io.rs`, produced by `const fn kernel_io()` that
`teeny_macros::kernel` generates) — pointer-argument roles (`InPtr`/`OutPtr`/
`InOutPtr`), used only to drive the pointwise-fusion probe. There is no tile-shape,
no traffic/cost model, and no shape-propagation mechanism anywhere in the repo
(confirmed by full-repo grep for "cost model" / "memory traffic" / "bytes_moved" —
zero hits).

## Current architecture facts (from a codebase survey; use as ground truth for design)

**Two separate graph representations exist; only one matters here.**
`teeny_core::graph::Graph`/`Op` (`core/teeny-core/src/graph/mod.rs`) is the
nn-layer-traced graph consumed by the Triton/`teenyc` pipeline (`teeny-kernels`,
`teeny-cuda`) — this is where fusion and `RuntimeOp` dispatch happen, and where a
tile-graph scheduler would plug in. `FXGraph`
(`compiler/teeny-compiler/src/fxgraph/`, `support/teeny-fxgraph/`) feeds the
separate LLVM/MLIR/`ndarray` backend and is unrelated to Triton codegen.

**Fusion today (`kernels/teeny-kernels/src/graph/optimizer/`).** `Op::Fused` as a
graph-`Op` variant was added (#19) then dropped (#26); the current mechanism is a
`CustomOp` impl, not an `Op` variant:
- `graph/optimizer/ops/pointwise_fuse.rs` — `PointwiseFuse` (`members: Vec<Op>`),
  wrapped as `Op::Custom { data: CustomData::new(fused) }`.
- Driver: `graph/optimizer/anduin.rs`, `Anduin::optimize` ->
  `fuse_pointwise_chains` (fixpoint loop, anduin.rs:44-189). Fuses a child into
  its parent only when: single-input, single-consumer, same dtype (F32/F64 only),
  CTA-probe-compatible (`PointwiseFuseProbe::compatible`, same `BLOCK_SIZE`), and
  no non-terminal bool-producing member (`is_bool_terminal_only` rejects
  `IsNaN`/`IsInf` mid-chain).
- Lowering: `PointwiseFuse::lower()` -> `lower_pointwise_fuse`
  (pointwise_fuse.rs:281-348) concatenates each member's kernel body and
  synthesizes one entry point chaining calls through `scratch0..scratchN-2`
  ping-pong buffers (`synthesize_entry`, pointwise_fuse.rs:472-525).
- Scope: strictly unary elementwise/pointwise chains
  (`pointwise_parts`/`probe_pointwise_op`, anduin.rs:60-68, gated on
  `KernelIo::is_unary_elementwise` + `BlockSized`+`NElementsTiled`). No
  reduction, matmul, conv, or binary-elementwise fusion at the graph level.
  Conv+BN+SiLU fusion exists only as hand-written kernel structs
  (`nn/fused/conv2d_bn_silu*.rs`), not a graph-rewrite decision.

**`RuntimeOp` trait** (`core/teeny-core/src/model/mod.rs:75+`) — the runtime
dispatch interface every kernel implements by hand: `n_activation_inputs`,
`param_shapes(input_shapes, output_shape)`, `pack_args(inputs, params, output,
output_shape, output_row_stride, visitor)`, `grid(output_shape) -> [u32;3]`, plus
optional/training hooks. Every kernel hand-derives its own `grid()` (e.g.
`MatMulRuntimeOp::grid`, gemm.rs:285-291, computes `pm*pn` CTAs from
`output_shape`/`block_m`/`block_n` — the same `div_ceil` arithmetic duplicated in
every `RuntimeOp` impl in the tree).

**`teeny_macros::kernel` is a pure string transform**
(`macros/teeny-macros/src/macros/kernel.rs`, ~994 lines) — "Rust fn -> embedded
DSL source string + C-ABI entry wrapper," no structured tile/grid IR. It
classifies pointer params into `PtrRole` (`KernelIo`, the only structured
metadata it emits) and, if `BLOCK_SIZE`+`n_elements: i32` are present, implements
`BlockSized`/`NElementsTiled`, which combine into `PointwiseFuseProbe` — the sole
existing (very narrow) precedent for "kernel declares its own tiling shape as
queryable data."

**Codegen is textual, not IR-based.** `Triton` trait
(`kernels/teeny-triton/src/triton/mod.rs:141-770`, `program_id`/`load`/`store`/
`dot`/`make_tensor_descriptor`/etc.) is implemented exactly once, by
`LlvmTriton`, and that impl is an explicit type-check-only dummy (every method
returns zero/null). The real path: `teeny_macros::kernel` embeds each kernel's
literal Rust source as a string; `triton_lang::TRITON` embeds the whole DSL
crate's source as a constant; `LlvmCompiler::compile`
(`compiler/teeny-compiler/src/compiler/backend/llvm/compiler.rs:216-237`)
concatenates the two and shells out to the external `teenyc` binary with
`--frontend=triton -Zcodegen-backend=mlir`. **There is no in-process AST/IR to
attach tile metadata to after macro expansion** — any structured tile-shape
representation has to be captured *at* macro-expansion time (as a `const fn`
alongside the generated kernel, mirroring `kernel_io()`), not recovered later
from generated text.

**Shape inference is coarse and has no reverse/tile-propagation direction.**
`Shape = Vec<Option<usize>>` (`core/teeny-core/src/graph/mod.rs:66`).
`infer_output_shape(op, inputs)` is a single big match, purely
output-shape-from-input-shapes. Binary/variadic elementwise ops (`Add`, `Mul`,
`Sub`, `Div`, `Pow`, ...) are handled with the literal comment "Binary /
variadic element-wise — approximate as first-input shape" (graph/mod.rs:2037) —
i.e. there is no real broadcast-shape computation anywhere in the codebase today.
`CustomOp::infer_output_shape(&self, input_shapes: &[&Shape]) -> Shape`
(graph/mod.rs:114) is the only per-op hook a Welder-style tile-propagation layer
could extend.

## The Welder paper — mechanics to port (OSDI'23, Shi et al.)

- **`tile-graph`**: a DFG of *operator-tiles* rather than full tensors. Each
  node computes one data-tile of its output from a tile-shaped region of its
  inputs, described by the op's tensor expression (e.g. Conv computes a
  `[1x1xC]` output tile from a `[3x3xC]` input tile).
- **`SetConnect(edge, level)`**: mark two adjacent op-tiles as sharing a
  *reuse-tile* at a given memory level (register / shared / global / host),
  so the consumer reads the producer's tile directly instead of round-tripping
  through a full materialized tensor.
- **`Propagate(graph, output_tile_shape)`**: back-propagate a chosen output
  tile shape through the graph; each op's dependent input region is derived
  from its tensor expression (conservative upper bound for irregular access
  like `Gather`/strided `Conv`). If a tile-graph has multiple output nodes,
  their shapes must agree or the graph doesn't connect.
- **Two-step scheduling algorithm** (paper Fig. 7, `GraphConnecting` +
  `SubGraphTiling`), relying on **inter-layer independence** (traffic at
  memory level L depends only on the tile config *at* L, so levels can be
  optimized independently once the level below is fixed) and **intra-layer
  independence** (independent sub-tile-graphs at the same level can be
  scheduled independently):
  1. `GraphConnecting(graph, device)`: topological walk over nodes/edges; for
     each edge, try every memory level via `SetConnect`, extract the resulting
     connected subgraph, call `SubGraphTiling`, profile/estimate latency, keep
     the best level.
  2. `SubGraphTiling(subgraph, level, parent_config)`: enumerate candidate
     output tile shapes for this level (Roller-style expansion from size-1
     towards hardware-aligned shapes), `Propagate` each, reject if it exceeds
     `MemFootprint` for the level, keep the top-K by `MemTraffic`; recurse to
     `level+1` for the upper sub-graph.
- **Cost model**: analytic memory-traffic count — `MemTraffic(tile_graph)` =
  sum of input/output tile byte sizes, scaled by penalty factors for
  uncoalesced access, under-parallelism relative to hardware thread count, and
  an infinite penalty if `MemFootprint` exceeds the level's capacity. Purely
  analytic (no profiling in the inner loop), which is what makes the search
  cheap: ~20 tuning trials/subgraph vs. Ansor's ~800/operator (Table 5).
- **Codegen**: four abstracted device interfaces — `Allocate`, `LoadTiles`,
  `ComputeTile`, `StoreTiles` (Table 1) — the hierarchical tile-graph is
  unrolled recursively per memory level (`ExecuteGraph`, Fig. 8) into these
  four ops, each mapped to backend (TVM) codegen. `ComputeTile` is opaque to
  the scheduler; only tiling/placement is scheduled, not the arithmetic.
- Headline results: 89 previously-unexplored fusion patterns discovered
  automatically (up to 48 ops fused into one kernel), 4.29x/2.07x geomean
  speedup vs PyTorch/ONNXRuntime, compilation ~40-100x faster than Ansor
  because the cost model is analytic rather than search-and-profile.

## Proposed tile DSL sketch (kernel-authoring layer, phase 1)

Maps directly onto Welder's four device interfaces at the *single-kernel*
granularity: automate `Allocate`/`LoadTiles`/`StoreTiles`, leave `ComputeTile`
as an opaque user-written body (same math as today, unchanged).

**Core types** (new module, e.g. `teeny-triton::tile`):

```rust
/// Declared, not computed: shape of one tensor's tile, in terms of BLOCK_*
/// consts (compile-time) and grid axes (runtime pid).
pub enum TileDim {
    Block(&'static str),  // references a `const BLOCK_M: i32` etc in scope
    Full(&'static str),   // whole dimension, e.g. HEAD_DIM in flash-attn
}

pub struct TileAxisBinding {
    pub dim: usize,                  // axis of the tensor's total shape
    pub tile: TileDim,
    pub grid_axis: Axis,             // which program_id drives this tile index
    pub stride_param: &'static str,  // name of the i32 param holding this dim's extent
}

/// Structured per-tensor-argument tile metadata — the thing that doesn't
/// exist anywhere today. This is the queryable analog of `KernelIo`.
pub struct TensorTileSpec {
    pub param: &'static str,
    pub rank: usize,
    pub axes: &'static [TileAxisBinding],
    pub reduction_axis: Option<usize>,  // Some(k) if looped/accumulated, e.g. GEMM's K
}

pub struct KernelTileSpec {
    pub inputs: &'static [TensorTileSpec],
    pub outputs: &'static [TensorTileSpec],
}
```

**Macro surface** — extend `#[kernel]` with per-arg `#[tile(...)]` attributes
rather than a parallel macro, so existing kernels stay one family. Example
rewrite of `elu_forward` (flat 1D case):

```rust
#[kernel]
pub fn elu_forward<T: Triton, D: Float, const BLOCK_SIZE: i32>(
    #[tile(dim = 0, block = BLOCK_SIZE, axis = X, extent = n_elements)]
    x_ptr: InPtr<T::Pointer<D>>,
    #[tile(dim = 0, block = BLOCK_SIZE, axis = X, extent = n_elements)]
    y_ptr: OutPtr<T::Pointer<D>>,
    n_elements: i32,
    alpha: f32,
) {
    // macro has already bound `x: Tensor` (loaded+masked) and
    // `y_store: impl FnOnce(Tensor)`, generated from the #[tile(...)] specs
    let one = T::full(&[BLOCK_SIZE], D::from_f64(1.0));
    let alpha_t = T::full(&[BLOCK_SIZE], D::from_f64(alpha as f64));
    let x_pos = T::gt(x, T::zeros_like(x));
    y_store(T::where_(x_pos, x, alpha_t * (T::exp(x) - one)));
}
```

Expansion generates exactly what `elu_forward` hand-writes today (code-shape
preserving, so generated source stays debuggable). `RuntimeOp::grid()` is also
derived automatically from `extent`/`block`, removing the duplicated
`m.div_ceil(block_m)`-style arithmetic in every hand-written `RuntimeOp` impl.

**Multi-dim / swizzled / reduction case** (GEMM) needs multiple axis bindings
per tensor plus a generated reduction loop:

```rust
#[kernel]
pub fn matmul_forward<T: Triton, D: Num, const BLOCK_M: i32, const BLOCK_N: i32, const BLOCK_K: i32, const GROUP_M: i32>(
    #[tile(dims = [0,1], block = [BLOCK_M, BLOCK_K], axis = [swizzled_m(GROUP_M), reduce], extent = [M, K])]
    a_ptr: InPtr<T::Pointer<D>>,
    #[tile(dims = [0,1], block = [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N], axis = [reduce, X], extent = [K, N])]
    b_ptr: InPtr<T::Pointer<D>>,
    #[tile(dims = [0,1], block = [BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N], axis = [swizzled_m(GROUP_M), X], extent = [M, N])]
    c_ptr: InOutPtr<T::Pointer<D>>,
    M: i32, N: i32, K: i32,
) {
    let mut acc = T::zeros::<D>(&[BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N]);
    for_reduce!(k in a_ptr, b_ptr => {
        acc = T::dot::<D, D>(a_ptr.tile(k), b_ptr.tile(k), Some(acc), InputPrecision::TF32, None);
    });
    c_ptr.store(acc);
}
```

`swizzled_m(GROUP_M)` is a named pid-decode strategy (matches the existing
`group_id`/`pid_in_group` swizzle already used in `matmul_forward`) — an
escape valve limited to the handful of index-decode patterns actually present
in this codebase (flat, 2D-swizzled, 3-axis batch/head/row for flash-attn),
not an attempt at full generality. Conv's sliding-window masked-load pattern
and flash-attn's online-softmax accumulator loop are further cases this needs
a concrete answer for before the DSL covers all four sampled kernel families
(elu/gemm/conv2d/flash_attn2).

## Relationship to a phase-2 Welder-style scheduler

`KernelTileSpec` becomes a `const fn tile_spec() -> KernelTileSpec` on every
`#[kernel]`-annotated fn, parallel to today's `const fn kernel_io() -> KernelIo`.
That's the structured data `PointwiseFuseProbe` currently fakes with a narrow
hand-rolled `BlockSized`/`NElementsTiled` check. With it, `Anduin`'s optimizer
pass could get:
- A real `Propagate` equivalent: per-op tile-shape inference from declared
  axis bindings instead of `infer_output_shape`'s "approximate as first-input
  shape" for binary ops.
- A real `MemTraffic` cost model: `sum(tile_bytes) * num_tiles`, computable
  directly from `extent`/`block` in `TensorTileSpec`, replacing today's
  all-or-nothing unary-elementwise-chain fusion with Welder's per-edge
  `SetConnect` + top-K `SubGraphTiling` search.

## Relationship to teenygrad-1bf

`teenygrad-1bf` specs `TritonFusionBackend` — the graph-level fusion
*decision + lowering* trait, enumerating 12 fusion cases (elementwise chains,
fan-in/fan-out, reduction-terminated regions, multi-reduction/softmax,
free reindex, GEMM/conv epilogue, hard barriers, custom ops, dtype-promotion,
training/backward). This issue is one layer lower and largely orthogonal in
scope: it's about *how a single kernel declares its own tile shape* so that
(a) hand-written kernels stop duplicating index/grid boilerplate, and (b) a
future fusion/scheduling pass — whether that ends up being
`TritonFusionBackend` itself, or a Welder-style tile-graph scheduler that
supersedes it — has real structured tile-shape and traffic-cost data to work
from instead of the current allowlist/probe approach. `teenygrad-1bf`'s open
question "when is fusion decided" (allowlist in `Graph::optimise()` vs. a
post-RuntimeOp decision in `TritonLowering`) and this issue's `KernelTileSpec`
proposal should be resolved together — worth flagging in whichever issue is
picked up first that they need to agree on where tile/traffic metadata lives
relative to `RuntimeOp` construction.

## Suggested phased scope

1. **Phase 1a — flat 1D tile DSL only.** `TileDim`/`TensorTileSpec`/
   `KernelTileSpec` + `#[tile(...)]` attribute restricted to the single-axis
   `block`/`axis = X`/`extent` case, prototyped against the existing
   pointwise/elementwise kernels (`elu_forward` and friends) — the case
   `PointwiseFuse` already handles by convention, so it validates the macro
   without also solving swizzle/reduction/multi-axis extraction.
2. **Phase 1b — multi-axis + reduction + named pid-decode strategies**
   (`swizzled_m`, batch/head/row for flash-attn, conv's masked sliding
   window), validated by rewriting `matmul_forward`, `conv2d_forward`, and
   `flash_attention2_forward` and diffing generated source against the
   hand-written originals (should be identical modulo cosmetic differences).
3. **Phase 2 — Welder-style scheduler.** `Propagate`/`SetConnect`/
   `MemTraffic`/two-step `GraphConnecting`+`SubGraphTiling` in `Anduin`,
   consuming `KernelTileSpec`. Explicitly out of scope until phase 1 lands and
   is validated against at least the GEMM/conv/flash-attn tile shapes, since
   Welder's cost model assumes accurate per-op tile-shape propagation that
   phase 1a alone (flat elementwise only) can't yet provide.

## Non-goals (this issue)

- No implementation — this issue is the design spec, matching
  `teenygrad-1bf`'s "spec, not code" framing.
- Does not re-litigate `teenygrad-1bf`'s 12-case fusion taxonomy or its open
  "when is fusion decided" question — flags the interaction point but leaves
  resolution to whichever issue is implemented first.
- Does not commit to Welder's exact cost-model constants (coalescing penalty,
  parallelism penalty) — those are GPU-microarchitecture-specific and need
  their own calibration pass against this project's CUDA driver, not the
  paper's V100/MI50/IPU numbers.

## References

- Yining Shi et al., "WELDER: Scheduling Deep Learning Memory Access via
  Tile-graph", OSDI 2023. https://www.usenix.org/conference/osdi23/presentation/shi
- `teenygrad-1bf` — spec: TritonFusionBackend (graph-level fusion trait this
  issue's phase-2 scheduler would either feed into or supersede).

## Impact on teenygrad-1bf's 12 fusion cases

Case-by-case read of how this tile DSL + a Welder-style scheduler would change
`teenygrad-1bf`'s fusion taxonomy, once phase 2 (the scheduler) exists:

**Directly resolved / substantially extended:**
- **Case 1 (elementwise chains)** — subsumed. `SetConnect` + register-level
  connection generalizes what `PointwiseFuse` already does by convention.
- **Case 2 (fan-in/multi-input elementwise)** — the case `Anduin::fuse_pointwise_chains`
  structurally cannot do today (single-consumer linear-chain assumption only).
  The tile-graph is a real DAG of operator-tiles, not a chain, so multi-producer
  nodes connect naturally without special-casing.
- **Case 4/5 (reduction-terminated, reduction+epilogue)** — Welder's paper
  describes this almost verbatim: "input tiles that contain reduction axes can
  be further partitioned into smaller ones... loaded and consumed sequentially
  by accumulating results," with the tiling size along the reduction axis
  chosen by the search. That is a concrete algorithm for the open "retiling
  mechanism" question below (replacing "most demanding member wins" with
  `SubGraphTiling`'s actual top-K-by-traffic search). `TensorTileSpec::reduction_axis`
  in the phase-1 sketch is exactly the hook this needs.
- **Case 7 (free reindex vs staged transpose)** — maps directly onto
  `SetConnect`'s level choice: reshape/slice/concat/transpose-that-doesn't-touch
  the coalescing dim connects at register level (free, index relabeling only);
  transpose that does touch it gets routed to a shared-memory connection (a
  staging tile) because that is what the traffic cost model favors. Mechanical
  answer to what case 7 currently flags as unresolved.
- **Case 3 (fan-out, materialize-vs-recompute)** — the tile-graph gives the
  right knob (per-edge `SetConnect`, so a producer can be register-connected to
  one consumer and materialized-to-global for another) and `MemTraffic` gives
  the right comparator. Caveat: the paper doesn't spell out an explicit
  "recompute vs cache" decision procedure — this is "the mechanism generalizes
  cleanly," not "Welder solved this outright."

**Partially helps:**
- **Case 6 (multi-reduction/softmax)** — Welder's results section states it
  fuses Q·K with softmax "when the sequence length is not long": the
  tile-graph trick of keeping the *entire* reduction axis resident as one tile
  at a memory level that fits it, collapsing two sequential passes into one
  `ComputeTile` body instead of two kernel launches. Covers the bounded case
  only; does not solve the case where the axis doesn't fit anywhere on-chip —
  that remains a genuinely grid-wide problem, same hard boundary as case 9.

**Changes the stated framing, not just the mechanism:**
- **Case 8 (GEMM/conv epilogue)** — `teenygrad-1bf` states as fact (citing
  Myelin/TensorRT profiling) that fusion "does not attempt to merge GEMM/conv
  main loops... only epilogue absorption." Welder's own Table 4 contradicts
  that as a *general* limit — it shows multiple convolutions fused into one
  48-op kernel, and §4.1 binds M/N/K tile axes to TensorCore MMA within the
  same scheduling framework as everything else. Adopting this DSL means case
  8's premise needs revisiting, not just its mechanism.

**Loosens but doesn't remove:**
- **Case 10 (custom ops)** — still opaque by construction today. Nothing stops
  extending `CustomOp` with an optional `Propagate`/tile-shape-inference hook
  (parallel to the existing `CustomOp::infer_output_shape`) so an op author can
  opt a custom op *into* the tile-graph instead of it being an unconditional
  hard boundary. A future loosening, not claimed as solved now.

**Doesn't move the needle:**
- **Case 9 (grid-wide barriers: topk/sort/NMS)** — still a hard boundary;
  Welder doesn't attempt this either.
- **Case 11 (dtype-promotion)** — orthogonal; a correctness gate applied on
  top of whatever the cost model picks, not something `Propagate`/`MemTraffic`
  reasons about.
- **Case 12 (training/backward)** — Welder is a static-inference compiler; no
  backward story in the paper at all. Same open question `teenygrad-1bf`
  already has.

## Impact on teenygrad-1bf's open questions

- **"Representation"** — resolved in favor of a real subgraph/region type over
  `Op::Fused`'s linear chain; the tile-graph model forces this, it isn't
  optional.
- **"When is fusion decided"** — the sharpest resolution. `teenygrad-1bf` is
  blocked because `RuntimeOp` (where `block()`/`grid()` live today) doesn't
  exist until post-lowering, so `Graph::optimise()` can't compare shapes.
  `KernelTileSpec` is a `const fn` generated by the `#[kernel]` macro at
  *compile time*, decoupled from `RuntimeOp` construction — so
  `Graph::optimise()` can query real tile-shape data before any `RuntimeOp` is
  built, removing the blocker outright rather than picking between the two
  options `teenygrad-1bf` currently lists.
- **"Kernel body composition"** — Welder's register-level `SetConnect` is
  implemented via TVM's `compute_inline`, i.e. genuine value-level
  composition, not scratch-buffer ping-pong. Concrete argument for
  `teenygrad-1bf`'s "harder refactor" option over keeping the ping-pong
  approach as permanent v1.
- **"Retiling mechanism"** — resolved via cost-model search (`SubGraphTiling`
  enumerates candidate output tile shapes, propagates, keeps min traffic)
  rather than a "most demanding member" heuristic.
- **"Stop-list location"** — still needed, but now has a principled test:
  an op belongs on the stop-list iff it cannot provide a `Propagate`
  (tile-shape-inference) implementation — unifying cases 9 and 10 under one
  predicate instead of two separately maintained allowlists.

title: tile DSL phase 1a: flat 1D TensorTileSpec + #[tile(...)] for elementwise kernels
description:
## Goal

First slice of the tile DSL sketched in teenygrad-3w0: `TileDim`, `TileAxisBinding`,
`TensorTileSpec`, `KernelTileSpec` restricted to the single-axis case (one
`BLOCK_*` const, `axis = X`, one `extent` param), plus a `#[tile(...)]` attribute
on `#[kernel]` fn args that generates the load/mask/store boilerplate and derives
`RuntimeOp::grid()`.

## Scope

- Core types in a new `teeny-triton::tile` module (`TileDim::Block`/`Full`,
  `TileAxisBinding{dim, tile, grid_axis, stride_param}`, `TensorTileSpec`,
  `KernelTileSpec`), restricted to rank-1 tensors / single grid axis.
- `#[tile(dim = 0, block = BLOCK_SIZE, axis = X, extent = n_elements)]` attribute
  parsing in `teeny_macros::kernel` (macros/teeny-macros/src/macros/kernel.rs),
  expanding to exactly the boilerplate hand-written today:
  `pid = T::program_id(Axis::X); block_start = pid*BLOCK_SIZE; offsets =
  T::arange(0,BLOCK_SIZE)+block_start; mask = offsets.lt(extent); T::load(...)`.
  Code-shape preserving — generated source should read like the hand-written
  original, not obscure it.
- Emit `const fn tile_spec() -> KernelTileSpec` per kernel, parallel to today's
  `const fn kernel_io() -> KernelIo`.
- Derive `RuntimeOp::grid()` automatically from `extent`/`block` where the DSL
  is used (removes the hand `n.div_ceil(block_size)` currently duplicated
  per-kernel).
- Rewrite `elu_forward`/`elu_backward` (kernels/teeny-kernels/src/nn/activation/elu.rs)
  and a small sample of other flat unary-elementwise kernels already covered by
  `PointwiseFuse` (kernels/teeny-kernels/src/graph/optimizer/ops/pointwise_fuse.rs)
  to use it.

## Acceptance criteria

- Generated kernel source for rewritten kernels is unchanged in observable
  behavior (existing snapshot/golden tests pass) — cosmetic diffs only.
- `PointwiseFuse`'s existing `BlockSized`/`NElementsTiled`/`KernelIo::is_unary_elementwise`
  probing still works unmodified against DSL-generated kernels (this phase does
  not touch `Anduin`/fusion decision logic at all).
- `RuntimeOp::grid()` for rewritten kernels comes from the derived
  implementation, not a hand-written override.

## Non-goals

- No multi-axis tiles, no reduction loops, no named pid-decode strategies
  (swizzle, batch/head/row) — that's phase 1b (teenygrad-3w0's phase 1b child).
- No scheduler, no `Propagate`/`SetConnect`/`MemTraffic` — that's phase 2.

## References

Parent spec: teenygrad-3w0 ("Proposed tile DSL sketch" section, phase 1a of
"Suggested phased scope").

title: SetConnect: per-edge memory-level search (register/shared/global)
description:
## Goal

Implement Welder's `SetConnect`: represent each graph edge as connectable at
a memory level (register / shared / global), and choose the best level per
edge using calibrated `MemTraffic` — replacing Anduin's current all-or-
nothing fusion decision (`PointwiseFuse`/`TileFuse` either fully fuse at
register level or don't fuse at all; there's no shared-memory middle ground
today).

## Scope

- An edge-labeled subgraph representation (a real generalization beyond
  `PointwiseFuse`'s/`TileFuse`'s fixed `Vec<Op>` chain — teenygrad-1bf's
  "Representation" open question, resolved in favor of a real region type).
- Per-edge enumeration of candidate memory levels, costed via
  teenygrad-3w0.4's calibrated `mem_traffic`.
- Wire into Anduin as (or alongside) the existing fusion passes.

## Acceptance criteria

Demonstrate at least one case where a shared-memory connection is chosen
over both full register-level fusion and no fusion, validated against the
calibrated cost model — i.e. the cost model's choice is shown to differ from
(and beat) the two extremes Anduin can express today.

## References

Parent: teenygrad-3w0 (Welder-mechanics section, `SetConnect`). Depends on
teenygrad-3w0.4 (calibrated `MemTraffic`) and teenygrad-3w0.8 (`Propagate`)
for correct per-level tile-shape/cost derivation.

comments.author: Arshad Mahmood
comments.text:
Phase A (teenyc MLIR primitives) landed and committed on branch feat/ttg-shared-memory-primitives in ../teeny (local commit e8077d27e16, not yet pushed). Added ttg.local_alloc/local_store/local_load + a MemDescType C-API constructor, built via the raw OperationBuilder::new("ttg.xxx", ...) idiom (avoiding a new melior_macro::dialect! block that would pull ~50 unrelated TritonGPUOps.td ops through a macro not proven to support every op's TableGen shape). All three ops build and pass MLIR's per-op verifier in isolation (104/104 rustc_mlir tests passing, including the new test_local_alloc_store_load).

Real, load-bearing finding from the pipeline-tolerance smoke test (test_shared_memory_pipeline.rs): the primitives do NOT survive teenyc's actual CUDA compile pipeline. convert-triton-to-tritongpu rewrites every tt.* op's tensor operands/results to carry an inferred TritonGPU layout encoding (e.g. tensor<128xi32, #ttg.blocked<{...}>>). A ttg.local_load result type built by hand before that pass runs has no such encoding and can't be unified with the encoded types around it -- "failed to legalize unresolved materialization ... that remained live after conversion". This reproduces for any realistic kernel (anything with tt.load/tt.store around the shared-memory stage), because TritonCompiler::compile runs the whole TTIR->TTGIR->LLVMIR->PTX pipeline as one opaque call with no exposed mid-pipeline injection point.

Fixing this needs either (a) a new hook to inject ttg ops after convert-triton-to-tritongpu runs (no such mechanism exists in teenyc's CudaBackend.cpp today), or (b) replicating enough of Triton's own layout-encoding inference to hand-construct correctly-encoded types up front -- real compiler-engineering depth comparable to why upstream Triton itself pushed explicit shared-memory management into a separate "Gluon" sub-language rather than mainline tl. Both are materially larger than Phase A's scope and were not attempted here.

Realistic scope for this issue given this finding: the two tiers Anduin can actually express today are register (teenygrad-3w0.9's FusionCore splicing -- genuinely register-resident, no round-trip) and global (PointwiseFuse/TileFuse/no-fusion -- all literal cudaMalloc scratch buffers, same memory tier, differing only in launch count). A cost-driven SetConnect choosing between those two, with the shared tier explicitly documented as blocked on the above, is the defensible deliverable -- not the original three-tier acceptance criterion as literally written. Awaiting direction on whether to implement that two-tier version now, keep pushing on the shared-memory blocker, or move on to teenygrad-3w0.11.

comments.author: Arshad Mahmood
comments.text: Explored the Language::GLUON pipeline further (per user follow-up): confirmed it's real and reachable -- wired use_gluon_pipeline through CudaCompileOptions/FFI, added a gluon.auto_encoding attribute constructor, and got it to genuinely skip convert-triton-to-tritongpu. But driving it with hand-built MLIR (rather than IR from Gluon's own Python frontend) hit a sequence of distinct issues: 'functions returning auto encoding must be fully inlined' (fixed by restructuring to a void-returning kernel), then a SIGSEGV inside the Gluon C++ passes on a fuller round-trip (load -> shared stage -> compute offsets -> store back), then a different 'arith.constant failed to infer return type' error even on a minimal version with no debugger available to diagnose further. Each fix surfaced a new, unrelated failure rather than converging, suggesting Gluon's pipeline expects IR built the way its own frontend builds it, not hand-rolled ops satisfying just the type/encoding rules. Reverted all of this (never installed) at user's request -- teenyc is back to exactly the Phase A commit (e8077d27e16). Decision on how to close out .10 (two-tier register/global SetConnect, vs. further shared-memory investigation with better tooling, vs. deferring) is still open.
